stories.title: Man crushed to death by car in Kanpur:Laid on roof, dragged 1.5km with hand trapped in window before being run over and abandoned
stories.summary: A young man was murdered in Kanpur. He was first hit by a car, then beaten and made to lie on the car's roof. Both his hands were pinned in the window panes as the car was driven at high speed for around 1.5 km. The attackers then brought the young man down from the car, ran the vehicle over him and fled. Passers-by informed the police and his family. He was subsequently taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead at 3 p.m. on Wednesday. The entire incident was captured on around 12 CCTV cameras installed in the area, and some of the footage has also emerged. The family alleges that the police did not register an FIR despite their complaint. The incident took place on Tuesday night in the area under the jurisdiction of Hanumant Vihar police station. First, two CCTV videos Accused of hitting him with a car over an old feud Beeru Singh Bhadauria (37), a resident of Arra, worked as a salesman for a food products manufacturing company. His family comprises his wife, Reena; two daughters, CV and Ishani; his son, Viraj; his father, Ram Shankar Singh; and his elder brother, Kuldeep Singh Bhadauria. Father Ram Shankar Singh said that a few days ago, Biru had a quarrel with Rajveer and Mewalal, residents of Khadepur Nai Basti. Since then, the two had harboured a grudge against him. On Tuesday night, Biru was returning home after attending the Dussehra fair. Mewalal arrived in a car on the way. Rajveer and three other youths were also travelling with him. They stopped Biru and assaulted him. When Biru tried to escape, they hit him with the car. They then laid him on the car's roof, trapped both his hands in the glass panes of the front windows and locked the windows. Injuries on body, fingers badly crushed According to the family, the accused drove the car at high speed through the streets. After travelling about 1.5 km, they untied Biru's hands and threw him out near Ashwani Trading Company in Rajendra Nagar. They then drove the car over him. Devendra Singh Chauhan, who was passing by, recognised Biru. He informed the family. They took him to a private hospital, from where he was referred to Hallett Hospital. Doctors declared him dead there on Wednesday. According to the family, Biru had injury marks in several places on his body. His fingers had also been badly crushed after his hands became trapped in the car windows. Family says: Incident captured on more than 12 CCTV cameras Two CCTV videos of the incident have emerged. One shows a car travelling at high speed, with a young man apparently trapped on its roof. The family alleges that the entire incident was recorded on more than 12 CCTV cameras, yet the police took no action. Angered by this, the family members created a disturbance on Wednesday, demanding action. DCP South Deependra Nath Chaudhary said that the victim's family had initially lodged a complaint about the accident at Hanumant Vihar police station. The family is now alleging murder. The matter is being investigated. Action will be taken against the accused if the allegations are found to be true. When the police traced the car number and the mobile phone locations of the accused, they were found in Jahanabad, Fatehpur. The accused are being searched for.

stories.title: UP freezes transfers of DMs and SDMs:Final voter list to be published on 4 January 2027, model code of conduct to come into force
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, officials involved in preparing the voter list will not be transferred without the Election Commission's permission. The restriction will apply to officials engaged in adding, deleting and correcting names on the voter list. The commission has made it clear that these officials cannot be removed until the voter list is finalised. Their positions will not be left vacant either. Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said the rule has been implemented for preparing the 2027 voter list. The aim is to ensure that the voter-list preparation process is completed without interruption. What will happen when? 12 November: The preliminary voter list will be published. 12 November to 11 December: People will be able to apply to have their names added to the voter list, get incorrect names corrected or have names deleted, and file complaints. By 28 December: The applications and complaints will be decided. 4 January 2027: The final voter list will be published. The Election Commission has informed all concerned departments about these rules. Officials have been instructed to complete the work within the stipulated time. News is being updated...

stories.title: Sanjay Nishad warns BJP over reservation:Says party will pay for betrayal; dares Akhilesh to contest from Gorakhpur
stories.summary: Ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad issued a stern warning to the BJP on Wednesday. He held a show of strength at Delhi's Talkatora Stadium under the pretext of a conference. He said the fishing community would have to be given reservation. "We will extend our support only when there is a commitment to reservation." Sanjay Nishad said his party was a friend of the BJP and did not want the alliance to suffer. The BJP would have to take a decision soon. If the demand was not met, the BJP would be deceived. Referring to the 2027 Assembly elections, he said the election would be important for the future of the Nishad community. Sanjay claimed that both the BJP and the Samajwadi Party wanted the Nishad Party's support. Power was incomplete without the Nishad Party, and the government would have to fulfil its demand. Sanjay Nishad told workers, "Get ready to fight; Delhi is not far away. The day the people take action, they will be left sweating." He claimed that major parties had panicked at the very mention of Talkatora. Sanjay Nishad challenged Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest the election from Gorakhpur. He said he would contest without the Bharatiya Janata Party's support and win by securing more votes than the Samajwadi Party. 'We have a share in the Constitution and will secure reservation' Addressing the convention, Sanjay Nishad said the Nishad community had been fighting for its constitutional rights for a long time. He claimed that the community accounts for around 18 per cent of the population and should receive the benefits of reservation. He said, "Our share is written into the Constitution. What do we want? Reservation." Calling on the BJP to fulfil its promise, he said the Nishad community was now uniting and raising its voice for its rights. In his address, Sanjay Nishad also referred to Nishadraj's fort and episodes associated with Lord Ram. He said that, along with honouring the Nishad community's historical heritage, its children should also receive the benefits of reservation. Demand to include Majhwar and Turaiha in the SC category At the conference, the Nishad community prominently demanded that the Majhwar and Turaiha communities be included in the Scheduled Caste category. Sanjay Nishad said Majhwar needed to be understood as a group of castes rather than as a single caste. Citing the reservation granted to some Nishad sub-castes in other states-Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi-he questioned why the Nishad community across the Yamuna should not receive the same benefit. He also demanded that the Turaiha community be given the benefit of reservation. Sanjay Nishad said securing reservation for the Nishad community was his key issue and that he had continued to raise it in the Legislative Assembly and on various other platforms. He demanded that the Centre and the state government take a firm decision on the matter. If there is a conspiracy to defeat my son in Chauri Chaura, the BJP will have to face the consequences In his speech, Sanjay Nishad also referred to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. He said the Nishad community's political participation and the issue of reservation would remain important before the election. He warned the BJP that if no decision was taken on the community's demand, the party could suffer political losses. Speaking about his son's defeat in the Khalilabad Lok Sabha seat, he said that BJP members had conspired against him, resulting in the BJP losing several neighbouring seats. Now, some people linked to the BJP want to carry out a similar conspiracy in Chauri Chaura. If that happens, the Nishad community is ready to teach the BJP a lesson in other seats as well. He appealed to the BJP to expel such people from the party, saying that the Nishad community would deal with them. Akhilesh should clarify his stand on securing reservation for Nishads Sanjay Nishad said that the interests of his community were paramount for him. He appealed to workers to strengthen the organisation in every village and unite the community through the flag of Nishadraj. He said that if the BJP did not take a positive decision on the issue of reservation, the party would have to consider its future political strategy. He also questioned Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, asking him to clarify his stand on providing reservation to the Nishad community. He should state whether he would provide reservation to Nishads by taking it from the 9 per cent OBC quota and adding it to the Scheduled Caste quota. People arrived from different states across the country According to the organisers, people from the Nishad community arrived from different states across the country to attend the convention. Issues related to reservation, social representation and the future of the community's children were raised at the convention. The programme emphasised the unity of the community and the demand for constitutional rights. Sanjay Nishad called on those present to continue the struggle.

stories.title: Wife kills husband 12 years younger, stuffs body in trunk:Dumps it on Unnao highway; allegedly having affair with tenant
stories.summary: A wife murdered her husband, who was 12 years younger than her, with the help of her lover in Unnao. She then wrapped the body in a bedsheet and blanket, locked it in an iron box, transported it in a pick-up vehicle and dumped it by the highway. Police found the body of a young man inside the box on the Rae Bareli-Unnao Highway on Tuesday. After an investigation, police arrested the woman, her lover and two others on Wednesday, solving the murder case. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Sadar Kotwali police station. Read the full case... Body found inside a box by the highway At around 10 p.m. on Tuesday, police received information that a suspicious box had been placed by the roadside in front of Health Hospital on the Raebareli-Unnao Highway. When police opened the box, they found the blood-soaked body of a young man wrapped in a sheet and blanket. Police examined CCTV footage from the scene and the roads in the surrounding area. The footage showed a Chhota Hathi loader arriving from the Gadankheda side with the box and, some time later, travelling towards Kanpur without it. Loader's number traced through CCTV cameras Police traced the loader's number (UP 35 AT 1938) through footage from cameras installed along the nearby roads. The pickup was found to be registered in the name of Rajesh Gupta. Police gathered information about the pickup and the people linked to it. It emerged that on 20 October, Neha had hired the pickup for ₹1,200 to vacate her rented room and move her belongings to another place. When police questioned Neha, she confessed to killing her husband with the help of her neighbouring tenant, Jitendra. The involvement of Tauheed and a minor in disposing of the body also emerged. Attacked her husband on the head with a grinding stone Neha, 42, is originally from Haroni village in Lucknow. She married Jagdish, a resident of Ataura in the Malihabad area, around 23 years ago. They have five daughters. Seven to eight years ago, Neha came into contact with Sonu, 30. The two later got married. They also have a five-year-old son. Sonu worked in a private job. Sonu and Neha often quarrelled and physically fought after their marriage. As a result, Sonu became addicted to drugs. Meanwhile, Neha began an affair with her neighbour and tenant, Jitendra alias Rahul, 42. Rahul lived in the rented accommodation with his wife. Neha and Jitendra then conspired to murder Sonu. On the night of 19 October, they attacked Sonu on the head with a grinding stone, leaving him covered in blood. They then pressed a blanket over his mouth and nose, causing his death. After the crime, they left the body in the room. Body placed in a box and left by the roadside along the highway According to the police, after the murder, Jitendra contacted his acquaintance Rajesh Gupta, who owned a pickup vehicle. A pickup was arranged to deliver goods to the location specified by Neha. The body, placed in a box, was then transported in the pickup. Tauheed and a minor also assisted Neha and Jitendra in the operation. The box was taken from Kanchan Nagar in Shuklaganj to Gadan Kheda. On the night of 20 October, the box was left by the roadside along the highway in front of Health Hospital. All of them then left the scene. Neighbour says: She had earlier tried to attack him with scissors Khushboo, Neha's neighbour and a tenant, said Neha and Sonu had been living as tenants in Kishan Lal Yadav's house for about a month. They often quarrelled. Khushboo claimed that Neha had earlier tried to attack Sonu with scissors. The two had quarrelled two days earlier as well. At around 6 p.m., four people had arrived two days before the incident and had the household belongings unloaded. On Wednesday morning, the police and SOG team took Rahul, alias Jitendra, with them. According to police records, two cases had already been registered against the arrested man, Tauheed. These include a 2025 Arms Act case and a theft case registered in 2026.

stories.title: Shraddha Dubey gets 72-hour transit remand:STF to bring her from Nagpur to Lucknow by car; aide Aamir also arrested
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh STF has obtained 72-hour transit remand for Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver Danish from the Nagpur district court. The STF will leave Nagpur for Lucknow with the three accused shortly. Shraddha Dubey was initially to be brought by air, but there was no direct flight to Lucknow. The plan was therefore changed. Lucknow is 850 km from Nagpur, so the journey will take 15-18 hours. Shraddha will be produced in a Lucknow court on Thursday. Meanwhile, two more audio recordings surfaced after her arrest, in which she is heard threatening Shiva while abusing him. Shraddha Dubey, Rashmi Dubey and Danish were arrested from an apartment in Nagpur on Tuesday. Meanwhile, the Uttar Pradesh STF has arrested Shraddha's driver Aamir. Aamir is reportedly said to have been with Shraddha when Shiva died. Shiva Sharma died under suspicious circumstances on 9 October after falling from Shraddha Dubey's flat in Lucknow. Shiva's mother filed an FIR against Shraddha Dubey for murder. Shraddha had been absconding since the incident. It is murder accused Shraddha's birthday today. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has arrived in Haridwar today to immerse her son's ashes. She left for Haridwar after Shraddha was arrested.

stories.title: Yogi raises uniform allowance for PPS officers by ₹8,600:Police personnel to get ₹2,500 for mobile recharges; CM makes three major announcements
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath made three major announcements for the police department. On Police Commemoration Day, he said, "The uniform allowance for police personnel has now been increased from ₹6,500 to ₹15,000. The motorcycle allowance has also been increased from ₹700 to ₹1,000. Police personnel will now receive ₹2,500 instead of ₹2,000 for SIM cards. Now, read two stories of martyrdom as well..." Read about those acts of police courage that everyone is saluting... A fire suddenly broke out at around 3 a.m. on 4 August in the Ecotech-3 industrial area of Greater Noida. Within moments, roaring flames and clouds of poisonous smoke engulfed the entire building housing the electronic PCB chip manufacturing unit. A fire engine reached the site with its siren blaring. The team that arrived to extinguish the fire included Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav. The biggest challenge was to bring the raging fire under control because chemicals and electronic equipment were stored inside the factory. Visibility was almost impossible amid the dense clouds of smoke. However, without worrying about their own lives, the team of firefighters entered the building carrying hoses. Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav were at the forefront. Holding the water hose, Rohit Yadav stayed at the front and sprayed water directly at the flames. Teerthpal Singh maintained the water pressure and supply. After considerable effort, when the team was very close to bringing the fire under control, the company's solid wall and heavy iron girder weakened due to the extremely high temperature and intense heat and suddenly collapsed. As the wall and iron beam fell without warning, five personnel, including Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav, were trapped under the debris. Cries rang out all around, and a cloud of smoke engulfed the area. Their fellow personnel and police force immediately launched a rescue operation. After considerable effort, all the trapped personnel were pulled out and taken to hospital. Despite the doctors' efforts, fireman Rohit Yadav and driver Teerthpal Singh could not be saved. The most emotional aspect of the operation was that all 450 employees working at the company were safely evacuated. Rohit Yadav was only 32 years old. He leaves behind a wife and two young daughters. Teerthpal Singh was 48 years old. His family includes his wife, a son and a daughter. Jalaun property dealer Vijendra Mor was kidnapped. It was suspected that a conspiracy had been hatched to kidnap and kill him in order to seize his land worth crores of rupees. Police received a tip-off that he had been taken to Haryana. The team consisted of four police personnel and one complainant. They were Sub-Inspector Mohit Kumar Yadav, Sub-Inspector Satyabhan Singh, Constable Ashok Kumar, Constable Pradeep Kumar and Vijendra's relative, Amrik Singh. They were all travelling in the Scorpio towards Jind in Haryana to conduct a raid in search of the businessman. Near Nuh, the Scorpio went out of control and collided with another vehicle on the KMP Expressway. Five people, including Sub-Inspector Satyabhan, Mohit Yadav, Constable Pradeep and Ashok, died in the accident. Later, an investigation revealed that Shribhagwan, Sanjeev alias Kokila, Mohit Malik and Amarjeet Suhag had forcibly put Vijendra into a Creta and kidnapped him. They then killed him and took his body to the Kupra forest in the Jalalpur police station area of Hamirpur. They poured around 40 litres of diesel over the body and set it alight so that the identity and evidence could be completely destroyed. On 29 July, police arrested Mohit Malik and his wife, Sapna Rani, from Chitaila farmhouse in Kadaura. During questioning, Mohit admitted to killing the businessman and also told police where the body had been disposed of. Acting on information provided by Mohit and Sapna, police recovered a skeleton from the Kupra forest.

stories.title: Revolt in BJP ahead of UP MLC elections:Devendra Singh says officials are threatening teachers; urges them to choose their leader on 23rd
stories.summary: BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh once again struck a rebellious note on Wednesday. He alleged that teachers in Uttar Pradesh were being threatened in an attempt to secure votes in the MLC elections. He said the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) in Azamgarh was threatening managers of unaided schools with the cancellation of their recognition. In Mau, the DIOS and the minority welfare officer were allegedly visiting schools and madrasas to threaten teachers. Similar letters were also allegedly issued in Ballia. Devendra Pratap Singh described this as a violation of the Model Code of Conduct and demanded that the Election Commission of India and the Uttar Pradesh Election Commission take action against the officials concerned. He said such threats could not be tolerated in a democracy. Devendra Pratap Singh, an MLC from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Graduates' Constituency, wrote a letter to teachers on 19 October. He appealed to them to vote against injustice and humiliation in the Legislative Council elections scheduled for 23 October. He has been hurt since being removed from the stage at a teachers' convention in Gorakhpur on 12 October. A photograph of him with Gorakhpur councillor Vishwajeet Tripathi, who has joined the Samajwadi Party, had also surfaced.

stories.title: Two UP women linked to Tiger Shroff firing:Supplied pistols and cartridges; family claims temple visit was a trap
stories.summary: A Uttar Pradesh connection has emerged in the firing at actor Tiger Shroff's car. Babita from Azamgarh and Radha from Sitapur transported consignments of pistols and cartridges to the shooters by train, taking them to Mumbai. They were paid between ₹10,000 and ₹12,000 for this. Radha is the girlfriend of Kunal, one of the shooters arrested. Both women are 23 years old. They have no criminal records and were working only as couriers. On the evening of 18 October, three men on motorcycles opened fire at Tiger's car in Juhu, Mumbai, as he was returning after playing football. Tiger was safe in the attack, while his driver was injured. Tiger himself took him to hospital in the car. On Tuesday, Delhi Police arrested Kunal (21) and Sumit (19), both from Sonipat, Haryana, along with Babita and Radha. On Monday, the police arrested the firing suspects, Hrithik from Bihar and Rehan and Phool Singh from Haryana, in Kota. Now, Babita's family speaks... Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Babita's sister Neelam. She is a resident of Kothiyar village in the Tahbarpur police station area of Azamgarh. Neelam said, "My younger brother Deepak works in Rajasthan. At around 11 a.m. on Tuesday, Deepak received a phone call from Delhi Police. The caller said that your sister Babita and her friend had been detained. Weapons were found in their bags." According to Neelam, a woman named Radha from Sitapur took Babita to Mumbai, saying they were going to visit a temple. Babita went to Mumbai on the pretext of visiting the temple and got trapped. Babita is not at fault. She had gone to Sonipat two years ago, where she worked in the packing section of a savoury snacks factory. Father says: Villager Rajnath took Babita to Sonipat Babita's father, Ramjatan Ram, works as a farm labourer in addition to farming. He said that Rajnath, a resident of the village, worked in Sonipat with his wife, Pooja, doing packing work. They had come to the village around two years ago. They had said that packing work in Sonipat paid ₹10,000-12,000. After this, Babita went to Sonipat with her cousin. A few months later, Pooja and her husband returned to the village, while Babita stayed there and began working. It was in Sonipat that Babita became friends with Radha, who lived in Nahvaiya village in the Naimisharanya police station area of Sitapur district. Babita had come to the village to attend a wedding on 9 June 2026. At the time, she had spoken about Radha. Babita is the youngest of three sisters. Both her elder sisters are married. She studied up to the graduation level. She has two brothers, one of whom lives in Rajasthan and the other in Ludhiana. Police reach Radha's home in Sitapur; her relationship with her husband had ended in 2018 Arrested Radha is a resident of Nahvaiya village in the Mishrikh police station area of Sitapur. Police officers in plain clothes reached her home and conducted a search. It emerged that Radha's relationship with her husband, Sunil, had ended in 2018. According to Sunil, they got married in 2015. Two or three years after the wedding, Radha left with her maternal cousin, taking their one-year-old son with her. The young man was a resident of Dadurpur in Kanpur. He took Radha to Mumbai, where they both did odd jobs. During this period, Radha met Kunal. Radha lived in rented accommodation with Babita in Sonipat Babita and Radha lived in rented accommodation in Bahalgarh, Haryana. Kunal, a resident of Sonipat in Haryana, had passed Class 10 and worked at a hotel. He was acquainted with Radha. Kunal had previously been jailed in a case. Amitabh and Salman were the real targets before Tiger The accused who opened fire at Tiger Shroff's car had come to Mumbai to target a major star. The Mumbai Crime Branch and Kota Police revealed during questioning that their targets included Amitabh Bachchan, Aamir Khan, Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar, among several other leading actors. According to Kota Police, the accused had been sent to Mumbai around a month earlier. Anil Pandit, an operative of the Lawrence gang, had asked them to target a major star. The accused conducted reconnaissance of the actors' homes and sent their videos to Anil Pandit. However, they changed their plan after seeing the tight security. The accused then planned to target Tiger Shroff. They learnt that Tiger came to play football every Sunday evening. The accused gathered information about him from Google and conducted reconnaissance for seven days. They planned to approach Tiger's car on the pretext of taking a selfie and open fire. Accordingly, the accused reached the spot on Sunday, but began shooting because of the crowd outside the park.

stories.title: Congress alleges 13,150 Muslim voters’ names altered in Pilibhit:Claims software manipulation; DM-SDM denied access
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress held a press conference today, 21 October, at its state headquarters in Lucknow. The Congress accused the Election Commission of large-scale manipulation in the voter list. Congress leaders claim that the EPIC numbers of around 13,150 voters on the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly seat are identical. However, their names and their fathers' names have been changed. Congress national spokesperson Supriya Shrinate said: After the final draft list was released in Uttar Pradesh on 10 April 2026, voters' names were changed between July and September without using Form 6 or Form 7. On the same EPIC number, the voter's original name was removed and another name was entered. For example, the name 'Aslam' was entered in place of 'Mohammed Yusuf'. 'Rigging was carried out through software, DM-SDMs had no access' Supriya Shrinate has alleged that the changes were made under a specific pattern, mainly targeting male voters from the Muslim community, so that the head of the family would be unable to cast his vote. During this process, 2,600 new voters were added to the Pilibhit Sadar seat without following due process, while the names of 804 voters were deleted. Supriya targeted Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar and technical head Seema Khanna. Verification under way in 25 more Assembly constituencies State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said that in the 2022 election, the BJP candidate won this seat by just 6,920 votes. He said this was an Election Commission manoeuvre that could easily be used to make anyone win or lose. The Congress is currently also conducting a detailed examination of the electoral rolls in 25 other Assembly constituencies in the state. Congress's 3 main demands- Congress to approach court State president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' said that the party would go to court against this entire fraud. Just as Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi are fighting to save democracy in Delhi, Congress will fight this issue in every district of Uttar Pradesh, from the streets to the courts. Meanwhile, MP Imran Masood praised the local workers in Pilibhit, saying that they had detected the irregularity with great precision; otherwise, the general public would never have known what had been done with their votes.

stories.title: Man dragged off moving scooter, slapped in Jhansi:Woman alleges molestation; chases him 100 metres as he begs for mercy
stories.summary: In Jhansi, a young man riding a scooter was chased and caught while fleeing after molesting a girl. She grabbed him from behind as the scooter was moving, pulled him off and knocked him to the road. He was beaten with kicks and punches. Meanwhile, the girl's female relative arrived and slapped the youth five or six times. During the incident, the accused folded his hands and apologised. He also touched the girl's feet. The girl said that the accused had molested her and then slapped her. After that, he began fleeing. She chased him for around 100 metres and caught him. Two of his friends were with him. Premnagar police detained the accused. The accused said that the girl had suddenly placed her vehicle in front of his scooter. He said he had narrowly escaped death and had not molested her. The incident took place on Tuesday afternoon near the crossing in the Mal Godam Railway Colony area under Premnagar police station. A video of the assault emerged on social media on Wednesday. Young woman said, ‘He harassed me, slapped me and abused me’ According to the young woman, she lives in Nai Basti and works at a shop in Sipri Bazaar. On Tuesday, she was riding her scooter to pick up her sister. Later, her sister called and said she would come herself, so she began returning to the shop. The young woman said that three men on a scooter were passing near the crossing. The man sitting at the back molested her. When she objected, he abused and slapped her. People present there caught the accused and began questioning him. Meanwhile, a woman was recording a video on her mobile phone. When she began speaking to the young woman, the accused fled on the scooter with his two friends. Chased for 100 metres and pulled off the scooter The young woman chased the accused for about 100 metres, grabbed him by the collar and pulled him off the scooter. During this time, her female relative also arrived and began slapping the accused. The police were then informed. When the police arrived, the accused was handed over to them. Accused says: I narrowly escaped death; I did not molest her The accused identified himself as Ajay and said he lived in Rajiv Nagar, Nagra. Denying the molestation charge, he said the young woman had suddenly placed her vehicle in front of his scooter, causing him to narrowly escape being involved in an accident. He said he had only asked the young woman to leave quickly. The young woman beat him, but he had no complaint. He also said that he folded his hands and apologised and touched the young woman's feet. Premnagar police station in-charge Sher Singh said: After the incident, the young woman came to the police station with her family. The family has not yet filed a written complaint. Action is being taken after taking accused Ajay into custody.

stories.title: ‘I don’t consider Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh gods’:SP leader takes oath in Delhi; BJP questions Akhilesh over Hindu votes
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) national spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati has faced controversy over religious beliefs after a video emerged showing him at an event where participants took an oath to reject Hindu deities and refrain from worshipping them. The video prompted the BJP to target the SP and its national president, Akhilesh Yadav. BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi asked whether the party wanted Hindu votes, accusing it of repeatedly hurting Hindu sentiments through its leaders. The event was organised by the Bharatiya Bauddha Mahasabha at Ambedkar Bhawan on Rani Jhansi Road in Delhi on 20 October. Participants took pledges rejecting belief in Hindu deities and their worship. See the pictures... What does the video show? The video shows several people taking an oath that includes rejecting Hindu deities, including Gauri and Ganpati, and refusing to worship them. The pledge also rejects the belief in divine incarnations and the idea that Gautama Buddha was an incarnation of Vishnu. It includes statements rejecting Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh, Ram and Krishna as gods and refusing to worship them. BJP targets Akhilesh Yadav BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi accused the SP of following a broader strategy against Sanatan Dharma and repeatedly allowing its leaders to hurt Hindu sentiments. “Does the Samajwadi Party not want Hindu votes?” he asked. Tripathi said Azam Khan had earlier been at the centre of similar controversies and alleged that the party had later assigned another leader the task of tearing up or burning copies of the Ramcharitmanas. He accused the SP spokesperson of hurting Hindu sentiments during the Vijayadashami festival. Tripathi also alleged that the party was so focused on religious appeasement that it continued to insult Hindu beliefs. Bhati says, ‘I have no Intention of converting’ As the controversy grew, Bhati issued a clarification on social media. He said he respected every religion, caste, social group and community, adding that he was particularly drawn to Buddhism and the teachings of Gautama Buddha. He also said the ideas of Dr BR Ambedkar had deeply influenced him. “As a true socialist, I respect every religion, caste, social group and community. I attend events where I am invited and welcomed with respect,” Bhati said. He added that he visited gurdwaras when invited by members of the Sikh community, attended Muslim community events and participated in Hindu festivals. Bhati alleged that after the event, the BJP IT cell and what he called extremist elements spread misinformation on social media by claiming that he was converting to another religion. He clarified that he neither needed to convert nor had any intention of doing so. Bhati said people could serve humanity while remaining within their own religion and speak out against discrimination, untouchability, hatred, superstition and hypocrisy. He also urged people not to fall for what he described as misinformation spread by the BJP IT cell. He ended his post with the slogans “Jai Bhim” and “Namo Buddhaya”. Bhati has faced controversy before SP spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati has faced criticism over his remarks in the past as well. A few days ago, he was embroiled in a controversy over a comment comparing Brahmins to sex workers. The statement had also drawn criticism towards the SP. Fresh political challenge for the SP The latest controversy has put the SP in another politically difficult position. The BJP is using the episode to question the party’s position on religious beliefs, while Bhati has linked his participation in the event to his interest in Buddhism and Ambedkar’s ideas, accusing the BJP of spreading misinformation about his intentions.

stories.title: 2 govt employees stabbed to death in UP:One stabbed eight times in the stomach, the other’s throat slit
stories.summary: Two friends were stabbed to death on Dussehra night in Deoria on Tuesday. Both worked as government employees. One had eight stab wounds to his abdomen, while the other had his throat slit. The two had gone to watch the Dussehra fair. Their bodies were found lying on the road at around 12.30 am. Police identified the men using a railway identity card and a mobile phone. The incident took place near Badhaya Hardo village in the Mail police station area, around 50 km from the district headquarters. Both friends worked as government employees Vakil Yadav, 35, a resident of Karmaha village in the Mail police station area, worked as a Group D employee with the Railways. He was posted at Lar Road railway station. His friend Vinay Yadav, 35, lived in Itahura Hajam village, around 1.5 km away. He worked as a Group D employee with the Gorakhpur Housing Development Department. According to Kaushalya, Vakil’s wife, her husband returned home at around 6 pm on Tuesday after finishing his duty. His friend Vinay called him and invited him to watch the Dussehra fair in Lar. Vakil then left home on Vinay’s motorcycle. Vinay’s wife says police called at 1 am Vinay’s wife, Rinki, said the police called her at around 1 am to inform her that both men had been murdered. Their bodies were found near Badhaya Hardo on the Ram-Janki Marg, around 5 km from their homes. When family members reached the spot, they learnt that the men had been attacked with knives. According to the police, the initial investigation indicated that both men had been killed with a sharp-edged weapon. Vinay had around eight stab wounds on his body, while Vakil’s throat had been slit. A cut measuring around 2.5 inches was found on Vakil’s neck, which was partially severed. He also had a stab wound to his abdomen. Vinay leaves behind two sons; Vakil had four children Rinki said Vinay had returned home on Saturday for the Dussehra holiday. The couple have two sons, Vivek, 8, and Abhishek, 6. Vakil had four children — three daughters, Aakanksha, Ankita and Kaju, and a son, Adarsh. Three police teams formed to investigate murder After receiving information about the double murder, Superintendent of Police Abhijit R. Shankar reached the crime scene late at night and inspected the spot. He formed three police teams to investigate the case. Police are conducting raids to trace the suspects, and the bodies have been sent for post-mortem examinations. “The incident took place late at night. Both men were murdered with a sharp-edged weapon. Teams have been deployed to identify the accused. CCTV footage from the route and the call records of both men are being examined,” SP Abhijit R. Shankar said.

stories.title: Kashi air show grand rehearsal:Commandos land on cruise by helicopter as 52 fighter jets, including Rafale, perform stunts
stories.summary: A grand rehearsal for the air show was held in Varanasi on Wednesday. Commandos descended from a helicopter onto a cruise ship at Namo Ghat. Shortly afterwards, they climbed back onto the helicopter using a rope. Namo Ghat echoed with the roar of 52 fighter jets, including the Rafale and Sukhoi. The fighter jets thrilled spectators with touch-and-go manoeuvres and low-level flypasts over the Ganga. CCTV cameras monitored the entire premises. Spectators were allowed entry after three layers of security checks. A total of 100 aircraft took part in the air show rehearsal. Besides fighter jets, the aircraft included 15 transport planes, 32 helicopters and the vintage aircraft Sarnath. They arrived after taking off from 12 airports across the country. The air show is being organised in Kashi to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. It will be held over three days — October 22, 23 and 25. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also attend the air show on October 25.

stories.title: Bulandshahr ADM Judicial Bharat Ram Yadav dies of heart attack:57-year-old officer dies at Lucknow’s PGI; posted in city two years ago
stories.summary: Bulandshahr Additional District Magistrate (Judicial) Bharatram Yadav has died of a heart attack. He breathed his last at Lucknow’s Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGI) at 10 pm on Tuesday. He had been admitted to Fortis Hospital in Noida on Sunday after suffering a heart attack in Bulandshahr. He also suffered a brain haemorrhage. As his condition did not improve, Bharatram Yadav (57) was shifted to Lucknow PGI on Tuesday morning. Despite the doctors’ best efforts, he could not be saved. A native of Faizabad, he had been posted in Bulandshahr for two years. Promoted from SDM to ADM two years ago Bharatram Yadav was a 2015-batch promotee PCS officer. He had been posted as ADM (Judicial) in Bulandshahr since 2025. Earlier, he served as SDM in Pratapgarh. He is survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter. His daughter was married in 2020 to Ashwini Kumar, who is posted as SDM in Mathura. His elder son is a doctor posted at King George’s Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow, while the younger son is in Prayagraj, preparing for the civil services.

stories.title: Meeting held in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar for graduates’ constituency election:Support announced for BJP candidate Awanish Kumar Singh
stories.summary: A meeting was held at a private hotel in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar to discuss the graduates’ constituency election. BJP candidate and engineer Awanish Kumar Singh, who is contesting for the Legislative Council, attended the meeting as the chief guest. The event was organised by Kunwar Awanish Singh, founder of the Sanatan Task Force (STF) and national president of the All India Kshatriya Mahasabha (Youth). Engineer Abhay Singh Raghuvanshi, Bhanu Pratap Singh and hundreds of graduates attended the meeting. Pushpendra Singh, Rahul Singh and Mohammad Siddiqui announced their support for the BJP candidate along with their associates. Aam Aadmi Party state vice-president Abhishek Pratap Singh and Abhishek Dubey also announced their support for Awanish Kumar Singh along with their teams. The meeting also discussed issues related to education, employment and regional development.

stories.title: Chetak helicopters to shower flowers over Ganga:Air show begins with Surya Kiran’s Ganga formation, ends with a flypast over Dashashwamedh
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force has announced the schedule and format of the air show in Varanasi following a briefing. The show will begin at 11 am daily and feature two sessions lasting 50 minutes and 40 minutes, respectively. Preparations have been completed, with around 100 aircraft set to participate in the display. The show will begin each day with a Ganga formation by the Surya Kiran aerobatic team, showcasing the Kashi theme, and conclude with a flypast over Dashashwamedh. According to Air Vice Marshal PVS Narayan, the TK display will take place on the 22nd, 24th and 25th. No separate activities are planned for any particular day. Chinook to perform water touch-and-go The Air Force said the activities planned in front of Namo Ghat will also take place in front of the Ganga Gate of Kashi Vishwanath Temple. These will include a water touch-and-go manoeuvre by a Chinook helicopter and a flower shower over the Ganga by Chetak helicopters at both locations. Group Captain Parijat Saurabh outlined the air show’s programme during the Air Force briefing, explaining how the display would begin and conclude. Know the air show formation • KASHI: Three Kiran aircraft will fly in a V-shaped Vic formation, which symbolises victory. The aircraft will fill the sky above the Ganga with the colours of the Indian tricolour. • VARUNA: Three ALH Mk III helicopters from the Indian Air Force and Indian Army will take part and will also demonstrate slithering operations, an exercise involving descending with the help of ropes. • KEDAAR: A lone Rafale aircraft will fly behind the Kashi formation and perform precise aerobatic manoeuvres at low altitude. • HANUMAN AND SARNATH: A lone Su-30MKI aircraft will perform aerial manoeuvres at low altitude under the call sign "Hanuman". This will be followed by a lone Harvard aircraft demonstrating precise manoeuvres in the "Sarnath" formation. • Sarang (SARANG): The Indian Air Force's highly skilled Sarang Helicopter Display Team will also take part in the air display. • Omkar and Ganga (OMKAR AND GANGA): In the "Omkar" formation, three Mi-17 V5 helicopters will fly in a 'Vic' formation carrying the national flag and the Indian Air Force flag. This will be followed by the "Ganga" formation, in which three Chetak helicopters will shower flowers. • Rudra (RUDRA): A lone Sukhoi-30MKI aircraft will make a high-speed pass over the stage. • Bhagirathi (BHAGIRATHI): Two indigenous Light Combat Helicopters (LCHs) and Apache attack helicopters will fly together in a 'diamond' formation. • Tridev (TRIDEV): An Indian Navy Kamov-31 will lead the formation, accompanied by an Indian Air Force ALH MK III and an Indian Army ALH MK III flying in the 'Victory' formation. The Tridev formation will showcase the spirit of jointness, seamless coordination and inter-service synergy among the three services. • Alaknanda: A total of two Chinook and two ALH Mk IV helicopters will fly in an "inverted Victory" formation, with one Chinook at the rear. • Bhairav: One C-295 and two Dornier aircraft will fly past the front of the platform in a "Victory" formation. • KAILASH: One C-130 and two An-32 aircraft will fly in a 'vic' formation. • TRILOCHAN: One AEWC (airborne early warning and control) aircraft will fly in a 'vic' formation, escorted by two MiG-29 fighter aircraft. • Natraj (NATRAJ): A P-8I maritime patrol aircraft of the Indian Navy will fly alongside two Mirage-2000 fighter aircraft. This formation will symbolise the strong integration of maritime surveillance and aerial combat capabilities. • Mahadev (MAHADEV): An IL-78 aerial refuelling tanker aircraft will fly alongside three Mirage-2000 fighter aircraft. • VISHWANATH, PASHUPATI AND NEELKANTH: Three Sukhoi-30MKI aircraft will fly in a 'Vic' formation in the "Vishwanath" formation. This will be followed by the "Pashupati" formation, featuring four Jaguar aircraft in a 'Diamond' formation. Immediately afterwards, the "Neelkanth" formation of three Rafale aircraft will appear. • PRACHAND: Six fighter aircraft-Sukhoi-30MKI, Rafale, Jaguar, Mirage-2000, LCA (Tejas) and MiG-29-will fly together in an 'arrowhead' formation. The PRACHAND formation is a tribute to the Indian Air Force's unwavering combat capability, demonstrated recently during 'Operation Sindoor'. These frontline fighter aircraft will showcase the Indian Air Force's readiness to serve national objectives, its precision-strike capability and its ability to deliver decisive air power. • ASSI: India's indigenous aircraft, the LCA Tejas, will be the main attraction under the callsign "ASSI". It will showcase the expertise of indigenous aerospace engineering, advanced flight capabilities and the strength of India's growing self-reliance in fighter aviation. The aircraft will perform aerobatics at low altitude. • Dashashwa: In the "Dashashwa" formation, a C-17 Globemaster aircraft will lead, followed by nine Suryakiran Hawk aircraft performing a spectacular flypast over the venue. After that, the skies will be dominated by India's renowned Suryakiran Aerobatic Team.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to face 3-hour power cut today:Several areas to remain without electricity from 10 am to 1 pm for road widening work
stories.summary: Power supply will remain suspended for three hours in several areas of Gorakhpur on Wednesday due to road widening work and the shifting of insulated power lines. According to the electricity department, the work will be carried out from 10 am to 1 pm, affecting thousands of consumers connected to the concerned substations and feeders. Officials said power supply would be completely suspended in areas served by the 11 kV Rail Vihar and Karim Nagar feeders under the Raptinagar New power substation. Areas connected to the Shahpur power substation will also face the three-hour outage. Residents advised to complete essential tasks The electricity department has issued a public notice in advance to minimise inconvenience to residents. Consumers have been advised to store water and complete essential tasks requiring electricity before 10 am. stories.title: ‘Sister-in-law cooked without bathing’:Daughter blames brother’s wife for Lakhimpur fire; son arrested after father dies
stories.summary: My sister-in-law used to cook without bathing. In our family, food is prepared only after bathing. When my mother objected, she would complain to my brother. On the day of the incident, my sister-in-law served my father food made that morning, and my mother got angry. I believe my brother is innocent. My sister-in-law set my parents on fire. These are the allegations made by the daughter of a couple in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri district. Her father, Balram Shah, died on Tuesday (October 20), while her mother, Baijanti, remains in critical condition after the two were allegedly set on fire using petrol. However, their daughter-in-law, Chaya, has denied having any dispute with her father-in-law. “My father died when I was young, and I considered my father-in-law my own father. I never even had an argument with him,” she said. Before his death, Balram allegedly accused his son of setting them on fire. Police have arrested the son, Sapalu, in connection with the case. The incident took place in Chakhra village under the Nighasan police station area. A Dainik Bhaskar team travelled around 60 km from the district headquarters to the village and spoke to family members to understand what happened. Read the report... First, understand the case Balram Shah, 60, lived with his wife, Baijanti, 58, in Chakhra village. Their only son, Sapalu, 30, lived with his wife, Chaya, 28, in one half of the house. The couple had been married for 11 years and have three children. Balram also had three married daughters: Poonam, Mamta and Neelam. Balram sold tikki and samosas at the village crossroads to support his family. Sapalu ran a separate momos stall at the same crossroads, around 100 metres from their home. Family disputes reportedly preceded the incident Neighbours said Baijanti and Chaya frequently argued, while Sapalu also had strained relations with his parents. At around 10 pm on Saturday (October 17), an argument reportedly broke out between the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law. Sapalu joined the dispute. When his mother told him to stay out of it, he allegedly began arguing with her as well. Balram tried to intervene, but Sapalu allegedly pushed him. He then went outside to his motorcycle, took out petrol and poured it on his parents, who were standing under a thatched roof, before setting them on fire with a matchstick. Balram sustained severe burns, while Baijanti was admitted to a private hospital for treatment. Police arrested Sapalu in connection with the incident. Sister claims brother is innocent, blames sister-in-law Balram’s daughter alleged that her sister-in-law had threatened her parents during an earlier dispute. She said, “I do not know what my sister-in-law told my brother. About an hour later, the fire was started. I do not know whether my brother set them on fire or my sister-in-law did. I believe my brother is completely innocent. If he had started the fire, why would he try to put it out? His hand was also burnt while trying to extinguish the flames.” She further claimed that Chaya had threatened her parents in front of neighbours during an earlier argument, allegedly saying that she would burn them. The daughter also alleged that Chaya was involved with another man. These claims have not been independently established. Daughter-in-law says she was asleep when the fire broke out Chaya denied having any dispute with her in-laws and said she regarded them as her parents. “My father was no longer alive after I got married, so I considered my in-laws my parents. My father-in-law was a good man and never said anything hurtful to me. My husband did not consume intoxicants, but my in-laws drank alcohol. They used to argue with each other, but I never fought with them,” she said. Chaya claimed she had gone to sleep at around 8.30 pm while putting her children to bed. According to her, her father-in-law had not returned from his shop by then. “I did not know when he came home at night. I learnt about the incident when I heard people shouting. By the time I reached the spot, the fire had been completely extinguished. My father-in-law, mother-in-law and husband had all suffered burns. They were screaming in pain. All three were taken to hospital,” she said. Chaya has since gone to her parental home, according to Balram’s younger brother. Family says Balram was mistakenly believed to have died earlier After the incident, Balram was taken to the Nighasan Community Health Centre and then to the district hospital in Lakhimpur. As his condition deteriorated, he was referred to King George’s Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow. News of his death spread on Monday. However, his brother Radhe said doctors had described Balram’s condition as extremely critical, and the family had expressed a desire to take him home. While returning, they learnt that news of his death had spread in the village. When Balram’s breathing became rapid on the way, the family admitted him to a private hospital. He died there at around 6 pm on Tuesday (October 20). Radhe said Balram had made a statement before his death, based on which police registered a case. He demanded action against the accused. Uncle accuses nephew and suspects daughter-in-law’s involvement Balram’s younger brother, Baggu Lal, alleged that Sapalu had poured petrol on his parents and set them on fire. He rejected Chaya’s claim that she had been asleep. He said that when family members arrived, Chaya was sitting on a cot with her children. He also alleged that she could have been involved in the incident and demanded that the police question her. “If the boy is punished, the daughter-in-law should also be punished,” he said, alleging that Sapalu gave his earnings to his wife. These are allegations made by family members and have not been established by the police. Villagers reportedly broke through the door to reach the victims Another of Balram’s younger brothers, Jhabbu Lal, said he was asleep when he heard the commotion. “When I came out, I saw that there was a fire. We rushed there, but the door was locked from inside. We shouted for help, and villagers also gathered. Everyone tried to get inside, but the door would not open,” he said. He added that neighbours eventually removed bricks from the rear section of the house and opened the inside latch. “By the time we entered, everything had been burnt. My nephew’s hands were also burnt. I did not see anyone setting the fire, but these were the only people present at the time,” he said. Police investigating allegations Nighasan police station in-charge inspector Gopal Narayan Singh confirmed that Balram had died during treatment in Lucknow. “The accused son has been arrested. A post-mortem examination will be conducted. The allegations made by family members are being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and the complaint,” he said.

stories.title: 3 rebel Samajwadi MLAs set to get BJP tickets:Party organisation opposes strongman Abhay; Nishad quota complicates Vinod’s Kalpi seat
stories.summary: Three of the seven rebel Samajwadi Party MLAs are likely to get BJP tickets. They include Manoj Pandey, the MLA from Unchahar, who has been made a minister in the Yogi cabinet. The BJP has appointed Chayal MLA Pooja Pal as its state vice-president. Rakesh Pratap Singh joined the BJP on October 14. Along with him, MLA Abhay Singh and MLA Vinod Chaturvedi also joined the BJP. However, amid internal differences within the party, uncertainty remains over whether they will contest the Assembly elections. Two other rebel MLAs are Ashutosh Maurya and Rakesh Pandey. Both are still trying to find their place in the SP and have not joined the BJP yet. First, let’s look at the constituencies from which the three MLAs who rebelled against the SP could get BJP tickets. Manoj Pandey is considered one of the prominent Brahmin faces in the Awadh region. He won the Unchahar seat even during the strong BJP waves of 2017 and 2022. After rebelling against the SP in 2024, the BJP promptly made him a cabinet minister in the Yogi government, assigning him the Food and Civil Supplies portfolio, considering his political stature. Two factors are working in his favour for a BJP ticket. First, he is a prominent Brahmin leader. Second, he has a strong hold across the Awadh region. Considering his cadre and political influence, he is widely expected to contest the Unchahar seat on a BJP ticket. Rakesh Pratap Singh has been elected MLA from the Gauriganj seat in Amethi three consecutive times, in 2012, 2017 and 2022. He is an influential Thakur leader. Gauriganj has a sizeable Brahmin and Dalit population, while the Thakur community has long held political dominance in the constituency. Two factors are working in Rakesh’s favour for a BJP ticket. First, he is a prominent Thakur leader with a strong political presence. Second, he has an unblemished image. The path to securing a ticket is also considered almost clear for him within the BJP organisation. Pooja Pal, the MLA from the Chayal seat, belongs to an extremely backward community. The Pal community has a significant population across Prayagraj, Kaushambi, Bundelkhand and the Awadh region. This is why Pooja Pal was given a key post as the BJP’s state vice-president. Her husband, Raju Pal, a BSP MLA at the time, was publicly murdered by the Atiq Ahmed gang in 2005. Two factors are working in her favour for a BJP ticket. First, she is a prominent woman leader. Second, the BJP wants to build political momentum in eastern UP and Bundelkhand by giving her a ticket. Political analyst Ratanmani Lal says these three leaders won on SP tickets in the 2022 Assembly elections despite the difficult circumstances and the BJP wave. By giving them tickets, the BJP can not only increase its seat tally but also directly capture constituencies that have long been strongholds of the SP. Ticket prospects of these two rebel MLAs hang in the balance 1. Abhay Singh faces Khabbu Tiwari; deadlock over Gosainganj seat A tussle continues between Abhay Singh, a strongman MLA who switched from the SP to the BJP, and Indra Pratap Tiwari, popularly known as ‘Khabbu Tiwari’, a traditional BJP cadre leader, over the Gosainganj seat. During the 2022 Assembly elections, Khabbu Tiwari was in jail, so his wife, Aarti Tiwari, contested on a BJP ticket. Abhay Singh defeated her by 13,079 votes. UP Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has openly backed Abhay Singh. Meanwhile, several senior leaders, including national general secretary Harish Dwivedi, support Khabbu Tiwari. Ignoring Khabbu Tiwari could prove costly for the BJP as it seeks to retain the support of Brahmin voters in the Ayodhya region. The party is also deliberating over Abhay Singh’s strongman image. It is possible that both leaders could be accommodated in two different Assembly constituencies in Ayodhya district. 2. Vinod Chaturvedi’s seat caught between Nishad Party’s claim and local opposition Kalpi MLA Vinod Chaturvedi has joined the BJP, but his path ahead is not easy. The Kalpi seat was part of the seat-sharing quota of the Nishad Party, an NDA ally. In 2022, Vinod Chaturvedi defeated Nishad Party candidate Chhote Singh Chauhan by just 2,816 votes. Nishad Party president Dr Sanjay Nishad wants to reclaim the seats his party lost. If the Kalpi seat goes to the Nishad Party, Vinod Chaturvedi will have to contest on its terms. Another challenge for Vinod is that the BJP’s local cadre and Chhote Singh’s supporters are opposing his candidature, calling him an outsider. Will the remaining two MLAs join the BJP or return to the SP? Rakesh Pandey, Jalalpur (Ambedkar Nagar): During the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections, he cross-voted in favour of BJP candidate Sanjay Seth. The SP has still not expelled him. Rakesh Pandey wants his son, Ritesh Pandey, to enter the Assembly through the SP. This is why he has not joined the BJP yet. Ashutosh Maurya, Bisauli (Badaun): After rebelling, Ashutosh Maurya met SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and apologised. After receiving Akhilesh Yadav’s forgiveness, he has remained active in the SP. However, he won the 2022 election by a margin of just 1,834 votes. If the SP does not give him a ticket, he could switch sides. BJP wants to regain lost ground in Awadh and Bundelkhand The question now is why the BJP is focusing so much on these seven rebel SP MLAs. There are three major reasons. First, the BJP lost high-profile Lok Sabha seats such as Faizabad (Ayodhya), Amethi and Kaushambi in the 2024 elections. The party is banking on these influential local leaders to strengthen its lost foothold in these areas. Second, the rebel MLAs include prominent Brahmin leaders such as Manoj Pandey and Vinod Chaturvedi, Thakur leaders such as Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh, and an extremely backwards-class leader like Pooja Pal. By bringing these leaders on board, the BJP wants to consolidate the vote banks of these communities and strengthen its position in the Awadh and Bundelkhand regions ahead of the 2027 elections. Third, these leaders managed to win their respective seats on SP tickets in the 2022 Assembly elections despite the BJP wave. The BJP believes that bringing them into its fold could not only increase its seat tally but also help it make direct inroads into the SP’s strongholds. SP MLAs rebelled after cross-voting In February 2024, elections were held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. The contest became complicated as 11 candidates were in the fray for the 10 seats. The BJP fielded Sanjay Seth as its eighth candidate, while the SP did not have enough votes to win all three seats contested by its candidates. On polling day, seven SP MLAs- Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh, Pooja Pal, Vinod Chaturvedi, Rakesh Pandey, and Ashutosh Maurya- defied the party whip and cross-voted in favour of BJP candidate Sanjay Seth. As a result, all eight BJP candidates won, while the SP’s third candidate lost the election.

stories.title: Judge throws pen after sentencing Muskaan and Sahil to death:Orders them hanged by neck until dead; quotes Mahabharata verse
stories.summary: In the high-profile murder case of Merchant Navy officer Saurabh Rajput, who was killed by his wife, Muskaan Rastogi, and her lover, Sahil, a Meerut court sentenced both accused to death on Wednesday. The brutal murder had shocked the nation. Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the verdict at 4.22 pm. As soon as the sentence was announced, Saurabh’s mother and brother, who were seated in the courtroom, broke down. His mother folded her hands and thanked the court before wiping away her tears with the pallu of her sari. Quoting a Hindi rendering of a verse from the Mahabharata, the district judge said, Punishing those who commit wrongdoing is also a duty of righteousness. When the people sleep, the court delivers punishment. The judge immediately threw into a dustbin the pen he had used to write the death sentence for Muskaan and Sahil. Read what happened, and when, inside the courtroom on Wednesday, the day Muskaan, who cut Saurabh’s body into five pieces and packed them in a blue drum, and her lover Sahil were sentenced… Muskaan joined the courtroom with her daughter in her lap 20 minutes before the sentence 4 pm: The Meerut district judge’s courtroom was packed with people waiting to hear the verdict in the sensational blue drum murder case. Saurabh’s mother, Renu Devi, and his elder brother, Rahul alias Bablu, were seated on chairs. Several senior and junior lawyers were also present. After 4 pm, Muskaan and Sahil were connected to the courtroom from jail through a video conference. Muskaan was wearing a blue kurta and a black dupatta. Her 10-month-old daughter was in her lap. Sahil was wearing a white T-shirt. Muskaan looked towards Sahil, with tears in her eyes. Sahil also looked at Muskaan one last time. After looking at each other, both lowered their eyes. Muskaan repeatedly wiped her tears with her dupatta. Muskaan began crying loudly as soon as she saw the judge District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra arrived and took his seat. He looked at Muskaan and Sahil on the computer screen. As soon as Muskaan saw the judge, she began crying loudly. Her cries could be heard throughout the courtroom. Sahil, who had been looking down, also began sobbing after seeing Muskaan. The judge said, “Muskaan and Sahil Shukla, both of you have murdered Saurabh Rajput.” As soon as the district judge said this, silence fell over the packed courtroom. The lawyers representing Muskaan and Sahil, who were standing in front, appeared tense. Their eyes filled with tears as they waited to hear what punishment the judge would announce. As soon as the district judge declared, “The court sentences both of you to death for the brutal murder of Saurabh Rajput,” Muskaan and Sahil began crying intensely. The district judge also imposed fines on both of them. Muskaan told the court in the morning, ‘Please look after my daughter’ 10.30 am: Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra entered the courtroom and took his seat. The courtroom was empty, with only prosecution lawyer DGC KK Chaubey, defence lawyer Rekha Jain and a few senior advocates present. Muskaan and Sahil were connected to the courtroom from jail through video conferencing. Muskaan was wearing a light blue kurta and a black dupatta. She kept her eyes lowered, as did Sahil, who was wearing a white T-shirt. Muskaan briefly glanced at Sahil before lowering her eyes again. The judge said, “Muskaan and Sahil, both of you have murdered Saurabh Rajput.” He then asked them one by one about their names, ages, education, addresses, and family details. Both answered his questions. After this, the judge first asked Muskaan, “Do you have anything to say about your sentence?” Sobbing, Muskaan replied only, “Please look after my daughter, who is with me in jail.” The judge then asked Sahil, “Sahil Shukla, do you have anything to say about your sentence?” Sahil kept his head bowed and did not respond. The judge then said, “All right, we will announce your sentence later.” As soon as he said this, both were disconnected from the video conference. Saurabh’s lawyer says, ‘The minimum sentence should be the death penalty’ After this, Vijay Bahadur Singh, the lawyer representing Saurabh’s family, began his arguments. He strongly presented his case by connecting the statements of all 22 witnesses in the Muskaan-Sahil case with the various pieces of evidence. He urged the court to award both accused the death penalty as the minimum punishment. After hearing the arguments of all three lawyers, the district judge announced that the sentence would be pronounced after lunch and rose from his chair. Saurabh’s mother said tearfully, ‘We received justice very peacefully’ Muskaan-Sahil’s lawyer says, ‘They have two young daughters; award a lesser sentence’ After this, Rekha Jain, the lawyer representing Muskaan and Sahil, began her arguments and presented their case. Rekha Jain said that Muskaan and Sahil had not committed the murder as part of any premeditated plan. Muskaan has two young daughters, and there is no one to look after and raise them. Her parents are elderly and unwell. Therefore, the court should consider the responsibility of raising the children. Sahil is also a student, and his entire future depends on the court’s decision today. The future of a young person is at stake. Therefore, I request the court to award a lesser sentence to both of them. Based on the evidence and witness testimonies as well, Muskaan and Sahil deserve the minimum possible sentence, she argued. Saurabh’s lawyer says, ‘The minimum sentence should be the death penalty’ After this, Vijay Bahadur Singh, the lawyer representing Saurabh’s family, began his arguments. He strongly presented his case by connecting the statements of all 22 witnesses in the Muskaan-Sahil case with the various pieces of evidence. He urged the court to award both accused the death penalty as the minimum punishment. After hearing the arguments of all three lawyers, the district judge announced that the sentence would be pronounced after lunch and rose from his chair. Saurabh’s mother said tearfully, ‘We received justice very peacefully’ After Muskaan and Sahil were sentenced to death, Saurabh’s mother broke down in tears. She said, “We received justice very peacefully.” Saurabh’s brother, Bablu, said, “We were hopeful that we would get justice. From the beginning, we had only one demand: the death penalty. We are very happy that both have been sentenced to death. If Muskaan and Sahil appeal or take any further legal action, we will also approach the court.” Muskaan’s parents tell court in writing, ‘We have nothing to do with our daughter’ No one from Muskaan’s or Sahil’s family appeared in court. On Wednesday morning, Muskaan’s parents wrote a letter and sent it to the court through the police. In the letter, they stated that they had no concern about whatever punishment Muskaan received. They would never meet her again and wanted nothing to do with her young daughter either.

stories.title: Vindhyachal Dham is Siddhpeeth, not Shaktipeeth:'Trikone Parikrama' fulfills wishes; complete guide from reaching Mirzapur to temple darshan
stories.summary: If you are planning to visit Vindhyachal Dham in Mirzapur during Navratri for darshan, you must know about the 'Trikon Yatra'. According to beliefs, until you complete the Trikon circumambulation, the pilgrimage is considered incomplete. The first stop of this pilgrimage is the Maa Vindhyavasini Temple. The second stop is the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple. The third stop is the Kali Khoh Temple. Whether you are coming to Vindhyachal by train, bus, or in your own vehicle and wish to have an easy darshan while avoiding heavy crowds of devotees, this simple route map will prove very useful to you. How to Reach the Shrine by Bus, Car, or Train By Train: To reach the Vindhyachal Temple, you will need to alight at Mirzapur Railway Station. The distance from Mirzapur Station to Vindhyachal Dham is approximately 8 to 9 kilometres. From here, it takes 20 to 30 minutes to reach by auto-rickshaw or e-rickshaw. Vindhyachal Railway Station is also located near the shrine, but only a few express and passenger trains halt there. By Bus or Car: UP Roadways buses to Vindhyachal are easily available from Varanasi, Prayagraj, and nearby districts. Vindhyachal Dham is connected by road from all four directions. If you are arriving by car, take these routes: East: To come from Varanasi, you can reach Vindhyachal via NH-19 (old GT Road) through Aurai and by crossing the Shastri Bridge (over the River Ganges). You can also come directly via the Varanasi-Mirzapur route (Kachhwa Road). West: The most direct route from Prayagraj is NH-135 (Prayagraj-Mirzapur Highway), which connects to Vindhyachal via Naini, Meja, and Manda. Another option is coming via Handia-Gopiganj from NH-19. North: Passengers coming from Jaunpur and Bhadohi can reach Vindhyachal via Aurai directly through the Shastri Bridge route. South: Devotees coming from Rewa or the Madhya Pradesh border can arrive directly at Vindhyachal via NH-135 (Drummondganj route) or through Lalganj. By Air: The nearest airport is Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (Babatpur), which is approximately 75–80 km away from Vindhyachal. From there, Vindhyachal can be reached by taxi or bus. After reaching Vindhyachal Dham, separate parking arrangements are available for parking buses and cars. After parking your vehicle here, you can begin your 'Trikon Yatra'. Near the temple lies 'Pakka Ghat', the most prominent and famous ghat where devotees take a holy dip. You, too, should begin your pilgrimage with a bath in the Ganges. After that, proceed for the darshan of Maa Vindhyavasini. Thanks to the recently constructed grand Vindhya Corridor, reaching the temple directly from the Ganges ghat has become extremely convenient. This temple is considered a 'Siddhapeeth' rather than just a Shaktipeeth. It is believed that the Goddess herself resides here in person. Entry into the sanctum sanctorum remains closed during peak crowd hours on Navratri or regular days, and darshan is allowed only through the viewing window (Jhankhi). In the temple, the Mother Goddess is adorned in different forms (Shringar) and worshipped with Aarti four times a day. Temple priest Ashish Pandey explains—arriving during the morning Mangala Aarti is the best time for darshan. The doors for darshan remain closed for about 30–45 minutes during the afternoon Shringar Aarti and the main night Aarti. Immediately after offering prayers to Maa Vindhyavasini, step out of the temple premises and visit the Kaal Bhairav Temple located near Kotwali. According to beliefs, visiting Kaal Bhairav after the Vindhyavasini Temple is mandatory. The unique aspect of this temple is that Bhairav and Bhairavi are enshrined together here. Reach the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple, situated on the hills about 3 kilometres away from the Vindhyachal Temple. This is the second major stop of the Trikon Yatra. Ashtabhuji Devi is considered an incarnation of Goddess Saraswati and Yogamaya. Devotees can climb 108 steps to reach this hilltop temple for darshan. A ropeway facility is also available for elderly and infirm devotees. According to the Shrimad Bhagavata Mahapurana, when Kansa attempted to dash the newborn baby girl of Yashoda against a stone, mistaking her for the 8th child of Devaki and Vasudeva, the child suddenly slipped from his hands and flew into the sky. She made a celestial announcement saying, 'The one who will kill you has already been born in Gokul.' Following this, Yogamaya vanished upon reaching this very Ashtabhuji hill. During Navratri, the temple remains open 24 hours for darshan. The doors are closed for a short duration at night for special rituals and cleaning. During the Trikon Yatra, the best time to visit the Ashtabhuji temple is between 6:00 AM and 11:00 AM, or after 4:30 PM in the evening. After seeking blessings at the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple, visiting the nearby Batuk Bhairav Temple is also considered auspicious. Proceed further from the Ashtabhuji Temple to reach Kali Khoh, which is the final and third main stop of the Trikon Yatra. The Kali Khoh Temple is located about 3 kilometres from the Vindhyachal Temple and approximately 2 kilometres away from the Ashtabhuji Temple, nestled in the hills. Here, the Goddess is worshipped in her Mahakali form. This site is world-famous for Tantric rituals and special worship of Mahakali. Devotees who perform sattvic worship offer symbolic sacrifices of lemons and nutmegs along with coconuts to appease the Mother Goddess. After seeking the blessings of Maa Mahakali, it is considered mandatory to visit Anand Bhairav (Lal Bhairav) located within the temple complex. Seeking the darshan of Anand Bhairav completes your holy 'Trikon Yatra'.

stories.title: Livestock recruitment scam:Minister’s signatures on files, arrest likely; rules changed for arbitrary appointments, EOW awaits govt’s signal
stories.summary: Raj Kishor Singh, who served as the Animal Husbandry Minister during the Samajwadi Party (SP) government, may face arrest. On October 14, the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) arrested retired Principal Secretary Yogesh Kumar. The case pertains to the 2014 recruitment for 1,198 posts of Livestock Extension Officers. At that time, Raj Kishor Singh was the minister, while Yogesh Kumar served as the Principal Secretary in the department. The EOW has been investigating this scam since December 2017. In 2022, permission was sought from the government to prosecute the former minister and the principal secretary. While sanction was granted for Yogesh Kumar, the EOW has yet to receive any indication regarding former minister Raj Kishor Singh. Under these circumstances, the EOW is awaiting a signal from the government. Read the full report to find out how the former Samajwadi party minister got entangled in the scam… DG EOW Jai Narayan Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that the Animal Husbandry Department had initiated the recruitment process for 1,198 posts of Livestock Extension Officers across 17 divisions of the state. For this, a written examination was conducted on 2 February 2014. Irregularities in the recruitment examination occurred at three levels. Let us understand this: 1. Recruitment for the post of Livestock Extension Officer was to be conducted at the divisional level by an officer of Additional Director Grade-2 rank. However, without government permission, rules were altered to strip divisional selection committees of their authority. 2. After approval at the ministerial level, the examination process was centralised after its conduct. This meant recruitment started at the divisional level but was completed at the state headquarters level. A file was moved for this, bearing signatures from the bottom up—including the Deputy Director, Additional Director, Director, and Principal Secretary, along with the then-minister Raj Kishor Singh. 3. Changes to the rules were made without obtaining permission from the government. The written examination was conducted for 80 marks instead of 100, reserving 20 marks for the interview. Subsequently, evaluation of the OMR sheets was not carried out according to the rules, and they were tampered with at the headquarters level. Evaluation Done at Raebareli Institute, Arbitrary Marks Awarded DG EOW Jai Narayan Singh explains: To evaluate the answer sheets (OMR sheets) of the recruitment exam, officials fabricated two excuses. First—a shortage of funds. Second—difficulty in evaluating answer sheets at every district or divisional level. Citing these reasons, they altered the rules. Instead of having the answer sheets evaluated fairly at different locations, all answer sheets were handed over to the 'Feroze Gandhi Institute'. It is also alleged that prescribed rules were not followed while assigning the task to the institute, and contracts were backdated. The investigating agency also suspected that arbitrary selections were made through manipulation during evaluation and scoring. The DG EOW stated that owing to the case being old, the entire recruitment process was not cancelled. Consequently, individuals who secured jobs through foul play are still working. The government's stance regarding them remains unclear. Rajkishore in BJP, Hence Permission for Case Withheld The EOW has gathered evidence against Raj Kishor. Permission was subsequently sought from the government to prosecute both individuals. Recently, the government granted approval against Yogesh Kumar, but Raj Kishor's case was kept pending. Had the government granted permission to proceed with the case, Raj Kishor would also have been arrested. Departmental sources state: 'Raj Kishor is currently with the BJP.' After the SP government fell in the 2017 elections, he joined the Congress just ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. During this period, he contested the election from Harraiya but lost. In 2024, Raj Kishor left the Congress and joined the BJP. He has not been given any post in the organisation, but he is preparing to contest elections once again. Action Before Assembly Elections: What Will Be the Political Advantage? The recruitment took place during the tenure of the Samajwadi Party government. The Yogi government has consistently alleged irregularities and favoritism towards a specific group in recruitments held under the Akhilesh government. Coming ahead of the elections, these arrests naturally put the SP and Akhilesh Yadav on the back foot, which could give the BJP political leverage. However, since Raj Kishor Singh is currently with the BJP, if permission to prosecute him is withheld despite the presence of evidence, it will raise questions about the government as well.

Please do not sensationalise my name like this. You have linked my name to several leaders and officers. Please do not link my name to everyone.
