stories.title: Died rescuing people from burning building:Four more policemen laid down their lives saving innocents; Yogi to honour their families
stories.summary: Some entered a burning building and pulled hundreds of lives back from the brink of death, while others lost their own lives while trying to rescue innocent people from criminals. These are the six brave Uttar Pradesh Police personnel whose stories of supreme sacrifice are bringing tears to every eye on Police Commemoration Day. Today, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will pay tribute to these heroes by honouring their families at the Lucknow Police Lines. Between September 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, 154 police personnel lost their lives in the line of duty across the country. Six of them were from Uttar Pradesh. They died while on duty in two separate incidents. The first was a fire at a factory in Greater Noida, in which two police personnel lost their lives. The second incident involved the kidnapping of a businessman in Jalaun. Four police personnel who were on their way to rescue him from the criminals died. Read the stories of these courageous police personnel whose bravery has earned widespread respect… Two fire personnel died while trying to control the blaze in Greater Noida At around 3 am, a fire suddenly broke out at an electronic PCB chip manufacturing unit in the Ecotech-3 industrial area of Greater Noida. Within moments, raging flames and thick clouds of toxic smoke engulfed the entire building. A fire engine arrived at the scene with its siren blaring. The team that arrived to tackle the blaze included Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav. The biggest challenge was controlling the rapidly spreading fire because the factory contained chemicals and electronic equipment. Visibility was almost impossible amid the thick smoke. However, without worrying about their own safety, the firefighting team entered the building with hoses. Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav were at the front. Rohit Yadav led the way, holding the water hose and directing a jet of water at the flames. Teerthpal Singh maintained the water pressure and supply so that the other firefighters could move forward. After considerable effort, the team was close to bringing the fire under control when the extreme temperature and intense heat weakened a solid factory wall and a heavy iron girder, causing them to collapse. As the wall and iron beam suddenly came crashing down, five personnel, including Teerthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav, were trapped beneath the debris amid the intense heat of the fire. Cries for help and thick smoke filled the area. Fellow personnel and the police force immediately launched a rescue operation. After considerable effort, all those trapped were pulled out and taken to hospital. Despite the doctors’ efforts, firefighter Rohit Yadav and driver Teerthpal Singh could not be saved. The most emotional aspect of the operation was that all 450 employees working at the factory were evacuated safely. Rohit Yadav was just 32 years old. He is survived by his wife and two young daughters. Teerthpal Singh was 48 and leaves behind his wife, a son and a daughter. Four police personnel died while going to rescue a kidnapped businessman in Jalaun Vijendra Mor, a property businessman from Jalaun, was kidnapped. It was suspected that the kidnapping and murder plot had been hatched to seize his land, worth crores of rupees. The police received a tip-off that he had been taken to Haryana. The team comprised four police personnel and one complainant. They were Sub-Inspector Mohit Kumar Yadav, Sub-Inspector Satyabhan Singh, Constable Ashok Kumar, Constable Pradeep Kumar and Vijendra’s relative, Amreek Singh. All five were travelling in a Scorpio SUV towards Jind in Haryana to conduct a raid and search for the businessman when a tragic accident occurred on the KMP Expressway near Nuh. The Scorpio carrying the team lost control and collided with another vehicle. Five people died in the accident, including Sub-Inspectors Satyabhan Singh and Mohit Yadav and constables Pradeep Kumar and Ashok Kumar. A subsequent investigation revealed that Shribhagwan, Sanjeev alias Kokila, Mohit Malik and Amarjeet Suhag had forcibly put Vijendra into a Creta car and kidnapped him. They later murdered him and took his body to the Kupra forest in the Jalalpur police station area of Hamirpur. They poured around 40 litres of diesel over the body and set it on fire to destroy his identity and all evidence. On July 29, the police arrested Mohit Malik and his wife, Sapna Rani, from Chitaila Farmhouse in Kadaura. During questioning, Mohit confessed to murdering the businessman. He also revealed where the body had been disposed of. Based on information provided by Mohit and Sapna, the police recovered a skeleton from the Kupra forest and sent it for a post-mortem examination.

stories.title: Why BJP suddenly needs Raja Bhaiya:Kshatriyas form 6% and Dalits 26% in Kunda, yet he has been MLA for 33 years; who gains from an alliance?
stories.summary: The meeting between Kunda MLA and Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik) president Raghuraj Pratap Singh, alias Raja Bhaiya and BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary has become a talking point in Uttar Pradesh. It is being linked to efforts to secure support in the recent MLC elections. However, Raja Bhaiya has been extending unconditional support to the BJP in previous Rajya Sabha and MLC elections. So, what has suddenly made the BJP need Raja Bhaiya so much that its state president had to visit his home to meet him? What does this meeting signify? Read this UP Explainer… Question 1: Why does the BJP suddenly need Raja Bhaiya? Answer: At first glance, there appear to be two immediate reasons behind this. Reason 1 – Making up for losses in the Lok Sabha elections Raja Bhaiya’s displeasure is believed to be one of the reasons behind the BJP’s defeat in the Pratapgarh and Kaushambi Lok Sabha seats in 2024. At the time, Apna Dal leader Anupriya Patel, an ally of the BJP, said at a rally in Pratapgarh, “Kings are no longer born from their mothers’ wombs; the people choose their king.” The remark was seen as a reference to Raja Bhaiya. Raja Bhaiya did not respond publicly, but his supporters were deeply upset. It is even said that there were attempts to defeat Anupriya Patel in the election, but she won. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party candidate Pushpendra Saroj from Kaushambi had met Raja Bhaiya personally. Although Raja Bhaiya was also unhappy with Akhilesh Yadav, he supported Pushpendra because of their personal relationship. Pushpendra defeated the BJP’s Vinod Sonkar by more than one lakh votes. Pratapgarh and Kaushambi together have 10 Assembly seats. Besides these, Raja Bhaiya has political influence in around a dozen districts across Awadh and Purvanchal, including Prayagraj, Kaushambi, Jaunpur, Sultanpur, Amethi, Rae Bareli and Gonda. The BJP could benefit across 50–60 seats if Raja Bhaiya joins forces with it. Political analysts say the 2027 Assembly election will be a major challenge for the BJP. Along with 10 years of anti-incumbency, there are several issues, including allegations of theft of offerings, the UGC-upper caste controversy and the SIR-vote theft issue. In such a situation, the BJP does not want to leave any room for regret by thinking, ‘Things would have been better if we had done this.’ Reason 2 – The October 23 teachers’ and graduates’ MLC elections Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary’s sudden visit to Raja Bhaiya’s home on October 18 was not just about the 2027 elections. Elections to 11 Legislative Council seats under the graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies are also scheduled for October 23. Educated young voters and teachers who are unhappy with government policies may vote for the Samajwadi Party. Raja Bhaiya has a strong network in constituencies such as Pratapgarh, Prayagraj and the Varanasi division. The BJP needs immediate help from this network to win the elections. Put simply, the BJP understands that to return to power in Uttar Pradesh with a strong mandate, it must bring its old and influential allies together not just in spirit but formally on the same platform. This electoral calculation and political necessity have brought Raja Bhaiya back into focus for the BJP. Question 2: The current MLC elections are not being held under the legislators’ quota. How can Raja Bhaiya help the BJP? Answer: Raja Bhaiya’s importance to the BJP in the MLC elections can be understood through four key points. (A) Direct influence over colleges and educational institutions Raja Bhaiya’s close associates run several prominent intermediate and degree colleges across many districts in Awadh and Purvanchal. Teachers working at these institutions and graduates who have studied there are directly connected to him. His support could play a major role in shifting these teachers’ and young voters’ preferences towards the BJP. (B) A strong network to bring voters to polling booths The biggest challenge in graduates’ and teachers’ MLC elections is getting voters to leave their homes and reach polling booths, as turnout is often low. Raja Bhaiya’s network of workers could help BJP candidates mobilise voters and bring them to the polling booths. (C) Influence in constituencies such as Allahabad-Jhansi and Varanasi The seats going to the polls this time include the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates’ constituency and the Varanasi constituency. The areas of Pratapgarh and Prayagraj fall directly within the reach of these constituencies. Raja Bhaiya has had a longstanding influence in these regions. Meanwhile, BJP MLC Devendra Singh from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad graduates’ constituency is reportedly unhappy with the party. He wrote an open letter urging people to vote ‘against injustice and humiliation’. This is being seen as a show of support for Samajwadi Party candidate Dr Sanjayan Tripathi. In this situation, Raja Bhaiya’s support could help the BJP consolidate upper-caste and young voters across this entire belt. (D) Addressing resentment among educated upper-caste voters and young people Teachers and young people are often unhappy with the BJP over issues such as the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) and employment, and tend to lean towards the Samajwadi Party. Raja Bhaiya has a strong image among upper-caste communities and young people. His public association with the BJP could act as a ‘buffer’, helping to ease the anger of these disgruntled voters and bring them into the BJP’s camp. Simply put, in elections involving this educated section of voters, Raja Bhaiya is an influential figure who can help deliver votes for the BJP and make the party’s candidates’ path to victory easier. Question 3: If Raja Bhaiya already leans towards the BJP, why is an alliance necessary? Answer: It is true that Raja Bhaiya is generally seen as leaning towards the BJP. However, there is a significant difference between being informally supportive and having an official alliance. In politics, friendship alone is not enough without a formal alliance. There are three fundamental reasons for this. (A) Ending confusion among voters Without an alliance, Raja Bhaiya’s party, Jan Satta Dal (Loktantrik), may field candidates in several seats across Awadh and Purvanchal. Raja Bhaiya and the BJP draw from almost the same voter base — upper-caste communities, particularly Rajputs. If they contest separately, their votes will split, directly benefiting the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance. A formal alliance between the BJP and Raja Bhaiya, however, would allow them to share seats and prevent the division of votes. An alliance would establish how many seats each party would contest. For example, the BJP could leave Kunda, Babaganj and some neighbouring seats for Raja Bhaiya’s party and not field its own candidates there. In return, Raja Bhaiya would put all his efforts into helping BJP candidates win the remaining seats. Such coordination is virtually impossible without a formal alliance. (B) Preventing friction between grassroots workers No matter how good the relationship between leaders may be, workers continue to fight against one another until an alliance is officially announced. Once an alliance is in place, workers from both parties can campaign together for a common candidate and put their full strength behind ensuring victory. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is currently campaigning on the slogan of ‘PDA’ — backward classes, Dalits and minorities. He is trying to break into the BJP’s traditional upper-caste vote bank and bring those voters over to his side. Raja Bhaiya’s alignment with the BJP would strengthen this vote bank like a wall, making it difficult for the opposition to break through. (C) Sending a strong message across the state When two prominent leaders shake hands in front of television cameras and newspaper reporters to announce an alliance, the impact is felt not just in their home districts but across the Thakur and wider upper-caste communities throughout Uttar Pradesh. It sends a message that the forces these communities favour have come together, boosting voters’ confidence. After Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Raja Bhaiya command considerable respect among the Kshatriya community in Uttar Pradesh. In recent times, local issues have appeared to push some Kshatriya voters away from the BJP. If Raja Bhaiya stands alongside the BJP on a shared platform, much of the resentment among Thakur and other upper-caste voters could ease, bringing their votes together in the BJP’s favour. Before we wrap up, let’s also understand the extent of Raja Bhaiya’s political influence… Raja Bhaiya has been an MLA from Kunda continuously since 1993. He initially won as an Independent and now wins on the ticket of his own party, Jan Satta Dal (Loktantrik). Although he is seen as a leader of the Thakur community, no leader can remain undefeated for 33 years on the strength of Kshatriya votes alone. The Kunda Assembly constituency itself confirms this. Kshatriya voters account for only around 6% of the electorate. Dalits form the largest group, at around 26%, followed by Muslims at 15%, Yadavs at 14% and Brahmins at 10–12%. The remaining voters belong to other upper-caste and backward-caste communities. People from all sections of society visit the public grievance court held at Raja Bhaiya’s ancestral residence, ‘Benti Raj Bhavan’. He also helps resolve domestic disputes, which has helped him build an image as a ‘protector’ among non-upper-caste communities as well. Raja Bhaiya has been seen alongside the BJP since 2017. Jan Satta Dal supported the BJP in the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections and the 2023 Uttar Pradesh MLC by-elections. Raja Bhaiya has also been seen aligning with the BJP on issues of Hindutva and nationalism. Even so, he has continued to remind the BJP of his political importance from time to time. In the 2022 Assembly elections, Raja Bhaiya fielded candidates in 16 seats across 10 districts of Uttar Pradesh. His party won only two seats — Kunda and Babaganj — but the BJP slipped to third place in both constituencies.

stories.title: Model Shraddha was in Shivpal’s party:Built links with leaders, wanted to contest elections, saying, ‘I may become a leader tomorrow’
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, the prime suspect in the case involving the death of her live-in partner, Shiva Sharma, is in police custody after remaining absconding since his death and will be produced before a court on 21 October. Her statements are expected to help establish whether she considers Shiva’s death a suicide or a murder. Shraddha, who reportedly had no criminal background initially, allegedly became involved in activities ranging from betting-related collections to associations with a Lucknow gangster in her pursuit of quick money and fame before gradually entering the modelling world. Before this, however, Shraddha had also tried her luck in politics. She became associated with Shivpal Yadav during the period when relations between Shivpal and Akhilesh were strained. Shivpal Yadav had formed a separate party, the Pragatisheel Samajwadi Party. Shraddha served as a secretary in the party. It has not been established who introduced her to Shivpal. She developed contacts with several political leaders but failed to establish herself in politics. However, her political connections proved useful. She began attending major events in Lucknow as a special guest. But behind her glamorous lifestyle, Shraddha's ambitions have now landed her behind bars. Read the report… Shraddha wanted to contest an Assembly election Shraddha, who is from Rae Bareli, came to Lucknow when she was 14-15 years old and began living at a relative's house. She visited her family home in Rae Bareli only occasionally. She got married in 2010, but disputes with her husband eventually left her on her own once again. She was struggling to establish her career. Her entry into politics came in 2016, when some political leaders introduced her to Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav. At the time, a dispute had already begun between Shivpal Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav. Shivpal later left the Samajwadi Party and formed the Pragatisheel Samajwadi Party. Shraddha also joined his party. While overseeing its work, she eventually became a secretary. Shraddha began preparing to contest an election through this political association. She wanted a ticket to contest an Assembly seat. People would see her lavish lifestyle and ask: Are you planning to contest an election? People from Shraddha's neighbourhood in Rae Bareli say she frequently visited her home in 2016. She lived lavishly, which quickly drew people's attention. She often attended small local functions in Rae Bareli. When people asked her whether she intended to contest an election, she would laugh and say, “Who knows what the future holds? Maybe I will become a politician one day.” Shraddha often spoke to people there about events involving Shivpal Yadav and his son, Aditya Yadav. Photographs of her with Shivpal and Aditya are now going viral on social media. The Pragatisheel Samajwadi Party did not perform well in the 2017 Assembly elections. Shraddha subsequently parted ways with the party. She later developed close ties with other political leaders. Through these connections, she began getting work in fashion and modelling. She also started building connections with senior officials in the Uttar Pradesh bureaucracy. Gradually, she became close to several prominent figures in politics and the bureaucracy. Lucknow University invited her by letter and appointed her a judge Shraddha's influence in the state capital, Lucknow, gradually grew. She began receiving invitations to attend the openings of restaurants, beauty parlours and other establishments as the chief guest. On one occasion, Lucknow University even appointed her as a judge at an event. A cultural and sports programme was held at the university's Faculty of Law on 27 February 2020. Shraddha was appointed as a judge for the fashion show and the 'Mr and Miss Sanskriti Surabhi' event. The letter sent by the university inviting Shraddha stated, “Your presence as an esteemed member of the jury will be a source of inspiration. It will provide an invaluable experience to the participants and members.” She described her parents as role models despite having little contact with them Shraddha Dubey's personal life was complicated. While she appeared bold and carefree in her reel life, her real life was different. By 2024, Shraddha had travelled to various states across the country, including Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Rajasthan and Haryana, to participate in fashion and modelling events. She was also honoured at several places. In her speeches, she often said, “My parents have supported me in my success. It is because of them that I have been able to do better in the modelling field.” However, the reality was different. Shraddha's father, SK Dubey, retired from the post of junior engineer (JE). Her mother, Pushpa Devi, died when Shraddha was just 7 years old. Her father remarried. Shraddha did not get along well with her stepmother, so she later moved to Lucknow. After her marriage, when differences arose between Shraddha and her in-laws, her family wanted to ensure that the matter did not end in divorce. However, Shraddha decided to seek a divorce. Because of these decisions, her father also kept his distance from her. When Shraddha's name emerged in connection with Shiva's murder, he told the media, “I have nothing to do with my daughter. She neither visits us nor do we have any communication with her.” However, people from the neighbourhood say that relations between Shraddha and her family had improved earlier this year and that she had visited her home. Previously, she would not visit them.

stories.title: Rakhi Sawant called him impotent:Friends say he became withdrawn after a show; sister demands punishment for actress
stories.summary: “Lakshman was my neighbour and friend. He got married in 2010. Before his marriage, he would talk to everyone with a smile and was always happy. But after the wedding, arguments started at his home. His wife went to her parents’ house and filed a case against him. After that, he began to remain upset. “Some time later, Lakshman went with his family to Rakhi Sawant’s show. There, Rakhi Sawant called him impotent and incapable of being a man. The entire world watched the show. After returning home, Lakshman became withdrawn. He hardly spoke to anyone and remained indoors. A few days later, he died.” Rohit, a resident of Jhansi, told Dainik Bhaskar this while recalling his neighbour Lakshman Ahirwar, who died in Jhansi in 2010 at the age of 24. It was alleged that Rakhi Sawant had humiliated him on her show by calling him impotent, and that he died after suffering emotional trauma. Sixteen years later, the CAW (Fast Track Court) in Jhansi issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Rakhi Sawant on 16 October. The case has since returned to the spotlight. The next hearing is scheduled for 1 December. ‘His mother also died while grieving for him’ Munagi Devi, a resident of Hansari in Premnagar, said, “Lakshman lived in a rented house directly opposite mine. His mother and siblings also lived with him. He sold vegetables from a pushcart and was a very good boy. After Lakshman’s death, his mother, Savitri, remained deeply distressed. “She used to tell us, ‘If he had not married, our son would not have died. His marriage took him away from us. It would have been better if he had remained unmarried all his life; at least he would still have been here in front of us.’ Savitri continued to cry for her son until her final days.” Sister says her brother deserves justice Lakshman’s sister, Meena, said, “My brother Lakshman had gone to Rakhi Sawant’s show with our mother, maternal uncle and aunt. There, Lakshman’s wife falsely accused our maternal uncle of trying to force himself on her. Rakhi also called Lakshman impotent. After this, my brother became extremely stressed. He remained sad at home. “He stopped talking to people and even gave up selling vegetables from his pushcart. A few days later, he died. He had no illness. He died because of the stress he was under. “Our mother, Savitri, died around five months ago. She lived with us and used to cry a lot after Lakshman’s death. Now, we want justice for our brother. Rakhi Sawant should be punished.” The photograph shows Lakshman Prasad Ahirwar sitting on the ground and speaking into a microphone. 16-minute video posted On Monday night, Rakhi Sawant posted a 16-minute-and-four-second video of her show Rakhi Ka Insaaf on Instagram. She wrote, “Friends, please watch the 2010 episode. This channel and show have been shut down. Even so, why are these people (Lakshman Prasad Ahirwar’s family) accusing me? “This boy had said that his death was not caused by me or my channel, but by a fever. The doctor gave a certificate to the court. Even then, these people want to harass me because I am supporting the students of India and people who are like cockroaches. “That is why they are accusing me in this case. The boy and his mother are no longer alive. I have nothing to do with this case. All the evidence is present in this video.” Rakhi Sawant released a video late on Saturday night to present her side of the case. Rakhi says, ‘I do not know that boy’ Earlier, Rakhi Sawant had released a video on social media on Saturday night, saying, “Hello, you must all be hearing the news about me. You probably know who is behind this. “Even if I have to go to jail for the people of this country, I will. Jai Bharat Mata, Jai Bhim, Jai Maharashtra, Vande Mataram. This is a 2010 case, and I have nothing to do with it. “I do not even know this boy. I cannot remember him; I have lost my memory. The man had a contract with the channel. After the show ended, he reportedly died in hospital after suffering from a fever. Now the blame is being put on the channel and us. We have nothing to do with him.” Rakhi Sawant said the case dates back to 2010 and claimed she had nothing to do with it. Savitri lived near her brother’s house Balveer Singh, a resident of Toriya in Hansari, said, “My sister Savitri lived in Sipri Bazaar with her family. After her husband, Gokul, died, she moved with her children into a rented house near mine. “My nephew Lakshman sold vegetables from a pushcart in 2010. He married Anita, a resident of Rajgarh, on 18 February 2010. The couple developed differences over some issue. “Just 12 days after the wedding, Anita went to her parents’ house. When my nephew went to bring her back, she refused to return. When he went again, he was beaten up. “Anita had alleged that one of her husband’s relatives had improper intentions towards her. She said she had complained to Lakshman, but he did not pay attention. She also alleged that Lakshman drank alcohol and assaulted her.” Balveer Singh’s house is in Toriya, Hansari. His nephew Lakshman died after consuming poison. Lakshman appeared on the TV show with his wife His maternal uncle, Balveer, said, “In 2010, the TV show Rakhi Ka Insaaf, hosted by actress Rakhi Sawant, used to air. “A woman from our neighbourhood brought some people associated with the show to us and asked us to participate. They said we would get justice, our travel and other expenses would be covered, and our daughter-in-law would return home. “That is why we agreed to appear on the show. I travelled to Mumbai with my nephew Lakshman, his mother Savitri and my wife Pooja. We went by train to Delhi and then flew to Mumbai. “The show was filmed in Mumbai. Rakhi Sawant used very insulting language and called my nephew Lakshman impotent and incapable of being a man. “The episode was broadcast on 23 October 2010. After that, Lakshman could not bear the humiliation and became stressed. In that state of mind, he consumed poison. “His condition deteriorated, and he was admitted to the medical college on 9 November 2010. He died there on 10 November. We filed a case against Rakhi Sawant, accusing her of abetting his suicide.” Balveer said the TV show Rakhi Ka Insaaf aired in 2010. Lakshman’s mother also died while grieving for her son Balveer said, “The case was registered following a complaint by my sister Savitri. At the time, we were assured that justice would be delivered. However, Rakhi Sawant obtained a stay from the High Court. We pursued the matter and got the stay lifted, but another stay was granted later. It remained in force until now. “My sister Savitri died around five months ago. She, too, continued to grieve for her son Lakshman. She would say, ‘My child is gone, but nothing has happened.’ Lakshman’s wife, Anita, has also remarried.” Around 10 months ago, Rakhi Sawant walked at an event in Meerut wearing a blue drum. Only one of Savitri’s three sons is alive Balveer said his sister Savitri had three sons Ramesh, Suresh and Lakshman and two daughters, Krishna and Meena. Suresh and Lakshman have died. Ramesh now lives with his family in Sipri Bazaar, while both daughters are married. “It has been 16 years, but we have not received justice. Now, we have renewed hope that justice will be delivered. We only want justice. We have complete faith in the court,” he said.

stories.title: Groom’s brother stabbed to death at wedding in Bijnor:Beaten during garland ceremony; 20 men surround and vandalise car while he is being taken to hospital
stories.summary: Groom's brother stabbed to death with an awl at a wedding ceremony in Bijnor at around 6 p.m. on Tuesday. A dispute had broken out between two groups during the exchange of garlands. When the groom's brother went to intervene, the accused also began beating him. During the assault, they struck him on the nose with an awl. While the family was taking the injured man to hospital, the accused surrounded their vehicle. Around 15-20 people pelted it with stones and chased the family members while carrying iron rods. The man was taken to the district hospital somehow, where doctors declared him dead. The incident occurred in the Kotwali City area. See two pictures... Dispute broke out during the garland-exchange ceremony Ashwani (32), a resident of Makhwada village, worked for a finance company. His father, Ashok Kumar, is an inspector with the ITBP in West Bengal. Ashwani's family includes his wife and two children, one of them a daughter. His younger brother is a driver. Ashwani arrived in Bakli village from Makhwada village with the wedding procession of Aakash, the son of his paternal uncle Gajraj. The procession was welcomed at the Heera Banquet Hall. After all the rituals had been completed, the exchange-of-garlands ceremony was under way. During this, a dispute broke out over an issue. People caught the youth in the washroom According to eyewitnesses, a young man from the groom's family had gone to use the washroom. It is alleged that village e-rickshaw driver Ravi and some other youths were drinking alcohol there. They caught the young man. After learning of this, Ashwani, the groom's paternal uncle's son, went to rescue him. During this, the youths also detained Ashwani. A heated argument then broke out between the two sides. During the dispute, the attackers struck Ashwani on the nose with an ice pick. Ashwani fell face-first as a result. When an attempt was made to take him to hospital by car, the attackers surrounded the vehicle and began pelting it with stones. Around 15 to 20 youths, armed with spades and iron rods, began attacking the vehicle. Somehow, the family members and wedding party took Ashwani to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. ASP says youth killed in ice-pick attack ASP City Dr Krishna Gopal Singh said: The youth was killed in an ice-pick attack. His family took him to the district hospital, where he died. A complaint is being taken from the family. A case will be registered and action will be taken. Teams have been deployed to arrest the accused.

stories.title: Shraddha dodged police for 11 days:Model fled to Nepal, returned to UP and moved around Agra and Nagpur in a burqa
stories.summary: Shraddha Dubey absconded on the night of 9 October. The next day, she reached the India-Nepal border in Bahraich and abandoned her vehicle. She stayed at different locations in Nepal and released three videos at 12-hour intervals. She was seen in CCTV footage. She returned from Nepal to her home in Rae Bareli, where she gave an interview to a news agency. She absconded again afterwards. Meanwhile, pressure continued to mount on the police over her arrest. DCP Central Vikrant Veer, ACP Hazratganj Rajneesh Verma and station in-charge Vikram Singh were removed. Finally, after 11 days, the Uttar Pradesh STF arrested Shraddha. The arrest took place in Nagpur, Maharashtra. The question now is: how did Shraddha manage to evade the police for 11 days? STF chief Amitabh Yash provided some answers to this question. However, some questions still remain unanswered. First, let us understand how Shraddha managed to evade arrest for so many days.... Limited use of taxis, travelled in private vehicles After Shiva's death on 9 October, Shraddha travelled to Rupaidiha in Bahraich in her Scorpio. She left the vehicle at Shukla Parking on the border and entered Nepal at 6 a.m. on 10 October. After returning from Nepal, she came back to Uttar Pradesh. Shraddha knew how the police trace absconders, which is why she changed her location every day. ADG (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash said that after going on the run, she mostly travelled in private vehicles. Sometimes she took lifts, and at other times she asked hotel staff to make bookings for her. She was so clever that she changed vehicles after crossing toll plazas so that even if the vehicle appeared on toll plaza CCTV, the tracking team would never be able to reach Shraddha. Shraddha continued booking hotels using the driver's Aadhaar card On 11 October, she was seen travelling on an e-rickshaw in Mahimnagar, Nepal. CCTV footage of the incident also emerged. Shraddha's sister Rashmi and the driver, Aamir, were seen with her in the footage. They chose a low-budget hotel there, where the driver provided his Aadhaar card. Shraddha spent her first night at this hotel. The next day, Shraddha left from there. She reached Nepal's Dang district. Shraddha switched on her phone there but turned it off shortly afterwards. She then contacted people using a Nepalese SIM card. However, the police obtained the location from the time she had switched on the phone, and Shraddha left that location the following day. It emerged after her arrest that Shraddha had stayed in five different hotels during her 11 days on the run. Reached Raebareli directly from Nepal, then went to Lucknow Shraddha left Nepal on 15 October and entered Uttar Pradesh via Kushinagar. She reached Rae Bareli directly on 16 October. Knowing that she might be seen on CCTV, she abandoned at the Rae Bareli bus station the vehicle in which she had travelled from Nepal. She reached Saras Tiraha in another taxi and booked an Ertiga car there on rent. Shraddha is said to have travelled to Rae Bareli to meet a betting trader. After the meeting, she reached Lucknow at around 12 a.m. Shraddha gave a soundbite to a news agency in Lucknow, in which she claimed to be innocent. On the same day, she filed an application in court seeking anticipatory bail. Shraddha then went on the run again. According to police sources, she travelled directly from Lucknow to Agra and stayed at Agra's Om Palace Hotel for 24 hours. Her sister Rashmi and driver Aamir were also with her during this period. Shraddha wore a burqa everywhere to evade the police. She is also said to have met a lawyer in Agra. After stopping in Agra, they left for Nagpur in Maharashtra via Jhansi. None of the three used their phones throughout the journey. According to police sources, they had a separate phone through which they contacted certain people who gave them instructions. These people arranged a lawyer for them and got them to give a byte to a news agency. The police interrogation will reveal who those helpers are. Shraddha kept gathering evidence to present in court Amitabh Yash said that Shraddha was aware of police procedures. She knew what kind of evidence is presented in court. That is why she had made and kept several videos of Shiva Sharma, which she continued releasing after Shiva's death. It is now also being believed that a police officer or employee was guiding her. This is because it has already emerged that Shraddha had connections ranging from the bureaucracy to the police department. 'Disappeared' right under the nose of the police and STF Shraddha filed an application for surrender at the High Court on Saturday. She gave a soundbite to an agency there. By the time the police were alerted and tried to arrest Shraddha after the soundbite was broadcast in the media, she had already fled again. The surprising thing is that the High Court where Shraddha had come to file for anticipatory bail has police security. The Uttar Pradesh STF is also less than 1 kilometre from the High Court. In these circumstances, how Shraddha managed to escape after coming right under the nose of the police and STF remains a major question.

stories.title: Dussehra scenes across UP:Ravana burnt in Kashi, minister carries Ram on shoulder, Ram-Sita sit-in in Prayagraj
stories.summary: Vijayadashami is being celebrated in Uttar Pradesh today. Preparations for Dussehra festivities have been completed in the cities. Ravana will be burnt in the evening after the Ramlila performances. This time, Lucknow's high-tech Ravana is the talk of the town. Its effigy will walk onto the ground on its own, move its hands and legs, and even wave a sword. In Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh's tallest 90-foot Ravana will be burnt, while in Kashi, an effigy of a country-destroying cockroach will be burnt. Here are the preparations across the state... Kanpur: 90-foot Ravana; worship at the Dashanan Temple A 90-foot-tall Ravana has been prepared at Kanpur's Parade Ground. According to the organisers, it is the tallest Ravana in the state. Effigies will also be burnt in Motijheel, Armapur, Shastri Nagar and Rail Bazaar. Meanwhile, Ravana will be worshipped in the morning at the Dashanan Temple in Shivala. The temple has a tradition of worshipping Ravana on Dussehra. Lucknow: High-tech Ravana, AI to be used in Ramlila At the Aishbagh Ramlila Ground, a high-tech Ravana will walk in on its own. Its arms and legs will move, and it will wave a sword. Fireworks will continue for around 45 minutes after the effigy is burnt. AI-generated scenes will be shown during the Ramlila, and a digital elephant will be seen in the Ram Baraat procession. The committee claims that Goswami Tulsidas started the Ramlila here around 500 years ago. Kashi: 70-foot Ravana with a single head A 70-foot Ravana, a 65-foot Kumbhakarna and a 60-foot Meghnad have been prepared at the BAREKA Stadium in Varanasi. The single-headed Ravana will be burnt here. A 45-foot Ravana will be burnt at Maldahiya crossing. Meanwhile, at Ramlila in historic Ramnagar, the 60-foot Ravana will be set alight according to Hindu rituals. 'Anti-national cockroach' to be burnt along with Ravana: An effigy of an 'anti-national cockroach' will also be symbolically burnt along with Ravana on 20 October in Varanasi's Ardali Bazar-Kachahri area. The Shri Ramleela Committee will organise the event at the Bade Mahavir Temple intersection. Committee president Anil Kumar Pandey and general secretary Vipul Pathak said the decision was taken to convey the message that national interest comes first. Why Vijayadashami is celebrated According to religious beliefs, on the tenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Ashwin, Lord Shri Ram killed Lanka's King Ravana, bringing an end to unrighteousness. On the same day, Goddess Durga killed Mahishasura and freed the gods from his atrocities. Since then, Vijayadashami has been celebrated as a symbol of the victory of good over evil and righteousness over unrighteousness. There is also a tradition of worshipping weapons on this day. stories.title: Congress seeks 87 seats from SP in UP:Priyanka Gandhi divides constituencies into two categories, stakes claim to all seats in Amethi and Rae Bareli
stories.summary: Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi held a major meeting in Delhi on Monday (19 October) regarding the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. Senior Uttar Pradesh Congress leaders attended the meeting, which lasted from 2 p.m. to 4.30 p.m. According to sources, the Congress has decided that it will not reach an agreement with the Samajwadi Party for fewer than 85-87 seats. The seats have been divided into two categories - A and B. In addition, the Congress has staked its claim to all Assembly seats in the Amethi, Rae Bareli and Saharanpur Lok Sabha constituencies. The party also wants to contest at least one seat in every district of the state. Read the full report... Option of alliance with others if talks with SP fail Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' and working president Imran Masood attended the meeting with Priyanka. It was decided that seat-sharing talks should be finalised by 15 November at all costs, so that there would be enough time to prepare for the election. Congress will initially present a list of around 150 seats to the SP. The meeting also discussed what should be done if no agreement was reached with the SP. According to sources, the party has kept the doors open for alliances with other parties as well. Congress not in the mood to compromise on 55 A-category seats Congress contested 17 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. These constituencies include a total of 85 Assembly segments. Congress had taken the lead in 39 of these seats. The party has now included these 39 seats in the A category for the 2027 Assembly election as well. According to a leader who attended the meeting, the party is not ready to give up its claim to these seats. About 12 of these 55 seats currently have Samajwadi Party MLAs. The SP won eight seats in the Assembly constituencies of Amethi, Rae Bareli and Saharanpur in the previous election. Two of these MLAs are now said to have distanced themselves from the SP. Some of the seats were previously allotted by the SP to the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. However, the candidates contested there on the SP's election symbol. Congress has staked its claim to these seats as well. The party says that its claim to these seats is justified in view of its performance in previous elections and the local political situation. 30 to 32 seats in the B category: Congress wants these too Congress has placed 30 to 32 seats in the B category. The party believes that if an alliance is formed with the Samajwadi Party and both parties contest the election with full strength, they could win several of these seats. Congress leaders say that the movements being conducted under Rahul Gandhi's leadership have increased the party's activism. A large number of people from Uttar Pradesh travelled to Delhi for the recent protests. The party hopes that the organisation will become stronger after Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi on 1 November. Discussion on 175 seats, talks to begin with 150-seat list The meeting discussed around 175 Uttar Pradesh Assembly seats. These seats were selected based on the Congress's performance in the previous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. The party also included the results of elections held after 2009 in its assessment. The Congress plans to begin talks with the Samajwadi Party on seat-sharing with a list of around 150 seats. The party says it was allocated 104 seats under its alliance with the Samajwadi Party in the 2017 Assembly elections. In addition, candidates from both parties contested against each other in 10 seats. This is referred to as a friendly fight. The Congress won seven of these seats. According to the party, its candidates finished second in 44 seats. Priyanka Gandhi's Role Crucial, Both Parties Form Committee Priyanka Gandhi is likely to play a crucial role in talks with the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing. A committee led by Priyanka Gandhi will hold talks with the Samajwadi Party on behalf of the Congress. It will include Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra Mona, working president Imran Masood and K.C. Venugopal. Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav, Prof. Ram Gopal Yadav and other leaders will represent the Samajwadi Party's position in the talks. The seat-sharing discussions between the two parties will focus particularly on three points: What are the chances of winning each seat? How strong is the party's organisation there? How has it performed in previous elections?

stories.title: Model Shraddha Dubey arrested in Nagpur for live-in partner’s murder:She had been absconding for 11 days; UP STF also arrests her sister and driver
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, who was absconding in the Shiva Sharma murder case in Lucknow, has been arrested in Nagpur. The Uttar Pradesh STF also arrested her sister and driver Danish on Tuesday. All three may be brought to Lucknow today. Shraddha Dubey had been absconding for 11 days. On 9 October, millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments under suspicious circumstances. It is claimed that she travelled from Lucknow to Nepal via Sitapur and Bahraich. She returned to Uttar Pradesh from Nepal on 18 October and gave an interview to the ANI news agency. Shraddha said, “I did not murder Shiva. Shiva jumped from the fourth floor of the building right in front of my eyes.” Her last known location was subsequently traced to Agra. According to sources, model Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and the driver first travelled to Delhi by car. The three then took a flight from there and left for Maharashtra. Take a look at these 2 pictures… Shraddha released 3 videos while absconding While absconding, model Shraddha Dubey, who is accused of murder, released 3 videos within 12 hours. In these videos, she claimed to be innocent and denied any conspiracy. She claimed that Shiva was heavily in debt and had died by suicide. Find out what the model said in the videos… First video: Model Shraddha Dubey presented her side of the story in a 5-minute-and-18-second video. According to her, she had not spoken to Shiva for 5-6 days before 7 October. On that day, Shiva called her driver from a tea shop at Kapurthala crossing. Shiva was crying. Shraddha called him twice, but he did not answer. At around 2 am, Shiva called again. After receiving her location, he arrived in his BMW to meet Shraddha. They talked and then went to a cafe. According to Shraddha, Shiva had been drinking beer. Afterwards, Shiva left in her car, while her driver drove Shiva's car. Shiva then went to her house with Shraddha. Second video: Shraddha said that her sister had come to her house on the morning of 8 October. She had nothing to do with the case and did not even know Shiva well. According to Shraddha, her sister's call records would make this clear. Shraddha claimed that they spent the day together, went out and everything was normal. In the evening, Shiva's friends Ashwini Mishra and Harsh also came to the house. She said that if Shiva had been harassed, his friends would have informed the police. According to Shraddha, she had known Shiva for four months, and they had been in a relationship for the past two months. Responding to Shiva's mother's claim that they were living together, she said Shiva did not stay with her continuously. After staying with her for around 15 days, he would disappear for 2-4 days. During the period when they were not speaking, Shiva had gone to Kedarnath with his sister and brother-in-law. Third video: Shraddha Dubey claimed that Shiva Sharma had debts of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. According to her, Shiva was distressed by calls from people demanding repayment. Shraddha said she had screenshots related to the debt and had sent Shiva's phone to the police. She urged the police to examine the call records. According to Shraddha, Shiva used to talk about committing suicide because he could not repay his debts. She claimed that they had tea together on the morning of 9 October. That day, when Shiva locked the bathroom door for the first time, she became suspicious. She sent her sister to check inside, but before her sister could reach him, Shiva jumped from the balcony. Shraddha questioned why anyone would throw someone off their own flat. She said she was also grieving the loss of Shiva. Appealing to the media not to harass her, she spoke about her mental distress. Now, find out about Shiva's videos… Two videos of Shiva Sharma also surfaced on Thursday. They were recorded before his death. In the videos, a woman can be heard threatening Shiva. It is claimed that the woman is Shraddha Dubey, although the police have not confirmed this so far. Shraddha is accusing him of stealing three gold chains and a bracelet. She asks Shiva to return around ₹6 lakh. Shiva assures her that he will repay the money. He says, “I am giving it to you in writing that I will return the money. Keep my car and give me the money.” Now, read the full case… On 9 October, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments in Hazratganj. Shiva had been living with Shraddha for the past 4 months. After the incident, he was wearing only underwear. There was lipstick on his face. Several cigarette-burn marks were also found on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has filed a murder case against 5 people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and the driver Adil, in connection with his death. The allegation is that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya displays collection of 500 weapons:Performs worship in saffron turban, says appearances can be deceptive
stories.summary: Strongman MLA from Kunda in Pratapgarh, Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, displayed a cache of weapons on Dussehra. He performed the ceremonial worship of weapons at his mansion at 1 p.m. on Tuesday. Raja Bhaiya, dressed in a dhoti-kurta and saffron turban, was seen worshipping more than 500 Indian and foreign-made weapons. His twin sons, Shivraj and Brijraj, also took part in the ceremony. All the block chiefs, the district panchayat chairperson's representative and hundreds of supporters attended the ceremony with their weapons. The licences for all the weapons had also been placed alongside them. A video of the ceremony has also emerged. Following allegations made by his wife, Bhanvi Singh, Raja Bhaiya performed the ceremonial worship of weapons in front of the public with his supporters for the second consecutive year on Dussehra. On the occasion, Raja Bhaiya said: "The worship of weapons is an ancient Indian tradition. Weapons have been worshipped on Vijayadashami since time immemorial. As far as our family is concerned, this is our longstanding tradition." See two photos... The puja continued for two hours at the ancestral home The festival was celebrated at Benti Kothi (Raja Bhaiya's residence). Acharya Atul Ji Maharaj conducted the worship for around two hours amid the chanting of Vedic mantras. This was followed by a grand aarti and the distribution of prasad. Raja Bhaiya said, "Weapons have been worshipped on Vijayadashami since time immemorial. This is an old tradition in our family. Today, there is a need to familiarise everyone with India's glorious ancient traditions and connect them with them." Says: Wear indigenous clothes at least on festivals Everyone present here today can be seen wearing indigenous clothing such as dhoti-kurtas. We are trying to revive Indian identity, which is gradually disappearing. Young people today rarely wear dhoti-kurtas, but we request that they wear indigenous clothing at least on festive occasions. Licensing weapons and attaching labels to them is routine. When managing so many weapons, names are asked for and slips bearing the names are attached so that no one faces any inconvenience. He also said that everything belonging to him and his supporters belongs to one another. Wife had made allegations a year ago On 3 June 2025, Raja Bhaiya's wife, Bhanvi Singh, submitted a letter to the PMO and accused him of possessing a cache of illegal foreign weapons. Some of these weapons are capable of causing mass destruction, meaning that many people could be killed in an attack. After this, Raja Bhaiya publicly began the tradition of worshipping weapons during last Dussehra. He displayed his weapons as part of the ceremony. Since when has Bhanvi Singh been living separately from Raja Bhaiya? Bhanvi Singh, the wife of Kunda MLA Raja Bhaiya, filed a petition for divorce in Delhi's Saket court in November 2022. She sought divorce on the grounds of cruelty. Bhanvi Singh also accused her in-laws. She said she had left the house and that Raja Bhaiya was in an illicit relationship. She said Raja Bhaiya had barred her from entering the house since September 2020. Bhanvi Singh levelled several allegations against Raja Bhaiya, including domestic violence, assault, not providing money for expenses and neglecting their children. What are Bhanvi's sons and daughters doing? Raja Bhaiya and Bhanvi Singh have two daughters, Raghvi and Brijeshwari, and twin sons, Shivraj and Brijraj. Both daughters live with their mother, Bhanvi, while the sons live with their father, Raja Bhaiya. Brijeshwari is practising law. Raghvi is trying to pursue her studies in the United States. Both sons, Shivraj and Brijraj, completed their studies in Mumbai and are now learning the basics of politics alongside their father. They were actively involved in campaigning with their father during the 2022 Assembly elections. In 2025, both sons joined the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik). It is believed that sooner or later, Raja Bhaiya will make both sons active in politics. Why Are Weapons Worshipped on Dussehra? The tradition of worshipping weapons on Dussehra dates back to ancient times. On this day, Kshatriya kings worshipped their weapons to achieve victory over their enemies. Prof. Vinay Kumar Pandey of the BHU Department of Astro says that weapons are needed to destroy demonic forces. Goddess Durga destroyed the demons and became known as Aparajita Vijaya, after which she began to be worshipped by the people. Therefore, on Dussehra, that is, Vijayadashami, Goddess Vijaya is worshipped along with weapons, the symbols of valour.

stories.title: ₹6.50 lakh lost to trading fraud in Noida:Victim contacted via Telegram and WhatsApp, files complaint with bank statements
stories.summary: A woman in Noida was allegedly duped of ₹6.50 lakh on the pretext of earning huge profits through online share trading. The accused contacted her through Telegram and WhatsApp and persuaded her to transfer money in multiple instalments in the name of investments. The victim filed a complaint at the cybercrime police station on Sunday, seeking action against the accused and the recovery of her money. In her complaint to the police, Manisha Sharma, a resident of Mahagun Moderne Society in Sector 78, said she had connected with four people named Arun, Karan, Abhishek and Nitin through social media. Initially, the four spoke to her about share trading on Telegram. Later, they began contacting her through WhatsApp messages and phone calls. The accused allegedly collected money from her under various pretexts, including fees related to stock market investments and trading. Money transferred to two bank accounts Between August and October 2026, Manisha transferred money on several occasions over a period of nearly two months. During this time, she transferred a total of approximately ₹6.50 lakh to bank accounts provided by the accused. She transferred ₹2,41,212 from one bank account and ₹3,29,224 from another. She also attached statements of both bank accounts to her complaint. Evidence submitted to police The victim also submitted receipts related to her cybercrime complaint and other available evidence to the police. She has requested that the police identify the accused, trace the transferred money, and initiate legal action against them. The police are investigating the bank accounts into which the allegedly defrauded money was transferred.

People are still experiencing heat during the day as bright sunshine continues, while a slight chill has begun to be felt in the morning and evening. The sky has been clear since Tuesday morning, with bright sunshine. The heat persists in the afternoon because of the sun's intensity, but the weather becomes pleasant after sunset. According to the weather forecast, Gorakhpur's maximum temperature is expected to be 32°C and the minimum temperature around 18°C to 20°C on Tuesday. For now, there are no signs of any sudden major change in the weather. What will the weather be like from Wednesday to Sunday? Gorakhpur is likely to have clear skies and bright sunshine on Wednesday as well. The maximum temperature may be around 30 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is expected to remain around 18 degrees Celsius. It will feel hot during the day because of the sunshine, while slight coolness in the morning and at night will provide relief. The weather is also expected to remain dry on Thursday and Friday. Light haze may appear in some areas, but the likelihood of rain is low. On both days, the maximum temperature is expected to remain around 30 to 31 degrees Celsius and the minimum temperature around 18 to 19 degrees Celsius. Sunshine and heat to continue over the weekend No significant change in the weather is expected on Saturday and Sunday either. With clear skies and sunshine during the day, the effects of the heat may continue. However, temperatures will fall in the morning and evening, making the weather feel relatively cooler. With limited rainfall activity, people may continue to experience dry weather for now. Difference between day and night temperatures will be noticeable The difference between day and night temperatures is clearly visible amid this change in the weather. The strong sunshine is making it feel hot during the day, while lower temperatures in the morning and at night have brought a slight chill. The same conditions are expected to continue over the coming days. The weather in Gorakhpur may remain clear and dry for the next five days. A combination of daytime heat and slight coolness in the mornings and evenings is likely to be felt. The likelihood of rain is currently low, and no major changes in temperature are expected.

stories.title: Builder’s son flees after hitting CO’s vehicle:Knocks over police bike in Jhansi, leads hour-long chase before arrest
stories.summary: A video has emerged showing a car fleeing in a cinematic fashion amid a police cordon in Jhansi. On Monday evening, the builder's son reached a deserted area along the dam with his friends in the car. City Circle Officer Priya Singh arrived there, whereupon the builder's son saw the police, reversed the car at high speed and fled. The car had a number plate and black-tinted film on its windows. Suspecting something was amiss, a Chita Mobile constable gave chase. The railway crossing ahead was closed, so the car reversed and came back, ramming the Chita Mobile motorcycle of the constable who was trying to stop it. CO Priya Singh and the inspector then pursued the car. The builder's son also rammed both vehicles. For nearly one hour, he continued driving the car from place to place in cinematic fashion, while the police followed. Villagers also arrived in tractors to catch the people in the car. The car tried to run over pedestrians as well. Meanwhile, the inspector stood with his gun pointed. With the help of villagers, police arrested the builder's son, who was driving the car, and his four friends at around 9 p.m. The car had no number plate, and all four windows were covered with black film. A case of attempted murder has been registered against all of them. The incident took place at Sirmadha Dam in the Sipur Bazaar police station area. Several videos of the incident have emerged. See six pictures... Now read the entire matter in detail Idol immersion is scheduled to take place at Simardha Dam in the Sipri Bazar police station area. Therefore, City Circle Officer Priya Singh and Sipri Bazar Station House Officer Inspector Jai Prakash Chaubey arrived with a police team to inspect the site. When the police reached the dam, an unregistered Baleno car suddenly reversed at high speed and sped away. Suspecting something was amiss, constable Akhilesh Patel chased the car on a Cheetah Mobile patrol bike. The railway crossing ahead was closed. The car then made a U-turn, came back and rammed the Cheetah bike. The constable somehow saved his life. A short while later, the car returned towards the dam. The CO and inspector then chased the car in their vehicle. The road ahead was blocked because of the forest. The car turned back and rammed the vehicle carrying the CO and inspector. It then sped away again. The car's rampage created an atmosphere of panic. It also tried to run over pedestrians. The CO then informed the control room and senior officers and called in additional forces. Villagers also arrived with tractors. After considerable effort, the police cordoned off the area and stopped the car. Car driver Shoaib, Samarth Tiwari, Sagar Pal, Veer Chaudhary and Shashank Shukla were arrested. They are all residents of Premnagar. The car is registered in the name of Shoaib's father, Ali Anwar. He is a builder. Car rammed into them with the intention of killing City SP Preeti Singh said, "Instead of stopping the car, the driver rammed it into the official vehicle of the City CO and the Sipri Bazar police station in-charge, as well as the official two-wheeler used by Cheetah Mobile, with the intention of killing them." The five occupants of the car have been arrested. A case has been registered on the inspector's complaint.

stories.title: Father and son die while breaking cobra’s fangs:They were performing a stunt in Barabanki; 20 injections failed to save them
stories.summary: A father and son died after being bitten by a cobra in Barabanki on Monday night. Both worked as snake catchers. They were breaking the snake's teeth and displaying it at a worship pandal when the cobra bit the son. When the father rushed to save him, the snake bit him too. After being bitten by the cobra, both began banging their heads. They also lost their eyesight. People present at the scene took them to the district hospital, where doctors declared the father dead. The son, who was referred to Lucknow, also died despite being given 20 injections. The incident took place in Jarhara village under the Nagar Kotwali police station area, around 5 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures... Now read the full incident in sequence Mahesh (60) and his son Naumeelal (28), residents of Munakkipurwa village in Satrikh, worked as snake catchers. At 10 p.m. on Sunday, the two had gone to Jharhara village with two snakes to perform. They had caught the cobra from an orchard just a day earlier. They were making the snakes dance to the tune of a been in front of people. During the performance, Naumeelal began trying to break the cobra's venomous fangs. But as his grip loosened, the cobra slipped from his hand and bit Naumeelal on the leg. After being bitten, Naumeelal tried to catch it. Meanwhile, his father Mahesh rushed to save him and tried to catch the cobra, but it also bit him on the leg before leaving the spot. The father and son also worked together at a brick kiln. Mahesh had two daughters, Shikha and Radha. Both daughters are married. However, Shikha lives with her parents because of disputes at her marital home. His son Naumilal also kept his beard and hair grown out like a snake charmer. Son lost his eyesight and died in agony As soon as the cobra bit them, both their conditions began to deteriorate. During the Durga Puja celebrations, committee members took them to the district hospital. Doctors declared Mahesh dead. Naumilal was given 20 vials of anti-snake venom, but his condition continued to worsen. He lost his eyesight, and his voice also disappeared as his throat constricted. He repeatedly got up, sat down and began banging his head. As there was no improvement in his condition, doctors referred him to Lucknow's Lohia Hospital. He died there after a short period of treatment. 24 snakes found in two sacks at home The family was devastated after the deaths of the father and son. Both daughters were inconsolable. The family members said, "Mahesh and Naumilal used to catch snakes and keep them locked in a room at their home. Around 24 snakes were found in two sacks in their room. They used to take different snakes to different events."

stories.title: Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora portrayed as Ravana in Lucknow:10-headed hoarding features AISA-CJP leaders’ photos, calls them ‘Ravanas against India’
stories.summary: Hoarding politics has once again surfaced in Lucknow. A hoarding featuring Ravana's 10 heads was put up on Monday night ahead of Dussehra. It shows photographs of leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party and AISA (All India Students' Association) as Ravana's 10 heads. The hoardings have been put up in different upscale and VIP areas of the city, including Gomtinagar 1090. Passers-by stopping to look at the hoardings The first head is that of Ashutosh Ranka, followed by those of Saurav Das, Imran Khan and Umar Khalid, with Abhijit Dipke in the centre. Pictures of Neha Bora, Prashant Bhushan and Ajinkya Shinde have been placed after them. The words "Ravanas Who Oppose India" are written at the top of the hoarding. The hoarding has been put up by Yogi Sena (India). Passers-by are stopping to look at it as they walk past. Yogi Sena's Mohit Mishra put up the hoarding Mohit Mishra, who put up the hoarding, said, "This hoarding depicts people who oppose Sanatan. Most of them are people who promote jihadi forces and an extremist mindset. These people have never worked in the interests of or in support of Sanatan. "They have always insulted Sanatan, whether on the issue of the Babri Masjid or any other matter related to Sanatan. We want the whole world to identify them through the hoarding. People who follow Sanatan Dharma should not be misled by such people."

stories.title: Yogi’s warning to those who harass girls:Says they will face Ravana’s fate; performs Lord Ram’s rajtilak and aarti
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took out a procession in Gorakhpur on Vijayadashami. Riding in a bulletproof vehicle, Yogi reached the Ramlila Ground, 1.5 km from Gorakhnath Temple. He performed the rajtilak ceremony of Lord Ram there. He then performed the aarti of Lord Ram, Lakshman and Sita. Yogi was welcomed along the procession route with drums, conch-shell blowing and showers of flowers. Young members of the Hanuman Dal performed astonishing stunts, including blowing fireballs from their mouths. Members of the Muslim community also welcomed him. As soon as Yogi's chariot emerged from the main gate of Gorakhnath Temple, traffic on the Gorakhpur-Sonauli Highway was stopped to allow an ambulance to pass. Earlier in the morning, Yogi performed worship for more than two hours, wearing the special traditional attire of the Gorakshpeethadhishwar. The Gorakshpeethadhishwar offered jawara, grown at the altar of the Shaktipeeth, to Mahayogi Gorakhnath, performed the aarti and waved a chamar by hand as an act of devotional service. He then performed special rituals for the eternal flame, all the deities, the revered figures of the Nath sect, the eternal sacred fire pit, the yagyashala and Bhim Sarovar at the temple. stories.title: MBBS student found hanging in Muzaffarnagar medical college hostel:Room locked from inside; SSP says she had an argument with a friend
stories.summary: An MBBS student at Muzaffarnagar Medical College died by suicide after hanging herself in her hostel room. At 9 p.m., police broke open the door when it did not open. The student's body was then brought down from the noose. She was studying in the final year of the MBBS course. After receiving information about the incident, the SP City reached the spot. The police and forensic team inspected the scene. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The reason behind the student's death is not clear yet. The police are investigating the matter from all angles. The incident took place in the Mansurpur police station area. See 2 pictures According to station house officer Vipin Tyagi, student Shagun Saini (23) was a resident of Kaithal in Haryana. Shagun returned from outside in the evening and went to her room. Her roommate, Jia, was not in the room at the time. When Jia returned at around 8.30 p.m., she found the room locked from inside. After her attempts to get the door opened failed, she looked inside through the window and saw Shagun's body hanging from a noose. Roommate informed college administration Jiya informed the college administration about the incident. The police then reached the spot, broke open the door and entered the room. The student's family was informed of her death. The police did not find any suicide note at the scene. Dispute with a friend comes to light SSP Suraj Kumar Rai said questioning roommate Jiya revealed that Shagun often had disputes with a friend. The police are treating this as part of the investigation as well. Further action will be taken after her family arrives.

stories.title: ‘The truck was a foot away from crushing me too’:Varanasi crash survivor recounts horror as five bodies lay scattered within five minutes
stories.summary: Five friends who had stopped a Scorpio on an overbridge in Varanasi to take selfies died. Three are in critical condition. Rajkumar survived the accident. He said they had stopped the Scorpio on the NH-19 overbridge so they could relieve themselves. Everyone got out of the vehicle and walked ahead. I was urinating about 5 feet behind the vehicle. It had been five minutes since we got out of the vehicle. That was when the truck hit the Scorpio. Two people fell 30 feet from the bridge immediately after the collision. The others were thrown into the air and landed on the road. The truck ran over the people and continued on its way. If there had been just 1 foot less distance, I would have been run over too. In fact, at 6 a.m. on Monday, a speeding truck approached from behind on the overbridge of the Prayagraj-Varanasi Highway (NH-19) and hit the Scorpio. The collision was so severe that the bodies were scattered up to 25 feet away. Half of the Scorpio was destroyed. The bodies of three friends were found on the overbridge, while another body had fallen 30 feet below it. A youth was also found writhing beneath the overbridge. Around 12 hours after the accident, one of the injured people died in hospital. Anand Yadav (25), Alok Mishra (30), Pradeep Singh (36), Vidwanshu Yadav (30) and Kishan Yadav (35) died in the accident. The injured included Sawan Yadav (26), Rajkumar Yadav (35) and Nikhil (32). All the injured are undergoing treatment at the trauma centre. The accident occurred in Roopapur village, within the jurisdiction of Mirzamurad police station, 27 km from the district headquarters. The last rites of four people had been performed by late evening. I lost consciousness after the accident Rajkumar Yadav said, "We were all returning after offering prayers at Vindhyachal. We had left there at 4:30 a.m. The accident occurred at around 6 a.m. When I saw the accident, I fainted and fell on the road. People from the surrounding area reached the spot. They sprinkled water on me and brought me round." I saw bodies scattered on the road. Half of the Scorpio had been destroyed. I called my paternal aunt's sons. When they arrived, I urged them to call an ambulance. Rajkumar said that the Scorpio was being driven by Kanhaiya Yadav, his maternal uncle's son. The police have arrested the truck's helper, while the driver fled after abandoning the vehicle. Rajkumar said there was not a single friend of his in the vehicle. They were all friends of his maternal uncle's son, Kanhaiya. He had simply gone along with everyone. The bodies of Alok Mishra, Pradeep Singh, Anand Yadav and Vidwanshu Yadav were cremated at Manikarnika Ghat late on Monday evening. Truck was travelling at 80 to 90 km/h According to the police, the truck was also travelling from Prayagraj towards Varanasi. It was carrying apples. The truck was travelling at between 80 and 90 km/h. This is why the driver was unable to control it after suddenly seeing the Scorpio stopped on the overbridge. The truck rammed into the Scorpio from behind. As a result, the Scorpio was dragged forward for around 30-40 metres. All eight friends were standing around the vehicle. The truck ran over four of them, while the other four friends were also caught in its path. After the accident, the driver abandoned the truck about 200 metres away and fled. Police are working to trace him with the help of CCTV footage. During the investigation, boxes of prasad, coconuts and chunaris were found inside the Scorpio. Friends visited Vindhyachal Dham on Nikhil's birthday All the friends had gone to Vindhyachal Dham on Nikhil's birthday. After paying their respects, they had a photograph taken. Seven people can be seen in the photograph, while the eighth friend is taking it. Pradeep was a manager at an e-commerce company, while Vidwanshu worked as a contractor 1. Alok Mishra - He was a resident of Pisaur, Shivpur. His father, Ajay, is a farmer, and his mother, Urmila, is a homemaker. Alok was the second of three siblings. He had studied up to Class 12. His father said, "He was due to join JIO five days later." 2. Vidwanshu Yadav - He was a resident of VDA Colony, Shivpur. He worked as a contractor. He was the second of three brothers. He had been shouldering the responsibility of the household since his father's death. His mother, Mridula Devi, is a homemaker. 3. Pradeep Singh - He was a resident of Cholapur. He worked as a manager at the e-commerce company Meesho. He has a son. After receiving the news of his death, his wife, Sona, was inconsolable. 4. Anand Yadav - He was a resident of Shivpur. Pictures of the friends at Vindhyachal Dham Chandauli MP Virendra Singh reaches the post-mortem house Chandauli MP Virendra Singh reached the post-mortem house after receiving information that five people had died. He offered condolences to the family. Earlier, Samajwadi Party district president Sujeet Yadav Lakkad had also reached the scene of the accident. Mirzamurad Inspector Gopalji Kushwaha said: Enquiries with local residents revealed that the people travelling in the car had stopped on the flyover and were taking selfies. However, the exact cause of the accident will be known only after the investigation.

stories.title: Second audio of Shiva and model Shraddha:She says, 'Are you cheating the punters? I treated you like a dog and beat you; I recorded your gold business'
stories.summary: The second viral audio recording of a conversation between the main accused Shraddha Dubey, and deceased Shiva Sharma in the Shiva Sharma murder case has surfaced. In it, Shraddha Dubey is heard abusing Shiva and saying that she would hurt his ego. She also threatens Shiva, saying, "I have recorded your gold business as well. You are cutting off my punters (bettors)." Dainik Bhaskar does not verify the authenticity of this audio. Listen to the audio that has emerged... Shraddha Dubey: Go towards his house, you coward…. Come on, I am coming towards your house. Come. I will speak to you in front of your gate. Come on." Shiva Sharma: So, am I heading towards your house right now? Shraddha Dubey: No, no. Until now, you were at some such place, you... gathering punters…. Do you understand? I am coming to your house." Shiva Sharma: Hey brother, I got a call from Aamir-who is collecting the punters... I got a call from your punter. Shraddha Dubey: You're driving me crazy, poaching my punters…. I also recorded your gold-related work. Shiva Sharma: Brother, where am I poaching your punter? Your punter called me; I didn't call. Shraddha Dubey: The whole city is laughing that I beat you after turning you into a dog. The more you irritate me, the more I will spread this matter now. I will also show the video to other people. The more you irritate me, just understand that now. Because you irritated me, behaved rudely and played with me." Shiva Sharma: Hey, who played with whom, mate? Shraddha Dubey: Come on, I will... I will tell everyone, actually, and show them... What happened and what did not, okay? You do not need to get into that. You are depressing me now, you know. You are hurting my ego a lot and depressing me terribly. Okay? Wait... 2 videos emerged about Shiva's gold and transactions... First VIDEO: I will return the money in one month Shraddha: When did you steal from my place? What time did you do it? Was it in September or October? When did you do it? I am asking you very calmly. I have not called the police yet. I will call them after this, but first tell me. Shiva: In September... and when we were going to the washroom... Shraddha: What was I doing in the washroom? Approximately how long did it take me? Shiva: It took about 20-25 minutes. Shraddha: It took 20-25 minutes, so did you steal all the jewellery at once or in separate instances? Shiva: I took it all at once. Shraddha: All at once? Three chains and one bracelet? Shiva: Yes. Shraddha: Where did you sell them? Shiva: In Chowk. Shraddha: Whose shop in Chowk? Shiva: I sold them inside the Gol Darwaza area in Chowk. I do not know which shop it was, because a boy took me there and sold... I mean, the items... Shraddha: You sold them and gave me the money? Shiva: (Nods in response.) Shraddha: So my total amount is around ₹6 lakh. By when will I receive it? Shiva: You will receive it within a month. Shraddha: Does your mother know about this? Shiva: No. Shraddha: That you stole them? Shiva: No one knows. Shraddha: No one knows about this at all? Shiva: No one knows. Shraddha: All right! And I am not making you record this video by putting pressure on you, am I? Brother, you admitted it yourself... Shiva: Yes, I did not make you record it... SECOND VIDEO: Shiva said, "Keep my car" Shraddha: When will you return the money? Shiva: Within a month. Shraddha: Okay! Shiva: Then I will give that in writing. Until then, keep my car. I will take my car back after paying the money. Now read the full story...
