stories.title: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal launches new political party:Names it Jan Neeti Bharat, will contest the election from Mirzapur Sadar
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh IAS officer Divya Mittal has announced the launch of her own political party. The party has been named ‘Janniti Bharat’. In a video posted on Facebook at 1 pm on Thursday, she announced that she will contest the 2027 Assembly elections from the Mirzapur Sadar constituency. Divya Mittal said: In Janniti Bharat, the rule will be yours. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections. The government will run according to your wishes for five years. Earlier, on September 30, Divya Mittal had announced her entry into politics. She had said that she would remain in Uttar Pradesh, would not be afraid and would continue to raise questions. She had also said that she would not join any political party and would walk alone. Her aim, she said, was not to change politicians but to change the entire political system. “I do not want money or muscle power,” she had said. Divya, a 2013-batch IAS officer, had written on Facebook two days ago, on Tuesday, that she would announce the next step in her political journey on October 15. Since then, there had been speculation about her future plans. Divya had studied BTech at IIT Delhi and an MBA at IIM Bengaluru before taking up a high-paying job in London. Here is what Divya Mittal said in the video, word for word: 1. First pledge of ‘Janniti Bharat’ — From people to policy, from policy to India Divya Mittal said, “I am forming my own political party. You may ask, are there not enough political parties already? There is no shortage of parties; there is a shortage of people being heard. “I am standing in front of the Ganga. In the Ganga, every drop is equal. All the drops together determine the course. I want to build a party in the same way, where every person is a drop and every drop has a role. The party that has emerged from this idea is called ‘Janniti Bharat’. “In Janniti Bharat, the rule will be yours. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections. The government will run according to your wishes for five years — not just for one day, but at every step. “Janniti Bharat has three pledges. People will be at the centre of the country’s policies and people themselves will decide the policies. “You may remember Devkali Devi. Despite not having water at home, she had asked me for a school. After my video, work on the school began. The foundation was being laid, but then it was discovered that the land belonged to the forest department, so the work was stopped. The children whose future was supposed to be built on that foundation are still waiting. “The question is, when the country’s biggest industrialists need a road to be built, the forest gives way in 80 days. But when a poor person needs a school, a road or a factory, why does that file remain pending for 80 years? “The second policy is justice — where everyone is heard. Ask the people where they should get justice. Ask the people how policies should be made. A mother eats one less roti but makes sure her child has enough to eat. A father cuts down on his own expenses but sends his child to school. This is the kind of thinking our policies will reflect. “There will be a farming policy with farmers at the centre. Farmers know what problems they face from the field to the mandi and where prices collapse. Similarly, trade policy will focus on small traders and the problems they face from their businesses to the ports. “A girl is looking at the moon from the roof of her house today. One day, she will reach it.“The first pledge of Janniti Bharat — from people to policy, from policy to India.” 2. Every decision will be based on need, not identity “The second pledge of Janniti Bharat — every decision will be based on need, not identity.” She said, “A road was being built and hope had emerged in the village. Then someone pointed a finger and changed the direction of the road. On one side, thousands of people would have benefited; on the other, there was one person. The road was diverted towards the other side, where there were hundreds of houses. Courtyards were destroyed and homes were demolished. The road was built for someone. “In Janniti, everyone will be able to point to a location on the map. If there is a dark stretch where girls are afraid to pass, where will they report it? They will mark the location on a mobile app. When 100 people mark the same spot, there will be lights, patrolling and cameras there. The decision will not be taken by the police or a politician, but by those girls. “Whether it is a hand pump, a road or a paved lane, people will point out where the work is needed most and work will begin there. There will be no caste, religion or status involved. Everyone will decide together.” 3. Decisions based on need and equality in decision-making The third pledge of Janniti Bharat is — decisions based on need and equality in decision-making. She said, “The public will keep an account of every piece of work. At present, people do not even know about the work, while the middleman gets to know first. “A woman applied for a permanent house, but she did not know that her house had been approved. A middleman came to her and said, ‘Mother, I will get it done. Give me Rs 5,000.’ If the woman knows about the approval first, then who will the middleman approach? “Every piece of work carried out in that village through any fund should be visible on a mobile phone. But what happens now is that the person who carried out the faulty work is asked whether everything was done properly. What answer will he give? He will say everything is fine. “If you give children their own notebooks to check, they will say everything is fine. Who is the first person to know that a road is in bad condition? The people who use that road. “If we use three colours for a bad road — green means good, yellow means average and red means bad — the same colours can be used for places people depend on every day, such as schools, hospitals and ration shops. “Were books provided at the school? How was the teaching? The same three colours. These three colours can be used for hospitals as well. These three colours can cover the entire block and district. The officer will know, the minister will know and the entire district will know. “This is the third pledge of Janniti Bharat — the public will have the right to demand an account, and that accountability will lead to improvement.” 4. We will fight together — not do politics, but practise Janniti She said, “If you are going to do everything yourselves, then what will the MLAs do? What will the MLAs of Janniti Bharat do? The MLA’s job will be to go to your doorstep. To write for those who cannot write and to mark things on the phone for those who cannot do it themselves. “Today, the MLA sits between the people and the government, but faces the government. In Janniti Bharat, the MLA will sit in the same place, but will face the people. “You may ask, if this is so easy, why has it not happened until now? There is a phone in every hand. If train tickets can be booked on a phone, why can’t this be done on a phone? Because the question here is not about convenience, but about power. “The person who takes Rs 5,000, the person who leaves a road incomplete, the person who investigates his own wrongdoing and the person who changes the direction of a road are not different people. They are the four legs of the same chair. “I had said earlier that you are the sun. The sun does not need anyone’s permission to rise. The day the sun rises, the rule will belong to every person. “This party has neither money nor s. Therefore, this fight will not be fought through posters, but from house to house. Every house will be an office and every person will be a campaigner. “Invite me to your village or town as well. We will fight this battle together. “I had said earlier that you are the sun. I have opened one window; you open three more windows. Send this video and message to three people and write three words — ‘Not politics, but Janniti.’” Four days ago, she visited Mirzapur for the first time after announcing her entry into politics Earlier, Divya Mittal had reached Mirzapur on Sunday, the first day of Navratri. It was her first visit to the district after announcing her entry into politics. Her supporters gave her a grand welcome. Slogans of “Divya Didi Zindabad” were raised. Women presented her with garlands of roses and showered flowers on her. Divya became emotional when people touched her feet. She told the people, “You have weighed me down with flowers and garlands. This is your love. You make me emotional every time. It feels as if Mirzapur has taken a contract to make me cry. Mirzapur should always keep smiling. No one should cry.” Divya Mittal was Mirzapur DM and had helped bring water to Lahuriyadah Divya Mittal became the District Magistrate of Mirzapur in September 2022. She was discussed for her work involving public outreach programmes and drinking-water initiatives in rural areas. The initiative to provide piped water to Lahuriyadah village was also undertaken during her tenure. Her farewell after she was transferred from Mirzapur also attracted attention. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Later, her tenure in Deoria also made headlines after a dispute over powers between elected representatives and the administration. After resignation was accepted, she wrote — ‘Move forward, move forward’ Former IAS officer Divya had resigned from service on August 30. Her resignation was accepted on September 14. After her resignation was accepted, Divya wrote, “My resignation from the IAS has been accepted.” She also quoted lines from poet Jaishankar Prasad’s play Chandragupta: “Prashast punya panth hai, badhe chalo, badhe chalo.” “Prashast punya panth hai” means that the path of protecting and gaining freedom for the motherland is vast, clear and sacred. “Badhe chalo, badhe chalo” is a call by the poet to the brave sons and soldiers of the country to continue moving forward on this sacred path without stopping or being afraid. Divya left her London job to join the civil services Divya is originally from Rewari in Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she worked in London. She met Gagandeep Singh there. The two had a love marriage. However, after a few years, the couple left their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC examination. She cleared the IPS examination on her first attempt without coaching and was allotted the Gujarat cadre. She continued preparing for the IAS examination even during her IPS training. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya’s husband is from Punjab, cleared UPSC in his first attempt Divya’s husband Gagandeep Singh’s family is from Gidderbaha in Punjab’s Bathinda district. He studied chemical engineering at IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002 and management at IIM Bengaluru from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt in 2010 and was selected for the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned as Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

stories.title: Model accused of murder says Shiva died by suicide:Claims she saw him jump with her own eyes; releases three videos from Nepal in 12 hours
stories.summary: Another video of model Shraddha Dubey, accused in the murder of Lucknow millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma, has emerged. Shraddha, who has fled to Nepal, has released her third video in the past 12 hours. In the video released on Thursday, she says, "It was not murder; it was suicide. I saw him jump with my own eyes." "If the CCTV cameras there are checked, everything will come out. It will show how he jumped. It is not that we are not distressed. At that time, I was in no condition to say anything. My health deteriorated badly because someone from my house attempted suicide, so it was natural for my condition to worsen." 7 October incident This happened on the 7th, when Shiva, through a tea seller in Kapurthala... There is a tea seller at Kapurthala's main crossroads where we used to often have tea. Through him, Shiva had my driver called. Shiva Sharma and I had had no contact for, let us say, six or seven days before the 7th. We had not spoken for five or six days. He had my driver called through the tea seller. During that call, he was crying a lot. Then I called him twice from my number. He did not answer at the time. At 2:00 a.m., I received a call from Shiva. I asked him, "What happened? Why are you crying?" He said, "Where are you?" I replied, "I am standing at Dainik." He came to Dainik in his BMW and met me. He also said on the call-if the call details are obtained, they will show that he said, "Babu, I am coming, okay?" He came and spoke with me. He had drunk a lot of beer, okay? We went to Paddlers Café. At Paddlers Café, he ordered matcha for me and juice and other things for my driver, and got something for himself as well. After that, he went home with me. We drove home as we usually did. He was driving my car, while my driver was driving his car, okay? Reference to his sister's arrival and meeting friends After 7, on 8... Navratri was approaching, and it was on 11. My sister came to my house on 8 to discuss something related to the puja. She came to my house in the morning on 8. My sister has absolutely no connection with this case. She did not even know Shiva well. If her call details are obtained, they will show that she had neither spoken to Shiva nor anything else. She knew very little about Shiva Sharma. My sister... my sister had absolutely nothing to do with it. She had come to my house after so many days, okay? Even when my sister came on the 8th, we continued to relax and everything remained fine. We went out. In the evening, some of Shiva Sharma's friends came, one of whom was named Ashwini Mishra and the other Harsh. If Shiva Sharma had been subjected to any kind of torture or anything else, why did his friends not go to the police and report that he was being tortured? There was no such torture; nothing of the sort happened to Shiva. Shiva and I were happy and were doing very well. I had known Shiva Sharma for only two months; he had been my friend for four months. We had been in a relationship for the past two months, so we knew each other, okay? He... His mother said that he lived with me in a live-in relationship. Sometimes he stayed for 15 days, and sometimes he would disappear for two to four days; that is what he used to do. Five days before I met him, when we were not in contact, he had gone to Kedarnath or somewhere else on a trip with his sister and brother-in-law. Claim of debt and suspicion of suicide I have some screenshots that I will share with you. They clearly show that Shiva had accumulated a huge debt-outstanding loans of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. Whenever he sat with us, calls from creditors would start coming in. If his call records are retrieved-I have sent Shiva Sharma's phone to the police-and everything is checked, they will show that Shiva Sharma was receiving calls from a large number of creditors. He had become so troubled by his debt that he would tell me, "If I am unable to repay the debt, I might even commit suicide." Right? He was extremely distressed, but at the time we were taking what he said lightly. Just think for yourself: why would a girl kill someone and throw them down from her own flat, right? So, my request to the media is: please do not spread such things or circulate such rumours about anyone. I was not in that condition because, while our driver and we were rushing around, her mother arrived there. We called her mother, 112 and 108. Her mother arrived and then began assaulting my driver there, which will have been recorded on the hospital's cameras, all right? Without knowing anything, she directly accused us of murder. I mean, without thinking or finding out the facts, she immediately blamed us for murder. She made such a serious allegation against us that we may never be able to escape that blame for the rest of our lives, all right? Reference to the events of 8 and 9 October So, on the 8th, we... and on the 9th, we remained normal as well. On the 8th, we went out and drove around, going on a long drive. During that time, there were several conversations with Shiva Sharma, her mother, her brother-in-law and her sister. Calls came in in front of me, and conversations took place, all right? Then, on the 9th, he was depressed-I do not know myself what was going on. When we wake up, we have tea served in the drawing room. Shiva went inside to use the washroom, but whenever he went to the washroom, he never closed my main gate. As soon as he closed the main gate, I became suspicious because he had already told me that he had so many debts. I immediately sent my sister to go and check what he was doing. By the time my sister opened the gate, he had jumped from the balcony. It is not as though you have lost your son; I have lost my man too. I am also extremely distressed. Please, I request the media not to harass me, please. You have lost one life, and if you continue to torture me like this, I will kill myself. I really will kill myself.

stories.title: Model Shraddha Dubey escapes police again:Nepal CCTV surfaces; cops suspect insider leak
stories.summary: Police are searching for model Shraddha Dubey, an accused in the murder case of Lucknow resident Shiva Sharma, after she allegedly crossed into Nepal with her sister and a friend. CCTV footage reportedly shows the three heading towards a bus station in Nepal after leaving their SUV near the India-Nepal border. Two videos featuring Shraddha have also surfaced from Nepal, in which she claims to be innocent. Police suspect that she is receiving information about their investigation and movements. Investigators are trying to find out who is helping her evade arrest and how she is getting updates about the police operation. Meanwhile, Shraddha's Instagram followers have increased from around 141,000 to 142,000 since the incident, while the number of accounts she follows has fallen from 421 to 410. Police teams fail to trace her in Sitapur and Lakhimpur Three teams from the Lucknow Police Crime Branch and Hazratganj police station are searching for Shraddha. The teams include an inspector, six sub-inspectors and 16 police personnel. According to the police, when a team reached Sitapur to find her, she had already left. Her location was subsequently traced to Lakhimpur, but the police failed to find her there as well. Investigators believe Shraddha travelled to Rupaidiha on the India-Nepal border with her sister, Rashmi, and friend Adil. Her Scorpio SUV was found abandoned in a private parking area. The three allegedly crossed the border on foot and reached Mahim Nagar in Nepal. CCTV footage reportedly shows Shraddha, Rashmi and Adil crossing a road and entering a bus station. They are believed to have spent the night there before leaving by bus the following morning, before the police team arrived. Who is leaking information about the police operation? Investigators suspect that Shraddha is receiving updates about police movements and the progress of the investigation. According to police sources, screenshots containing information about the reward announced for her arrest and other developments may also have been sent to her. The police are trying to identify those allegedly passing on the information. Action may be taken against them if their involvement is established. The release of two videos while Shraddha remains at large has also raised questions about who is helping her record and circulate the clips. In the videos, she claims to be innocent. The police are investigating how she is obtaining information about the case and whether anyone is helping her evade arrest. Instagram followers increase after the incident Shraddha's Instagram account has also drawn attention since the case came to light. Her follower count reportedly increased from around 141,000 to 142,000, while the number of accounts she follows dropped from 421 to 410. The report suggests that some high-profile accounts may have been blocked or unfollowed. However, it is unclear whether Shraddha herself made these changes. Shraddha's sister Rashmi also remains on the run Rashmi Dubey, Shraddha's sister, is also absconding in connection with the case. According to details emerging during the investigation, Rashmi previously worked at a private bank. She later became interested in social media influencing after seeing her sister's growing popularity, reels and large following. Rashmi began posting more actively on social media. Her Instagram account reportedly features videos of her dressing up and attending late-night parties. The report also describes her as someone who enjoys parties and hookah. See three pictures of Shraddha's sister... What happened in the Shiva Sharma murder case? On 9 October, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments in Lucknow's Hazratganj area. He had reportedly been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the previous four months. According to the report, Shiva was found wearing only underwear, with lipstick on his face and several cigarette burn marks on his body. His mother, Ranjana Sharma, filed a murder complaint against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver, Adil. The family has alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. The allegation is part of the ongoing investigation and has not been established in court. Hazratganj police station in-charge Vikram Singh said teams had been deployed to trace the accused and that the police were working to arrest them soon.

stories.title: Weekly special train to run between Udaipur and Delhi Sarai:Six trips each way from October 21 to November 26 to ease festive rush
stories.summary: To meet the rising demand for train travel during the festive season, the Railway has decided to operate a weekly special train between Udaipur and Delhi Sarai. The special train will make six trips in each direction between 21 October and 26 November. The train will depart from Udaipur at 9:15 p.m. every Wednesday and from Delhi at 1:45 p.m. every Thursday. The operation of this new train will make it much easier for thousands of passengers travelling to and from Delhi from areas around Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Bhilwara, Ajmer and Jaipur to get confirmed tickets during major festivals such as Diwali and Chhath. North Western Railway Chief Public Relations Officer Amit Sudarshan said that train number 09617, the Udaipur City-Delhi Sarai weekly special, would operate from 21 October to 25 November. The train will depart from Udaipur City at 9:15 p.m. every Wednesday and reach Delhi Sarai station at 11:15 a.m. the following day. Special train to operate on the return journey from 22 October On the return journey, train number 09618 Delhi Sarai-Udaipur City Weekly Special will operate from 22 October to 26 November. The train will depart from Delhi Sarai at 1:45 p.m. every Thursday and reach Udaipur City at 4:00 a.m. the following day. The special train will stop at a total of 14 major stations in both directions along the route. These include Mavli, Chanderiya, Bhilwara, Bijainagar, Ajmer, Kishangarh and Phulera. It will also halt at Ringas, Neem Ka Thana, Narnaul, Ateli, Rewari, Gurugram and Delhi Cantt stations. The halt at Ringas will directly benefit devotees travelling to Khatu Shyamji. A total of 22 coaches have been attached to the train for passengers' convenience. It caters to passengers travelling in every class, from AC to general. The train will have two Second AC, six Third AC and two Third AC Economy coaches. In addition, it will have six Sleeper Class and four General Class coaches. It will also include one guard coach and one power car.

stories.title: 31kg of cannabis worth ₹15 lakh hidden in animal feed:One arrested in Varanasi; stock intended for festival supply
stories.summary: The Varanasi Police Commissioner has directed the Varanasi police to crack down on drugs ahead of the festival. Acting on these instructions, Siga Police in Varanasi on Wednesday surrounded the area near the old iron tank in Pachpedwa and arrested a notorious interstate smuggler. The smuggler had brought a consignment of ganja to Varanasi concealed in a vehicle carrying animal feed. It was intended to be sold during the festivals. The 31-kilogram consignment of ganja has been valued at ₹15 lakh. The arrested smuggler, Rajkishore Gaur, is a resident of Buxar, Bihar. He also supplies ganja under the guise of transporting animal feed. He will be sent to jail on Thursday. Siga police lay trap near Pachpedwa Siga Inspector Shivakant Mishra said while revealing details of the case that the police had received information from an informer that a large consignment of prohibited narcotics was being brought into the city in a pickup vehicle for sale. As soon as they received the information, the Siga Police team went on alert and intensified checking near the old iron tank in Pachpedwa. Meanwhile, police signalled a goods-laden pickup vehicle approaching under suspicious circumstances to stop. On seeing the police, the driver tried to flee, but the alert police team cordoned off the area and caught him at the spot. Smuggler from Bihar, cannabis packed in 30 packets Police questioning and investigation revealed that the arrested accused was identified as Rajkishore God. Inspector Shivakant Mishra said the accused, Rajkishore God, was a resident of Nawadera in Bihar's Buxar district. He had been involved in the illegal trade for a long time and supplied narcotics across the border. When police thoroughly searched the seized pickup vehicle, they found 10 sacks of animal feed (cattle feed) loaded inside it. At first glance, it appeared to be an ordinary goods vehicle. However, when police removed the sacks of animal feed and checked underneath, they recovered 30 packets of cannabis hidden there. Weighing revealed that the total quantity of cannabis seized was 31.275 kilograms. New method of smuggling The inspector said that during questioning, the shrewd criminal revealed that he constantly adopted new tactics to evade the police. This time, he used animal feed as a cover to deceive the police. Animal feed has a strong odour of its own, which easily masks the smell of cannabis. The accused hoped that the police would see the sacks of bran and let the vehicle pass without checking it, but his plan failed due to the vigilance of the Sigra police.

stories.summary: Customs officials at Lucknow’s Amausi airport have seized gold worth around Rs 70 lakh from a passenger arriving from Sharjah. On Wednesday, officials noticed the passenger limping and approached him for questioning. He appeared nervous and gave evasive answers. During a search, officials found 472.100 grams of gold in paste form packed inside a plastic pouch and concealed in his underwear. He had tied the pouch around his waist like a waistband to avoid suspicion. The seized gold was valued at Rs 70,81,500. Officials have seized the gold and detained the passenger, identified as Kedar Mahto, a resident of Gopalganj in Bihar. He is being questioned to determine who had instructed him to bring the gold to Lucknow and to whom he was supposed to deliver it. Here is the complete sequence of events: Gold suspected to have been brought in without paying customs duty Officials suspect that the passenger concealed the gold to bring it into the country without paying customs duty. Further investigation is underway to examine other aspects of the case.

stories.title: Cross-examination of witness completed in Gorakhpur:Confirms shop CCTV footage in case involving rape and murder of 10-year-old girl
stories.summary: In the case involving the abduction, rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl from Gorakhpur District Hospital, the defence completed its cross-examination of witness Ashhar Jameel on Wednesday. He proved in court the footage from the CCTV cameras installed at his plywood shop on Bank Road. During the investigation, the police had secured this footage on a pen drive. The defence began its cross-examination after the witness's examination-in-chief was recorded on Tuesday, but it remained incomplete due to a lack of time. The remaining questions and answers were completed on Wednesday. Special Public Prosecutors Raghavendra Tripathi and Ram Milan Singh represented the prosecution in the case. Brijesh Singh, the defence's Chief Legal Aid Defence Counsel, and Deputy Counsel Bhagat Gaur questioned the witness. The court has scheduled 15 October for the next hearing in the case. CCTV footage proved in court Ashhar Jameel, who runs a plywood shop opposite V-Mart on Bank Road, confirmed the CCTV camera footage from his shop in court on Tuesday. The police had preserved the footage on a pen drive during the investigation. According to the prosecution, the footage is important evidence in the investigation of the case. On Wednesday, the defence continued questioning the witness. His cross-examination was completed. Witness questioned for two days Special Public Prosecutors Raghavendra Tripathi and Ram Milan Singh recorded Ashhar Jameel's examination-in-chief on Tuesday. The defence lawyers then began cross-examining him. The entire process could not be completed on Tuesday due to a lack of time. On Wednesday, the defence asked the remaining questions and completed the witness's cross-examination. The next hearing in the case will be held on 15 October. What is the full case? On the night of 28 July, a 10-year-old girl went to Gorakhpur District Hospital to give food to her elder sister, who was admitted there. During this time, the girl suddenly went missing. When her family began searching for her, they learnt that a young man wearing a police uniform had taken her with him. Police then advanced the investigation with the help of CCTV footage and surveillance. The investigation indicated that constable Abhishek Yadav, a resident of Ghazipur and posted with Dial 112, was accused of abducting the girl. Body found along the Rohin River in Rohin on 30 July According to police, during interrogation in custody, the accused confessed to raping and killing the girl. The girl's body was recovered on 30 July along the Rohin River in Chiutaha. After the case came to light, the accused constable was dismissed from service and sent to jail. The hearing in the case is now proceeding in court on the basis of witness statements and evidence.

stories.title: UP weather to change, rain alert in 23 districts:Flood-hit Lucknow still has up to 4 feet of water in lanes; 10 new dengue cases reported
stories.summary: Weather conditions are set to change once again in Uttar Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms, rain and hail over the next 48 hours. Lightning is also likely in several areas. Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist in Varanasi, said, A fresh western disturbance has become active over the hilly regions, while easterly winds are bringing moisture from the Bay of Bengal. Under its influence, the rain system has strengthened over western UP today. Tomorrow, eastern and central UP may receive rain accompanied by strong winds. After that, the weather will clear up. Meanwhile, floods continue to trouble Lucknow. Although the water level in the Gomti has started falling, more than 3 lakh people in the Faizullaganj area remain affected. Homes have remained inundated with 3–4 feet of water for the 19th consecutive day. Boats are still operating in the streets and localities. The risk of dengue is also rising, with 10 new cases reported in the past 24 hours. Water enters more than 40,000 homes The floods have affected thousands of families. According to information, three to four feet of water has entered more than 40,000 homes. As a result, a population of more than 3 lakh people has been affected. With water entering their homes, people are facing a crisis in meeting their everyday needs. In several areas, people are struggling to reach safe locations and arrange essential supplies. Normal movement has been disrupted as roads and lanes are flooded. Several families are trapped in their homes and are also finding it difficult to buy essential supplies. Due to the persistent waterlogging, people are worried about stagnant water, filth and the spread of diseases in their homes.

stories.title: Brother-in-law dies by suicide after sister-in-law’s settlement at panchayat:Shoots himself in head in Sultanpur; she was refusing to live with her husband
stories.summary: In Sultanpur, a brother-in-law shot himself in the head after returning from a panchayat meeting concerning his sister-in-law. At the panchayat meeting in Jaunpur, a settlement had been reached between the sister-in-law's husband and her parental family, but her brother-in-law Digvijay did not agree with the decision. After returning home on Tuesday (13 October), he shot himself in the head with his father's licensed rifle. On Wednesday, his four-year-old son performed his father's last rites. Digvijay had gone to the panchayat meeting alone. His wife said that after returning home, he did not tell her anything about what had happened at the meeting. She said that as soon as her mother called, Digvijay went into the room and shot himself. The incident took place in the Lambhua area, around 37 km from the district headquarters. What exactly happened at the panchayat that left Digvijay upset? Read the full report... Read what happened... Digvijay shot himself with a rifle in Sultanpur on Tuesday evening. He had returned home from his in-laws' house just 10 minutes before the incident. Hearing the sound of the gunshot, his wife ran to the room, where she found her husband writhing on the floor, covered in blood. His wife telephoned the family and informed them about the incident. The family then took the young man to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. At the time of the incident, only the young man's wife and children were at home. On Wednesday evening, his four-year-old son performed his father's last rites. Had 18 bighas of land under cultivation Digvijay Singh (32), son of Lal Pratap Singh, lived in Dhanecch village and worked in agriculture. The family owned 18 bighas of land. Digvijay was the only son of his parents. His father, Lal Pratap Singh, also worked in agriculture but has been paralysed for 10 years. Digvijay married Amrita Singh, a resident of Sunjanganj in Jaunpur, eight years ago. Digvijay and Amrita had three children - Dhruvi (6), Surbhi (5) and their youngest son, Shaurya (4). Two years ago, Digvijay arranged the marriage of his sister-in-law Moni to Ayush, who also lived in the village. Ayush's house is 400 metres from Digvijay's home. Moni and Ayush began arguing soon after their marriage. Had tried several times to broker a reconciliation Initially, Digvijay tried several times to reconcile the two. However, six months ago, Moni left her marital home and returned to her parents' home. Digvijay made several attempts to reason with both sides, but no solution was found. Since Digvijay had arranged the marriage, he convened several village councils in an effort to persuade his sister-in-law to continue living at her marital home. Moni had made it clear that she would not live with Ayush. Ayush, too, had said that he would no longer go to bring Moni back. On Tuesday, Ayush was travelling to Jaunpur to try to reach a settlement. Digvijay also went to his in-laws' home to attend the village council. Both were supposed to travel there from the village, but they went separately. Digvijay was not in favour of brokering a settlement Talks of a settlement between Moni and Ayush began in Jaunpur. Digvijay was no longer in favour of a settlement. He said that after the panchayat and repeated efforts to reason with them had failed, the two should now live separately. When Digvijay refused, his mother-in-law and Ayush abused him. Ayush and Moni agreed to live together. When Digvijay returned home, he was angry. After reaching home, he did not tell his wife anything. He had not even changed his clothes. Just then, his mother-in-law called again from her home. As soon as he answered, Digvijay hurled an abuse and handed the mobile phone to his wife, Amrita. Amrita went to the tractor parked outside the house and began talking on the phone. Shot himself with his father's licensed rifle Digvijay went inside the house and took out his father's licensed rifle. He shot himself in the head. He fell to the ground covered in blood immediately after being shot. His wife rushed inside and raised the alarm. Local residents and family members took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination on Wednesday. On Tuesday night, former BJP MLA Devmani met the family and consoled them. Neighbours said that Digvijay owned around 18 bighas of land and worked as a farmer. Last year, he took out a loan to buy a tractor for farming. He had now begun preparing to repair the house. He was the family's sole breadwinner A villager said that 10 years ago, Digvijay's father, Lal Pratap Singh, shot himself in the leg to frame another villager. He has been paralysed ever since and remains bedridden. Digvijay was the family's sole breadwinner. Cousin Sonu Singh said that Digvijay had arranged his sister-in-law's wedding in this village. After talks in Alaiya village, a settlement was reached to bring the woman back. After returning home from her in-laws' house, he shot himself. I was in the fields when my nephew called. We took him to hospital, but he died. Lambhua CO Hrithik Kapoor said The body was handed over to the family after the post-mortem. No written complaint has been received from the family so far. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: ‘Nephew died by suicide after Rakhi Sawant called him impotent’:Uncle seeks justice after 16 years; court issues arrest warrant
stories.summary: “We arranged my nephew Laxman’s marriage to Anita in 2010. Around 12 days later, Anita returned to her parents’ home. When we went to bring her back, she refused to return. At the time, actress Rakhi Sawant hosted a show called ‘Rakhi Ka Insaaf’. Some people came to our house and said the show would deliver justice and bring our daughter-in-law back. I took my nephew and the family to the show. Rakhi humiliated us there. “She even called my nephew impotent and incapable of being a man. The whole world watched the show. Hurt by the humiliation, my nephew Laxman died by suicide after consuming poison. Laxman’s mother, Savitri, filed a case against Rakhi Sawant and others. It has been 16 years, but we have still not received justice. Now, the court has issued a warrant against Rakhi, raising our hopes of finally getting justice.” Balveer Ahirwar, from Jhansi, said this while speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. His nephew, Laxman Ahirwar (24), died in Jhansi in 2010. It was alleged that Rakhi Sawant humiliated him on her show by calling him impotent, leading to his death. Sixteen years later, on October 16, the CAW (FTC) court in Jhansi issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Rakhi Sawant, bringing the case back into the spotlight. The next hearing is scheduled for December 1. Read the full story in detail…. Sister lived near her brother’s house Balveer Singh, a resident of Toriya in Hansari, said his sister Savitri lived with her family in Sipri Bazaar. After her husband, Gokul, died, she moved with her children to a rented house near his home. In 2010, his nephew Laxman sold vegetables from a handcart. He married Anita, a resident of Rajgarh, on February 19, 2010. The couple later developed differences over an issue. Around 12 days after the wedding, Anita returned to her parents’ home. When Laxman went to bring her back, she refused to return. During a second attempt, he was allegedly assaulted. Anita had alleged that a relative of her husband had improper intentions towards her. She said she complained to Laxman, but he did not pay attention. She also alleged that Laxman would drink alcohol and assault her. Laxman appeared on the TV show with his wife Laxman’s maternal uncle, Balveer, said, “In 2010, the TV show ‘Rakhi Ka Insaaf’, hosted by actress Rakhi Sawant, was broadcast. A woman from our neighbourhood brought some people associated with the show to our house and asked us to participate. They assured us that we would get justice, receive some money to cover our expenses, and that our daughter-in-law would return home. “We agreed to appear on the show. I went to Mumbai with my nephew Laxman, his mother Savitri, and my wife Pooja. We travelled by train to Delhi and then flew to Mumbai. The show was filmed there. Rakhi Sawant used very offensive language and called my nephew Laxman impotent and incapable of being a man. “After the episode was broadcast on 23 October, 2010, Laxman could not bear the humiliation. He became stressed and eventually consumed poison. When his condition deteriorated, he was admitted to a medical college on 9 November, 2010. He died there the next day, on November 10. We filed a case against Rakhi Sawant, accusing her of abetting his suicide.” Laxman’s mother also died while mourning her son Balveer said, “The case was registered following a complaint by my sister Savitri. We were assured that we would get justice, but Rakhi Sawant obtained a stay from the High Court. We pursued the matter and managed to get the stay lifted. However, she obtained another stay, which remained in force until recently. “About five months ago, my sister Savitri, Laxman’s mother, also died. She would cry for her son and say, ‘My child is gone, but nothing has happened.’ Laxman’s wife Anita has also remarried. “It has been 16 years, but we have still not received justice. On October 16, the Jhansi court issued a non-bailable warrant against Rakhi Sawant. This has renewed our hopes of getting justice. We want nothing but justice. We now have complete faith in the court.” Only one of Savitri’s sons is still alive Balveer said his sister Savitri had three sons: Ramesh, Suresh and Laxman and two daughters, Krishna and Meena. Suresh and Laxman have died. Ramesh now lives with his family in Sipri Bazaar, while both daughters are married. The entire family is now hoping for justice. Rakhi says, ‘I don’t know that young man’ Rakhi Sawant posted a video on social media late on Saturday night and said, “Hello, you must have been hearing the news about me. You probably know who is behind this. If I have to go to jail for the people of this country, so be it. Bharat Mata ki Jai, Jai Bhim, Jai Maharashtra, Vande Mataram. “This is a 2010 case, and I have nothing to do with it. I don’t even know this young man. I don’t even remember him; I have lost my memory. This man had a contract with the channel. After the show ended, he reportedly died in a hospital after developing a fever, and the blame was placed on the channel and us. We have nothing to do with him.” Rakhi says, ‘Is the law only for you?’ Rakhi said, “I support children, students, and Gen Z. I am a celebrity, and someone wants to take advantage of my fame or dig up old cases. They are trying to threaten me with jail. Is the law only for you? Is the law blind? I respect every law and have always stood by the law. I stand with the Jhansi police and the law in Jhansi.” Rakhi Sawant often finds herself embroiled in controversies Rakhi called Kangana a ‘gutter mouth’ Around three months ago, Rakhi Sawant called actress and MP Kangana Ranaut a ‘gutter mouth’. The two exchanged sharp remarks on social media over the comment. In a video at the time, Rakhi said, “You have been given Z-category security, which is why you are saying whatever you want. If you go among ordinary people without security, you will understand their anger. You will no longer get public support.” Kangana responded that she had not targeted an entire generation but had opposed “obscene and immoral behaviour” in public places. She said she did not want children to be sexualised before their time. The controversy began with an Instagram Story posted by Kangana Ranaut, in which she questioned the young women who had participated in a gathering at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. Kangana wrote that some women wanted to imitate independent, career-oriented women but were unwilling to accept the responsibilities that came with that freedom. Rakhi said, ‘My kiss made Mika’s voice melodious’ Around nine months ago, Rakhi Sawant made a remark about singer Mika Singh. During a podcast, she said, “Mika had no voice to speak of before. The day he kissed me, his voice became melodious. Mika bhaji, don’t take offence. You know the truth.” Rakhi added, “Earlier, he used to sing, ‘Saawan mein lag gayi aag, dil mera haaye…’ After he kissed me, it became ‘Hudd dabangg, dabangg, dabangg’. In other words, Mika found his singing voice after kissing Rakhi.” The video of Rakhi Sawant making these remarks has since gone viral. The incident in which Mika Singh allegedly forcibly kissed Rakhi Sawant dates back to 2006. Mika had hosted a birthday party, where he lost his composure and forcibly kissed Rakhi. His sudden act left Rakhi and everyone else present at the party stunned. Rakhi remained quiet at the party but later raised the issue publicly. On June 11, 2006, she filed an FIR against the singer. A case was registered against Mika Singh under Sections 354 and 323 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). After nearly 17 years, the matter was settled amicably by mutual consent.

stories.title: Executioner says no mercy for ‘Blue Drum’ and snake-case killers:‘My hands won’t shake’; demands death warrants and punishment
stories.summary: “Why only the Neelam drum and snake cases? The women accused of killing Ketan, Raja, Atul Panwar, and Talib — Siya, Sonam, Damini, and Ilma, and their lovers, should also be sentenced to death. These people who snatched sons from their mothers must be punished. Whether they are women or men, they are criminals. I would not hesitate or waver while hanging Muskan, Sahil, Ravita, Amardeep, or anyone else. In fact, it would be a matter of pride for me. All I need is for the death warrants to be issued and for them to arrive at my gallows. I will personally hang such ruthless murderers.” Pawan Jallad, the only person in the country who carries out executions by hanging, said this in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar in Meerut. He said the law had done its job by punishing the criminals. Whether they approach the Supreme Court, High Court or the President, they should not be shown any mercy. Read the full interview… Courts and President should not pardon wives convicted of murdering their husbands Pawan Jallad said, “Whether it is Muskan or Ravita, I would consider myself fortunate to hang them. Their lovers destroyed other people’s families by taking their husbands’ lives. They do not deserve to live. “Ravita, Sahil, Muskan, Siya, Sonam, Ilma, Damini, Tushar, or Amardeep, whoever they are, all of them should be sentenced to death. “The law should also award the death penalty to those who have not yet been punished. I want neither the courts nor the President to pardon them. Only then will society receive the message that the relationship between a husband and wife is important. Those who treat marriage as a joke will learn a lesson. They are killing someone’s sons, and only then will such crimes stop. “I would consider myself blessed to hang any of them.” Hanging someone is not for everyone; it takes courage Pawan Jallad says hanging someone is not an easy task. A person may not even be able to kill an ant in their lifetime, but an executioner has to hang a living person. This requires courage and determination. Physical strength alone is not enough; one must also be mentally strong to become an executioner. He says he feels no fear or nervousness when hanging someone.“God has chosen us for this work. The Almighty has sent us into this world to put an end to sinners. “While carrying out an execution, I think only that I am bringing a crime to an end today. Do police officers’ hands tremble during encounters? Do doctors’ hands tremble while conducting postmortems or operations? Then why should our hands tremble?” I feel proud of carrying out executions; we are doing good work Pawan says carrying out executions is good work and that he feels proud of his profession. He does not mind being called an executioner, or his family being associated with the term, because he believes they are doing good work. He considers it a matter of happiness that he gets the opportunity to perform this duty. “Just as the law and judges sentence criminals, and the police protect society by arresting them, we executioners help free society of criminals by hanging them. For me, this is a matter of pride,” he says. Pawan Jallad said that if Muskan and Ravita are executed, they will be hanged in the execution chamber at Mathura Jail, as women are executed there. Sahil and Amardeep, however, could be hanged at Meerut Jail or any other jail in Uttar Pradesh. They will be executed at whichever jail is specified in the death warrant. Pawan is the country’s only executioner; the third generation is carrying on the family profession Pawan Jallad said the work of carrying out executions had been passed down through his family. His grandfather, Kallu Jallad, used to carry out executions. The work was then passed on to Kallu’s son, Mammu Jallad, who later handed it down to the third generation — his son, Pawan. Pawan said he is now teaching his son the techniques of carrying out executions so that he can take over the work after him. Pawan is the only executioner in the country, according to his account. He lives with his family in the Kanshiram Colony in Meerut. His family comprises his wife, one son and five daughters. Pawan said there is another executioner in Lucknow, but he has been unwell since the COVID pandemic. As a result, Pawan is the only active executioner called upon to carry out executions anywhere in India. The execution process takes around 15 minutes Pawan said the entire process of hanging a convict takes around 15 minutes. The prisoner is brought to the execution chamber after the executioner has completed all preparations and checked everything, from the noose to the lever. Before being brought to the gallows, the prisoner is asked if they wish to pray and is allowed to do so. The prisoner is then taken to the platform, where the executioner’s work begins. The executioner covers the prisoner’s face with a cloth. The prisoner is then positioned on the gallows, and the rope is placed around their neck. As soon as the signal bell for the execution rings, the executioner pulls the lever. This tightens the noose and opens the wooden trapdoor beneath the prisoner’s feet, dropping them into a pit around 15 feet deep. The body remains suspended in the pit. According to Pawan, pressure from the noose causes a fracture in the neck, resulting in death. He said the entire process takes around 15 minutes. What happens after a person is hanged? Pawan Jallad explained that after a person is hanged, officials wait for 30 minutes. The waiting period can last around 30–35 minutes to ensure that the convict has died. The executioner then checks whether the person is dead while the body is still hanging from the gallows. A doctor also conducts a check. The executioner then removes the noose from the deceased’s neck and lowers the body from the gallows with the help of prison staff. The executioner signs the execution records, which are also signed by the jail superintendent and magistrate. These signatures certify that the execution has been carried out. A complete record of the execution is maintained. If the deceased’s family requests the body, it is handed over to them for the last rites after the necessary paperwork. If the family does not claim the body, the prison authorities perform the last rites within the jail premises, following the deceased’s religious customs, either by burial or cremation. Pawan Jallad says he earns ₹10,000 a month, urges government to increase salary Pawan Jallad said an executioner in Uttar Pradesh is paid ₹25,000 for each execution. However, executions are very rare. He said he last carried out an execution in 2020, when he hanged the four convicts in the Nirbhaya case at Tihar Jail in Delhi. He said he would now get another opportunity after a long gap. Shabnam from Amroha was also sentenced to death in the intervening period, but she remains in prison. He said it was uncertain whether the four executions in Meerut would take place. “An executioner rarely gets an opportunity to hang someone during his lifetime. Even then, we receive ₹25,000 only when an execution takes place. Otherwise, we get nothing. I receive a monthly salary of ₹10,000, with no additional benefits. How can anyone make ends meet on ₹10,000 a month?” he said.

stories.title: Older faces proved more successful than newcomers in UP:Replacing 40% of MLAs could trigger rebellion; challenge to return to power for third term
stories.summary: The BJP did not repeat any of its sitting Rajya Sabha MPs, replacing all 8 faces. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the party had also denied tickets to 32% of its candidates. To secure a third consecutive victory in 2027 and address public resentment, the BJP is preparing to bet on new faces. There have been repeated indications that the BJP may adopt the pattern followed in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Assam in Uttar Pradesh. In these states, the BJP has returned to power three or more times consecutively. To counter anti-incumbency, it has often dropped a large number of sitting MLAs from its candidate lists. The BJP has indicated that it could deny tickets to 40% of its sitting MLAs this time. Two main reasons are being cited for this: The question is how successful this formula of dropping MLAs to counter anti-incumbency will be in a state like Uttar Pradesh, where caste equations play a major role. Will MLAs rebel after being denied tickets? First, here are 5 indications that a large number of MLAs could lose their tickets 77% of new candidates won, while 85% of sitting candidates secured victories How many MLAs will the BJP deny tickets to in the 2027 Assembly elections? To understand this, it is necessary to examine the Uttar Pradesh BJP's past trends. The BJP strengthened its position in the state during the 2014 Lok Sabha elections. Three years later, in 2017, it formed a full-majority government on its own after a long gap. The party's tally reached 312 MLAs. Before the 2017 Assembly elections, the BJP had 47 MLAs. It denied tickets to 12 of them, or around 25.53%. The remaining 35 were fielded again. The strategy worked. When the results were declared, the BJP won all 12 seats, where it had changed candidates, achieving a 100% success rate on those seats. After 5 years in power, the BJP faced the challenge of forming the government again in 2022. No government in Uttar Pradesh had returned to power consecutively for 37 years. Once again, to avoid public resentment, the BJP denied tickets to 104 sitting MLAs. This accounted for approximately 32%. The party won 80 of those seats again, securing 77% of them. Meanwhile, 175 of the 205 MLAs who were given another opportunity won, a success rate of 85.37%. The remaining 30 MLAs lost. Trend in the last two Lok Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh: Failure to drop candidates cost the BJP seats In the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP won 71 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 seats. In 2019, the party faced the challenge of repeating its previous performance. This time, it dropped 21 sitting MPs and shifted 4 MPs to different constituencies. In other words, the party changed its candidates in around 35% of the seats. This also paid off. Of the 21 seats where new candidates were fielded, the BJP won 14. Of the 4 MPs who were moved to different constituencies, 3 also won. Overall, the BJP won 62 seats in Uttar Pradesh in 2019, a loss of just 9 seats compared with 2014. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP dropped 16 of its 62 sitting MPs. The party won 11 of those seats with new candidates. In addition, it fielded new faces in 4 constituencies it had lost in the previous election. The BJP won 2 of those seats. However, in 2024, the BJP dropped fewer sitting MPs than it had in 2019. The party gave tickets to 46 sitting MPs again, but 26 of them lost. In other words, giving another opportunity to sitting MPs still costs the party seats in several constituencies. The BJP could face a similar challenge in the 2027 Assembly elections, particularly with MLAs who have been winning elections for 10 consecutive years. 2024 Lok Sabha elections: A lesson for the BJP Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi says, “The 2024 Lok Sabha elections could serve as a lesson for the Uttar Pradesh BJP. Even after serving as MPs for 10 consecutive years, most of those who were fielded for a third time lost.'' In the 2024 elections, public resentment was not directed at the BJP as much as it was against local candidates. Despite this, the BJP did not drop candidates in proportion to that resentment. As a result, only 33 of its MPs managed to win in Uttar Pradesh. Of these, 11 seats were constituencies where the party had dropped its candidates and given new faces an opportunity. “The BJP will face the same challenge in the 2027 Assembly elections. At present, 186 BJP MLAs have won two or more terms, while only 69 are first-time MLAs. The party's internal surveys and surveys conducted by other agencies clearly indicate public resentment towards MLAs. At the same time, people are satisfied with the performance of the government and the Chief Minister. If a large number of candidates are not replaced, the BJP could see results similar to those of 2024.” Will MLAs rebel after losing their tickets and damage the party's prospects? According to senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi, the BJP has two types of MLAs in Uttar Pradesh: MLAs associated with the organisation: These leaders have risen through the party organisation and have continued to win elections on the strength of the BJP wave. Many of them did little work during their 5-year terms, claiming that the government did not listen to them. The party is unlikely to suffer significant losses if such MLAs are denied tickets, and major protests are also unlikely. MLAs with strong local influence: These leaders have a solid support base in their constituencies and within local social equations. They remained active among the public and did not hesitate to question their own government when necessary. The party could suffer losses if such MLAs are denied tickets. An example was seen in the MLC elections, when Dr Sanjayan Tripathi joined the Samajwadi Party after being denied a ticket for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers' constituency. Could 30-40% of MLAs lose their tickets? Political analyst Amitabh Tiwari believes the BJP will have to take tough decisions for a third term, given public resentment towards MLAs and the Chief Minister's popularity. If the average rate of ticket cuts of 30-40% in Assam, Haryana, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh is applied to Uttar Pradesh, the number would reach around 102 MLAs. In the 2022 elections, the BJP had also dropped 104 sitting MLAs. Party preparing to appeal to Generation Z According to senior Lucknow journalist Akhilesh Vajpayee, the BJP may give opportunities to a large number of young candidates this time to attract younger voters. This is particularly likely in constituencies the party lost in the previous election. Sources say the party could give tickets to more than 50 new and young faces. In addition, following the examples of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, the BJP could field its defeated Lok Sabha candidates or former MPs in the Assembly elections. Long-serving workers who have remained dedicated to the party organisation may also be given tickets. A trend of replacing MPs and MLAs in states where the BJP returned to power for a third consecutive term According to senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh, states such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Assam and Haryana have now become strongholds of the BJP. The party has been in power continuously in Gujarat since 1998. In Madhya Pradesh, apart from a 13-month Congress government, the BJP has been in power since 2003. stories.title: UP panchayat elections to follow Assembly polls:State government to move SC for stay on High Court order, citing five reasons
stories.summary: Panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh are likely to be held after the Assembly elections, which are proposed between January and March. The Allahabad High Court has ordered that the panchayat elections be held within three months, but holding them just before the Assembly elections appears unlikely. The entire state administrative machinery, police force and resources will be engaged in the panchayat elections. This could affect preparations for the Assembly polls. The village heads’ association, the OBC Commission and the state government are preparing to approach the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the High Court’s order. According to political analysts, it is not just the ruling BJP that wants to postpone the panchayat elections. All opposition parties, including the Samajwadi Party (SP), Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Congress, also favour the delay. What arguments will the BJP present before the Supreme Court? How would holding the panchayat elections first affect the opposition? Read this report to find out… Government to hold high-level meeting after Dussehra According to government sources, following Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s instructions, the Panchayati Raj Department, Law Department and a team of senior lawyers have begun studying the High Court’s ruling. As soon as Dussehra is over, CM Yogi will hold a high-level meeting with ministers and officials from the departments concerned. The meeting will decide how to file a petition in the Supreme Court. According to Parliamentary Affairs Department officials, the Yogi government’s second term was sworn in on March 25, 2022. The first sitting of the 18th Assembly was held on May 23, 2022. Under constitutional provisions, the 19th Assembly must be constituted before May 23, 2027. If the scheduled Assembly election programme is delayed even slightly because of the panchayat elections, the government and the Election Commission will have only two months to complete the entire process. Neither wants to risk a constitutional crisis. Village heads’ association to approach Supreme Court too The village heads’ association will also appeal to the Supreme Court against the Allahabad High Court’s order directing the panchayat elections to be held within three months. The association’s national president, Dr Akhilesh Singh, said time would be needed to implement OBC reservation, correct voter list discrepancies and complete other necessary legal procedures. The government has appointed elected village heads as administrators of their respective panchayats. Therefore, the elections should not be rushed, he said. OBC Commission says report will take time The state OBC Commission is also working on its report. It is examining how many people from the OBC category were elected as village heads, block development council (BDC) members and district panchayat members in previous panchayat elections. It is also assessing areas where OBC communities have received limited political representation. The commission is collecting data on the population of OBC communities at the gram panchayat level and their socio-economic conditions, with assistance from district magistrates and the Panchayati Raj Department. When asked about the report, commission chairman Justice Ramavatar Singh said details about when it would be submitted and what steps would follow could not be made public through the media. He said the commission was carrying out its work honestly and would release the report at the appropriate time. 5 reasons why the panchayat elections may be postponed 1. Assembly election preparations could be affected A large number of employees, police personnel and administrative officers are required to conduct panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh. If the entire government machinery is deployed for these polls, preparations for the Assembly elections could suffer. Work on revising voter lists, preparing polling booths, deploying security forces and arranging EVMs could also be delayed. 2. Discontent among party workers could grow Elections for gram pradhan and BDC posts are not contested on party symbols. However, parties field candidates for block pramukh, district panchayat member and district panchayat chairperson posts. Those denied tickets or defeated in the elections could become disgruntled, and some workers may rebel. Such resentment just before the Assembly elections could create problems for political parties. 3. Panchayat results could influence the political mood Panchayat election results can offer an indication of the political mood in rural areas. If sentiment turns against a party, it could affect the Assembly elections as well. Political debate over victories and defeats in the panchayat polls could intensify, making it risky for parties to hold them just before the Assembly elections. 4. OBC reservation and voter list revisions are pending The OBC Commission has to prepare its report to determine reservation for the panchayat elections. The necessary surveys and data verification are underway. Voter lists also need to be revised. If elections are held before these processes are completed, disputes over reservation or voter lists could arise. If the matter reaches court, the election process could be delayed further. 5. Risk of disputes and violence could increase Panchayat elections are contested at the village level, where personal rivalries and factionalism often come into play. Disputes and violence are possible during the polls. Holding Assembly elections soon after the panchayat polls could therefore create additional law-and-order challenges. Election-related rivalries in villages could also spill over into the Assembly elections. What could the opposition gain or lose if panchayat elections are held first? A poor performance in the panchayat elections could dampen the morale of opposition parties. Leaders and workers could become increasingly disgruntled over denied tickets or local-level victories and defeats, with the effects potentially carrying over to the Assembly elections. Opposition parties would also have less time to strengthen their booth-level organisations because of their involvement in the panchayat polls. If the ruling party performs well, it could project the results as evidence of favourable public sentiment, increasing political pressure on the opposition. However, if rural voters express dissatisfaction with the government, opposition parties could benefit. The panchayat elections would also give political parties an opportunity to assess their rural support base and booth-level strength.

Owaisi asks, ‘What kind of relationship is this?’:Father in BJP, son with Akhilesh; alleges deal to send Nathwani to Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi arrived in Rampur on Sunday. There, he targeted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and the BJP. Owaisi said, "Akhilesh gave his uncle a Rajya Sabha seat. He made Nathwani the other candidate." Nathwani's father, Senior Nathwani, defeated the INDIA alliance candidate in Jharkhand. Now Akhilesh has made Junior Nathwani his candidate. The father is in the BJP, and the son is with you. Tell me, what is this relationship called? Owaisi said, "..." "On the one hand, Nathwani is congratulating the Modi government on completing 25 years, while on the other, whenever we contest elections, we are called the BJP's B-team. Akhilesh, you struck a deal with the BJP and gave its man an SP ticket. They are enemies masquerading as friends-our enemies all along." Owaisi arrived at the Manshab Ali Stadium in Tanda, Rampur, at around 8:45 p.m. on Sunday and addressed a public meeting. Read Owaisi's key statements now 1. Said, "There is not a single phrase against my Hindu brothers in my speeches" Owaisi said, "I have made so many speeches. Point out a single phrase in any one of my speeches where I have said anything against India or any of our Hindu brothers. I have certainly opposed the BJP. I am against the RSS ideology because I have studied it. I have read several books on the RSS. I have spoken to several experts. I know that the RSS's objective is to turn India into a Hindu nation." 2. Muslims will no longer make a Nehru, Gandhi or any Yadav their leader Owaisi said that the Muslim community would now develop its own political leadership. "We will no longer make any Nehru, Gandhi or Yadav our leader. Young men and women will emerge from our ranks. Muslim youth are just as capable as young people from other communities, but they do not get a platform. The Majlis is giving them an opportunity to lead so that they can lead India and secure justice for their community." 3. Abdul will no longer lay mats; he will become an MLA and MP Muslims should not remain confined to laying mats at political programmes. He said, "Abdul will no longer lay mats. Abdul, God willing, will become a leader, an MLA and an MP." Leaders of other parties come to programmes and sit, while Muslim workers remain standing at the back. This situation must now change, and the Muslim community must develop its own leadership. 4. Why Maulana Azad contested elections from Rampur and Gurgaon Owaisi responded to those who questioned his visits to Rampur, Moradabad, Matera, Azamgarh and Saharanpur. Referring to the first Lok Sabha election in 1952, he said that Maulana Abul Kalam Azad had contested the election from Rampur. Jawaharlal Nehru had asked him to go to Rampur because it had a larger Muslim population. In 1957, Maulana Azad contested the election from Gurgaon, whose parliamentary constituency also included Mewat. Owaisi alleged that political parties had never wanted Muslims to develop their own independent political leadership. 5. Said - Akhilesh, Baba, your time has come; our era will come Referring to the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Owaisi said, "As the elections draw closer, your opponents and the enemies of the alliance will become active. There is only a brief lull; the noise will follow. Your time has come. Akhilesh-Baba, your time has come; our era will come." He appealed to AIMIM supporters to work at the booth level instead of merely raising slogans at rallies. He said every worker should bring five people into the party so that it could be strengthened. 6. Prayed for the release of Azam Khan and Tauqeer Raza Owaisi said he wanted Azam Khan's troubles and difficulties to end. He said he had prayed for him. He also prayed for the early release of Maulana Tauqeer Raza Khan, who is lodged in Fatehgarh jail. Referring to Shifa-ur-Rahman, Safoora Zargar, Ishrat Jahan and Sharjeel Imam, Owaisi questioned why opposition leaders did not come out in their support when they were jailed, in the same way they become active in the cases of other leaders. He alleged that opposition leaders do not show the same level of activism when Muslims face such situations. 7. Said- What is the point of forming governments if poverty and injustice have not been eliminated? Owaisi said his fight was not merely to win votes, but to bring development and resolve people's problems. Referring to the 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024 elections, he spoke about the BJP's victories and mentioned the 2027 Assembly election. He questioned what the point was of forming governments if people could not even bring light into their homes, while facing poverty and injustice. Referring to Rampur and Moradabad, he alleged that Muslims and Dalits did not receive adequate facilities. He cited Rampur's literacy rate as 53%, Uttar Pradesh's as 67% and the literacy rate among women in Rampur as 44%. He also claimed that 70% of children in Rampur are affected by anaemia. 8. Said Muslim youths can also become leaders; the next generation must be lifted out of poverty Referring to bidi makers and other poor families in Tanda, Owaisi asked whether they wanted their next generation to continue doing the same work or attend school and college and prosper. Comparing a 21-year-old from Tanda with a young man from Saifai, he said one had education, facilities and his own political leader, while the other had no opportunities to move ahead. He asked whether it was justice if a grandfather and grandson continued doing the same work for generations. Targeting Akhilesh Yadav and the INDIA alliance, Owaisi said, “You do not consider them human beings; you consider them voters. I consider them human beings, my own son, my own brother, my future, and my leader.”

stories.title: Empty chairs at PDA conference:Akhilesh dissolves executive committee; Kannauj district president and all members removed
stories.summary: The entire Samajwadi Party district executive in Kannauj was dissolved after a poor turnout at the party's PDA conference. On Sunday evening, the party's state president, Shyamlal Pal, dissolved the district executive, including district president Kaleem Khan, with immediate effect. All frontal organisations and the state executive were also dissolved. The PDA conference was held on 16 October at the Samajwadi Party's district office in Kannauj in the presence of state president Shyamlal Pal. The number of party workers at the conference was negligible. Most of the chairs at the event remained vacant. Photos and videos showing empty chairs at the conference began to emerge. Questions were then raised about the party programme's preparations and the district organisation's activity. The matter of the conference failing to draw the expected crowd reached the state leadership. Following this, the state president decided to dissolve the district executive. State president Shyam Lala Pal's action is being seen as a major setback for the district organisation. After the entire executive, including district president Kaleem Khan, was dissolved, discussions have now begun over the formation of a new organisation. However, there may be other reasons behind the dissolution besides the low turnout at the conference. In this matter, outgoing state vice-president of the Yuvjan Sabha Haseeb Hasan said that he had been relieved of his post in the organisation. He added that the district's entire executive had also been dissolved. He said that only the party high command would know the reasons behind the action.
