stories.title: Chandrashekhar challenges Yogi to contest from Bijnor:‘I’ll quit politics if I can’t defeat him’; says only someone with a blue scarf can make Gyanesh Kumar resign
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad challenged CM Yogi to contest the election from Bijnor in Amroha. He said: "I contested against him from his seat in Gorakhpur in 2022. I say this publicly: Bijnor district has two reserved seats and six general seats. Let him come and contest from any seat, chest out. If I do not defeat him and send him back, I will quit politics." Taking a jibe at the Opposition's demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, Chandrashekhar Azad said that only the person wearing the blue scarf could get him to resign. Chandrashekhar Azad reached Amroha at around 1:30 pm on Sunday. He addressed a booth-level conference organised in support of Bhim Army candidate Shahnawaz Chaudhary in the Hasanpur Assembly constituency. Chandrashekhar Azad says: Yogi should contest from any seat in Bijnor Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief and MP Chandrashekhar said, "When I contested the 2022 Assembly election, the party appointed me as the in-charge of the Gorakhpur Assembly constituency, from where the Chief Minister contested, to take him on." "I recently saw that this activity is taking place in Uttar Pradesh. People are commenting on one another, saying, 'Come here and contest,' and, 'Come here and contest.' I have told the Chief Minister that I contested against you in your city. If you want to test your popularity, my district Bijnor has eight Assembly seats, two of which are reserved." So, choose whichever of the six seats you want and come contest the election. The Azad Samaj Party will demonstrate its strength. That is why I have invited him to come and prepare to contest from any assembly constituency where he has a sitting MLA. Once he is declared, I will also appeal to the party from that same assembly constituency to send me as its candidate. The Azad Samaj Party will defeat him in Bijnor district and send him back. Chandrashekhar said - Only those wearing blue scarves can force a resignation Protests are being held in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On this, Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad said that he would not be joining the protest this time. He is preparing for Uttar Pradesh. He said, "Only the person wearing a blue scarf can get the resignation secured. Remember my words." "Last time, he did not say anything. His people had worked hard. They got the result. Today, the entire Opposition and the workers are standing together, but has the resignation happened? The king's life is in the parrot. Do not get the king ruined by getting the parrot to resign, understand. Therefore, the votes that have been deleted in the SIR..." Targeting the BJP government over unemployment and ration Chandrashekhar Azad demanded that elections be held using ballot papers instead of EVMs. He said, "Elections should be fair so that the true picture of the people's mandate can emerge." He also questioned the Chief Minister's popularity. He discussed the gap between the survey figures and support on the ground. Chandrashekhar accused the BJP government of failing to provide employment to young people. He said that young people were unable to find jobs and that the poor were being misled by being given five kilograms of ration. He said the government should pay attention to the problems faced by young people and the poor. Akhilesh has also challenged Yogi to contest from Ayodhya On 8 October, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav challenged Chief Minister Yogi to contest the 2027 Assembly election from Ayodhya. While issuing the challenge, Akhilesh said that if the Chief Minister, who makes big claims, was so confident, he should contest the election from Ayodhya himself. CM Yogi accepted Akhilesh's challenge on 10 October. Responding in Balrampur, Yogi said: "Akhilesh ji, you should contest from Ayodhya, and so will I. You file your nomination, and I will file mine. Come, let us test our luck once. Why fight through our followers? We should face each other directly. Let us have a direct contest this time." After Yogi's statement, Akhilesh Yadav hit back on X without naming him. He wrote, "To defeat the donation thieves, a young 'PDA sentry' of ours is enough. Those who give the thieves a clean chit are their accomplices. This time, the public will bring all that arrogance down. Have you forgotten the Lok Sabha?" Owaisi had challenged Yogi to contest from Sambhal AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has also challenged Yogi to contest the election from Sambhal. He said in Azamgarh on 12 October: Baba is telling Akhilesh Yadav, "Come to Ayodhya." Owaisi is telling Baba, "Come to Sambhal." Akhilesh, "Go to Gorakhpur." Majlis (the people) will defeat both.

stories.title: Influencer abuses, threatens Akhilesh again after being released on bail:Says she does not fear police; fifth FIR filed
stories.summary: The reel-making girl from Gonda has again abused Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. After being released on bail, she made a video in which she hurled abuses and issued threats. She claimed that she was not afraid of the police either. After the video surfaced, an SP worker filed a case against the girl at around 5:40 p.m. on Saturday evening. This is the fifth FIR against her. Earlier, on 16 October, the girl had made objectionable comments about Akhilesh. The police arrested her. She was granted bail on 17 October against a personal bond of ₹50,000. Read what the accused girl said... They are hurling abuses again. We were watching to see whether the Kaudiya (Gonda) police or the Colonelganj police-or police from elsewhere-were coming to make the arrest. As for Akhilesh Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav, why should we be afraid? We are not afraid. Let Akhilesh come to Gonda; his ****** Akhilesh Yadav ****** We are now fully supporting MLA Bawan Singh; we will not support Akhilesh Yadav *****. Akhilesh Yadav ****** was hurling abuses, and why would anyone go to get an FIR registered ****** who would go to get one registered saying that his real father's****** SP worker says death threat was issued against Akhilesh Yadav Based on a complaint by SP worker Durgesh Kumar, a case was registered at Kaudiya police station on 17 October under Sections 352, 351(3) and 356(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Durgesh alleged that Pallavi Shukla had used objectionable language against the Yadav community and threatened to kill Akhilesh Yadav if he came to Gonda. Kaudia police station in-charge Shashi Kumar Rana said that the police were investigating the case and efforts were being made to arrest Pallavi Shukla. Could face up to 7-years in prison 1. Section 352 - Intentional insult Meaning: Intentionally insulting a person in a manner that is likely to cause a breach of peace or lead to another offence. Penalty: Up to two years in prison, a fine, or both. 2. Section 351(3) - Threatening to kill or cause grievous harm Meaning: Intimidating a person by threatening to kill them or cause them serious injury. Punishment: Imprisonment of up to 7 years, a fine, or both. 3. Section 356(2) - Defamation Meaning: Making, writing, or publishing a statement that harms a person's reputation and falls under defamation under the law. Punishment: Simple imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine, both, or community service. Family members cut ties with Pallavi Pallavi Shukla is a resident of Baunapur village in the Kaudia police station area. Her Facebook account has more than 42,000 followers. Her father, Panchanan Shukla, is a farmer. She studied up to the intermediate level. Her brother went missing seven years ago and has not been traced since. Her family has distanced itself from her because of her habits. Had also abused MP Chandrashekhar Earlier, on 16 October, a case was registered against Pallavi Shukla on the complaint of Waqar Khan, the Samajwadi Party's Katra Assembly constituency in-charge, for allegedly making indecent remarks against Akhilesh Yadav. The police arrested her the same day and produced her before the court. Later, the Karnailganj SDM granted her bail on a personal bond of ₹50,000. According to complainant Durgesh Kumar, after being granted bail at around 12 p.m. on Saturday, 17 October, Pallavi posted another video on social media. She has been accused of using objectionable language against Akhilesh Yadav and the Yadav community in the video. Samajwadi Party workers and members of the Yadav community are angry over the video. According to the police, a total of five cases have so far been registered against Pallavi Shukla at Gonda Nagar Kotwali and Kaudia police station. Earlier, on 3 July, a case was registered against her at Kaudia police station on the complaint of Sub-Inspector Sheshmani Pandey. The complaint alleged that Pallavi had made offensive remarks against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar and members of the Scheduled Castes. Two other cases have also been registered against her.

stories.title: Husband gets wife married to her lover after 17 years:Arranges garland exchange at Sitapur temple; she had eloped 22 days earlier
stories.summary: A young man sent his wife off with her lover 17 years after their marriage in Sitapu. The paperwork was completed at the tehsil premises beforehand. The husband then took his wife and her lover to a Hanuman temple. There, in front of Hanuman, the wife put a garland around her lover's neck. After this, the lover left for Delhi with the woman and four people who had accompanied him. The incident took place at 5 p.m. on Saturday in the Mishrikh tehsil area. Wife used to make reels, 2 pictures Read the full story... They married in 2009 and have two sons Vipin Bhargava supports his family by working in a private job. He married Rekha Bhargava on 12 March 2009. Rekha studied up to Class 12. The couple has two sons. Their elder son, Shivam Bhargava, is 16 years old, while their younger son, Rohan Bhargava, is 14. Everything was normal in the family. Vipin was living happily with his wife and children. Meanwhile, Rekha developed a fondness for making reels to film songs. She began making reels and posting them on Instagram and Facebook. Gradually, Rekha's interest grew. Returned after 22 days and said she wanted to live with her lover During this period, Rekha became acquainted through Facebook with Rahul Kumar Upadhyay, who lived in Ambedkar Nagar. The two began messaging each other. They then exchanged mobile phone numbers, after which they began having long conversations. Their closeness gradually grew, and they began an affair. It is said that Rahul often started travelling to Mishrikh to meet Rekha. One day, Rekha suddenly went missing from home. Her family searched for her. When they could not find her despite extensive efforts, Vipan lodged a missing-person report at the police station. When Rekha returned home around 22 days later, on the previous Wednesday (14 October), Vipan asked her what had happened. Rekha then told him about her relationship with Rahul. She said that she wanted to live with her lover Rahul. Vipan did not oppose her decision. In accordance with his wife's wishes, he decided to send her to live with her lover. Rahul was then called to Mishrikh. Rahul also told Vipan that he wanted to live with Rekha. Husband says: He has nothing to do with his wife anymore After this, paperwork was completed on Saturday evening at the Mishrikh tehsil complex to solemnise their marriage. Rekha and Rahul then exchanged garlands at a Hanuman temple. Husband Vipin was also present. Vipin said he had nothing to do with his wife Rekha anymore. He was happy with his two sons.

stories.summary: Shardiya Navratri: शारदीय नवरात्रि के पावन अवसर पर उत्तर प्रदेश के विंध्याचल में धार्मिक पर्यटन का विस्तार नई पहचान बना रहा है। मां विंध्यवासिनी, मां काली खोह और मां अष्टभुजा मंदिरों को जोड़ने वाला पारंपरिक ‘विंध्य त्रिकोण’ अब प्रदेश में शक्तिपीठ पर्यटन के प्रमुख केंद्र के रूप में विकसित हो रहा है। वर्ष 2025 में इन तीनों मंदिरों में करीब 1.84 करोड़ श्रद्धालुओं ने दर्शन किए, जबकि वर्ष 2023 में यह संख्या लगभग 1.15 करोड़ थी। इस प्रकार दो वर्षों में दर्शनार्थियों की संख्या में करीब 60 प्रतिशत की वृद्धि दर्ज की गई। श्रद्धालुओं की बढ़ती आमद के बीच प्रदेश सरकार का जोर मंदिरों के आसपास आधारभूत सुविधाओं के विस्तार, संपर्क मार्गों के सुधार और धार्मिक यात्रा को व्यवस्थित बनाने पर है। उद्देश्य विंध्याचल को केवल दर्शन का केंद्र नहीं, बल्कि एक समग्र धार्मिक पर्यटन स्थल के रूप में विकसित करना है।

stories.title: 13-year-old kidnapped and raped in Sitapur:Accused flees after girl loses consciousness, caught after being shot in the leg
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl was taken 30 km from her home and raped in Sitapur. The girl suffers from attacks and is undergoing treatment. On Sunday, police arrested the man accused of the rape after shooting him in the leg. He has been identified as 32-year-old Mulayam Singh, a resident of Barabanki. The girl's condition has been serious since the rape. Doctors have referred her to Lucknow. Doctors in Lucknow said she has been kept under observation for 10 days because of injuries to her private parts. The case concerns the Rampur Mathura police station area, 65 km from the district headquarters. Read the full sequence of events Took her on a bike on the pretext of buying her a toffee The victim's father told Dainik Bhaskar, "At around 4 p.m. on 14 October, I was going with my wife to the fields outside the village to harvest paddy. My daughter also started following us. I told her not to come with us, gave her ₹10 and asked her to return home." As she was returning home, she encountered Mulayam travelling on a bike along the way. He stopped her and asked her name and about our family. He then lured her with the promise of buying her a toffee and made her sit on the bike. He then took her by bike to the Ghaghara river's Thokar embankment near Angraura village, around 30 km from the village. He raped her there. When the girl became unconscious, Mulayam left her there and fled. She told a passer-by what had happened; police took her to her family The father said, "When my daughter regained consciousness, she freed herself and walked 2 km to reach the road. A passer-by found her there. Seeing that she was bleeding, he asked my daughter what had happened. The young man then called Dial-112 and informed the police." The police reached the spot and took my daughter to hospital. She underwent a medical examination there, and the police also informed us. As her condition was serious, doctors referred her to Lucknow. Police traced the accused through CCTV and surveillance Police registered a case and began an investigation following a complaint from the family. On the morning of 15 October (Thursday), the dog squad, SWAT and surveillance teams gathered evidence within a radius of around 2 km of the scene. CCTV footage from a shop in the market of Angraura village showed the girl riding away on a motorcycle with a young man. The police then intensified the search. After nearly 48 hours of searching, the police traced the accused. Mahmudabad Circle Officer Kapoor Kumar said, "The location of the accused, Mulayam Singh, was traced near the Krishnanagar Mod Tiraha in Lucknow on Sunday morning. When the police reached the spot to arrest him, he tried to flee and opened fire. Mulayam was hit by a bullet in the leg during the police's retaliatory action. The police then arrested him." Father said: Daughter has been undergoing treatment for five years The girl's father said, “My daughter used to study in Class 1, but she has been unable to attend school for the past two years. She suffers seizures. She is undergoing treatment.”

stories.title: Rakhi Sawant says she is ready to go to jail:'I said what the channel told me'; man died of shock after she called him ‘impotent’ in Jhansi
stories.summary: A Jhansi court issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Bollywood actress Rakhi Sawant on Saturday. Sixteen years ago, on the show 'Rakhi Ka Insaaf', Sawant humiliated 24-year-old Laxman Prasad Ahirwar, a resident of Jhansi, by calling him impotent. Laxman died after being traumatised by the incident. A case was registered against Sawant following a complaint by his mother. Sawant had not been appearing in court despite being summoned. On the non-bailable warrant, Sawant said, "Even if I have to go to jail, I will. I was only a host; I said whatever the channel told me to say." The next hearing in the case will be held at the CAW (FTC) court on 1 December. Rakhi said: I do not know that boy Rakhi Sawant released a video on social media and said, "Hello, you must all be hearing the news about me. You must know who is behind this, right? If I have to go to jail for the people of the country, I will. Jai Hind, Jai Bhim, Jai Maharashtra, and Vande Mataram. This is a 2010 case, and I have nothing to do with it." "I do not even know this boy. I do not even remember; I have lost my memory. This man had a contract with the channel. After the show ended, that boy died of fever in hospital somewhere, and the blame fell on the channel and us. We have nothing to do with him." Rakhi said, 'Is the law only for you?' Rakhi said, "I support children, students and Gen Z. I am a celebrity, and someone wants to exploit our name and dig up buried corpses. They are trying to threaten me with jail. Is the law only for you? Is the law blind? I respect every law and have always stood by the law. I stand with Jhansi Police and with the law in Jhansi." A quarrel broke out between husband and wife seven months after their marriage DGC Crime officer Mridulkant Shrivastava said that Laxman Ahirwar, who lived in the Toriya neighbourhood of Premnagar, sold vegetables from a handcart. He married Anita, a resident of Rajgarh, on 19 February 2010. About seven months after the wedding, a dispute broke out between the couple. Anita then began living at her parental home. Anita had alleged that one of her husband's relatives had improper intentions. She complained to Laxman about this, but he paid no attention. Anita also alleged that Laxman assaulted her after drinking alcohol. Laxman appeared on a television show with his wife In 2010, the couple's dispute reached the television show 'Rakhi Ka Insaaf'. Laxman travelled to Mumbai with his mother Savitri, maternal aunt Pooja and maternal uncle Balbir. The family travelled by train to Delhi and then flew from there to Mumbai. Laxman's mother, Savitri, had told the police that Rakhi had humiliated her son Laxman during the show and called him impotent. After the programme was broadcast on television on 23 October 2010, her son became afraid even to appear in public. He could not sleep at night and had stopped eating. When his mother asked him, he would say that Rakhi Sawant had ruined his life and that he no longer wanted to live. According to the family, Laxman was admitted to a medical college on 9 November 2010 after his condition deteriorated, where he died on 10 November. Rakhi Sawant is often embroiled in controversies Had called Kangana a "gutter mouth" About three months ago, Rakhi Sawant called actress and MP Kangana Ranaut a gutter mouth. This led to a heated exchange between them on social media. Rakhi had then said in a video, “You have been given Z-category security, so you are saying anything. If you go among the general public without security, you will understand the public's anger. You will no longer have the public's support.” Kangana had replied that she had not targeted an entire generation but had opposed the "obscene and immoral behaviour" seen on the streets. She said she did not want children to be sexualised prematurely. The controversy began with a post on Kangana Ranaut's Instagram Story, in which she questioned the young women who took part in the gathering at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Kangana wrote that some women want to imitate independent, career-oriented women but do not fulfil the responsibilities that come with that freedom. She had said, ‘My kiss made Mika melodious’ Around nine months ago, Rakhi Sawant commented on singer Mika. During a podcast, Rakhi Sawant said, "Mika did not even have a voice in his throat before. The day he kissed me, his voice became melodious. Mika bhaji, don't take it badly; you know the truth." Rakhi Sawant said, "He used to sing, 'Saawan mein lag gayi aag, dil mera haaye...' After kissing me, he started singing, 'Hud dabang... dabang... dabang.' In other words, Mika found his voice after kissing Rakhi." This video of Rakhi Sawant has now gone viral. The incident in which Rakhi Sawant was forcibly kissed dates back to 2006. Mika Singh had hosted a birthday party, where he lost his composure and forcibly kissed Rakhi Sawant. Everyone present at the party, including Rakhi, was shocked by Mika's sudden act. Rakhi remained quiet at the party but later created a ruckus. She had an FIR registered against the singer on 11 June 2006. A case was registered against Mika Singh under Sections 354 and 323 of the IPC. The matter was resolved by mutual agreement around 17 years later. Know About Rakhi Sawant

stories.title: Teacher pulls student's hair, slaps him in Gorakhpur:Father alleges harassment, says teacher threatened him over CCTV footage
stories.summary: Parents in Gorakhpur's Shahpur area have accused a schoolteacher of physically and mentally abusing their three-year-old son on Sunday. They alleged that the teacher slapped the child and scratched his head with her fingernails, leaving marks that are still visible. The parents said they obtained the school's CCTV footage, which allegedly shows the teacher hitting the child. They further claimed that they were threatened when they approached the school principal to ask for the footage. Father files complaint against teacher Atul Singh, a resident of Govind Nagari near HN Singh Chauraha, filed a complaint against the teacher at Shahpur police station on Saturday. Police are investigating the matter. Teacher accused of harassing child for a month Atul Singh said he has two sons. His elder son studies in Class 3 at a school in the city, while his three-year-old younger son was admitted to a nearby school in July. He alleged that the teacher had been physically and mentally harassing his younger son since then. According to Atul, the teacher beats children mercilessly. He said his son starts crying and screaming whenever anyone talks about going to school. Teacher made video call to father Atul Singh said the school made a video call to him four days ago. During the call, he saw that bread had been stuffed into his son's mouth and that the child was crying and trembling. The teacher told him that the child was not eating. Atul then went to the school and brought his son home. My son was very frightened. He told me that the teacher had beaten him. There were also nail marks on his head. After this, we went to the school and checked the CCTV footage, which showed the teacher slapping the child and scratching his head at one point. The parents then met the principal and requested that one month's CCTV footage be retrieved. The principal allegedly became angry and said, "Do whatever you want; you will not get anything from here." The father alleges that the teacher's actions have made the child afraid to go to school and adversely affected his mental health. Nail marks from scratching are also visible on the child's head. They alleged that this behaviour was not limited to their child and was also meted out to other children at the school. They have urged the police to collect the school's CCTV footage as soon as possible, otherwise the evidence could be destroyed later. This is not just about my son; it is a question of the safety of all the children.

stories.title: Model Shraddha Dubey appears before media for first time:Says she did not kill Shiva and saw him jump from fourth floor
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case in Lucknow, appeared before the media for the first time on Sunday. She said, “I did not kill Shiva. All the allegations are baseless. Shiva jumped from the building in front of my eyes.” A short while earlier, police had increased the reward for information on Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 each. All three have been absconding for 9 days. Ten police teams are searching for them. The ACJM-II court in Saharanpur has issued a notice to Shraddha Dubey. A case has been registered at the Cyber Crime Police Station under charges including cheating and violations of the IT Act. Dr Prabhat Verma has filed an application in court seeking the release of the car seized in the case. The court has summoned Shraddha Dubey to appear on October 30, 2026. She continues to evade the police and has also filed an application to surrender before a Lucknow court. Questions have also been raised about her alleged influential political and bureaucratic connections, though these claims have not been confirmed. Read what Shraddha Dubey said 1. All allegations are baseless; CCTV footage will prove my innocence Shraddha said, “All the allegations are baseless. Just because someone claims that we committed the murder does not make it true. We did not kill him. It was a suicide, and I saw with my own eyes that he jumped from the fourth floor of my building. “If the CCTV footage is retrieved, it will clearly prove my innocence. The cameras have not been checked yet. Footage from cameras near the Nepal border was retrieved, but why is there a problem retrieving footage from my building? Once the CCTV footage from my building is retrieved, it will prove that I am innocent because I have done nothing wrong.” Saharanpur court summons Shraddha for October 30 The ACJM-II court in Saharanpur has issued a notice to Shraddha Dubey. A case has been registered at the Cyber Crime Police Station under charges including cheating and violations of the IT Act. Dr Prabhat Verma has filed an application seeking the release of the car seized in the case. Following this, the court has summoned Shraddha Dubey to appear on October 30, 2026. Shraddha released 3 videos while absconding While on the run, Shraddha released three videos in which she narrated the entire sequence of events on the night of the incident. She said, “I have not fled. Shiva died by suicide. I want to tell the truth.” Two videos of Shiva, recorded before his death, have also surfaced. In the videos, a woman is seen threatening him. What the model said in her videos… During her time on the run, model Shraddha Dubey, the accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case, released three videos within 12 hours. In the videos, she claimed she was innocent, denied any conspiracy, and alleged that Shiva was heavily in debt and died by suicide. First video: In a fresh 5-minute-and-18-second video, Shraddha presented her version of events in the Shiva Sharma murder case. She said she and Shiva had not spoken to each other for five to six days before October 7. According to Shraddha, on October 7, Shiva asked her driver to call her from a tea stall at the main intersection in Kapurthala. The two often visited the stall to drink tea. Shiva was crying during the call. Shraddha then called him twice from her own number, but he did not answer. At around 2 am, Shiva called her again. When she asked why he was crying, he asked for her location. After she shared it, Shiva arrived in his BMW to meet her. They spoke, and according to Shraddha, Shiva had been drinking beer. The two then went to a cafe. Shiva took Shraddha's car, while her driver drove Shiva's car. Shiva later accompanied Shraddha to her home. 2. On 8 October, my sister met Shiva for the first time; we went out together My sister came to my house on the morning of 8 October. She has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva well. Her call details will make this clear. We relaxed throughout the day. Everything was fine. We went out together. In the evening, some of Shiva's friends came over, one of whom was named Ashwini Mishra and the other Harsh. If Shiva had been subjected to any kind of torture, his friends would have told the police. There was no such torture. Shiva and I were happy. The truth is that I had known Shiva for only four months. We had been in a relationship for the past two months. His mother said that he lived with me, but the truth is that he would stay with me for 15 days and then disappear for two to four days. When we were not in contact, he had gone to Kedarnath with his sister and brother-in-law. 3. Shiva was in debt of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh and received calls from creditors I have some screenshots that I will share with you. They clearly show that Shiva was in debt of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. Whenever he sat with us, he would start receiving calls from creditors. If his call details are retrieved, everything will be verified. I have sent Shiva's phone to the police. He was so troubled by his debt that he would tell me he might even commit suicide if he could not repay it. At the time, we did not take his words seriously. Just think for yourself-why would a girl kill someone and throw him from her own flat? I request the media not to spread such things. After the incident, I called his mother. I called 112. I called 108. His mother arrived and began assaulting my driver, which must have been recorded on the hospital's cameras. Without knowing anything, she directly accused us of murder. Perhaps we will never be able to escape that blame for the rest of our lives. Now, details of Shiva’s videos… Two videos of Shiva Sharma, recorded before his death, surfaced on Thursday. In the videos, a woman is seen threatening Shiva. She is alleged to be Shraddha Dubey, though the police have not confirmed her identity so far. The woman accuses Shiva of stealing three gold chains and a bracelet and demands that he return around ₹6 lakh. Shiva assures her that he will repay the money. He says, “I am giving it to you in writing that I will return the money. Keep my car and give me the money.” Shiva Sharma’s mother appeals to CM Yogi for justice Ranjana Sharma, the mother of Shiva Sharma, who died in the Lucknow murder case, has submitted a petition to CM Yogi Adityanath seeking a fair and high-level investigation. In her petition, she has made 7 demands, including an investigation into the roles of Shraddha Dubey, Rashmi Dubey and others; preservation of CCTV footage and digital evidence; and an inquiry under the supervision of senior officers. She has also sought action against anyone found negligent or involved in tampering with evidence, security for her family, and regular updates on the investigation. She has further urged the authorities to take strict legal action against all accused based on the available evidence. Now read the full story...

stories.title: 5 funeral biers carried together in Noida:Last rites performed late at night; dispute over 10 bighas of land, two sisters, brother-in-law arrested
stories.summary: Following the deaths of Mahesh (37), his wife Lalita (35), their sons Laddu (11) and Sakshat (3), and daughter Mishti (7), the bodies of all five were cremated at midnight in Nagla Shripadam village in Rabupura, Noida. The sight of five funeral biers from the same family being carried together left everyone in the village grief-stricken. Around 400 to 500 people attended the cremation. More than 100 police personnel from five police stations were present. Meanwhile, based on a complaint filed by Akash, brother of deceased Lalita, an FIR was registered at Rabupura police station against three people, including two sisters and one brother-in-law. Police arrested all three on charges of abetting suicide. DIG Rajeev Narayan Mishra said the preliminary investigation indicated a case of food poisoning. The situation will become clear after the post-mortem report is received. Police are investigating every angle. See two pictures... Questions over 10 bighas of land and compensation Mahesh's father, Kishanlal, worked for the Railways. Around 20 years ago, he moved from Kherakala village in Delhi to Nangla Padam with his wife, Chandrawati. Between 2000 and 2005, Kishanlal bought around 10 bighas of land in Nangla Padam Singh village in Chandrawati's name. It has been claimed that in 2009, compensation of around ₹1.25 crore was received from the Yamuna Authority in exchange for the land. Villagers claim that Kishanlal gave the compensation money to his three daughters. Kishanlal died in 2023. After this, Mahesh's mother, Chandrawati, transferred the ancestral house in Delhi to her daughters' names. It is alleged that on 18 August 2025, the 167-square-metre house was also sold to one of the daughters. Mahesh lived in this house with his wife and children. House transferred to younger daughter's name six months ago According to villagers, around six months ago Chandrawati transferred the ancestral house in the village to her younger daughter. It is being reported that Mahesh learnt about this a few days ago. There has since been talk of rising tensions between the mother and son. Mahesh supported his family by doing manual labour. His financial condition was not good. In such circumstances, the dispute over the land and house had become a crucial issue linked to the family's future. However, it is yet to be confirmed under which document the house was transferred to the younger daughter's name and how the property was actually divided. What is the link between the property dispute and the deaths? Several questions have been raised following the deaths of five family members. Was Mahesh not receiving a share of the ancestral property? Had tensions within the family increased over the transfer of the land and house titles? Is there any connection between the property dispute and the deaths of all five people? The answers to these questions have not yet emerged. Police questioning sisters-in-law and brother-in-law Rabupura police station Inspector-in-Charge Shyam Babu Shukla said Akash, the brother of the deceased Lalita, had filed a written complaint regarding the incident in Nagla Shri Padam. Based on the complaint, a case has been registered against three people, including sisters-in-law Sunita and Sapna and one brother-in-law. All three have been arrested for allegedly abetting suicide. Family ate noodles after returning from fair On Friday night, 16 October, Mahesh went with his wife and children to the Ramlila and Kali fair being held at the Rabupura grain market. The family returned home at around 10 to 10.30 p.m. Everyone then ate Maggi and went to sleep. At around 8 a.m. on Saturday, a friend of Mahesh's elder son Laddu arrived to call him to school. When there was no response for quite some time, the discovery was made that five people had died in the house. The incident triggered panic in the village. Audio found on Mahesh's mobile phone, acquaintances blamed for deaths During the investigation, police recovered Mahesh's mobile phone, in which an audio recording is reportedly believed to have been found. It is being discussed that in the audio, Mahesh blamed some acquaintances for the deaths of himself and his family. Police have taken the mobile phone into custody and begun a technical and forensic examination of the audio. Police are investigating the case from these three angles

stories.title: Elephant runs amok during Ramlila in Varanasi:Picks up and throws mahout; runs through streets, causing panic
stories.summary: An elephant suddenly went berserk during a Ramlila performance at Panchvati Maidan in Ramnagar, Varanasi, on Sunday. It threw its mahout to the ground, seriously injuring him. The injured mahout has been admitted to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, where his condition remains critical. The incident triggered chaos at the Ramlila venue and panic among the people. After receiving the information, police reached the spot and, as a security measure, barricaded Panchvati Maidan and the surrounding area, restricting people's movement. Police instructed devotees who had come to watch the Ramlila and local residents to stay away from the site. See 4 pictures... Elephant had been brought from Azamgarh The elephant that went berserk is reported to have been brought from Azamgarh to take part in the Ramleela. The son of Dr Anant Narayan Singh of the Kashi Raj family watches the Ramleela while riding this elephant. The sudden loss of control over the elephant on Sunday triggered panic among those present at the venue. After throwing down its mahout, controlling the elephant became a challenge. Efforts under way to control elephant Efforts to control the elephant began after the incident. However, the elephant had still not been brought under control by the time of writing. Police tightened security arrangements amid fears that another person could be injured. People were stopped from entering the affected area and urged to maintain a safe distance.

stories.title: UP to remain dry for next 7-days after rains stop:Lucknow residents struggle with mud and stench; paddy fields waterlogged in Sitapur
stories.summary: Rainfall has stopped across Uttar Pradesh after the impact of the western disturbance weakened. The weather remained clear across the state on Saturday, and the Meteorological Department has forecast dry conditions for the next week. Day temperatures may rise slightly during this period, while night temperatures are expected to drop by 2–3 degrees Celsius. No district in the state was issued a rain alert on Saturday. However, the impact of flooding continues in several districts. In Lucknow, residents of affected areas are struggling with mud, garbage and foul smells even as the water level of the Gomti river recedes. In Sitapur, waterlogged fields have raised concerns over damage to paddy crops. Meanwhile, a nearly 20-year-old, three-storey ashram located in the middle of the Ganga collapsed in Jhunsi, Prayagraj. Three people were reportedly trapped under the debris. Two have been rescued, while a search is underway for the third. No rain expected in UP for the next 7 days According to the Meteorological Department, rainfall activity has stopped after the western disturbance weakened. Dry weather is likely across the state for the next week. Sunshine during the day may lead to a slight rise in maximum temperatures, while minimum temperatures could fall by 2–3 degrees Celsius. Residents may feel a slight chill during the mornings and at night. Receding water leaves mud and foul smell in Lucknow As the Gomti river’s water level falls, floodwater is beginning to recede from affected areas of Lucknow. However, residents continue to face difficulties, with mud accumulating in colonies and lanes. Garbage piles and foul smells have added to their problems. With the floodwater receding, cleaning up affected areas and preventing infections have become major challenges. Reports of rising cases of vomiting, diarrhoea and viral fever have added to health concerns. The detection of 16 new dengue cases has also raised concerns over the health situation in the city.

stories.title: DPS student dies after falling from 5th floor in Vrindavan:Father posted with CISF; mother was staying with her uncle after a dispute
stories.summary: In Mathura, a class 9 student at DPS School died by jumping from the fifth floor of a posh housing society. Police arrived after receiving information from society residents and are investigating. The police are examining all possibilities, including an accident and suicide. At around 3 p.m. on Saturday, the student arrived at the home of his maternal uncle, Saurabh, in Sunrakh village with his mother, Neetu Gautam, and elder sister. After staying there for a while, he left the house for a walk. He reached the Hare Krishna Orchid Society at 7 p.m. and jumped from the fifth floor. When he did not return for a long time, his family began to worry. During the search, they were informed that Raj had fallen from the Hare Krishna Orchid apartment, located a short distance from the house. Raj was from Rajasthan The deceased has been identified as 16-year-old Raj Gautam, a resident of Januthar village in Rajasthan. He was studying in Class nine at DPS School, Refinery Nagar, Mathura. His maternal uncle, Saurabh Gautam, said, "Raj's father, Yogesh Gautam, is posted as a driver at the CISF Unit IOC in Mathura." He said Raj's mother had quarrelled with his father in the morning before coming to their house with her two children. According to Saurabh Gautam, Raj was mentally distressed. When they learnt about the incident, his maternal uncle, mother, sister and other relatives reached the hospital, where they were inconsolable. According to local residents, the teenager fell from the fifth floor of the society's 11-storey building. However, how this happened will be confirmed only after the police investigation. Police examining CCTV footage As soon as they received the information, Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh and Inspector Ashwani Kumar reached the spot. A forensic team was also called in, and evidence was collected from the scene. The police are examining footage from the CCTV cameras installed in the society to find out how Raj reached the fifth floor of the building and what happened to him. Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said: Raj Gautam was found dead at Harekrishna Orchid Apartment. Police are reviewing CCTV camera footage. They clarified that the cause of Raj's death has not yet been established. Police have not received any written complaint in the case so far. Questions raised over society's security Questions are also being raised about the society's security arrangements after the incident. It is being reported that Raj did not have any acquaintances living in the society. The matter of how he entered the premises and reached the building's fifth floor is being investigated. Police are also investigating whether the security guards stationed at the society's entrance noticed the teenager entering or leaving.

There is not the slightest truth in this. Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the BSP under any circumstances or at any cost.' He will stay at the central office in Delhi and handle election-related and paperwork duties. Mayawati appointed Aakash the party's national convener on 5 October. Exactly 31 days earlier, on 3 September, she had removed him from the post, saying that Aakash needed to become more mature. Mayawati has removed Aakash from the post three times so far. stories.title: Three friends die as Thar crashes into divider:They were travelling from Agra to Mussoorie; driver dozes off at the wheel
stories.summary: Thar SUV crashed into a divider in Saharanpur at 4 am on Sunday, killing three friends and injuring two others. All five friends were travelling from Agra to Mussoorie to celebrate Dussehra. The impact was so severe that the front of the SUV was badly crushed. Sahil Tiwari (25), Rahul Singh (25) and Saksham Gautam (22) died in the accident. Sachin and Hemant Verma, who are cousins, were seriously injured and have been admitted to Saharanpur District Hospital. The accident took place near Belda roundabout in the Nagal police station area. Rahul and Saksham’s fathers reached the post-mortem centre. They broke down in tears upon seeing their sons’ bodies. Sahil was the only son in his family. His parents, who live in Delhi, have left for Saharanpur. See some pictures… SUV overturns after hitting divider; two people fall off bridge Eyewitnesses said the Thar was travelling at high speed near Belda roundabout at around 4 am on Sunday when they suddenly heard a loud crash. When they reached the spot, they found the SUV overturned, with broken glass scattered across the road. The damage to the front of the vehicle suggested that it had first hit the divider before overturning. Two occupants of the Thar had fallen beneath the bridge. The police were immediately informed. Officers broke open the doors to rescue those trapped inside. Some people climbed down from the bridge and helped bring the two injured men back up. They were rushed to the district hospital by ambulance, where doctors declared three people dead. Injured friend says, ‘When I opened my eyes, I found myself lying on the road’ Sachin, who was injured in the accident, said Rahul worked as a compounder at a private hospital, while Saksham was an area manager at Sun Pharma Classic. Sachin works in Noida and had returned home for the Dussehra holidays. The five friends had left Agra at 9 pm on Saturday. Sachin’s cousin, Hemant, was driving the car. Sachin said he was asleep when the accident happened. He did not know how the car suddenly went out of control and hit the divider. “When I opened my eyes, I found myself lying on the road. Later, I learnt that the SUV had met with an accident,” he said. In Agra, Sahil lived in Shanti Nagar, Saksham in Kamla Nagar, and Rahul Kumar in Tehri Baghia. Rahul’s father says in tears, ‘I had told him not to go, but he went anyway’ Rahul’s father, Gopal Singh, said his son left home with the car at around 3 pm on Saturday. When he called Rahul at 8 pm, his son said he was on his way home. A little later, Rahul called back and said he was going out for a trip. His father asked him to return home, but he refused to listen. At around 5 am on Sunday, the family learnt about the accident. Their nephew, who lives in Kamla Nagar, called and informed them that Rahul had met with an accident and had been admitted to hospital. Gopal Singh said Rahul was one of five siblings. The news of his death has left the entire family devastated. Saksham’s father says, ‘We thought he had been injured’ Saksham’s father, Rajendra Gautam, said Saksham was the elder of his two sons. When he returned home from work on Saturday, Saksham told him that he had been granted three days’ leave and was going to Mussoorie. He left with his friends at around 7 pm. In the morning, the police called and informed the family that his son had been admitted to hospital. They thought he had sustained injuries and would recover after treatment. However, when they reached the hospital, they were informed of his death. The family is devastated and inconsolable. Police say cause of accident will be investigated SP Traffic Shailendra Srivastava said the police received information about a Thar SUV accident in the Nagal police station area and immediately reached the spot. Preliminary information suggests that overspeeding caused the accident. However, the exact reason why the vehicle went out of control will be known only after an investigation.

stories.title: Drunk driver runs over 7 in Balrampur:3 killed outside Durga pandal, caught after 15-km chase
stories.summary: A car ran over seven people standing outside a Durga pandal in Balrampur, killing three and seriously injuring four others. The accident took place at around 11 pm on Saturday, when people were watching a programme on a projector inside a tent set up beside the pandal. Suddenly, a speeding Ford car (UP 32 K 2425) rammed into the tent, ran over seven people and crashed into a wall. The impact was so severe that it sounded like an explosion. Some people were thrown 5–6 feet away. Screams filled the area. Police reached the spot and rushed the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Pateshwari Prasad (42), Manoj Singh (51) and Ganesh Pandey (45) dead on arrival. The four injured were referred to a higher medical centre in Bahraich for treatment. After the accident, the driver fled the spot with the car. The incident took place in Belha Gram Panchayat, under the Kotwali Dehat police station area, around 10 km from the district headquarters. Accident caused by darkness and speed: CO CO Abhishek Singh said some people were holding a programme by the roadside in Charangahi Belha village. Videos were being shown on a screen using a projector when a car passed through the area. According to the officer, darkness caused the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The car ran over seven people before the driver fled. Police launched a search operation, sealed the borders and set up barricades. The driver was caught along with the car within an hour. He is being questioned. Villagers watch devotional films every night during Navratri Eyewitnesses said films are screened near the temple every year during Navratri. Villagers gather to watch films related to Durga Puja, along with bhajans and religious discourses. On Saturday night, a Ford car coming from the Gaura Road side went out of control and ran over the people gathered there. All victims belonged to the same village According to police, all those attending the programme were residents of Charangahi Belha village. The injured include Chhedi Ram (50), Ghop Ram (31), W (37) and Mukesh Tiwari (30). All four are undergoing treatment in Bahraich. Preliminary investigations suggest that the driver may have been under the influence of alcohol.

The method used to plot the murder was inspired by Ravita's snake murder case. In both cases, the husbands were reported to have died after being bitten by snakes. Ravita murdered her husband, Amit, by having him bitten by a non-venomous snake and was caught. Learning from this, Damini had her husband, Atul, bitten by a genuinely venomous snake. However, the story changed after Damini grew closer to Tushar, the school's van driver. Damini and Tushar plotted to eliminate Atul and planned to make his death appear to have been caused by a snakebite. stories.title: Children skipping school due to leopard scare:People keeping vigil all night in Lakhimpur; leopard had carried away 2 kids from homes
stories.summary: As evening falls, doors to homes begin to close. There is silence on the paths leading to the fields. Many of the children who used to carry schoolbags are confined to their homes. Parents fear that a leopard will emerge from the fields and attack them while they are travelling to or from school. Attendance at schools has fallen by up to 42%. These are the conditions in more than 20 villages in Lakhimpur, where two children have died in leopard attacks over the past 48 hours. People are staying awake all night to keep watch. They are going to the fields in groups, carrying sticks. If children go to school, they travel in groups, making noise. Protective trenches have been dug along the routes leading from the forest to the villages. The Dainik Bhaskar team reached the villages in the North Nighasan Forest Range, around 75 kilometres from the district headquarters. It visited schools, fields and homes and spoke to local people. The Forest Department has captured 17 leopards in 10 months, but the terror has not subsided. People are afraid of who the next victim will be. Read the full report... 2 innocent children killed in two days On 12 October, a leopard carried seven-year-old Sanya away from the courtyard of her home in Bhojhia village, under the Dhaurahra Forest Range. Her half-eaten body was found the next day. Then, on the evening of 14 October, the leopard carried away six-year-old Manjot Singh, who was playing outside his home at Topper Farm in the North Nighasan Forest Range. His half-eaten body was found in the forest after a two-and-a-half-hour search. Father Joga Singh said that three days had passed since his son's death, but the leopard had still not been captured. He had received neither compensation nor a boundary wall had been built around the house for protection. The family feared that another child might also fall victim to the leopard. Father says-daughter was picked up right before his eyes Sanya's father, Sampat Giri, said, The leopard came from the direction of the fields. It pounced on my daughter and grabbed her from the courtyard right before my eyes. I ran after it, but the leopard fled into the fields with the child. We searched throughout the night, but could not save her. Sampat's neighbour Radhika said, I was sitting outside. The leopard carried the girl away right in front of me. Four of us ran after it, but it was of no use. The next day, only the girl's torso, legs and a small part of her head were found; the leopard had eaten the rest of her body. Radhika has been traumatised since the incident. She starts crying while speaking. Emerging from the forest and reaching areas near human habitation Tigers and leopards are emerging from the forests of Dudhwa Tiger Reserve and reaching areas close to human settlements. They are present in sugarcane fields around villages bordering the forest. Seven people have been killed in leopard and tiger attacks in the Nighasan tehsil area since January. The Forest Department has captured 17 leopards by placing cages in different villages over the past 10 months. Despite this, the attacks have not stopped. The situation is such that farmers are afraid to go into the fields. People are sitting outside their homes with sticks to guard their children. Trenches have been dug along roads outside the village. The leopard attacks are having the worst impact on children whose schools are near the forest and sugarcane fields. When we spoke to teachers at the school, we learnt that parents were reluctant to send their children to school. Only 59 of 102 children attended school in Aili The situation at Aili Primary School appeared even more worrying. Principal Yogesh Pandey said, "A total of 102 children are registered at the school, but only 59 attended. This means around 42% of the children were absent." According to the teachers, parents are keeping their children at home because of the fear of the leopard. Naubana principal says, ‘There is fear, but we have to do our duty’ Talewar Singh, principal of the composite school in Naubana village, said, A total of 103 children are registered at the school. Only 71 of them attended school. Children are children, but we ourselves have to travel through sugarcane fields and forest paths to reach the school. We are afraid, wondering when a leopard might attack. But we have to do our duty, and it is also important to teach the children. Only 250 of 400 children attended in Bathua DS Rana, principal of Bathua Primary School adjoining the forest, said more than 400 children study at his school. However, only 250 children are attending. Several children from the neighbouring village of Pradhan Purwa are not coming to school at all. He said the children and teachers here have encountered tigers and leopards several times while travelling to and from the school. It was very frightening initially, but teaching is a compulsion. The Forest Department had installed wire fencing in front of the school for the children's safety. Elephants have broken it in several places. Now, because of the damaged fencing, the security arrangements have collapsed. 172 of 207 children attend school in Mathia Avadhesh Kumar, a teacher at Composite School Mathahia, said that a total of 207 children study at the school. Only 172 of them are attending. The children and teachers have to pass by the sugarcane fields to travel to and from school. There is always a risk of an attack there. Despite this, the teachers are taking the risk and reaching the school to fulfil their responsibilities. Meanwhile, Sudhir, the principal of the Composite School in Naurangabad village, said that the school has a total of 357 children. Fewer children are attending because of the fear of the leopard. Attendance falls at Faradhiya school with 359 children Balwinder Singh, the principal of Composite School Faradhiya, said that a total of 359 children study at the school. Attendance has declined by around 4% because of the fear of the leopard. Villagers are keeping watch through the night The ordeal of Gurnam Singh's family, who live near Bathua village, is hair-raising. He said a leopard entered their house last night and attacked their pet dog. It fled towards the sugarcane field when they raised an alarm. Gurnam also showed the leopard's paw prints. His wife, Gurpreet Kaur, said she stayed awake throughout the night to guard the children. There is a sugarcane field right next to their house, from where the sounds of the leopard can be heard throughout the night. They are so frightened that they cannot sleep. Family members now keep watch over the children during the day as well, carrying sticks and clubs. The leopard is also attacking animals Baljeet Kaur said the leopard entered her house at night and attacked the buffalo. It fled when she raised the alarm. Her husband goes to the fields, leaving her alone at home with her daughters. She is therefore now afraid that the leopard may enter during the day as well. Guarding the fields is unavoidable, threatening livelihoods Farmer Jai Kumar, who was guarding his field, said the wire fencing installed around the forest is broken at several places. As a result, wild animals are destroying the crops. It is very frightening to venture outside, but we have no choice. Farming is the only means of feeding ourselves and our children. If we do not guard the fields, the family will be pushed to the brink of starvation. Elephants, monkeys and other wild animals were already damaging the crops. Now, fear of the leopard has put both their lives and livelihoods at risk. Children go to school in groups We met a group of children returning home from school. The children said they used to walk home alone, but now, fearing leopards, they travel to and from school only in groups. We make loud noises along the way so that if a wild animal is hiding nearby, it will move away. If we do not go to school, we will fall behind in our studies. That is why we have to take the risk. 17 leopards caught in 10 months, yet attacks continue Seventeen leopards have been caught in the North Nighasan Forest Range over the past 10 months, a record in the state. Although this may be a major achievement on paper, villagers are not satisfied. People are demanding that the leopard responsible for the attacks be caught immediately. The wire fencing damaged by elephants should be repaired immediately. The Forest Department should arrange patrols along school routes and in populated areas. Lighting and solar lights should be installed around mud houses. The affected families should be given compensation. Ranger Bhupendra Singh said... Two cages have been installed at Topar Farm and eight cages at sensitive locations. The Forest Department team is patrolling at night. People are being warned through loudspeakers to remain alert. A safety trench is being dug with a JCB near the forest. The family of the deceased child will be given compensation of ₹5 lakh.
