stories.title: ‘Trouble with EC today, PM may not please them tomorrow’:BJYM state president Rohit Mishra says youth need not become anyone’s tool
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) state president Rohit Mishra has described the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) as anti-national, saying its members, who currently oppose the Election Commission, may tomorrow turn against another ministry, the people of the country or even the Prime Minister. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Rohit said, “Every protest and movement has its limits. We will not allow India to become Nepal or Bangladesh.” He also spoke about the 2027 Assembly elections, allegations of donation theft at the Ram Temple and accusations against him over his disability certificate. Read the full interview… Question: Is the Yuva Morcha worried about the CJP's protests? Rohit: There is no question of being worried. In a democracy, both protest and dialogue are welcome, but they should not be part of sponsored politics. CJP is using the energy of young people to pursue its political agenda. Meanwhile, the BJP Yuva Morcha is working to connect young people with opportunities. Far more young people stand with the government's transparent recruitment processes and self-employment policies than those who have been mobilised for protests by spreading confusion. Young people should not become anyone's 'political pawns'. They should use their energy to build their future and contribute to nation-building. The Yuva Morcha has never shied away from issues, and it never will. Question: What will your stand be if CJP holds protests in Uttar Pradesh? Rohit: If any organisation raises genuine issues concerning young people, we are always ready to engage in dialogue. However, any attempt to disturb the atmosphere in the name of protests will not be tolerated. We are ready to listen to the demands of young people, but we will not allow anyone to exploit them for political gain. Question: What would you say about BJP leaders' statements on employment? Rohit: We talk about both 'weapons and scriptures'. Weapons are for defence, while scriptures are for earning a livelihood. Government jobs are not the only means of employment. There are several avenues, including Atmanirbhar Bharat, Startup India and the Chief Minister's Self-Employment Scheme. No job is small or big. Young people should take the initiative. Question: Why are terms such as 'tukde-tukde gang' and 'mental Naxals' used? Rohit: These are people who want to mislead young people and break up the country. Slogans and ideas give direction to young people. Therefore, it is extremely important to identify those who hold anti-national views. Question: Did you submit a fake disability certificate showing 50% disability to secure admission to a PhD programme? Rohit: On 20 January 2003, I suffered multiple fractures in my thigh bone in a road accident. I underwent surgery on 23 January and remained bedridden for months. A medical board comprising 14 doctors and the Indian Medical Association (IMA) issued the certificate after an examination. I used this certificate only when seeking admission to a PhD programme. Qualifying for NET is entirely merit-based. I did not obtain any unfair benefit through the certificate. I still have a rod implanted in my leg. Question: How much representation will Dalits and backward communities receive in the Yuva Morcha's new team? Rohit: In our team, the only identity will be 'young people', not caste. However, when it comes to representation, every section of society will be given its due place. Question: What issues will dominate the 2027 elections, and how will you respond to the Samajwadi Party's allegations? Rohit: The very name of the Samajwadi Party frightens people. It reminds them of the period from 2012 to 2017. At that time, the state witnessed riots every third day, law and order had collapsed, and women and girls were unsafe. They keep changing the definition of PDA, but the public understands everything. Question: Akhilesh has challenged Chief Minister Yogi to contest the election from Ayodhya. What is your response? Rohit: The Chief Minister does not go anywhere just because someone invites him. Those who are disguising themselves by adopting religious symbols are trying to mislead Hindus. As for the allegations of donation theft in Ayodhya, we took strict action against those responsible and sent them to jail. The law is taking its course in this matter. No guilty person will be spared.

stories.title: Lucknow flooded after just a 1-foot rise in water:Gomti stayed well below danger mark, so how did flooding occur?
stories.summary: The water level of the Gomti River in Lucknow is gradually receding. However, several areas remain submerged in waist-deep water. This is happening even though the river has not come close to the danger mark. According to the Irrigation Department, on 27 September, the Gomti's water level in Lucknow rose around 1 foot (42 centimetres) above its normal level of 105.7 metres. Several areas began flooding after this. The situation became so serious that all 10 gates of the Gomti Barrage had to be opened. On 3 October, the river's water level briefly reached 108.14 metres. This was the highest level recorded during the recent floods, but the river was still around 1.5 metres below the danger mark. By 15 October, the Gomti's level had fallen by another 1.5 metres, yet flooding continued. The surprising question is, if the Gomti never reached the danger mark, how did Lucknow flood? Today, we will decode this in UP Explainer… There is not a single dam on the Gomti River. Therefore, its water cannot be stored in a reservoir and controlled. There are four reasons why the river has no dam… 1. Dams require locations between mountains or high valleys, where a deep reservoir can be created to store water. However, the Gomti does not originate in the mountains. It emerges from the ground at Gomati Taal. There are no mountains or deep gorges along its route to the Ganga. Therefore, there is no natural location where a dam wall could be built. 2. Rivers flowing down from mountains descend rapidly. Dams are built on such rivers to generate electricity using their powerful flow. The Gomti, on the other hand, flows through a completely flat plain. As a result, its current is very slow. Without sufficient water flow, generating electricity by building a dam is also not feasible. 3. Dams work well where water flow remains relatively consistent throughout the year. The Gomti, however, depends entirely on groundwater sources and monsoon rainfall. Its water level falls considerably during summer. Wastewater and drains from cities along its banks flow into the river. If a dam were built to block its already slow flow, the river would turn into a stagnant, polluted pond. 4. Suppose a dam were forcibly built on the Gomti. What would happen? Since there are no surrounding mountains, stopping the water would cause it to spread towards villages and cities along the riverbanks, submerging those areas. These are the reasons why there is no dam on the Gomti. So, is Lucknow's ‘Gomti Barrage’ not a dam? No. A barrage is quite different from a dam. Instead of creating a reservoir, small gates are installed across the river. These gates raise the water level slightly so that water can be supplied to the city. The Gomti Barrage serves the same purpose. The river's water level here is maintained at 105.7 metres, which is the Gomti's normal level in Lucknow.

stories.title: Meerut snake case verdict mentions Damini, Ilma, Sonam-Siya:Judge warns others may follow Ravita’s example, using venomous snakes or pushing husbands off hills
stories.summary: Meerut’s snake murder case saw Ravita and her lover Amardeep sentenced to death two days ago. In his judgment, the judge referred not only to their case but also to several similar incidents across the country in which wives allegedly plotted their husbands’ murders because of extramarital relationships. The judgment mentioned the case of Damini from Hastinapur in Meerut, who allegedly learnt from Ravita’s case and used a venomous snake to kill her husband. While Ravita had used a non-venomous rat snake to make her husband’s death appear to be a snakebite, Damini allegedly arranged for a venomous common krait to bite her husband. The judge observed that such incidents had created fear among young people about marriage. The court also referred to the case of Ilma from Lohianagar in Meerut, who allegedly strangled her husband, Talib, with the help of her lover. Other cases included the murder of Indore businessman Raja Raghuvanshi, in which his wife, Sonam, allegedly conspired with her lover, and the Pune case in which Siya allegedly plotted the murder of her fiancé, Ketan, with her boyfriend. While sentencing Ravita and Amardeep to death, the judge said these incidents highlighted the seriousness of such crimes and that showing leniency in punishment would not serve the ends of justice. What similarities did the court identify in these cases? Here is a detailed account. 1. Damini-Atul case: Husband drugged and bitten by venomous snake In Hastinapur, Meerut, Damini allegedly plotted the murder of her husband, Atul Pawar (32), a school owner, with her lover Tushar and two snake charmers. On the night of 16 July 2026, Atul was given sleeping pills mixed with milk. After he became unconscious, Tushar, who worked as a school van driver, reached Atul’s house with the two snake charmers at 5 am on 17 July. Damini, Tushar and the snake charmers allegedly released a common krait, one of the world’s most venomous snakes, on Atul’s bed. The snake had reportedly been kept hungry for 10 days. Atul died after being bitten. Damini then raised an alarm and called family members, allegedly attempting to make the death appear to be a natural consequence of a snakebite. According to the police, she had arranged the venomous snake to make the murder look like an accident and avoid suspicion. She was seen crying beside Atul’s body that morning. However, Atul’s family suspected foul play and questioned whether he had been murdered, as in Ravita’s case. They lodged a police complaint and raised suspicion about Damini. During the investigation, call records revealed repeated conversations between Damini and Tushar on the night of the murder. Both were arrested, and the police sent four accused to jail. The key similarity between this case and the Ravita-Amardeep case was the use of a snake to stage the circumstances of the death. However, Ravita had allegedly strangled her husband, Amit, and then released a snake to make his death appear to have been caused by a snakebite. The snake was a non-venomous rat snake that had no teeth and could not have caused death through its bite. While sentencing Ravita to death, the judge observed that Damini appeared to have learnt from the earlier case and allegedly used a venomous snake to kill her husband. 2. Raja Raghuvanshi murder case: Husband killed during honeymoon trip Indore businessman Raja Raghuvanshi married Sonam Raghuvanshi on 11 May 2025. After their wedding, the couple travelled to Assam and Meghalaya for their honeymoon. According to the police investigation, Sonam was in a relationship with Raj Kushwaha, and the two allegedly plotted Raja’s murder. On 23 May, near Weisawdong in the Sohra area of Meghalaya, Vishal Chauhan allegedly attacked Raja on the head with a sharp weapon at Sonam’s signal. Akash Rajput also allegedly assaulted him. According to the police, the accused then threw Raja’s body down a hillside. His body was recovered on 2 June. During the investigation, Meghalaya Police used mobile phone locations and call records to establish the alleged roles of Sonam, Raj Kushwaha, Vishal Chauhan, Akash Rajput and Anand Kurmi. According to the police, Raj was the alleged mastermind, while Sonam played a role in planning the honeymoon trip. Sonam was found in Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, on 9 June, while the other accused were also arrested. Police in Indore also arrested some people over allegations of destroying evidence. The final determination of the accused persons’ roles and the charges against them remains subject to court proceedings. The case resembles the Ravita-Amardeep and Damini-Atul cases in that investigators identified an alleged extramarital relationship and a planned conspiracy as key aspects of the murder. 3. Siya-Ketan case: Fiancé allegedly pushed off 400-foot-high cliff On 18 June 2026, Pune real estate businessman Ketan Vishal Agrawal (26) was allegedly murdered by his fiancée, Siya Goyal (20), with the help of her boyfriend, Chetan Chaudhary (22). Ketan and Siya were due to marry in Udaipur, Rajasthan, in November. On 18 June, the couple visited Lohagad Fort to celebrate Siya’s birthday in advance and spend time together. Initially, Siya told the police that Ketan had slipped and fallen into a gorge about 400 feet deep. The police registered a case of accidental death, but an investigation into phone records and social media activity revealed information about the relationship between Siya and Chetan. The police alleged that Siya did not want to marry Ketan and that she and Chetan had conspired to eliminate him. According to the police, Siya and Chetan had also attempted to kill Ketan on 14 June, but their plan failed. They subsequently planned another trekking trip. Investigators found that Siya took Ketan to Lohagad Fort, while Chetan also reached the location. The two allegedly pushed Ketan into the gorge. Ketan’s body was recovered after a search operation. Police initially detained Chetan for questioning on suspicion, following which Siya was also arrested. A murder and criminal conspiracy case was registered on the complaint of Ketan’s father, Vishal Agrawal. The police are gathering evidence to establish the alleged conspiracy. 4. Ilma-Talib case: Wife allegedly strangled husband and claimed he had suffered a heart attack On 28 September, Ilma (27), a beautician from Zakir Nagar in Meerut, allegedly murdered her husband, Talib (30), with the help of her lover, Aman, and his friend. According to Ilma, she mixed a sedative into her husband’s food following an argument. Once Talib became unconscious, Aman’s friend held his hands, Ilma held his legs, and Aman allegedly strangled him with a scarf. Ilma then called family members and claimed that Talib had died of a heart attack. His family subsequently buried the body. Talib and Ilma had been married for four years and had a three-year-old daughter. On 5 October, the family found Talib’s mobile phone, which raised their suspicions about Ilma. During questioning, she reportedly confessed to the murder. On 8 October, the police had the grave opened in the presence of administrative officials and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. After the report confirmed murder, the police arrested Ilma, while Aman remained at large. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ilma said she missed her husband and regretted her actions. “I did wrong. I request the law to sentence me to death as well,” she said. According to Ilma, their three-year-old daughter witnessed the murder. The case bears similarities to the others in which investigators alleged that a wife conspired with her lover to kill her husband and then attempted to conceal the crime by giving a false explanation for the death. The Meerut blue drum murder case also featured in the court’s discussion The series of cases that raised questions about marital relationships began with the Meerut blue drum murder case, in which Muskan allegedly killed her husband, Saurabh Rajput, with the help of her lover, Sahil. His body was cut into pieces, which were then packed in a blue drum with cement. During arguments in the case, the prosecution’s lawyer, District Government Counsel KK Chaubey, repeatedly referred to several similar incidents. He argued before the court that a series of such crimes had been reported across the country following the Muskan-Sahil case. One incident followed another, with wives allegedly joining hands with their lovers to murder their husbands, bringing disrepute to the institution of marriage. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra considered this argument a significant part of the prosecution’s case. On 14 October 2026, Muskan and Sahil were sentenced to death in the Saurabh murder case.

stories.title: Blackmailer or killer, who is Shraddha Dubey?:Left husband and children for glamour, lived with don’s aide; in Nepal or fled to Dubai?
stories.summary: A girl from a middle-class family who lost her mother in childhood. She left home after failing to get along with her stepmother. She got married and had a child, but was determined to make a mark in the world of glamour. She entered fashion and modelling, then came into contact with the underworld, influential politicians and senior officials. Amid Lucknow's glitz and glamour, she was sometimes seen on luxury trips in the mountains, while her social media reels sometimes featured private bouncers and police personnel. Then, one night, a 28-year-old businessman suddenly died after falling from the same building where she lived. After this, her name became linked to allegations of blackmail and torture. We are talking about Shraddha Dubey, who has now become a puzzle for the police and investigating agencies. Shraddha, who carries a reward of ₹25,000 on her head, is on the run after allegedly fleeing through Nepal. The police are searching for her. Read the full story of Shraddha Dubey's journey from personal struggles to an alleged life of crime and finally to her disappearance, in today's Sunday Big Story… Shraddha Dubey is from Raebareli. Her home is in Ramjipuram Colony in the Bastepur area. Her father, S.K. Dubey, lives there. He retired as a junior engineer in the Irrigation Department. Shraddha was around 6-7 years old when her mother died. Her father remarried. This was when bitterness began to enter Shraddha's life. She never got along with her stepmother. Her father also often took his second wife's side. Fed up with the constant arguments, Shraddha moved to Lucknow with her younger sister, Rashmi. They began living with a relative. In 2010, her father, S.K. Dubey, arranged her marriage to Lokesh Pandey, a resident of Pratapgarh. Lokesh works for a major IT company in Hyderabad. After the wedding, he took Shraddha with him to Hyderabad. Initially, everything went well. Shraddha told Lokesh that she wanted to build a career in fashion design and modelling. Lokesh fully supported her and helped her enrol in a course. During this period, they also had a son. Residents of the Ramjipuram neighbourhood in Raebareli say Lokesh wanted Shraddha to settle down in Hyderabad with him and their child. However, Shraddha preferred Lucknow. This led to frequent arguments between the couple. Eventually, they divorced in 2022. Under a court order, Lokesh was granted custody of their child. After the divorce, Shraddha severed ties with her entire family. She also stopped visiting Raebareli altogether. For around a year after the divorce, Shraddha stayed away from social media and publicity. However, by the end of 2023, she had returned to the fashion industry. In early 2024, she participated in a major national dress competition held in Jaipur. After that, she began appearing at major fashion shows in Delhi and Lucknow. In 2024, Shraddha published dozens of promotional posts for which she received substantial payments. Her lifestyle during this period gave the impression that she had become a successful model. But this was only the story playing out in front of the camera… Shraddha wanted a luxurious lifestyle and to become rich quickly. Towards the end of 2024, she met Zulfiqar, alias ‘Zulfi Khan’, at a pub in Lucknow. Zulfiqar is from Khata Sarai in Jaunpur. He claims to be close to underworld don Abu Salem and uses the name to intimidate people. He has been living in Lucknow for the past 15 years. Shraddha's friendship with Zulfiqar soon turned into a partnership. The two began living together in a luxury flat near Butler Palace, an upscale area of Lucknow. Using his new Fortuner and influence, Zulfiqar introduced Shraddha to prominent politicians, police officers and builders. Shraddha allegedly drew these high-profile individuals into her web through her looks and persuasive conversation. Zulfiqar and Shraddha would then allegedly blackmail them and extort large sums of money. Apart from Zulfiqar, Shraddha was also linked to history-sheeter Abhishek Singh, alias ‘Babu Singh’. Babu Singh has previously been jailed in kidnapping and extortion cases. Modelling had now taken a back seat in Shraddha's life. Private bouncers, gunmen and underworld criminals had taken its place. The most horrifying alleged victim of Shraddha's dark world was 28-year-old businessman Shiva Sharma. Shiva ran a clothing shop named ‘Vande Mataram’ and a restaurant called ‘Aangan’ in the Aliganj area. Shiva met Shraddha at a pub through a mutual friend. He fell in love with her after becoming attracted to her charm. In July 2026, the two began living together in the upscale Awadh Green Apartments in Hazratganj. Shiva spent crores of rupees fulfilling Shraddha's extravagant spending habits and luxurious demands. As a result, his business was pushed to the brink of collapse. On the evening of 9 October, Shiva died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments. When his body was found below, he was wearing only his underwear. There were lipstick marks on several parts of his body. He also had deep cigarette-burn injuries on his chest and arms. Shortly before his death, Shraddha's sister, Rashmi, called Shiva's mother. She falsely claimed that Shiva had met with an accident and was being taken to Lohia Hospital. In reality, Shiva had been taken to the trauma centre, where doctors declared him dead. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, alleges that her son was murdered and tortured until he was forced to jump. A video recorded before Shiva's death has surfaced. In it, Shraddha can be seen scolding him and threatening to send him to jail. In fact, a shooting had taken place at a pub in Gomti Nagar on 30 August, and Shiva was also named as an accused in the case. When he went absconding, the police announced a reward of ₹50,000 for information leading to his arrest. Shiva was later arrested in Patna, Bihar. After spending a few days in jail, he was granted bail. Shiva had become frightened of going to jail, and Shraddha allegedly took advantage of this. She was continuously blackmailing him. In the video, Shiva can be heard saying, “I don't have any cash. You can take my BMW car, but please leave me alone.” As the case surrounding Shiva's death gained attention, Shraddha went missing overnight. At 6 am on 10 October, Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver reached Rupaidiha in Bahraich. They parked their Scorpio at Shukla Parking and crossed into Nepal. Shraddha had previously travelled to Nepal for fashion shows and events. She has an established network there. Several CCTV images of her in Nepal have also emerged. Her last known location was in the Bhaluwang area of Dang district, Nepal. She switched off her Indian mobile number there and may have continued communicating with people using a Nepali SIM card. Has Shraddha fled to Dubai via Nepal? At present, several teams from the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) and Lucknow Police are stationed in Nepal. Raids are being conducted at possible hideouts with the assistance of the Nepal Police. Investigating agencies suspect that Shraddha may have used a fake passport to flee from Kathmandu to Dubai or another Gulf country.

Gandhi for Gen Z: The Mahatma is suddenly cool again | A documentary by The Hindu
stories.summary: Is Gandhi still relevant to Gen Z? In the summer of 2026, a generation that never studied Mahatma Gandhi sat down at Jantar Mantar, refused to fight back, and unexpectedly rediscovered the power of non-violent resistance. What began as a protest against the NEET paper leak soon raised larger questions about dissent, democracy and the language of political action. As students organised sit-ins, fasts and peaceful demonstrations, echoes of satyagraha surfaced in places where few were consciously looking for Gandhi. From the Cockroach Janata Party’s unconventional movement to grassroots community work led by SEWA, this documentary follows the many ways Gandhian ideas continue to appear in contemporary India. Along the way, it explores the intersections and tensions between Gandhi and Ambedkar, the meaning of civil disobedience in the digital age, and the challenge of practising non-violence in an increasingly polarised society. Featuring Gopalkrishna Gandhi, Ramachandra Guha, Tushar Arun Gandhi, Saurav Das and Mirai Chatterjee, the film brings together historians, activists and organisers to examine Gandhi not as a monument of the past, but as a proposition for the present. This is not a film about what Gandhi said. It is a film about what happens when a new generation unknowingly begins asking the same questions.

stories.title: Ajay Rai says BJP has been luring him since 2014:Calls himself a loyal Congress worker; says he is in touch with Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai has dismissed speculation about leaving the party, saying he remains a loyal Congress worker. “I am a Congress soldier and I am where I was. The BJP has been trying to lure me since 2014. But it knows that Ajay Rai is neither someone who wavers nor someone who retreats,” he said. On Saturday, the occasion of Ashtami, Ajay Rai offered prayers at Mata Nakateshwari Dham before starting his election campaign in the Pindra Assembly constituency of Varanasi. He rang the temple bell 11 times and bowed before Mata Nakateshwari to seek her blessings. Rai said he visits the temple with his family during every Navratri to seek the goddess’s blessings. He added that the historic temple had been renovated with the support of the people of Pindra, who came together to carry out the work. See 3 pictures... Reached Kathiraon while conducting public outreach from Babatpur After offering prayers, Rai addressed local residents and began his campaign activities. He received a welcome in around 12 villages across the Pindra Assembly constituency. Rai reached Babatpur on Saturday afternoon. From there, he travelled with dozens of supporters, first on a tractor and then on motorcycles, to the Naktेशwari Bhawani Temple. After offering prayers, he left for Pindra market. People welcomed him at several places along the route. Calling it a day dedicated to Mata Rani, Rai said, “Every Navratri, we visit the court of Maa Nakateshwari and seek her blessings.” He reiterated that the temple was an old and historic place of worship and had been renovated through the collective efforts and support of the people of Pindra. Ajay Rai said, "I do not chase positions" Ajay Rai said, "I am where I was. We are all Congress soldiers. I do not chase positions, because positions come and go. I have been an MLA five times and have also served as a minister. I became a minister at the age of 32. I became an MLA at the age of 25 years and eight months. In 1996, when Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh were one state, I was the youngest MLA." "This is the love and support of the people that stands with me. I won the election as an Independent and joined the Congress. If I had wanted power, I would have joined the BSP government itself. Mayawati ji was offering to make me a Cabinet minister at the time. You can ask Naseemuddin Siddiqui ji if you wish. He called me several times." 'The BJP has been trying to bring me into its fold since 2014' Targeting the BJP, Ajay Rai said that the party's people were lying in wait across the country, setting hooks everywhere-just as a hook is used to catch fish. He said, "That hook is lying near me too, but I have kept it there myself." Ajay Rai alleged that BJP leaders worked to deceive the public, flaunt money, and offer inducements and enticements. The BJP has been continuously trying to bring him into its fold since 2014. It made such attempts in 2014 and 2019 as well. During the 2024 election, BJP leaders had gone down on their knees, desperate to somehow bring him around. 'The BJP does not have the courage to call me' Asked whether he had received a call from the BJP, Ajay Rai said, "They do not have the courage to call me. They know that Ajay Rai will neither waver nor back down." He said these people only deceive the public, and that stealing and dishonesty were their only pursuits. He said, "Our aim is not to attain power, but to struggle. Today, it is our duty to drive out those who are looting the country, destroying it and ruining the future of young people." He said the BJP had ruined the country and destroyed the future of young people and farmers. He also targeted the government over incidents of rape and atrocities against girls in the state. He said every Congress worker was standing firm. Best wishes for Aradhana Mishra When asked about Aradhana Mishra being given responsibility in the Congress, Ajay Rai extended his best wishes to her. He said Aradhana Mishra should work hard, make every effort and respect the party workers by staying among them.

stories.title: UP government raises cooks’ monthly pay to ₹3,000:Order issued, salary expected before Diwali
stories.summary: The honourarium for cooks preparing midday meals for children in government schools in Uttar Pradesh has been increased by ₹1,000. They will now receive ₹3,000 a month instead of ₹2,000. The increased honorarium will apply from September. The honorarium paid in October will also include ₹1,000 in arrears. Cooks are paid the honourarium for only 10 months of the year. Mid-Day Meal Director Prem Ranjan Singh issued instructions to the basic education officers and finance and accounts officers of all districts on 17 October. The order said arrangements should be made to ensure that the increased honorarium is transferred to the cooks' bank accounts on time. There should be no negligence of any kind in this regard. Centre to pay ₹1,000, state government ₹2,000 Under the PM POSHAN Scheme, the Centre and state government's shares in the ₹3,000 monthly honourarium paid to cooks have been fixed. Of this, ₹1,000 will be provided under the central scheme and ₹2,000 by the state government as an additional top-up. Previously, cooks received a total of ₹2,000 per month. The decision has been implemented in pursuance of the government's letter dated 22 August 2026. The Mid-Day Meal Authority has instructed all districts to ensure payment at the revised rate from September. Honourarium to be paid for only 10 months a year According to the order, cooks will receive an honorarium at the rate of ₹3,000 per month for 10 months a year. Thus, each cook will receive a total of ₹30,000 for the entire year. The increase in the honorarium will provide relief to cooks working under the PM POSHAN Scheme in the state's government schools.

stories.title: UP Police, Home Guard recruitment:High Court orders fresh height and chest measurements on October 31
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has issued a major order concerning the Uttar Pradesh Constable Recruitment 2025 and Home Guard Recruitment 2025. Candidates who were disqualified for being told that their height or chest measurement was below the required standard will be given another opportunity to take the physical examination. The High Court said that a person's height or chest measurement is unlikely to change in one or two years. Therefore, the possibility of an error in the initial measurement cannot be ruled out. Justice Manish Kumar Nigam ordered fresh measurements while hearing the petitions filed by Anuj Kumar and more than 60 others. The court directed the principal of King George's Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, to constitute a medical board to examine the height or chest measurements of candidates in four categories. The High Court said: 31 October: All the concerned candidates will have to report to KGMU at 10 a.m. 4 November: The medical board will submit its investigation report to the High Court in a sealed envelope. The next hearing in the case will also be held on the same day. Recruitment was conducted for 32,679 constable posts. Its result was announced on 14 October. Meanwhile, the results for 41,424 Home Guard posts were released on 3 October. The High Court issued this order on Friday, and it was uploaded on Saturday. Petitions divided into five categories Advocate Aniruddh Pandey and other lawyers represented the petitioners in court. Baleshwar Chaturvedi appeared for the medical university, while Additional Advocate General MC Chaturvedi represented the state government. Government Unable to Deny Facts in Court The court said that a person's height or chest measurement was unlikely to change within one or two years. Therefore, the possibility of errors in the measurements of candidates in the first two categories could not be ruled out. In the case of the third category as well, the state government could not deny that there had been a difference between the two measurements. Regarding the fourth category, the court observed that the petitioners were young candidates and did not have complete information about the recruitment process. The court also referred to the Supreme Court's ruling in the Saurabh Yadav case, in which a medical board had been constituted to measure the candidates. State Government's Arguments Rejected The state government argued in court that, under the rules, the measurement conducted after an appeal is considered final. The height recorded in previous examinations cannot be used as the basis for the current recruitment process. However, despite these arguments, the court ordered the formation of an independent medical board to remeasure the candidates. Police Recruitment Board Officer Will Also Be Present During Measurement The court has directed all petitioners to appear at King George's Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, by 10 a.m. on 31 October 2026. No separate notice will be issued for this. The candidates must bring their Aadhaar cards or other identity documents, their admit cards for the Physical Standard Test (PST) and a certified copy of the court order. Those who remain absent on the scheduled date will not be granted any further concession by the court. An official from the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board will be present with the necessary records to verify the candidates' identities. The Director General or Commandant General of Home Guards has been directed to send an officer for the Home Guard candidates. The court also made it clear that the medical board would not be informed of the candidates' previously recorded height or chest measurements, so that the re-examination could be conducted independently. The lawyers will inform their petitioners about the order. Meanwhile, the lawyers representing the state government and the medical university must inform the KGMU vice-chancellor and the recruitment board about the order within one week. No relief for those with private hospital certificates The court granted no relief to candidates who had claimed eligibility on the basis of certificates issued by private hospitals or doctors and dismissed their petitions. The state government argued that the candidates' identities had neither been verified before their measurements were taken nor had the certificates clarified that the measurements were being conducted to challenge their exclusion from the ongoing recruitment process on the grounds of inadequate height. Now, let us look at both recruitments... 1- Constable recruitment: 18,210 OBC candidates pass 2- Home Guard recruitment: 41,424 candidates selected, 25.32 lakh applications received

stories.title: Jyoti says she wants to stay with Pawan Singh:Warns of moving Supreme Court if she gets no justice; actor fined ₹3,000 in Ballia
stories.summary: Bhojpuri actor and BJP MLC Pawan Singh did not appear before the Ballia court on Saturday, while his wife Jyoti Singh appeared in court. The court imposed a ₹3,000 fine on Pawan Singh for failing to appear. The case concerns the divorce and maintenance of Pawan Singh and his wife Jyoti Singh. The next hearing will be held on 12 November. After the hearing, Jyoti Singh said, "I want to live with Pawan. If Pawan Singh does not want to keep me with him, I should be awarded maintenance. If I do not get justice, I will go to the Supreme Court." Meanwhile, Jyoti Singh's lawyer, Akhilesh Singh, said, "At the previous hearing too, the court had directed Pawan Singh to appear. As he remained absent today as well, the court has given him a final opportunity to appear at the next hearing." Mother's medical documents submitted to court During the hearing, Pawan Singh's lawyer Harivansh Singh submitted his mother's medical documents to the court. He also filed an application for mediation. Jyoti said, "It has been four years; even patience has its limits" Jyoti said, "Pawan Singh did not come to court again. I have now been given 12 as the next date. He has also made a mockery of the court. He keeps getting one date after another. He thinks everything is in his hands. I only have faith in the court." Her mother's medical certificate has been submitted again today. Her mother is unwell. However, I had sent my brother. She was discharged the very next day. Even so, her mother's illness has been cited as the excuse. Four years have passed. That is a long time. Now all I can say is that I want to live with Pawan Singh. When the issue of separation comes up, I have demanded alimony. If separation is being discussed, my life has also been affected. So I will think about what I need to do for myself going forward and how to do it. Four years have passed. There is a limit to one's patience. Jyoti filed a petition in 2022 Jyoti Singh filed a petition for maintenance in the Ballia Family Court on 22 April 2022. Pawan Singh had earlier filed a divorce petition in the Family Court in Arrah, Bihar. The court also attempted counselling to resolve the dispute between the two sides, but no solution could be reached. Now, find out the full details of Pawan Singh and Jyoti's divorce case... Jyoti is Pawan Singh's second wife. Pawan Singh's first marriage was to Neelam Singh in 2014. Neelam committed suicide just a year after the marriage. Three years later, on 6 March 2018, Pawan Singh married Jyoti in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh. Within a few months of the marriage, differences began to emerge between the two. Jyoti accused Pawan Singh of mental and physical harassment and forcing her to undergo abortions twice. Pawan Singh rejected the allegations. Jyoti Singh filed a divorce petition in April 2022. Pawan Singh also filed a divorce petition in the Ara Family Court. Both were supposed to appear in court on 11 February for an attempt at reconciliation, but Pawan Singh did not attend because he was unwell. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when Pawan Singh contested as an independent candidate from Karakat, Jyoti campaigned for him. Reports then emerged that the two had reconciled. However, after the election results were announced, reports of their separation began to surface. Jyoti has repeatedly appealed to him to stay together. Jyoti has sought ₹10 crore in alimony from Pawan Jyoti Singh's lawyer had said, "Jyoti Singh has sought justice from the judge. She has said that if Pawan Singh does not want to keep me, he should give me ₹10 crore and a house as alimony (maintenance)." Now, know what alimony is... When one person provides another with financial support for basic necessities such as food, clothing, housing, education and medical care, it is called maintenance (alimony), or financial support for living expenses. There are two types of alimony (maintenance) under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Interim maintenance: When court proceedings are ongoing and a person does not initially have money to meet expenses, they continue to receive maintenance under Section 24 until the court delivers its decision. Permanent maintenance: Alimony received after divorce under Section 25 is called permanent maintenance. This maintenance does not include stridhan, over which only the wife has rights. The court decides the amount of maintenance after considering the husband's income, assets, responsibilities and other factors. Story being updated

stories.title: Greater Noida encounter:3 child trafficking suspects shot in legs; ₹5 lakh deal finalised
stories.summary: Police had an encounter with the gang that kidnapped a six-year-old child in Greater Noida. Three criminals were shot in the legs. Police arrested seven accused, including two women, and safely rescued the kidnapped child from their possession. Police recovered a car, a motorcycle, country-made pistols, and cash worth more than ₹2 lakh from the criminals. The accused were preparing to sell the child to a woman from Delhi for ₹5 lakh. The incident took place at 4 pm on Saturday in the Kasna police station area. Three criminals shot in encounter, child rescued DCP Shravan Kumar Singh said that a police team was conducting checks near Dadha roundabout in the Kasna police station area. During the operation, the police tried to stop a car. The criminals inside the car attempted to flee. When the police chased them, their car crashed into a tree. The criminals then opened fire at the police team. In retaliatory action, three criminals were shot in the legs. The police arrested the injured criminals, Gurmeet Singh, Sumit Kumar and Ankit Kumar. Based on their identification, Vikas and Nakul, son of Dharampal Singh, were arrested from Dadha roundabout village. Based on information provided by the five accused, Pushpa and Kamlesh, who were taking the child to sell him, were arrested from Kasna village. The abducted child was safely recovered from the possession of the two women. Child abducted from outside hospital on 13 October According to police, the child was kidnapped from outside Kanshiram Hospital on the evening of 13 October. A motorcycle was used in the abduction. During police questioning, Ankit said he had kidnapped the child with Nakul. Gurmeet, Sumit and Vikas then took the child to Ghaziabad by car. Sumit's maternal aunt, Pushpa, had suggested selling the child. She said Kamlesh, who lives in Delhi, would pay in exchange for the child. The accused then planned to sell the child. The deal to sell the child was struck for ₹4.50 lakh During police questioning, the criminals said the deal to sell the child had been fixed for ₹4.50 lakh. Of this, ₹2 lakh had already been paid, while the remaining ₹2.5 lakh was to be paid later. Police have recovered ₹1.50 lakh from the shares of Gurmeet, Ankit and Sumit, ₹20,000 each from Vikas and Nakul, and ₹32,800 from Pushpa. Police recovered three illegal country-made pistols, three spent cartridges and three live cartridges from the criminals. In addition, the car used in the crime, the Splendor motorcycle used for the kidnapping, and cash were also recovered. A case is also registered in Bulandshahr Police said a case had been registered at Kasna police station under the relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) in connection with the child's kidnapping. In addition, a case has been registered against Gurmeet, Ankit and Sumit at Sikandrabad police station in Bulandshahr under the BNS and the Arms Act.

stories.title: Yogi targets SP over MLC elections:Says party sold jobs for money and is an 'enemy of education'
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said in Lucknow on Saturday, "Under the previous government, candidates who took the examinations were not selected, while some people joined government jobs after securing appointment letters without even appearing for the examinations. Jobs were obtained by paying money. In one recruitment conducted by the commission, candidates from a single caste were selected for 56 of the 86 SDM posts." The Chief Minister advised BJP office-bearers and workers to remain vigilant during the Legislative Council election. He said, "You are working hard, but you must not become overconfident. Thieves and robbers commit robberies and break-ins only in the dark of night. The opposition will also try to break in. They have accepted defeat, but they will attempt to break in." Yogi said, "A pernicious tendency to put constitutional institutions in the dock has begun. This election should also be a response to it. He said that the election is being held through ballot papers, not EVMs. Voters must deliver the result in favour of justice." The Chief Minister was speaking at the BJP's teacher-graduate voters' conference at the Defence Expo ground in Lucknow. Yogi sought votes for the BJP's graduate candidate, engineer Avanish Kumar Singh, and teacher candidate, Umesh Dwivedi. Polling for 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) seats will be held on 23 October. The main contest for these seats across five graduate and six teacher constituencies is between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party. Before the 2027 Assembly elections, the contest is being seen as a major prestige battle for both parties and an opportunity to test their political strength. Key points from Yogi's speech- 1-People used to get joining letters without taking examinations Under the previous government, candidates who appeared for examinations were not selected, while some people joined jobs with appointment letters without even taking the examinations. Jobs were obtained by paying money. In one recruitment drive conducted by the commission, candidates from the same caste were selected for 56 of the 86 SDM posts. 2- SP gave One District, One Mafia Yogi alleged that the mafia held sway during the Samajwadi Party government and that land was illegally occupied. He said, "The Samajwadi Party gave One District, One Mafia; we gave One District, One Product and One District, One Medical College." The Chief Minister claimed that the BJP government had worked to improve law and order, along with development, the expansion of medical colleges and increasing employment opportunities. 3- Also targeted dynastic and family-based politics The Chief Minister appealed to teacher and graduate voters to reject the politics of family rule and dynastic succession. He said a representative should have the commitment and ability to raise people's problems. Referring to the MLC elections being held through ballot papers, Yogi said voters had the responsibility to ensure that the result favoured justice. He appealed to people to vote cautiously. 4- Cashless treatment for teachers up to ₹5 lakh Yogi said teachers from various categories and their families had been provided cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh annually. He also mentioned insurance cover for Shikshamitras, instructors and cooks. He said facilities such as classrooms, toilets, drinking water, smart classes and digital libraries in schools had been improved under Operation Kayakalp and the NIPUN Bharat campaign. The Chief Minister claimed that the dropout rate in basic education had fallen from 20% to 3%. 5- Claim of 9.5 lakh government jobs in nine and a half years The Chief Minister said the state government had provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh young people over the past nine and a half years. He also mentioned preparations to appoint another one lakh young people. He further claimed that employment opportunities had increased through investment in the private sector and startups.

stories.title: PM Modi to visit Gorakhpur region in November:To inaugurate agriculture university in Kushinagar, address rally
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Gorakhpur region in November. He will inaugurate the agricultural university established in Kushinagar district and address a public meeting held there. The administration and BJP leadership have received information about the Prime Minister's programme, and preparations are being made accordingly. The administration is looking for a venue for the public meeting. Along with the agricultural university, Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for several other development projects. Modi's visit is being considered important in view of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. In a way, it will also mark the beginning of the BJP's election rallies. Work has begun on a strategy to make the Prime Minister's programme a success. There had been considerable discussion for several days about the prime minister inaugurating the agricultural university. His programme in November is almost finalised. An atmosphere will be created in Purvanchal The Prime Minister's visit will create a favourable atmosphere for the BJP in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The public meeting will have a direct impact on Kushinagar, Gorakhpur, Maharajganj and Deoria. Held two months before the notification for the Assembly elections is issued, the event is being considered highly significant from the BJP's perspective. It will have an impact on all 62 Assembly seats in the Gorakhpur region. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath may be joined on the stage by Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party national president Om Prakash Rajbhar and Nishad Party national president Dr Sanjay Nishad. The venue for the public meeting will be finalised soon. Preparations under way to draw a historic crowd Preparations are under way to draw a historic crowd for the Prime Minister's visit. All key office bearers in the Gorakhpur region will be given responsibilities for this. However, from the BJP state president to the regional president, everyone is currently engaged in preparations for the teachers' MLC election. Voting for this election will take place on 23 October. After that, the party's focus will shift to the Prime Minister's programme.

stories.title: Tailor's son tops UP Police exam:Mother stopped father from sending him to work as a labourer; 2 sisters are also in police
stories.summary: Sarang, a resident of Baghpat who topped the UP Police constable examination with 276 out of 300 marks, said his father had asked him to work as a labourer at the age of 13 due to the family’s poverty, but he was allowed to continue his studies after his mother intervened. He said he studied with dedication and scored good marks in high school and intermediate before deciding to join the police after Class 12; although he was also selected for the CISF, he did not join, and he added, “My hard work paid off, and I will now serve while staying in my home state.” The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Sarang’s home to meet him and learn more about his journey. His father stitches clothes at home Sarang's home is in Doghat town, around 42 km from the district headquarters. His mother, Babli Prajapati, is a homemaker, while his father, Lokendra, is a tailor. He stitches clothes at home. He has two elder sisters, Asha and Abha. Asha is with the Uttar Pradesh Police and is posted in Unnao, while his younger sister Abha is with the CISF. She is posted in Kerala. Twenty-year-old Sarang has excelled in his studies from the beginning. Despite the family's weak financial position, he worked hard to pursue his education. Father says-if his wife had not understood, his son would have become a labourer Father Lokendra says, "We were very poor. When my son was 13, I had decided to send him to work at a grocery shop in our neighbourhood. However, after his mother and both sisters persuaded me, I did not stop his education. Sarang subsequently scored 81.5% in high school and 78% in intermediate." Mother says, ‘There was milk at home, but we could not give it to the children’ Sarang's mother, Babli, says they made their children successful by educating them after working hard. She had kept animals at home ever since she got married. However, she could not give her children milk to drink or even tea. The family was raised by selling all the milk. Arranging vegetables for the children's meals was also a major challenge. But she had faith in God. The children's hard work helped the family move forward. May God bless everyone with children like mine. Sarang says he fell in love with the uniform in childhood Sarang says, "I had decided to join the police service. Whenever I saw policemen visiting our village during my childhood, I fell in love with the uniform. I was selected for the ITBP about six months ago. However, I did not join it because I wanted to join the Uttar Pradesh Police. I even left that job because I wanted to be recruited into the police force. My dream has finally come true. Only the medical examination remains now." Stayed away from social media for a year Sarang says, “I stayed away from social media while preparing for the police recruitment examination. That was when I achieved success. I had been away from social media for the past year. Watching social media reels made me feel distracted. I did not want any obstacles in my way. I relied on online courses for my studies. I devoted around 12 hours every day to preparing for the examination. Whenever necessary, I also helped my father with his work.”

stories.title: Truck runs over motorcyclists, killing three:Two nursing students die in Lakhimpur; driver flees, abandoning truck
stories.summary: A truck ran over motorcyclists in Lakhimpur Kheri, killing three people, including two nursing students, on the spot. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was so severe that the motorcycle became trapped beneath the truck. After the accident, the driver abandoned the truck and fled the scene. Police personnel reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examinations. The deceased have been identified as Priyanka (24) and Kranti (18), both residents of Botan Purwa in Nighasan. Both were nursing students at Van Beit College of Medical Science in Santgarh, Bhira. The third victim was around 32 years old, but his identity has not yet been established. The accident occurred at around 3 pm on Saturday on the Bhira-Palia National Highway, under the jurisdiction of Bhira police station. See two pictures of the accident... Students travelled 60 kilometres to attend college The two nursing students travelled 60 kilometres from their homes to study at Van Beit College of Medical Science. They commuted to and from college every day. On Saturday, they were returning home after classes when the accident occurred. Kranti was the daughter of Ram Lotan, a resident of Bojhiya village under Nighasan police station. She was pursuing a BSc in Nursing. Priyanka was the daughter of Prithvi Pal, a resident of Botan Purwa. Long traffic jam after the accident Station House Officer Amit Pandey said, “Since this is a national highway, the accident led to a long traffic jam on both sides of the Bhira-Palia road. The police cleared it after considerable effort. The truck driver fled the scene after the accident, and a search is underway to trace him.”

stories.title: Youth sets himself on fire after pouring petrol:Upset over a road being forcibly built on his land in Jaunpur
stories.summary: In Jaunpur, a young man set himself on fire after pouring petrol over himself in protest against a road being forcibly built on his private land. He ran around with his body on fire. When people saw him, they began filling buckets and tubs with water and throwing it over him. They then used clothes and sacks to put out the fire. He was taken to hospital, where his condition remains critical. The incident took place in Pariyawa village under Line Bazar police station, 12 km from the district headquarters. The young man has been identified as Dinesh Kumar Maurya. A video of him has also surfaced. In it, he alleged that the village head was having a road forcibly built on his land. He said he was beaten when he opposed it. Following the incident, the police stopped the road construction. See the pictures... Here is the full story, in sequence Dinesh Kumar Maurya (35) is a farmer. He lives in the Laukri Maurya settlement in Pariyawa village with his wife, Savita Maurya (32), two daughters, Happy (15) and Lucky (13), his father, Tribhuvan Maurya (55), and his brother's wife, Shivdevi. He owns a total of four biswa of land. A dispute has been ongoing for four years over the construction of a road measuring around 300 metres through this land. According to the video that has emerged, a village council meeting was held on 14 October over the dispute. It was agreed that a 300-metre road would be built. He had also agreed to give half the passage from his share of the land. However, he alleges that on 15 October, the village head forcibly began having a passage built on his land. He claims that no official passage is recorded there in the revenue records or map, although villagers have been using this route for a long time. Dinesh had gone to BHU with his ill sister He had gone to BHU in Varanasi with his ill sister on 15-16 October. During this time, his relatives Gulab Chand Maurya, Dharmraj Maurya, Subedar Maurya and Chandrabhan Maurya called the police and began having a cart track built through the middle of his house. It is alleged that the opposing parties called the police again on Friday. His wife and family members were then subjected to obscene abuse. The mobile phone of children who were recording the incident was snatched and thrown away. According to Dinesh, he left BHU at around 11 pm on Friday and reached home at around 2 am on Saturday. He then complained to the police, but his grievance was not heard. He alleged that, distressed by this, he decided to attempt self-immolation. Poured petrol over himself and set himself on fire Dinesh poured petrol over himself and set himself on fire at around 10 a.m. on Saturday morning. When his family members saw him burning, they poured water over him. They put out the fire using clothes and sacks. He was then taken to hospital, where he is undergoing treatment and remains in critical condition. Police said construction had been stopped on Friday itself Line Bazar police station in-charge Vipin Rai said, "The police are aware of the dispute over the road. Police went to the spot on Friday and stopped the construction work. It is not yet known why the farmer attempted self-immolation. The youth is undergoing treatment at the district hospital." SP City Anant Chandrashekhar said, A person in Pariyawan village attempted to set himself on fire by pouring petrol on himself. The injured man was sent to hospital. He suffered burns over 40 per cent of his body. Police are investigating the matter. Necessary legal action will be taken.

stories.title: SP’s slap controversy puts BJP on edge:Nishads and Thakurs clash, why the party could face challenges in eastern UP
stories.summary: The slap row between two Samajwadi Party leaders in Gorakhpur has heightened the BJP's concerns. The leader who slapped the other belongs to the Thakur community, while the victim is a Nishad. Before the 2027 election, the BJP does not want to risk upsetting either of these communities. Mobilisation along Nishad-versus-Thakur lines has begun in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Both communities are important to the BJP. The incident took place at the Gorakhpur Journalists' Press Club on 3 October. The dispute began over sitting in the front row. Kamlesh Singh, son of ticket aspirant Anshuman Singh, slapped former SP district president Nageena Prasad Sahani. A video of the incident also went viral. Nishad Party president and Cabinet minister in the Yogi government, Dr Sanjay Nishad, linked the incident to an insult to the Nishad community. In response, members of the Kshatriya community began holding meetings. Amid protests and counterattacks, the dispute appears to be spreading from Gorakhpur to other districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. The question now is: how much could the BJP's difficulties increase as the Thakur and Nishad communities come face to face in Purvanchal? If the two communities vote against each other in the Assembly election, who will suffer the most? Read the full report... Sanjay Nishad said, "The hand will be cut off" Ram Nageena Sahani belongs to the Nishad community. Therefore, Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad came out in his support. Addressing a gathering, he told his supporters, "Put up the Nishad Party flag and wield its stick. If anyone threatens us, we will gouge out their eyes. If anyone raises a hand, their hand will be cut off." Thakur community says, ‘A neck for a hand’ Following Sanjay Nishad's statements, meetings began being held in Gorakhpur by members of the Kshatriya community in support of Anshuman Singh. Bansgaon Nagar Panchayat chairperson Vijay Singh, alias Bablu, also responded. During this, objectionable language such as "cutting off the neck instead of the hand" was used. Some members of the Kshatriya community demanded that an FIR be registered against Sanjay Nishad. Samajwadi Party's Rambhual Nishad takes up the fight In response to the Thakur community's meeting on 9 October, Samajwadi Party leader and Sultanpur MP Rambhuaal Nishad took up the cause. He called a mahapanchayat of the Nishad community at the Nishadraaj Temple premises in Rustampur, Gorakhpur district. People from the Nishad community gathered at the mahapanchayat from several districts of Purvanchal. Rambhuaal said that if any candidate from the community of the person who slapped Nagina Prasad Sahni contested an election on behalf of any party, the Nishad community would not vote for that candidate. Why Thakur and Nishad votes matter to the BJP The Thakur community has long wielded political and social influence in Purvanchal. At the same time, the Nishad community has played a key role in the BJP's strategy of bringing non-Yadav OBC communities into its fold. After 2017, the BJP focused on aligning smaller backward communities with itself. The alliance with the Nishad Party further strengthened this equation. The Nishad community's political significance is not limited to Gorakhpur. Its presence in several districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Sant Kabir Nagar, Basti, Deoria, Kushinagar, Mau, Ballia, Ghazipur, Jaunpur and Varanasi, could influence electoral outcomes. According to senior journalist Anand Rai, the challenge before the BJP is to take both the Thakur and Nishad communities along. If the dispute escalates, resentment in one community could unite the other. This could affect not only the BJP but also the strategies of the Samajwadi Party and the Nishad Party. Whenever the Nishad community in Purvanchal has moved away from the BJP, the party has suffered losses. The Nishad community also played a crucial role in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election. In that election, Samajwadi Party candidate Praveen Kumar Nishad, backed by the Nishad Party, defeated the BJP. A no-win situation for the BJP Upper castes, particularly the Thakur community, and non-Yadav OBC communities have played an important role in the BJP's electoral strategy in Purvanchal. The demand to include the Nishad community among the Scheduled Castes has been raised for a long time. This issue has also remained central to Sanjay Nishad's politics. Despite the alliance with the BJP, the demand has not been fulfilled. In such a situation, the dissatisfaction among a section of the Nishad community cannot be viewed solely in connection with the current controversy. If the slap incident and the statements made afterwards are repeatedly raised as an issue of the Nishad community's honour, it could fuel the discontent that already exists. It will now be important to see to what extent Sanjay Nishad turns the issue into a political campaign and what stand the BJP leadership takes on it. With the two communities now facing each other, the BJP finds itself caught between a rock and a hard place. Speaking in support of either side carries the direct risk of angering the other community, which is why the BJP's top leadership is currently maintaining silence on the entire episode. Nishad voters decisive on 42 seats in Purvanchal According to political analysts, the Nishad community plays a decisive role in around 42 of Purvanchal's 124 Assembly seats, where its population ranges from 50,000 to 80,000. 2022 Assembly Elections: The BJP won all 9 seats in Gorakhpur. These included the Nishad-dominated Gorakhpur Rural, Pipraich, Campierganj, Sahjanwa, Chauri Chaura and Bansgaon seats. Lessons from the 2018 by-election: When the Nishad community turned against the BJP in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election, the BJP lost its traditional seat. Sanjay Nishad's son, Praveen Nishad, won the election. Despite the BJP's major victory in 2017, it lost the Chillupar seat. At the time, the Nishad Party was opposed to the BJP. Similarly, the Nishad Party won the Shahganj seat in Jaunpur district in 2022. The party fielded a Thakur candidate there and wrested the seat from the Samajwadi Party. The Nishad Party also won the Gyanpur seat in Bhadohi and the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj, both considered strongholds of the Samajwadi Party. The alliance with the Nishad Party also helped the BJP win several seats in the districts of Deoria, Kushinagar and Sant Kabir Nagar. If the Thakur and Nishad communities mobilise against each other's candidates in the upcoming elections, the BJP may have to completely change its strategy in seats such as Gorakhpur Sadar, Campierganj and Gorakhpur Rural, where the sitting MLAs are currently Thakurs. What is the challenge for the SP? This dispute could also add to the SP's difficulties. The incident took place at the party's own programme, raising questions about organisational discipline. The party expelled Anshuman Singh, sending a message that action would be taken. In addition, the Gorakhpur district and metropolitan units were also dissolved. If resentment over the incident persists among the Nishad community, the BJP and Nishad Party may try to turn it into a political issue. They may allege that the Nishad community is not respected in the Samajwadi Party. The SP will face the challenge of addressing the Nishad community's resentment. The space the party gives to the Nishad and other OBC communities in the selection of candidates could also prove important. However, it is difficult to say at present whether the SP will make any changes to ticket distribution to minimise the impact of the controversy.

stories.title: ₹37 lakh stolen from Lucknow flat in 17 minutes:Thieves break lock and flee with 250g gold, 1.5kg silver and ₹1.5 lakh cash
stories.summary: A flat in Silver Line Apartment near Crown Mall, in Lucknow's BBD police station area, was burgled. After breaking the lock, the thief took jewellery worth lakhs of rupees and cash. At the time of the incident, the flat owner had gone to pick up his son from school, while his wife had gone to the hospital to collect medicine. The thief broke open the lock of an iron cupboard and stole around 250 grams of gold jewellery, 1.5 kilograms of silver jewellery and utensils, along with approximately ₹1.50 lakh in cash. The entire incident was captured on the CCTV camera installed in the flat. Had gone to pick up son from school Siddharth Pandey, originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, lives in the Silver Line Apartment on rent with his wife and three-and-a-half-year-old son. In his complaint to the police, he said that at around 12:15 p.m. on 16 October, he had gone to pick up his son from school. His wife had gone to see a doctor at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital at 11:30 a.m. During this time, no one was at the flat. When Siddharth returned home at around 12:45 p.m., he found the lock on the door broken. On entering, he saw that the door of the iron cupboard had been bent and its locker was open. The belongings were scattered. On checking, he found that gold and silver jewellery and cash were missing. Thief stayed in the house for 17 minutes According to the victim, CCTV footage shows a suspect breaking the lock of the house and entering at 12:24 p.m. He bent the cupboard door, broke its lock, stuffed the belongings into a bag and left at 12:41 p.m. The suspect was wearing a red half-sleeved shirt and black half trousers. He was also carrying a black bag on his shoulder. Suspected the guard and domestic help The victim said that after the incident, he called the guard and neighbours by shouting and informed his wife over the phone. In his complaint, he expressed suspicion that the guard and domestic help were involved in the theft. He said the guard and domestic help knew that the family would be away from home. Police said they were identifying the accused with the help of CCTV footage.

stories.title: Government doctor beaten up for inappropriate touching:Woman raises alarm during ultrasound in Siddharthnagar, draws crowd
stories.summary: People assaulted a government doctor in Siddharthnagar on allegations of inappropriate touching. The doctor is accused of touching a young woman's private parts during an ultrasound examination. When the doctor did not stop despite her protest, the woman raised an alarm and called people over. They then beat up the doctor. The incident took place at Diamond Diagnostic Centre, near the Bansi Kotwali intersection, around 22 kilometres from the district headquarters. The doctor was identified as Dr L.S. Singh, posted at the government hospital in Bansi. A video of the assault surfaced on Friday evening. The incident is reportedly from 13 October. According to police, the two sides have reached a settlement in the matter. First, here is what the video shows In the two-minute-and-six-second video, the doctor is seen sitting on a chair. Several people are slapping him. During this, the young woman continued crying and accusing the doctor of molesting her. Police officers are also seen at the scene in the video, but they were unable to stop the people beating the doctor. Now read the full matter... Dr L.S. Singh is posted as a radiologist at the 50-bed government hospital in Bansi. On 13 October, he went to conduct examinations at a private ultrasound centre named Diamond Diagnostic Centre. Meanwhile, a 20-year-old woman from the area arrived at the centre for an ultrasound examination. At around 2 p.m., it was her turn. She was taken into the ultrasound room. The young woman alleged that during the examination, the doctor began touching her private parts inappropriately. He did not stop even when she protested against his actions. Frightened, the woman began screaming loudly. Hearing the commotion, people standing outside the room came inside. After learning what had happened, they caught the accused doctor and began beating him. Police brokered a compromise between both sides Bansi Kotwali in-charge Mahendra Pratap Chaturvedi said The matter was brought to the police station. Both sides were called in and questioned. After this, they reached a compromise. No one has filed a written complaint. Chief Medical Officer Sanjay Kumar Dohre said- He was not aware of the matter. It is against the rules for a government doctor to practise at a private ultrasound centre. The matter will be investigated. Information will also be sought about the allegations of molestation, and action will be taken.

stories.title: Engineer and father killed in Purvanchal Expressway crash:Family was travelling to Mau for a wedding; wife, daughter and one other injured, CCTV captures accident
stories.summary: An engineer and his father were killed in a road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Azamgarh. His mother, sister and brother were seriously injured. The speeding car suddenly hit the divider, crossed the entire lane and fell by the roadside on the other side. CCTV footage of the accident, which took place at 10 am on Friday, emerged on Saturday. The car was reportedly travelling at 110–120 kmph. The accident occurred near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area, 18 km from the district headquarters. Police reached the spot and took the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab (52) and his father, Khurshid Ahmed (83), dead. Shadab’s wife, Asma Bano (45), daughter Myra (15) and son Adnan Ahmed (9) were injured. Shadab originally belonged to Sultanpur village in the Ghosi police station area of Mau district. He worked as a civil engineer in Delhi and lived with his family in Haji Colony, Jamia Nagar. The accident is suspected to have occurred after the driver briefly dozed off. Family was travelling to attend a relative’s wedding Shadab’s family was travelling by car from Delhi to their native village, Sultanpur, to attend a relative’s wedding. Due to the high speed, the car first hit the divider on the right side, then veered left in the same lane and overturned. Car overturns after hitting divider At around 10 am on Friday, the family’s red car reached the Purvanchal Expressway near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area of Azamgarh district. Near stone marker 216.2 on the expressway, the driver reportedly dozed off. The car lost control within moments due to the driver’s drowsiness. Travelling at high speed, it first hit the divider on the right and then overturned towards the left in the same lane. The impact was so severe that the car was badly damaged. The CCTV footage shows pieces of the car flying through the air. Father and son declared dead at hospital Following the accident, a rescue team from the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) reached the spot and took all the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab and his father, Khurshid Ahmed, dead. Meanwhile, Asma Bano, Mayra and Adnan Ahmed were admitted to a private hospital for treatment. Adnan Ahmed, one of the children, is reported to be in stable condition. The police are investigating the case. Wedding celebrations turn into mourning News of the deaths of Shadab and his father, who were returning to their village from Delhi with their family, sent shockwaves through their relatives. The family was travelling home to attend a wedding, but the accident turned the celebrations into mourning. The village is grieving following the incident.

stories.summary: Flooding continues to cause problems in Uttar Pradesh. Floodwaters have begun to recede in Lucknow and Sitapur, but waterlogging has worsened the situation. Hundreds of bighas of paddy crops remain submerged in Sitapur. Farmers are harvesting their crops in waist-deep water. In Lucknow, mud has filled the colonies after the water level in the Gomti fell. The lanes are covered with rubbish. Amid the foul smell, residents are finding it difficult to stay in their homes. The number of patients with vomiting, diarrhoea and viral fever has increased. Sixteen new dengue patients have been found. A 20-year-old three-storey ashram built in the middle of the Ganga collapsed in Jhunsi, Prayagraj. Three people were trapped under the debris. Two have been rescued. The search for the third is continuing. Meanwhile, the weather is clear across the state on Saturday. There is no rain alert anywhere today.

stories.title: Yogi tells law students, ‘Rule of mafia’ prevailed earlier:Even judges were stopped to let mafia convoys pass
stories.summary: CM Yogi said, without naming Atiq Ahmed, that there had been a mafia figure in Prayagraj against whom no law applied. Whether it was the Chief Minister, the Governor or a judge, nothing mattered. Whenever his convoy went out, it was given passage first. Any land he set foot on became his. Before 2017, there was the 'rule of the mafia', but we removed it from the law book and honestly implemented the 'rule of law'. On Saturday, CM Yogi attended the fifth convocation ceremony of Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University in Lucknow. Justice Vikram Nath, the next Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Arun Bhansali, Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court, and Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay were also present. Justice Vikram Nath said in a light-hearted manner, "CM Yogi had asked me to deliver a speech without reading it, but the Vice-Chancellor has asked me to read the written speech. This time, I will follow the Vice-Chancellor's instructions. The next time I come, I will follow the Chief Minister's instructions and deliver the speech without looking at the paper." Degrees were awarded to 260 students and research scholars at the ceremony. Twenty medals were presented to 17 meritorious students. These included 11 gold, five silver and four bronze medals. The gold medal recipients comprised eight female students and three male students. See the pictures... Now read CM Yogi's key points at the convocation... 1- Every lawyer must speak the truth and follow dharma Yogi said that it was essential for every lawyer to speak the truth, follow dharma and study continuously. He explained the meaning of 'Speak the truth. Practise righteousness. Do not neglect self-study,' which was quoted at the beginning of the vice-chancellor's convocation address. He said this was an important message for lawyers. 2- History will never forget Justice Khanna's dissent Referring to Supreme Court Justice H.R. Khanna's dissent during the Emergency, the Chief Minister said that history had not forgotten his dissent despite the price he paid for it. He said the incident explained the difference between the rule of law and the ruler's law, which operates according to the will of the ruler. 3- Students should embrace Ram, Krishna and Shiva Yogi referred to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia's views on Ram, Krishna and Shiva. He said Lohia had described a mind like Shiva's, a heart like Krishna's and words like Ram's as India's three great ideals. One should learn from Shiva to make decisions in difficult circumstances, from Krishna to show compassion towards the poor, and from Ram to observe propriety. He urged students to adopt these ideals in their lives. 4- A single party secured a full majority in 2014 after 30 years The Chief Minister said the rule of law and the justice system have an important role in building a developed India. Just as winning a case is important, winning the people's trust is also important for the country and the government. He said that on 16 May 2014, a single party secured a full majority after 30 years and Narendra Modi became Prime Minister. After this, the government accelerated the process of reforms. 5- More than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws were repealed Yogi said that more than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws had been repealed. Under the Jan Vishwas Act, minor errors in 183 provisions of 42 laws were decriminalised. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was introduced, and GST was implemented under the "One Nation, One Tax" framework. Article 370 was abrogated in Jammu and Kashmir, and the Nari Shakti Vandan Act was passed. He said reform did not mean merely enacting new laws, but also removing laws that were no longer useful.
