stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment candidates protest in Lucknow:Gherao Deputy CM, police carry them away; protester’s health deteriorates
stories.summary: Some 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment candidates staged a protest in Lucknow on Monday. The candidates surrounded Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya's residence and began raising slogans demanding appointments. The police, who arrived at the spot, began taking them into custody. A scuffle broke out between the police and the protesters. During this, the health of a protesting candidate named Manoj deteriorated. Police accused of tearing protesters' clothes The protesters raised slogans such as, "What is the compulsion? This is theft of reservation," and "The Backward Classes Commission has accepted it-this is a reservation scam." The police tried to remove the protesters from the spot. The police carried all the candidates away from there. The protesters accused the police of tearing their clothes and misbehaving with them. Ministers and officials acknowledged the scam Toofan Singh, who had come to protest, said that on 10 September, all of them met Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh and Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi. Several senior officials from both the Basic and Secondary Education departments were also present at the meeting. Along with the two ministers, the officials also accepted that a scam had taken place. When the State Backward Classes Commission has accepted it, the National Backward Classes Commission has accepted it, and now ministers and officials in the government are also acknowledging that a scam took place, why are jobs still not being provided? "We have been wearing out our slippers for eight years" Ashutosh Verma, who was among those protesting, said that they had been struggling to find jobs for the past 8 years. He alleged that a large-scale reservation scam had taken place in the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers. The State and National Backward Classes Commissions have also acknowledged irregularities in the reservation system and ordered that the rules be followed. 'Protesting on Navami is distressing' Ashutosh said, "Our demand is that the commission's orders be implemented. The recruitment notification was issued in 2018, and we filled out the form at the time. Since then, we have spent eight years wearing out our slippers in the hope of getting a job. Today, while people are busy with prayers and rituals on Navami, we will be picked up from here and made to sit at Eco Garden. The holy day will pass there. It is very distressing to protest during a festival, but we are being forced to do so."

stories.title: UP student’s skeleton found in Dehradun forest:Body recovered after 93 days, identified through scooter; friends suspected of murder
stories.summary: The skeleton of a 22-year-old BSc final-year student who had been missing for 3 months in Dehradun has been found in the Kimadi forest. His family identified the skeleton, found about 7 kilometres inside the forest from Kimadi, based on the scooter and clothes. Mohammed Shariq was a resident of Sherkot in Uttar Pradesh's Bijnor district. He had been missing since the night of 17 July. After the skeleton was found, the police stepped up their investigation. Meanwhile, his family accused two youths who lived with him of murder and demanded a thorough investigation into the case. Full sequence of events in three points He left home on his scooter on 17 July: Mohammad Shariq, a resident of Sherkot in Uttar Pradesh's Bijnor district, lived in a rented room in Dehradun's Azad Colony. He was pursuing a BSc in radiotherapy technology there. At around 10 p.m. on 17 July, he left his room on his scooter. He told his roommate that he would return within half an hour. However, he did not return. When Shariq failed to return, his family members and the youths living with him searched for him. However, they found no clue, and his mobile phone also began showing as switched off. Police complaint filed on 18 July: The day after the youth went missing, on 18 July, his father, Mohammad Tariq, filed a missing-person complaint at the Patel Nagar police station. The police began searching for him, but could not trace him for a long time. The police then registered a case under kidnapping charges and began an investigation. Skeleton found in forest after 93 days: Police used a drone to recover the skeleton of a young man who had been missing for around 93 days from a forest nearly seven kilometres from Kimadi. His family identified him based on his clothes. After the skeleton was found, police are now investigating the circumstances of the young man's death and whether anyone was involved. Uncle tells Bhaskar: Suspect his friends of murder Bhaskar spoke to Mohammad Shariq's uncle, Khaleeq. He said the entire incident dates back to 17 July. Shariq had gone missing on 17 July. Some boys were staying with him in the room, and they called home on the night of 18 July to report it. We asked those boys why they had not informed us earlier. They said they had been searching for him. We filed a missing-person report on 18 July. The police registered a case on 19 July. We then continued searching for him. On 17 October, I told his father to come so that we could go and meet the superintendent of police. Meanwhile, we received a call from the police. They said they had found a scooter and asked whether it belonged to our child. We said yes. We then reached the spot. When the police searched the forest, they found body parts. Several boys used to visit the room where Mohammad Shariq lived. They were his friends. We suspect that he was murdered because of a dispute.

stories.title: Shraddha Dubey gives interview amid police search:Appears near Agra Expressway; 10 police teams fail to trace her for 10 days
stories.summary: The state's most high-tech Lucknow Police have been unable to arrest Shraddha Dubey, the main accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case. Besides Shraddha, her fellow accused are also still out of reach. Since the incident, the police have appeared helpless in the face of Shraddha's network. Shraddha has been releasing videos and even gave the media a film-style interview, while the police have been left merely speculating. Even after 10 days, the police have been unable to trace her and kept claiming that she had been spotted in Nepal. In the meantime, Shraddha also gave a soundbite to news agency ANI. After failing to trace the model Shraddha, action has been taken against DCP Central Vikrant Veer and Vikram Singh, the station house officer of Hazratganj. However, Shraddha is still absconding with her sister and driver. The entire police network, from Lucknow to Nepal and western Uttar Pradesh, has been unable to trace Shraddha, even though she confidently gave the media a soundbite in Lucknow near the Agra Expressway. Despite this, she remains missing from the police radar. In the entire case, the Lucknow Police appear focused only on tracking Shraddha and the other accused. 10 days, 10 teams, zero results Ten police teams remained stationed from Lucknow to Nepal for 10 days and followed the accused. People travelling through districts along the Nepal border were searched for. The police also showed people photographs and questioned them. The search continued through CCTV footage and surveillance systems, but the police could not get any closer to Shraddha. The Crime Branch and STF teams have also drawn a blank in the case. Senior police officials are now directly monitoring the investigation, but there has still been no result. She would appear in videos or before the media, then disappear Shraddha's byte, given to just one news agency near the Agra Expressway, has raised questions over the police's entire investigation and elaborate arrangements in the case. How is it that Shraddha voluntarily comes into contact with certain people, gives a byte and then disappears? The police had been claiming that Shraddha kept changing her location after the incident, but she allegedly gave her account at a hotel. After that, she once again went on the run in filmi style. Helpers so powerful that police are on the back foot For now, Shraddha has conveyed her version on her own terms following the murder of Shiva Sharma. The question is: when the incident took place on 9 October, why did the police not take immediate action against the accused? How did all the accused leave Lucknow and reach Nepal after crossing several districts? During the police investigation, allegations are also emerging that influential people may have helped them. This could include politicians, bureaucrats and others, which is why Shraddha remains beyond the police's reach. The police could not reach the accused for nine days in the case. On the 10th day of her absconding, Shraddha reached a media agency. Shraddha Dubey preparing to surrender According to sources, Shraddha is currently preparing to surrender to the police through the court. Activity related to this continued at the district court throughout Sunday. Although the police have issued a non-bailable warrant against Shraddha, she has filed an anticipatory bail petition in court against it. She can therefore surrender through the court. It has emerged that DCP Central Vikrant Veer and Inspector Vikram Singh are being removed for taking the incident lightly and for negligence. Vikrant Veer has been attached to police headquarters as a Superintendent of Police, while Inspector Vikram Singh has been sent to the police lines. Read the sequence of events 13 October - Audio recording surfaces In the alleged audio recording, Shraddha Dubey can be heard questioning Shiva Sharma about the theft from her flat. 'Sanjay sir' is also mentioned, and Shiva is threatened with being sent to jail. The question is: Who exactly is this Sanjay sir? 14 October - First video Shraddha Dubey released a video denying that she was missing. She claimed that Shiva Sharma had died by suicide. She also appealed to the media not to link her name to politicians or officials. 14 October - Second video A few minutes after the first video, Shraddha's second video emerged. In it, she expressed her wish to surrender and repeated that this was not a murder case. 15 October - Third video Shraddha gave details of the incident on the night of 9 October. She claimed that Shiva Sharma, who was deeply in debt, jumped from the balcony after his sister opened the door. Two videos of Shiva emerge 15 October afternoon - fourth video An undated clip has emerged. In it, Shiva Sharma appears to promise to return Shraddha's money within a month and says he will leave his car as security. 16 October afternoon - fifth video In another clip, Shiva Sharma's voice, allegedly recorded by Shraddha, can be heard. In it, he appears to admit stealing jewellery worth ₹6 lakh from his apartment. Now read what the entire case is about... Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of the Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj on 9 October. Shiva had been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the past four months. After the incident, he was wearing only underwear. Lipstick was smeared on his face. Several cigarette-burn marks were also found on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has filed a murder case against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Adil, in connection with his death. stories.title: Yogi performs Kanya Pujan at Gorakhnath Temple:Washes girls’ feet, applies tilak; Vijayadashami procession tomorrow
stories.summary: Gorakshpeethadhishwar and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will perform the Kanya Pujan ritual at the Gorakhnath Temple on Monday morning (19 October), on the Mahanavami day of Sharadiya Navratri. On the occasion, he will wash the feet of the feminine power, conveying the Sanatan faith and tradition's message of respect for women. On Tuesday (20 October), the day after Mahanavami, rituals will continue throughout the day at Gorakshpeeth in accordance with the Nathpanth's distinctive tradition on Vijayadashami. In the evening, a grand traditional procession will be taken out under the leadership of Gorakshpeethadhishwar. Worship of Shakti at Gorakshpeeth is distinctive during Sharadiya Navratri. On Pratipada, the first day of Navratri, Gorakshpeethadhishwar and the Chief Minister ceremonially installed the kalash at the temple's Shaktipeeth. He has been staying at the temple again since Sunday. As part of the same sequence, Chief Minister Yogi will perform Kanya Pujan at 11 a.m. on Monday, Mahanavami, after worshipping Goddess Siddhidatri, the ninth form of Goddess Durga. This ritual at the Gorakshpeeth offers a direct glimpse of the tradition of according the highest place to feminine power in Sanatan culture. As per tradition, the Gorakshpeethadhishwar will wash the feet of unmarried girls in the form of Goddess Durga and perform their worship according to ritual by applying a tilak of roli, sandalwood, curd and akshat on their foreheads. He will also seek their blessings after serving them a meal with full devotion and presenting them with dakshina and gifts. Batuk worship will also be performed during the ceremony as per tradition. Vijayadashami celebrations to begin with worship of Guru Gorakhnathji On Tuesday, the Vijayadashami festival, celebrating the victory of righteousness over unrighteousness and truth over falsehood, will begin at 9:35 am with Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath performing a special puja of Shivavatar Guru Gorakhnathji. After worshipping Shri Nathji, Gorakshpeethadhishwar will worship all the idols of the deities in the Gorakhnath temple complex. From 1 pm to 3 pm, the tilak ceremony of Gorakshpeethadhishwar will be held. During the programme, Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will bless the devotees. A grand Vijayadashami procession led by Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will set out at 4 pm. After receiving the blessings of Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath, Gorakshpeethadhishwar will mount his chariot. Accompanied by the sounds of trumpets, drums and bands, the procession will reach the Mansarovar Temple. There, Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will perform puja and abhishek of Devadhidev Mahadev and other deities at the Mansarovar Temple associated with Gorakshpeeth. After this, the procession will reach the Mansarovar Ramlila Ground. There, they will perform the coronation of Lord Rama at the ongoing Ramlila. Lord Rama, Mata Janaki, Lakshman and Hanuman will also be worshipped, followed by the aarti. Subsequently, the procession will return to Gorakhnath Temple from the Ramlila Ground, and a traditional prasad distribution ceremony (a feast for the poor, Brahmins and guests) will be held from 7 pm. A large number of people from all sections of society attend this feast, regardless of distinctions between rich and poor or caste and religion.

stories.title: Man’s head severed and thrown 5 feet away by rotavator:Got caught in machine while ploughing field; wife collapses on seeing body
stories.summary: A young man in Barabanki died after being caught in a rotavator while ploughing a field with a tractor. After hearing a sound suggesting that something had become entangled in the rotavator, he climbed down from the running tractor to inspect it. During this, his head became trapped in the rotavator. Within seconds, his head was severed from his body and thrown about 5 feet away. The accident occurred late on Sunday night in Hasuwapara village in Nindura block, about 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as 30-year-old Prem Prakash, a resident of the village. As soon as she received information about the accident, Prem Prakash's wife reached the field. She broke down on seeing her husband's body and became unconscious shortly afterwards. The police admitted her to hospital after she repeatedly fainted. The police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. See the pictures Here is the full story Prem Prakash, a resident of Hasuwapara village, was a farmer. He had married Geeta Devi (28) around five years ago. The couple had a four-year-old daughter, Avishka, and a one-year-old son, Lavi. He also used his tractor to plough other people's fields on contract. According to reports, he had gone to plough the field belonging to his uncle Ravi. Potatoes were to be planted in the field. At around 9 p.m., he was ploughing it with a rotavator attached to his tractor. After ploughing for around 40 minutes, he suddenly heard a sound suggesting that something had become stuck in the rotavator. Prem Prakash then put the running tractor into neutral and climbed down. He bent over to inspect the rotavator. Its shaft was rotating at the time. During this, his head was caught in it. Before anyone could understand what had happened, Prem Prakash's head was severed from his body and landed around 5 feet away. His torso fell to the ground. Seeing the accident, Ravi, the owner of the field, rushed over. He first switched off the tractor and raised the alarm to call the villagers. Wife faints after seeing her husband's body As soon as news of the accident reached her, Prem Prakash's wife, Geeta Devi, arrived at the field crying. She fainted on seeing her husband's head. Villagers hurriedly admitted her to a nearby private hospital. Four-year-old Avishka is inconsolable after her father's death. Family members somehow managed to calm her. After receiving the information, Baddoopur police station in-charge Manoj Kumar Sonkar reached the spot with police personnel. The police took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Police said-No one has filed a complaint yet Police station in-charge Manoj Kumar said- The young man's head had been severed from his torso. His wife's condition had also deteriorated, following which she was admitted to hospital. The victim's family has not filed a complaint. Further action will be taken once a complaint is received.

stories.title: Video of lawyer’s murder in Prayagraj surfaces:Accused steps back after being hit with rod, then shoots him in abdomen as cops watch
stories.summary: A video showing the killing of advocate Satish Chandra Srivastava has emerged from Prayagraj. It shows a fight between Satish and the main accused, Devendra Nath Mishra. During the scuffle, Devendra pulls out a revolver and shoots Satish. Police personnel can also be seen standing at the scene during the incident. Advocate Satish was shot dead on 15 October in a dispute over the encroachment of government land. The main accused, Devendra, and his son Nripendra have already been sent to jail. His other son, Amarendra Mishra, and wife, Shail Mishra, have also been named as accused. Police are searching for them. The identities of 10 unidentified people are being established. The 59-second video that emerged on Monday begins with nine to 10 people entering a room with their faces covered with cloth. Most of them are wearing black coats. When a scuffle breaks out inside, everyone is seen quickly running outside. The next part of the video shows the area outside a house. Two groups are seen fighting and arguing at the house gate. People are seen attacking each other with sticks and batons and pushing one another. Satish, wearing a yellow T-shirt, is seen attacking Devendra with a rod. Devendra falls backwards during the attack. At the same time, Devendra shoots Satish in the stomach with a revolver. Satish steps back, clutching his stomach, and falls to the ground. The entire video is said to have been recorded at Satish's house in Salori. Watch the third footage... Daughter ran towards her father, then screamed Satish's daughter Vaishali can also be seen in the video. On seeing Devendra fall, she runs towards him. Meanwhile, after someone says that Satish has been shot, she turns around. She starts screaming on seeing her father unconscious. Dispute was over possession of Nazul property During police questioning, Devendra Nath Mishra said that he had been involved in a long-standing dispute with Satish Chandra Srivastava over possession of Nazul property. Both sides had previously filed cases against each other in this connection. According to the police, on 15 October, Devendra reached the disputed land with his son Nripendra and others. They all entered by jumping over the boundary wall. Satish was then assaulted, after which Devendra shot him with his licensed revolver. Satish, who was critically injured, was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. A case was registered on the complaint of Satish's wife, Varsha Srivastava, against Devendra, his sons Amarendra and Nripendra, his wife Shail and others. Police arrested Devendra and Nripendra and sent them to jail. An investigation into the roles of Amarendra, Shail and the other accused is continuing. Family members took away the body four hours later Following Satish's death, the family had sought financial assistance, government jobs for both daughters and lifelong security. His wife, Varsha Srivastava, had told police officials that her husband was the family's sole breadwinner. She had asked how the family would manage with their two daughters and how they would arrange their marriages. The family had also demanded the arrest of all those accused of the murder, that no counter-FIR be registered in the case and that the accused persons' homes be demolished with bulldozers. After the post-mortem, the family reached home with the body at around 2:30 p.m. on Friday but refused to take it away until their demands were met. Police and administrative officials continued trying to convince them. Around four hours later, at 6:30 p.m., the family left for the cremation after being assured that two accused would be arrested and that appropriate action would be taken on the other demands. Section 30 of the Arms Act also added The police have also added Section 30 of the Arms Act to the case. This section concerns violations of the conditions of an arms licence. According to the police, the possibility that a licensed revolver was used in the incident is also being investigated. After the murder, lawyers and the family had protested, demanding the arrest of the accused, financial assistance and other measures. On Saturday evening, the family took out a candle march from the district panchayat office to the district magistrate's residence and submitted a memorandum demanding a fair investigation and raising their other demands.

stories.title: Father of seven slashes wife’s abdomen with sickle in Gorakhpur:Intestines protrude after attack; accused arrested
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a father of seven attacked his wife with a sickle during a domestic dispute. The attack tore open the woman's abdomen, causing her intestines to protrude. She also suffered serious injuries to her head and neck. With the help of the police, her family somehow tied up her intestines and admitted her to BRD Medical College. Her condition is critical. The incident took place at around 5 p.m. on Sunday. The husband allegedly suspected his wife's character. The couple had argued over the issue. When the dispute escalated, the husband attacked his wife with a sickle. Hearing the woman's cries for help, local residents reached the spot and informed the police. The incident took place in Haraia village under the Geeda police station area. Strikes inflicted on her head and neck Jalaluddin, alias Pangul, 45, a resident of Haraia village, argued with his wife, Safia, on Sunday evening. It is reported that Jalaluddin suspected his wife of having an affair with another man. Following a heated exchange over the issue, he attacked her with a sickle. The attack tore open Safia's abdomen, seriously injuring her. Police reached the scene, sent the injured woman to hospital and took her accused husband into custody. According to police, a case has been registered under relevant sections, including attempted murder, based on a complaint filed by the couple's eldest daughter, Rahnuma, and further action is under way. On receiving information about the incident, police from Geeda police station reached the spot. An ambulance took the injured woman to BRD Medical College, where a team of doctors is treating her. Daughter says-Dad often beats Mum Police cordoned off the village and detained the accused, Jalaluddin. Jalaluddin has seven children-six daughters and one son. His eldest daughter, Rehnuma, said that her father frequently attacks her mother. The two have been involved in a dispute for quite some time. Geeda Circle Officer Aabha Singh said: The accused is being questioned. Preliminary information indicates that the incident stemmed from a domestic dispute. A case has been registered under relevant sections, including attempt to murder, and further action is being taken.

stories.title: Air show security on Maha Kumbh lines:20 lakh people expected in Varanasi over 3 days; PM and CM may attend, green corridor planned
stories.summary: Varanasi is set to witness, for the first time, the historic valour, courage and strategic capabilities of the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. A grand and large-scale air show has been proposed in Varanasi on 22, 24 and 25 October. Around 15 to 20 lakh people are expected to attend the historic event. In view of the massive turnout, the Uttar Pradesh government and the local administration have made extensive security arrangements of the kind usually seen during the Prayagraj Mahakumbh. The air show is expected to be attended by the Prime Minister, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, senior officials of the Ministry of Defence, the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force, as well as several prominent and distinguished personalities from India and abroad. The Varanasi police and administrative machinery have gone into full alert mode to manage VIP movement and the crowd of lakhs of people. Security to follow Maha Kumbh model According to Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal, a three-tier security plan is being prepared on the lines of the Maha Kumbh to make the event completely safe and well-organised. Additional police forces will be deployed along all the city's major routes, the ghats along the Ganga and sensitive areas. Temporary police stations and outposts are being set up in key parts of the city and near the venue to control crowds and make the security arrangements more effective. Along with security, discipline and better management will be the main pillars of the entire event. Police personnel arriving from outside are being trained in the lanes of Kashi The CP said, "Kashi is known for its narrow lanes, ghats and unique geographical layout. A special plan has therefore been drawn up to ensure that police personnel arriving from other districts face no difficulties while on duty. The Police Commissioner said that all personnel deployed for security would not only be assigned responsibility for their respective duty points, but would also be familiarised with Kashi's geographical features and layout." As part of this, police personnel from outside the city are being given detailed briefings and training on Varanasi's narrow lanes, major roads, Ganga ghats and important locations. The purpose of this special training is to ensure that personnel can easily identify routes during emergencies or when dealing with heavy crowds, enabling effective crowd management, traffic control and the prompt delivery of assistance to the public in any emergency. Diversion plan will be prepared for traffic To ensure the city's traffic does not come to a standstill because of the movement of hundreds of thousands of spectators and VIP vehicles, the traffic police are preparing a comprehensive traffic diversion plan. Entry of heavy vehicles into the outer and inner parts of the city will be restricted, and separate routes are being designated for VIPs and the general public. • Parking arrangements: Large parking areas are being identified at the city's entry points and near the venue to prevent traffic jams on the roads. • Green corridor: A 'green corridor' will be arranged between major hospitals and the venue to deal with any medical emergency, allowing ambulances to travel without any obstruction. • Temporary medical camps: Temporary medical camps and teams of doctors will be deployed around the venue to provide immediate first aid and necessary treatment. The sole purpose of these extensive arrangements is to ensure the smooth movement of the lakhs of spectators visiting Kashi, showcase the valour of the Indian Air Force to the public without any hindrance, and ensure the convenience of local residents.

stories.summary: The railway administration has changed the routes of eight trains due to unavoidable reasons. The changes will remain in effect on different dates. The affected trains will now run via Mahad Khedi, Bina Malkhedi and Agasod. They include the Surat-Muzaffarpur, Gorakhpur-Okha, Ahmedabad-Darbhanga and Ahmedabad-Varanasi City Express trains. The railway has appealed to passengers to check their train's route and date before beginning their journey. Routes of these trains changed According to the railway, train number 19053 Surat-Muzaffarpur Express will run on the diverted route on 23 October. Meanwhile, train number 19054 Muzaffarpur-Surat Express was operated on the same route on 18 October. Similarly, train number 15045 Gorakhpur-Okha Express will be operated on the diverted route on 22 October, while train number 15046 Okha-Gorakhpur Express will be operated on the changed route on 18 October. Ahmedabad and Darbhanga trains also affected

stories.title: Municipal corporation on alert for CM’s Vijayadashami procession:Hanging wires to be removed in Gorakhpur, route to be decorated with lights
stories.summary: In view of Vijayadashami, the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has stepped up preparations for the Chief Minister's procession. Work is being expedited to ensure the timely completion of road repairs, the installation of slabs over drains, lighting, decoration and cleaning along the procession route. On Sunday, Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain inspected the designated procession route with officials and engineers. He directed them to complete the unfinished work quickly and ensure proper security and sanitation arrangements. The Municipal Commissioner instructed officials of the construction department to speed up the patchwork on the route and complete the installation of slabs over open drains at the earliest. He made it clear that devotees and the general public should not face any inconvenience while travelling during the procession. He directed officials to address the shortcomings along the route in time so that there was no disorder on the festival day. Hanging wires to be removed The municipal commissioner also directed the concerned officials regarding arrangements for lighting and decoration along the procession route. The Lighting Department was instructed to ensure that the installation of decorative lights and string lights was completed within the stipulated deadline. Instructions were also issued to have the electricity wires hanging along the route removed so that there would be no risk of any accident during the procession. The municipal commissioner stressed the need to maintain coordination with officials of the Electricity Department. He said arrangements must be ensured for immediately shutting off the electricity supply in the event of any possible accident. Instructions were issued to maintain better coordination among the departments concerned so that action could be taken without delay in an emergency. Wall painting and fabric decorations to be completed soon The ongoing wall-painting work to make the route more attractive was also reviewed. The municipal commissioner directed Additional Municipal Commissioner Pramod Kumar and the other officials concerned to complete the painting of the walls promptly. He also instructed them to ensure that the fabric decorations were completed by the next day at all costs, so that the route's decoration could be finished before the procession. Sanitation workers to be deployed in shifts The municipal commissioner directed officials to exercise special vigilance to maintain cleanliness along the procession route. He said sanitation workers should be assigned their duties on time and shifts should be changed as needed. Regular cleaning should be ensured along the entire route, and no rubbish should be allowed to accumulate anywhere. During the inspection, the municipal commissioner instructed the officials concerned to ensure that all work was completed within the stipulated deadline and to work in coordination with one another. He made it clear that the procession route must remain clean, safe and orderly during Vijayadashami.

stories.title: Four killed while taking selfies on overbridge:Speeding truck hits group standing outside parked Scorpio in Kashi, two fall 30 feet
stories.summary: A truck collided with a Scorpio on the Prayagraj-Varanasi Highway (NH-19) near Rupapur village in the Mirzamurad police station area of Varanasi on Monday morning, killing four people and seriously injuring three others. The victims were returning to Kashi after visiting Vindhyachal Dham. The accident took place around 6 am on an overbridge, about 27 km from the district headquarters. The seven people travelling in the Scorpio had stopped their car and were standing near the railing when a speeding truck hit them from behind. The truck ran over people standing outside the car. One injured person dies in hospital After receiving information from passersby, police reached the spot and sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. Three injured people were taken to the hospital by ambulance. One of them later died, while the other two remain in critical condition. The deceased have been identified as Aman Yadav, Golu and Alok Mishra. Kanhaiya Yadav and Nikhil Kumar are among the injured. The identities of one deceased person and one injured person are yet to be confirmed. Investigation underway The crash occurred while the occupants were travelling from Prayagraj to Varanasi. Further details about the victims and the circumstances leading to the accident were not immediately available.

stories.title: Flood victims get trapped after buying land in Lucknow:‘We fear our houses may sink’; plot prices could rise further if embankment is built
stories.summary: Lucknow’s Faizullaganj now looks like a waterlogged island. Water has almost disappeared from the roads, but 2 to 4 feet of water still remains in the narrow lanes. The flooding has caused the greatest distress to people living in single-storey houses. They are covering their rooftops with tarpaulins to protect their valuable belongings, including refrigerators, cupboards and televisions. Aman Verma, who lives on 60 Feet Road in Faizullaganj, also has a single-storey house. When water entered his home, he gathered his belongings and moved to the roof. Speaking with a choked voice, Aman says, “Many people are saying that our houses were built on the river, which is why they got submerged. I want to ask them how the water reached Palassio and Ekana.” Like Aman, thousands of people in Faizullaganj have been forced to live on their rooftops. Many of them came from other districts, bought plots of land here and built houses. Now, watching the flooding, they regret their decision. They say, “If we had known this earlier, we would never have bought land here.” The Dainik Bhaskar team has been continuously covering the flood-affected areas. This time, we spoke to people who bought land and built houses in the floodplain. Listen to what they are going through amid the flooding and what they have to say. Nagma Khatoon, who originally belongs to Biswan in Sitapur, is sitting by the roadside in the Daudnagar area. She is waiting for the water to recede and for a boat to arrive. Nagma, who moved here with her family in 2020, says, “Our entire house is submerged. The fridge, cupboard, groceries... everything is floating in the water. We could not rescue even a single item safely. My son and husband are trapped in the flood. I received news that their health had deteriorated, so I risked my life to come and see them.” Nagma continues, “Around seven to eight years ago, we invested our entire life savings in buying land here. We have been living here for six years. If we had even the slightest idea that Lucknow could also experience flooding, we would never have bought land here.” ‘We built our house with our hard-earned money, and now it is sinking’ Sushil Tiwari, who moved here from Hardoi, shares the same pain. Sushil says, “We had heard stories about the 2008 floods, but conditions remained normal for years afterwards. We bought land here in 2017 and built a house with our hard-earned money. Today, my entire house is submerged. Everything inside has been ruined. People say we must have bought the land because it was cheap, but that is absolutely not true. We bought the plot at a very high price.” ‘Land in the floodplain is being sold at the highest rates’ Faizullaganj and Daudnagar gradually began developing after 2010. After 2018, real estate activity increased sharply in these areas. Salaried people arriving from other districts invested their hard-earned money in plots here. Local resident Moinuddin says, “The price of land on Daudnagar’s 60 Feet Main Road has now reached ₹6,000 per square foot. In prime locations, people are charging as much as ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 per square foot. Even in the inner lanes, you will not find land for less than ₹2,000 to ₹3,000 per square foot. This was not an unplanned settlement where land was available for next to nothing.” When Moinuddin was asked whether land prices would fall after such severe flooding, he replied with a smile, “Absolutely not! Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has now announced that a dam will be built. Property dealers and builders will publicise this announcement and sell the land at even higher prices. The real problem is that earlier, when some water accumulated, it could be pumped out using pumping sets. But this time, that was not possible.” Expert says river’s width was reduced in the name of a riverfront, and that was wrong More than 40,000 houses in Faizullaganj have been affected by the flooding, of which around 50% are single-storey houses. More than 4 lakh people have been affected by the flooding in Lucknow. According to a 2018 report published in the research journal Environmental Sustainability, the width of the Gomti River in Lucknow was reduced from 450 metres to 240 metres during the construction of the riverfront. The river’s flow corridor was also narrowed from 250 metres to between 100 and 125 metres. Tall concrete walls were built along both banks of the river. As a result, when a heavy flow of water arrived this time, the river could not pass through the narrow concrete channel. The water backed up and began wreaking havoc in residential areas. Water level was below the danger mark, yet 40,000 houses were flooded The Gomti has flooded five times, and the threat remains Professor Dutta explains that the Gomti River originates in Pilibhit and travels around 900 kilometres before reaching Ghazipur. Along the way, 185 tributaries and streams, including 35 major rivers, flow into it. Unfortunately, several tributaries were officially classified as ‘drains’, filled in and built over. Nature never forgets its course, and Lucknow is now bearing the consequences.

stories.title: Ajay returns without meeting Rahul, may quit Congress:Political debut with Anupriya could complicate contest for Pindra seat
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai will demonstrate his strength today at Maa Nakateshwari Dham in Pindra, Varanasi. He is reportedly upset with the party. The reason is a dispute involving Mamta Chaudhary at the Congress headquarters in Lucknow on 11 October. The party's top leadership had called him to Delhi to contain the damage. He went there on 14 October but did not meet Rahul Gandhi. Questions are now being raised about whether Ajay Rai will leave the Congress. If he does, will he return to his former party or begin a new political innings with Anupriya Patel? Read the full story… Ajay Rai served as Uttar Pradesh Congress president for more than 3 years, but on 2 October, he was suddenly removed, and Aradhana Mishra, 'Mona', was appointed as the state president. Before this, Aradhana Mishra was the Congress Legislature Party leader. Ajay Rai accepted the decision and congratulated Aradhana Mishra. He also said, “I am a soldier of Rahul Gandhi.” The dispute began with the taunt, ‘Who is the president?’ On 11 October, the first day of Navratri, Aradhana Mishra had organised a programme to take charge as the state Congress president. Ajay Rai also arrived from Varanasi with his supporters to attend the event. At the state Congress office, Ajay Rai's supporters were asking the crowd to make way, saying, “The president is coming.” In response, Mamta Chaudhary, the president of the Congress Mahila Morcha for the central region, taunted them, saying, “Who is the president? I would not even like to look at such a president.” Ajay Rai's supporters objected to Mamta's remark. An argument then escalated between the two sides. The dispute became so heated that Ajay Rai's supporters even took off their shoes. Angered by the incident, Ajay Rai began leaving the party office. Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari, Aradhana Mishra's father, somehow managed to persuade him to stay. However, the incident intensified speculation that Ajay Rai was upset with the party. Sources associated with the party say Mamta Chaudhary has a good relationship with Aradhana Mishra. This has led to speculation that Mamta had Mona Mishra's backing when she made the remark. However, this claim has not been confirmed. The party has not taken any action against Mamta Chaudhary so far. Conspiracy against Ajay? He was not even given a chance to present his case Ajay Rai took charge as Uttar Pradesh Congress president on 19 August 2023. At the time, the party had suffered a crushing defeat in the 2022 Assembly elections, winning just two seats. The morale of party workers had also fallen. During his tenure of more than three years, Ajay Rai tried to boost the morale of party workers. He remained active on a range of local and state issues and worked to strengthen his connection with the public. It is reported that he also bore the entire cost of running the party office himself. The number of Congress MPs in Uttar Pradesh increased from one in 2019 to six in 2024. Ajay Rai was now working to strengthen the party ahead of the Assembly elections, but he was suddenly removed from his post. It is reported that Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, had been working to have Ajay Rai removed for the past month. He reportedly convinced senior party leaders that the Congress would not perform well in the Assembly elections under Ajay Rai's leadership. Ajay Rai's strict manner of dealing with people is also being cited as a reason for the change. Caste equations have also emerged as a factor in the discussions. According to sources, Rahul Gandhi was not in favour of the change and wanted the decision to replace the state president to be postponed until after the Assembly elections. Initially, the party considered appointing a Muslim leader as state president. However, Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi wanted the post to go to Aradhana Mishra, a Brahmin leader. Aradhana Mishra was eventually appointed state president. It is reported that Ajay Rai is also upset because he believes a conspiracy was plotted against him to remove him from the post. He was reportedly called to present his side after Rajendra Pal Gautam submitted his report. However, sources claim that his views were not heard because Priyanka Gandhi and K.C. Venugopal opposed giving him that opportunity. Leaving the Congress will not be easy for Ajay According to sources associated with the party, after Ajay Rai was removed as state president, Rahul Gandhi immediately offered to make him a member of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) and appoint him as the party's in-charge for a state. However, Ajay Rai did not accept the offer. Rahul Gandhi remains in regular contact with Ajay Rai. Therefore, deciding to leave the Congress will not be easy for him. A leader close to Ajay Rai, speaking on condition of anonymity, said he would not leave the Congress. According to the leader, Ajay Rai might consider leaving the party only if Rahul Gandhi himself mistreated him. The leader added that Ajay Rai also has limited political alternatives. Could Ajay Rai return to the BJP? Ajay Rai began his political career with the RSS and the BJP's student organisation, ABVP. He was elected MLA from the Kolasla Assembly constituency on a BJP ticket in 1996, 2002 and 2007, winning three consecutive terms. When the BJP denied him a ticket for the 2009 Lok Sabha elections, he resigned from both the party and his position as MLA. He then joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) and contested the Lok Sabha election from Varanasi, but lost. His resignation left the Kolasla Assembly seat vacant. He was elected MLA again in the by-election as an independent candidate. Before the 2012 Assembly elections, Ajay Rai joined the Congress. That year, he won the Pindra Assembly seat on a Congress ticket. He subsequently contested the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi against Prime Minister Narendra Modi but lost on all three occasions. The road ahead in Pindra will not be easy either According to senior journalist Anand Rai, Ajay Rai's return to the BJP would be difficult. Ajay Rai is preparing to contest the Pindra Assembly seat. At present, BJP MLA Awadhesh Singh represents the constituency. Like Ajay Rai, he also belongs to the Bhumihar community. In the 2022 Assembly elections, Ajay Rai finished third in Pindra, while BSP candidate Babulal came second. The result was similar in the 2017 elections. A source associated with the BJP claims that, while serving as state Congress president, Ajay Rai openly criticised the theft of offerings at the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Therefore, the chances of his returning to the BJP are low. Even if he joins Anupriya Patel, the seat-sharing issue will remain Why did he not meet Rahul Gandhi despite travelling to Delhi? On 14 October, reports emerged that Rahul Gandhi had called Ajay Rai to Delhi. Ajay Rai travelled there but did not meet Rahul Gandhi. Earlier, senior Congress leaders had been called to Delhi to participate in Rahul Gandhi's protest, but Ajay Rai did not attend that either. This led to speculation that he had avoided meeting Rahul Gandhi because he was upset with the party. However, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ajay Rai denied being upset with the party. He said: I had gone to Delhi for my child's admission. There was no programme to meet Rahul Gandhi. Does anyone get upset with their own family? The Congress is my family and my home. Why is Ajay Rai suddenly demonstrating his strength in Pindra on 17 October? Following the dispute at the Congress office on 11 October, Ajay Rai posted a message on social media on the night of 14 October. In the post, he announced a rally near Maa Nakateshwari Dham in Pindra at 12:30 pm on 17 October. He wrote, “Pindra is my family.” According to senior journalist Anand Rai, after being removed as state president, Ajay Rai's option now is to focus on preparations in his assembly constituency. By demonstrating his strength in Pindra, he will want to boost the morale of his supporters. Meanwhile, people associated with the party believe that the committee formed to investigate the 11 October dispute is also due to submit its report on 17 October. Ajay Rai therefore wants to demonstrate his strength through the rally. He also wants to send a message about how important he is to the Congress. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’, responding to a question from Dainik Bhaskar, said, “Ajay Rai is a member of our family. He is a senior leader and our elder brother.”

stories.title: UP PET centres set 500–600 km away:35 lakh candidates angry; commission chairman says centres were allotted through automated system
stories.summary: Candidates appearing for the PET examination are facing long journeys to reach their allotted centres, with Siddharth Singh from Jaunpur having to travel 520 km to Mainpuri and Mohammad Rehman from Prayagraj being assigned a centre in Ghaziabad, 650 km away. Their plight reflects the concerns of 35 lakh candidates who have been allotted examination centres 500 to 600 km from their homes and are struggling to decide whether to focus on exam preparation or spend additional time travelling, with some preparing to begin their journeys a day in advance. Dainik Bhaskar asked commission chairman Satyanarayan Sabat about the issue. He said the commission takes steps to prevent cheating in examinations. Examination centres are now allotted through automation, which is why some candidates have been assigned centres farther away this time. The PET-2026 examination will be held on 25 and 30 October and 1 November. Around 35 lakh candidates are expected to appear. Candidates must take this eligibility test for government jobs under the UPSSSC. Only those who pass can apply for Group B and Group C jobs. On 12 October, the commission announced on its website the cities where the examination would be held. This triggered anger among candidates. Students are now demanding that the government and commission change their examination centres. To understand the difficulties they are facing, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to candidates. Himanshu Pandey from Pratapgarh says, “We cannot apply for UPSSSC jobs without passing the PET examination. At present, we are studying for 18 hours every day. Now we have learnt that my examination centre has been allotted in Firozabad, 470 km away. Just think about it. I will have to travel through the night to reach the centre. I will be so exhausted that I will not be able to write my answers properly during the examination.” R.K. Maurya from Pilibhit is facing a similar problem. He says, “My examination centre has been allotted in Bijnor, 240 km away. It takes five hours to get there by train, and then I have to struggle to reach the centre. If I am even a few minutes late, they will send me back from the examination centre. The commission has not taken our convenience into account.” Only 10 days left for the examination, but confirmed seats are unavailable Only 10 to 15 days remain before the examination. Candidates complain that they are unable to get confirmed train tickets because their centres are 500 to 600 km away. There are also no direct bus or train services to several districts, forcing candidates to change buses or trains once or twice. Since the centres are far away, they will have to arrive a day in advance. Travel fares, accommodation and food could together cost each candidate up to ₹2,000. Women candidates face an additional difficulty, as they feel unsafe travelling away from home alone. Naturally, they will have to take a family member along. The combined cost of travel, accommodation and food for two people can reach ₹3,500 to ₹4,000. As a result, daughters from poor families are being forced to consider skipping the examination. ‘Why so much travelling for just a screening test?’ Since the admit cards were released, candidates have been demanding a change of examination centres on social media. They argue that the PET is only an initial screening test for Group B and Group C government jobs, such as Lekhpal, Junior Assistant and VDO. It is not an examination that directly determines final job appointments, so there is no reason to send candidates such long distances for it. Five times the population of Sikkim in PET candidates The examination will be conducted over three days, with two shifts each day. The commission has set up a total of 1,372 centres across 60 districts in the state. A record 35 lakh 41 thousand 296 candidates have applied this time. An average of 6 lakh candidates will appear in each shift, with around 12 lakh candidates taking the examination each day. The total number of PET candidates is approximately five to six times Sikkim's population of around 7 lakh. Commission chairman says, ‘Allotments were made by computer’ Commission chairman Satyanarayan Sabat says, “Uttar Pradesh is a large state, with a distance of around 1,100 kilometres from one end to the other. The most suitable arrangement has been implemented in view of the examination centres available for 35 lakh candidates. The number of candidates is high in eastern Uttar Pradesh districts such as Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia and Jaunpur. In comparison, there are fewer examination centres. Meanwhile, western Uttar Pradesh has fewer candidates and more centres. Therefore, candidates have been allotted centres according to requirements.” Understand in 3 points: Who has been allotted a centre, where and why Candidates with disabilities: Under the government's policy, they have been given examination centres in their home districts as a concession. Women candidates: Keeping their safety in mind, they have been allotted centres outside their home districts but in another city within their administrative division. Male candidates: They have been allotted examination centres in other administrative divisions.

stories.title: Ravita’s love story behind husband’s murder using a snake:Showed injuries to boyfriend on video calls; Meerut court sentences both to death
stories.summary: A Meerut court has sentenced Ravita and her lover Amardeep to death for murdering her husband, Amit Kashyap, and trying to pass off the murder as a snakebite. Additional District Judge (ADJ-12) Jayveer Singh Nagar said that giving them life imprisonment would not be enough for the crime. In his judgment, the judge wrote that Amit's murder had shaken the foundation of married life. He said Amit had trusted his wife and made her the mother of his three children, but she joined hands with her lover to kill him by strangling him. The judge described the murder as a cruel betrayal of the husband-wife relationship. He said the case fell under the “rarest of rare” category and required the harshest punishment. After the death sentence was announced on Friday evening, Ravita and Amardeep were shifted to the prisoners' barracks. Both kept crying and did not touch the food sent to them. Ravita also developed a high fever. Judge says husband-wife relationship is based on trust The judge wrote that the relationship between a husband and wife is traditionally seen as a bond of trust, sacrifice and commitment. He said Amit's murder was not just the killing of one person but also a serious blow to the values associated with marriage in Indian society. He observed that a husband expects his wife to protect him, just as she expects him to stand by her. In this case, the person Amit trusted most allegedly became involved in his murder. The judgment referred to Hindu religious beliefs that describe a wife as an “Ardhangini”, or the other half of her husband, and a partner in his duties, happiness and sorrow. Judge says Ravita went against the ideals of Savitri The judge also referred to the story of Savitri, who, according to Hindu tradition, brought her husband Satyavan back from the god of death, Yama. He said Ravita had acted against the ideals linked with Savitri. The judge noted that people traditionally pray for their spouses' long lives during festivals such as Karwa Chauth, but Ravita had allegedly joined her lover to kill her husband. He wrote that Amit had trusted Amardeep like a brother. Amardeep used to visit Amit's house and had worked with him on tile installation. The judge said this trust had also been betrayed. Judge warns against using murder to remove a partner from the way The judgment said such crimes could weaken people's faith in the marriage bond and create a wrong message that a spouse could be killed for the sake of an outside relationship. The judge also referred to the couple's three young children. He said they had lost their father and their mother would now be in prison, leaving their future uncertain. He held Ravita responsible for the situation caused by the crime. The judge said a lenient punishment in such cases could send the wrong message to society. He stressed that strict punishment was needed to prevent similar crimes. Defence lawyer did not appear for the hearing At around 11:30 am on Friday, ADJ-12 Jayveer Singh Nagar entered the courtroom. Ravita and Amardeep joined the hearing from jail through video conference. Amardeep was wearing a white shirt, while Ravita was wearing a brown suit and had covered her head with a dupatta. The two looked at each other briefly. The judge told them that they had been found guilty in the Amit Kashyap murder case and that the hearing was to decide their punishment. Additional District Government Counsel Farzana Khatoon represented the prosecution, while Balraj Singh appeared as the lawyer for Amit's family. The defence lawyer, Omkar Singh Bhati, did not attend personally and sent a junior lawyer in his place. Farzana argued that the murder was extremely cruel and could not be forgiven. She said Ravita and Amardeep had strangled Amit and attacked him several times. The postmortem report had recorded scratch marks on Amit's face, hands, and chest. She also said Ravita had allegedly planned the murder with Amardeep to marry him and then tried to hide the crime by placing a snake on Amit's bed to make it look like a snakebite. The lawyer representing Amit's family cited more than five Supreme Court rulings and requested the death penalty for both accused. The arguments lasted around 20 minutes. The defence did not present arguments. Ravita asks court to care for her three children After the arguments, the judge asked Amardeep whether he should be given the death penalty or life imprisonment. Amardeep replied that his parents were elderly and requested that someone take care of them. When Ravita was asked the same question, she said she had three young children and requested that they be looked after. Both fell silent when asked to respond further. The judge then said the verdict would be announced after lunch. Ravita and Amardeep cry as judge reads verdict At around 3:05 pm, Amit's mother, Munesh, and his brother, Sonu, were present in the courtroom. Ravita and Amardeep were again connected from the district jail through video conference. As soon as the judge began reading the verdict, both accused started crying. Their cries could be heard in the courtroom. The judge read translations of verses from the seventh chapter of the Manusmriti and the Atreya Samhita. He referred to the role of punishment in maintaining order and said justice requires punishing wrongdoers, respecting good people and treating those seeking justice fairly. Judge breaks pen after announcing death sentence While explaining his decision, the judge said that the “rarest of rare” category was not limited to cases in which a body was cut into pieces. He said a planned murder in which a wife and her lover allegedly strangled her husband and then used a snake to make the death look accidental was also an exceptionally serious crime. The judge then sentenced Ravita and Amardeep to death, saying life imprisonment would not be enough. The courtroom broke into applause, and some lawyers raised slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. Amit's mother began crying and folded her hands to thank the judge. Both Ravita and Amardeep also cried after hearing the sentence. The judge further ordered that the district magistrate would be responsible for ensuring the care, upbringing, and education of Amit and Ravita's three children. After giving the order, the judge broke his pen and left the courtroom. He delivered the verdict in around 12 minutes.

Ayush got into an argument with the accused, Rahul Sahni, over possession of the plot. Rahul then allegedly shot Ayush with his licensed pistol. After the shooting, Rahul tried to flee the scene. However, Hindu Raksha Dal workers caught him and severely beat him. After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot, rescued Rahul from the crowd and took him into custody. Read the full story below : Sahibabad ACP Amit Saxena said that in the Sahibabad area, a woman named Namita Sharma had sold a 180-square-yard plot to Poonam, the wife of Hindu Raksha Dal president Pinky Chaudhary. Pinky Chaudhary claims that he has already paid Namita Sharma several crore rupees for the plot. A 280-square-yard plot of land next to this plot is lying vacant. It is green-belt land. Namita Sharma claims it as her own, while Pinky Chaudhary also claims it. The two sides have previously disputed the land. The two sides again clashed over it on Friday evening. Gunfire followed an exchange of abuse On Friday evening, Rahul Sahni arrived at the plot with some people on behalf of Namita Sharma. Meanwhile, Pinky Chaudhary and workers of the Hindu Raksha Dal also reached the spot. The two sides first exchanged abuses, after which a physical fight broke out. Rahul Sahani fired a shot from his licensed pistol. The bullet hit Ayush Valmiki. He was immediately taken to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Ayush was a resident of Gokulpuri in Delhi. Hindu Raksha Dal workers caught Rahul Sahani and beat him. The police, who arrived after receiving the information, rescued him from the crowd and detained him. ACP Amit Saxena said that a report was being registered on the basis of the complaint. Action will be taken in the entire matter based on the evidence. Pinky Chaudhary had gone to jail for distributing swords to Hindus Pinky Chaudhary has been embroiled in controversies before. A 21-second video of him emerged on 29 December 2025. The video was from the Shalimar Garden area of Ghaziabad. It showed Pinky Chaudhary distributing swords from house to house along with his supporters. In the video, her supporters were carrying swords and battle-axes. Chanting "Victory to Mother India", they were knocking on the doors of houses. When the owner came outside, they handed him a sword. They said the sword was for protecting sisters and daughters. If a situation like the one in Bangladesh arose, they said, it should be used to protect oneself from non-believers. In this case, the police arrested Pinky Chaudhary and her son on 6 January. After being released on bail on 15 January, Pinky Chaudhary took out a 25-kilometre-long procession.

As soon as the police were informed about the fire, Sadar Kotwali police reached the spot and safely evacuated all the children and teachers from the bus. stories.title: Elderly woman breaks down on seeing Divya Mittal:Hugs her in Mirzapur and says, 'Daughter, I had longed to see you; today my wish has come true'
stories.summary: An elderly woman broke down in tears on seeing former IAS officer Divya Mittal in Mirzapur on Friday. Hugging her, Duiji Devi said, “Daughter, I had been waiting for you for a long time. Today, my wish has been fulfilled. I have seen you to my heart's content. May the goddess continue to bless you. May you progress greatly.” Divya Mittal visited Mirzapur for the first time on Friday after forming a political party. She first visited the Maa Sheetla Temple in Gadbada Dham, where she offered prayers. During her visit, supporters raised slogans such as, “Divya, keep fighting; we are with you,” and “Long live Divya Didi.” At around 4 pm, Divya Mittal reached Lahuriyadah village, where she met Duiji Devi. In 2023, when Divya Mittal was serving as the Mirzapur district magistrate, she had inaugurated a drinking water facility in the village. At that time, Duiji Devi had blessed her. The villagers also garlanded Devkali, the woman who had demanded a school in the village. Divya Mittal told the villagers that she would make every possible effort for the development of Lahuriyadah village. She spoke to the villagers for around half an hour. Check out the pictures below : Divya Mittal announced her political party on Facebook on Thursday Former IAS officer Divya Mittal began her political journey on Thursday, October 15, by launching her own party, named Janniti Bharat. At 1 pm, she posted a video on Facebook announcing that she would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election from the Mirzapur Sadar constituency. Divya Mittal said, “In Janniti Bharat, you will be in charge. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh election. The government will run according to your wishes for five years.” Divya Mittal had said, “My aim is to change politics” On September 30, Divya Mittal had announced her decision to enter politics. She had said, “I will stay in Uttar Pradesh. I will not be afraid; I will ask questions. I will not join any party. I will walk alone. My aim is not to change politicians, but to change politics entirely. I do not need money or muscle power.” Divya Mittal, a 2013-batch IAS officer, resigned from service on August 30. At the time, she was serving as special secretary in the Revenue Department. Her resignation was accepted on September 14. After completing her BTech from IIT Delhi and MBA from IIM Bengaluru, she had worked in London in a job that offered a salary package worth lakhs of rupees. 1. First pledge of 'Janneeti Bharat' — People at the centre of policies Divya Mittal said, “I am forming my own party. There is no shortage of parties, but there is a shortage of people being heard. Like the Ganga, where every drop is equal and helps determine the way forward, I want to build a party where every person has a role. This party is called 'Janneeti Bharat'. Its first pledge is to put people at the centre of the country's policies and let them decide those policies. She recalled how Devkali Devi had asked her for a school even when her home had no water. Work began after Divya's video, but stopped when the land was found to belong to the forest department. Children are still waiting for the school. She questioned why forest land could be cleared within 80 days for roads needed by big industrialists, while files for schools, roads or factories for poor people could remain pending for 80 years. The second pledge is justice for all, where everyone is heard and people help decide how policies are made. She said policies should reflect the sacrifices of parents who eat less to feed their children and cut their own expenses to educate them. She also called for farming policies shaped with farmers, who understand problems from fields to markets and falling prices, and trade policies that consider the challenges faced by small traders from business to ports. She added that a girl looking at the moon from her rooftop today should one day be able to reach it. The pledge is: Policies from the people, and India shaped through those policies. 2. Every decision will be based on need, not identity: Janniti Bharat's second pledge- every decision will be based on need, not identity. A road was being built, raising hopes in the village, when someone pointed a finger and diverted its route. On one side, thousands of people would benefit; on the other, there was one person. The road was diverted towards the latter, where there were hundreds of houses. Courtyards were destroyed and homes were demolished. The person for whom the road was built was somebody. In public policy, everyone will be able to point to a location on the map. If there is a dark stretch or a turn where girls are afraid to pass, they will be able to flag it there. The spot will be marked through a mobile app, and once it receives 100 markings, it will have lighting, patrols and cameras. The decision will be made neither by the police nor by a politician, but by the girls themselves. Whether it is a hand pump, a road or a brick-paved path, work will begin wherever people point first. There will be no consideration of caste, religion or status; everyone will decide together. 3. Decisions based on need and equality in decision-making Janneeti Bharat's third pledge is: decisions based on need and equality in decision-making. A woman applied for a permanent house, but she did not know that her house had been approved. An intermediary came to her home and said, "Mother, I can get it done; give me ₹5,000." If the woman knew about the approval beforehand, where would the intermediary go? All the works carried out in that village, using funds from any source, should be visible on mobile phones. If you give the children notebooks to check, they will say everything is fine. Who is the first to know about a bad road? Those who travel on it. This is Janneeti Bharat's third pledge-accountability to the people and improvement based on accountability. She served as Mirzapur's district magistrate and brought water to Lahuriyadah Divya became Mirzapur's district magistrate in September 2022. She drew attention there for her work involving public meetings in rural areas and drinking water. The initiative to supply water through a pipeline to Lahuriyadah village was also launched during her tenure. Even after her transfer from Mirzapur, her farewell remained a talking point. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Her tenure in Deoria also subsequently drew attention. A dispute over powers between public representatives and the administration there put her in the spotlight once again.

stories.title: UP declares holiday on October 19 for Mahanavami:Offices to remain closed for 3 days in a row
stories.summary: The Yogi government has changed the holidays for Mahanavami and Vijayadashami in Uttar Pradesh. Now, Mahanavami will be a holiday on Monday, October 19, while Dussehra will be observed as a holiday the next day, October 20. Earlier, the government had announced a combined holiday for Mahanavami and Dussehra on October 20. Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department, SVS Rangarao, has issued an order in this regard. October 18 is a Sunday. This means government offices, schools, banks and other institutions across the state will remain closed for three consecutive days. Sandhi Puja to be held on October 19 for 48 minutes Kashi astrologer Pt. Rishi Dwivedi said the period between Maha Ashtami and Mahanavami during Navratri holds special religious importance. The last 24 minutes of Ashtami and the first 24 minutes of Navami together form the Sandhi Kaal, during which Sandhi Puja is performed. This year, Sandhi Puja will take place on October 19, from 10:27 am to 11:15 am. According to religious beliefs, Goddess Durga took the form of Chamunda during this period and killed the demons Chand and Mund. Therefore, worship during these 48 minutes is considered especially important. Devotees pray to Goddess Durga for happiness, peace and the well-being of their families. Devotees can complete their fast on October 20 or 21 Both Navami and Vijayadashami fall on October 20 this year. Devotees can perform the havan, worship and Purnahuti (the final offering in the ritual) on the morning of October 20, during Navami Tithi. However, the correct time to complete the Navratri fast depends on family traditions and religious practices. Religious scholar Vinay Pandey said Navratri begins on Pratipada of the Ashwin Shukla Paksha and continues with the worship of the nine forms of Goddess Durga until Navami. Due to changes in the timing of lunar dates, Navratri sometimes lasts eight days, nine days or even ten days. He explained that different traditions are followed for completing the fast. Some devotees break their fast on Dashami after performing the havan and Purnahuti, while others prefer to do so during a full Dashami Tithi. Therefore, devotees should follow their family traditions and religious beliefs to decide whether to complete their fast on October 20 or October 21. Goddess Durga to arrive on an elephant and leave on a rooster this Navratri Dr. Subhash Pandey of the Astrology Department at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) said that since Navratri begins on Sunday this year, Goddess Durga will arrive riding an elephant. According to religious beliefs, an elephant is a symbol of good rainfall, rich harvests and prosperity. It is also believed to bring purity to the surroundings and help devotees overcome illnesses and problems. Since Navratri will end on Tuesday, the goddess will leave riding a rooster, also known as a cock. 3 other things to know 1. Stability in India and the world According to astrological beliefs, Goddess Durga's arrival on an elephant may bring peace and stability to India and the world. The current atmosphere of global unrest may calm down, and enemy countries may begin talks and improve their relations. It may also help spread a sense of brotherhood in society. 2. Stronger financial conditions The goddess arriving on an elephant is also considered a symbol of wealth, prosperity and abundance. Therefore, people may see greater financial stability after Sharadiya Navratri. Markets such as the stock market and real estate may see growth, while new job opportunities may also emerge. 3. Political changes According to astrology, Goddess Durga's departure on a rooster may bring political changes in India and across the world. These changes are believed to be positive. The ongoing conflict between the ruling parties and the opposition may reduce, while greater stability may also be seen in global politics.
