Polish PM Donald Tusk to visit India from October 21 to 23, hold talks with PM Modi
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is set to visit India from October 21 to 23. During this visit, he will hold talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi. The discussions will focus on enhancing bilateral relations across various sectors, including trade and defense. Tusk will also meet with business stakeholders in Bengaluru and participate in business forums.

stories.title: Mississippi woman keeps $1.2m farm despite ex-husband’s claim after using it to finance their home
stories.summary: Ellen Harrison successfully retained sole ownership of her 432-acre Butler Road Farm after her divorce from Wiley Harrison. The Mississippi Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's ruling classifying the farm as non-marital property, given its purchase before their marriage. Wiley challenged the ruling, claiming marital asset status due to financial connections and alleged contributions. Courts evaluated the evidence and determined that such claims did not prove ownership.

stories.title: 'OIC being misused by Pakistan': India rejects 'malicious' remarks on J&K, flags credibility of agency
Shaquille O’Neal’s $24M Las Vegas youth complex nears completion
Manipur violence: Protesters place bodies outside CM's bungalow after militant attack
A 400-year-old mourning pendant resurfaces with a dead child's hair
Priest caught on CCTV sprinkling holy water on disputed fence as fight with neighbour escalates
stories.summary: A dispute over a metre-wide strip of land between a Russian Orthodox priest and his neighbour in West Yorkshire has escalated into police complaints, CCTV surveillance and criminal proceedings. The priest was also filmed sprinkling holy water near the disputed fence, which his wife described as an attempt to restore peace. With both households claiming ownership, the matter may now reach a civil court.

stories.title: Around 1575, a Mughal artist painted a cheetah family on cloth during Akbar's reign; about 450 years later, the tiny work from Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan's collection sold for nearly Rs 120 crore in London
stories.summary: A Family of Cheetahs, attributed to Basawan, was sold at Christie's auction for approximately Rs 120 crore. The painting, created during Mughal Emperor Akbar's reign, highlights wildlife in its natural habitat. This artwork signifies the Mughal interest in depicting nature rather than just royal figures or religious scenes. Its sale price dramatically exceeded the pre-auction estimate by 14 times, indicating high demand.

stories.title: 'Holiday mode on': BJP alleges Rahul Gandhi travelling abroad to meet 'chaos collaborators'
‘Product which failed every time’: Shivraj Chouhan mocks Rahul Gandhi for 'expiry date' remark
stories.summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan responded to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's prediction about the BJP's decline. Chouhan called Gandhi's remarks laughable, labeling him a failed product. Gandhi addressed a public gathering in Goa, urging voters to support Congress in the upcoming elections. He accused BJP leaders of corruption and electoral malpractice during his speech at the Congress’s ‘Goy Rakhon Yatra’ event.

stories.title: At 7, she was 'gifted' to Queen Victoria; 176 years later, her descendant revisits her life
stories.summary: In 1850, a seven-year-old African girl named Aina was presented to Queen Victoria as a diplomatic 'gift' after losing her family and spending two years in captivity. Renamed Sarah Forbes Bonetta, she grew up under royal protection but faced restrictions on her freedom. Now, 176 years later, a new biography is examining her life, while her great-great-grandson, Bayo Randle, reflects on her struggles, achievements and complicated relationship with the British monarchy.

stories.title: Russia’s finance minister Anton Siluanov named deputy PM in Putin’s reshuffle
Gas Station Mass Shooting: Two killed, three hurt at West Baltimore BP; liquor store attack adds to toll
stories.summary: A tragic shooting occurred at a gas station in West Baltimore, claiming the lives of two individuals and leaving three others injured. Police arrived promptly to find multiple victims suffering from gunshot wounds. Investigations indicate that the attack may have been carried out by two or three assailants armed with high-powered rifles.

stories.title: Tiger Shroff assassination bid: Why Mumbai Police can't get custody of Lawrence, Anmol Bishnoi
$3.1 billion St. Louis data centre plan faces court fight over 120-MW project
stories.summary: St. Louis is undergoing a notable shift with the establishment of several data centres throughout the region. However, community members have voiced considerable opposition, raising health and environmental issues linked to these facilities. Legal actions have been launched by residents and developers encountering permit restrictions, leading to new legislation governing the operation and placement of data centres. Amidst this turmoil, national debates about AI infrastructure's effects on communities intensify.

stories.title: Kandinsky painting sold under Nazi occupation returns to heirs, fetches £31.56m at London auction
stories.summary: A remarkable Wassily Kandinsky painting achieved a staggering £31.56 million at auction, after being returned to the Lewenstein heirs. This valuable artwork had a tumultuous history, changing ownership during World War II amid sales disputes. Following an independent inquiry, it was restituted to the family, underscoring persistent endeavors to reclaim art stolen during the Nazi era.

stories.title: Oregon teen, 16, earns Honor Medal after rescuing couple at 14
NBA coach Tyronn Lue transforms former segregated school into community centre
‘India is not Bangladesh or France’: Tharoor hits back at BJP, says opposition backs peaceful protest
Festive India unplugged: Experiential travel during Navratri and Dussehra
Tiger Shroff firing case: Oppn targets Fadnavis govt with 'jungle raj' claims
Radio tags reveal Amazon anacondas were spotted at just 17.7% of tracked locations
Indian-origin couple spent over $100,000 to open cafe in Australia; an arson attack has them crodwfunding for repairs
stories.summary: Ashish Sharma and Manali Purohit's dream of running their vegan cafe 'And Bodega' in Fitzroy North, Melbourne, turned tragic when it suffered extensive damage from an arson attack shortly after opening. This incident, linked to a nearby tobacco shop, cost them their life savings and brought additional theft. To recover, they initiated a crowdfunding campaign and are searching for new locations, buoyed by the unwavering support of their community.

stories.title: Camera giant Kodak operated a uranium-based nuclear device beneath its laboratory
stories.summary: For 31 years, Kodak operated a uranium-based research device beneath its Rochester laboratory, using it to examine materials and detect impurities. Installed in 1975 and shut down in 2006, the machine attracted public attention in 2012 because it contained highly enriched uranium. A new Popular Mechanics report explains how the device produced neutrons through nuclear fission but could not sustain a chain reaction independently, making it different from a conventional nuclear reactor.

stories.title: Texas rerouted a highway after taking their land; now owners want it back
‘Shame on petty men’: Shashi Tharoor slams Centre’s silence Indian-origin Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay's Nobel win
BJP veteran LK Advani discharged from Delhi hospital after health improves
stories.summary: BJP veteran and former deputy prime minister LK Advani, 98, was discharged from Delhi’s Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Monday after his health improved. The BJP stalwart Advani was admitted on October 16 with a chest infection and remained under medical observation, including a stay in the intensive care unit (ICU).

stories.title: ‘Protocol, not power’: Ex-IMF director rebuts Pakistan’s 'historic milestone' claim over 2027 leadership
6 in 10 men over 45 unaware of their prostate cancer screening status: Survey
stories.summary: 69% unable to name a single risk factor; only 1 in 6 report ever being screened

stories.title: Tiger Shroff shooting: The Salman Khan connection and a trail of threats linked to Lawrence Bishnoi
stories.summary: The firing at Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai has brought the Lawrence Bishnoi gang’s alleged threats against Bollywood personalities back into focus. A purported claim of responsibility linked the attack to Shroff’s association with Salman Khan. The incident has revived scrutiny of past threats against Khan, shootings involving his associates and the gang’s alleged network across borders, while police verify the claims.

stories.title: Is college worth it in 2026
‘Will track them down’: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis vows action over Tiger Shroff firing, flags overseas links
British man told no action needed after Brexit, now hides in caravan to fight deportation from Sweden
stories.summary: Mark Smith, who moved to Sweden seeking a better life, is now facing possible deportation. After being misinformed about Brexit residency requirements, he and his wife now live in hiding. The couple's application for residency was denied on grounds of not being married at the time. There are broader concerns about the treatment of British citizens under Sweden's residency rules post-Brexit.

stories.title: Civilian Toll From Drone Strikes: HRW alleges Mali, Russia killed 94 civilians; strikes more than doubled
stories.summary: Mali's armed forces and their Russian allies have intensified drone strikes against insurgents, resulting in civilian deaths. Human Rights Watch reported that civilian casualties doubled from the previous year during this period. Some drone strikes targeted marketplaces and health centers, causing significant collateral damage. Insurgents have also been implicated in executing soldiers and committing abuses amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: AIIMS removes uterus of 98-cm-tall woman through keyhole surgery
stories.summary: A 44-year-old woman endured extreme menstrual cramps attributed to deep pelvic endometriosis and adenomyosis. Due to her osteoporosis, any surgical intervention posed fracture risks, necessitating a cautious approach. A laparoscopic hysterectomy at AIIMS was performed, considering her petite frame and bone weakness. The successful procedure lasted about 90 minutes; she was carefully positioned and discharged three days after, recovering well.

stories.title: 'Laal Hit Janta Party': New outfit emerges to counter CJP's protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Species Fund Beats Habitat Target: Evaluation finds 4,800ha restored; 51,000 people engaged
stories.summary: A transformative £25 million conservation initiative has revitalized wildlife across England. By restoring vast areas and planting over 127,500 trees, the programme fostered community engagement with nature for more than 51,000 individuals. Various projects played a critical role in reconnecting segmented habitats and enhancing wetlands and rivers, underscoring the necessity of strategic investment in preserving thriving ecosystems.

stories.title: Tiger Shroff shooting: Videos piece together moments before, during and after attack
IMD launches WebGIS-based decision support system to improve cyclone disaster preparedness
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department has launched an advanced WebGIS platform designed to boost disaster preparedness against cyclones. This Decision Support System will deliver vital cyclone alerts and marine weather updates to various stakeholders. By enhancing public awareness of the risks and effects associated with severe weather, it aims to further curtail cyclone-related fatalities, which have dropped dramatically in recent years.

stories.title: SIT files 1000-page chargesheet in Kishtwar teen’s rape and abortion death
Muizzu begins 3-day Pak visit tomorrow, 1st Maldives prez trip in over a decade
France counts cost of worst unrest in years as tensions flare again in Paris
Congress’s post-truth politics: Manufacturing distrust, undermining democracy
Phone on speaker in train? You may be penalised, jailed
Shinde meets Tiger Shroff after firing incident; pics show actor with bandages
CJP leaders’ bail hearing put off as magistrate cites threat to life
Woman returns to her former North Carolina school, now senior housing, nearly 60 years later
stories.summary: Cassandra Henderson has returned to her old school, now transformed into Dillard School Senior Apartments. After sitting empty for twenty years, this historic building has emerged as a vital haven for seniors, featuring thoughtful designs and amenities tailored to their needs. Originally a cornerstone for Black education, this repurposing highlights how adaptive reuse can effectively tackle housing shortages.

stories.title: When John Legend donated $500,000 to give Ohio students a stage
stories.summary: John Legend has pledged $500,000 to revitalize a former high school auditorium in Springfield, Ohio, transforming it into the John Legend Theater. This venue now hosts youth concerts and community events, reflecting Legend's personal ties to the space, where he performed as a child. With state-of-the-art production facilities, the theater fosters arts education, empowering local students to showcase their talents since its grand opening.

stories.title: Omar Abdullah seeks action over attack on J&K-bound bus in Haryana
Missouri woman accused of pointing gun at neighbour during property-line dispute
stories.summary: A dispute over property lines in St. Charles County turned alarming when a neighbour was allegedly shot at. Facing felony charges, Paula Kohensky is at the center of this escalation tied to a fence repair matter. The ongoing tension between the neighbours is highlighted by surveillance footage that contradicts her version of events. A preliminary hearing is set for December 2, as the case unfolds.

stories.title: Indiana legal secretary faces 42 felonies over alleged fake court orders and stolen client fees
stories.summary: Following a lengthy three-year investigation, Heather Ann Textor, a legal secretary, has been taken into custody for alleged fraudulent activities. She is accused of forging court documents and misappropriating client funds intended for legal fees. The investigation was sparked when a local resident submitted a counterfeit expungement petition to the state police, leading to further scrutiny of suspicious transactions that funneled money into Textor's personal accounts.

stories.title: John Oliver bought $15 million in medical debt for $60,000, then erased bills for 9,000 people
stories.summary: In June 2016, John Oliver's show made headlines by acquiring nearly $15 million of unpaid medical debt for only $60,000. This debt was funneled through a newly established company aimed at giving it away. Rather than pursuing payments, the debt was assigned to a nonprofit dedicated to alleviating medical debt, drawing attention to critical flaws in the American healthcare system.

stories.title: Rare hawks nest in California county after 30 years as abandoned farmland gets a new life
stories.summary: A California floodplain restoration project launched in 2023 has recorded its first confirmed nesting Swainson’s hawks in Shasta County in about 30 years. More than 32,000 native trees and plants were introduced across 150 acres of damaged land near the Sacramento River. Conservationists have also recorded rare indigo buntings breeding at the site, raising hopes for wildlife recovery.

stories.title: Colorado judge blocks solar power lines through shared easement, bars trespassing
Espionage case on Army officer’s wife, lens on ‘China links’
Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
Aretha Franklin’s Detroit estate sold for $300,000, now restored for $2M+
Indiana father leaves everything to fiancee; daughter's failed fight leaves her with $22,208 bill
stories.summary: An Indiana woman who challenged her late father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her legal battle. Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208 in attorney fees after failing to prove the will was invalid. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the ruling and ordered her to pay additional legal fees after finding serious problems with her appeal.

stories.title: In 2023, California moved 246 endangered abalone; by 2026, counts rose from 54 to 302, with juveniles found
stories.summary: In 2023, researchers relocated 246 black abalone to a protected coastal site to encourage population growth. After three years, surveys recorded an increase in individuals from 54 to 302, showing signs of recovery. Juvenile abalone were also found, which raises hopes for future reproduction. This project involved collaboration among several scientific organizations and demonstrated the feasibility of habitat restoration. Ongoing monitoring will be crucial to determine the population's long-term sustainability.

stories.title: London woman loses boundary dispute over 48cm strip of land claimed by neighbours
stories.summary: In a surprising turn of events, a homeowner in Surbiton, London, lost a legal dispute concerning a narrow 48-centimetre strip of land. It was determined that the neighbours' kitchen extension had effectively claimed squatters' rights, having occupied the land uncontested for over two decades. The First-tier Tribunal's decision highlights crucial insights into property borders and emphasizes the importance of diligent title plan checks for prospective buyers to avoid future complications.

stories.title: 'Stop politics of shoot and scoot': BJP slams Congress over readable electoral roll issue
‘Should focus on actual criminals’: Dipke jabs police after shots fired at Tiger Shroff
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke expressed his frustrations on social media regarding the recent shooting incident involving actor Tiger Shroff. The attack occurred while Shroff was leaving a birthday celebration in Mumbai, resulting in injuries to his driver and a fan. Three assailants on motorcycles fled the scene shortly after the incident. Police are investigating a social media post claiming responsibility for the attack and threatening others in the film industry.

stories.title: 'Barged in, cut power': AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj claims Delhi Police harassing Bengali community in CR Park
Akshay Kumar meets Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami, discusses state’s film policy
stories.summary: Akshay Kumar recently met Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to discuss the state's film policy. The discussion aimed to identify ways to attract film productions and enhance local employment opportunities. During the meeting, Dhami highlighted the state's natural beauty and cultural heritage as advantages for filmmakers. Akshay is currently shooting a comedy film in Uttarakhand that features actor Raashii Khanna.

stories.title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
stories.summary: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam expressed his willingness to contest in the upcoming Manipur Assembly elections. He stated his decision was for the future of the state and would respect the party's ticket offering. Akoijam currently faces serious allegations of sexual harassment and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University. Multiple complaints from female students prompted a police investigation into his conduct and actions.

stories.title: Michigan father's free Halloween display draws 18,000 visitors, sparks dispute with city officials
stories.summary: Nate Taylor launched Dead Ends on Spruce, a Halloween experience dedicated to families seeking a safe and fun outing. The festive display, equipped with animatronics and eerie soundscapes, started after an ad for complimentary decorations. Despite legal hurdles imposed by city officials, Taylor persevered. Last October, the event delighted around 18,000 visitors and provided special sessions for children with special needs, emphasizing inclusivity in community celebrations.

stories.title: Amit Shah to meet families of Punjab drug-trade victims on Oct 19, vows crackdown on ‘chitta’ trade
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to meet families affected by drug-related deaths in Punjab. Multiple incidents have highlighted the growing issue of 'chitta' trade in the state. Recent deaths involve a father of a drug addict and two anti-drug activists. Shah has criticized the Punjab government for its handling of the drug crisis and promised action.

stories.title: Rajnath to represent India at SCO council of heads of govt meeting in Tajikistan today
Global uranium production to dip by 50% by 2040 as demand set to double, says IAEA report; forecast could pinch India too
Eva Longoria’s $55,000 fund for six women grows to $525,000 in loans, supporting 150 jobs
stories.summary: Eva Longoria’s foundation and nonprofit lender Accessity launched a $55,000 loan fund in 2013 to help six Latina entrepreneurs start or grow their businesses. Since then, the initiative has facilitated 65 loans worth nearly $525,000 and helped create or maintain 150 jobs. A new three-year, $500,000 grant will expand business training and financial support for Latina entrepreneurs.

stories.title: Centre issues advisory to Meta, asks it to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram
stories.summary: The Centre has mandated Meta to ensure diverse recommendation algorithms for users on its platforms. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released an advisory emphasizing due diligence under the IT Rules. It highlighted the need for rapid identification and review of content with public disturbance potential. Additionally, Meta must assist law enforcement agencies by providing necessary information promptly.

stories.title: Lost Eloise portrait found in dumpster sells for $100,000 after decades in closet
stories.summary: In a fascinating twist of fate, Eloise's original portrait, crafted by Hilary Knight in 1956, mysteriously disappeared during a Junior League Ball in 1960. Rediscovered in a dumpster, it lay dormant in Knight's closet for years, only to be brought back to life at a 2017 exhibition at the New-York Historical Society. Its subsequent auction at Bonhams in 2018 for $100,000 underscores the unpredictable journey and enduring value of art.

stories.title: Insurer denies heart procedure for 12-year-old with Kawasaki disease
stories.summary: Rowan Lowry, a 12-year-old boy, urgently needs a stent procedure to address complications stemming from Kawasaki disease. His family faces an insurance denial categorizing the procedure as medically unnecessary. Undeterred, they plan to seek treatment at Boston Children's Hospital, driven by their concern for Rowan's deteriorating health and the fear of open-heart surgery. Determined, they vow to advocate fiercely for their son's well-being despite the financial strain.

stories.title: Shots fired at Tiger Shroff, actor's driver hurt; Bishnoi gang claims responsibility - top developments
Teen Builds Rural Stem Access: Ontario student launches Project RISE; initiative widens STEM opportunities
stories.summary: At just 17 years old, Amara Wilson-Zegil is on a mission to bridge the gap in STEM education for children in rural areas. With an impressive outreach to over 1,800 students through robotics initiatives and camps, she has launched Project RISE. This groundbreaking initiative aims to combat educational disparities by providing vital tech experiences, ensuring more youth in Northern Ontario can access quality STEM opportunities.

stories.title: US visit after settler attacks: Officials go to Taybeh; violence keeps rising
CJP's Dipke accuses state of delaying proceedings to prevent release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke accused the state of deliberately prolonging the arrests of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He claimed they are using delaying tactics to obstruct court proceedings and prevent their release. The Cockroach Janta Party plans to take legal action if the individuals are not released soon. CJP's legal head, Ratna Singh, criticized the Special Executive Magistrate for arbitrary behavior during the hearings.

stories.title: 'Attempts to weaken India's unity cannot be accepted': RSS leader Indresh Kumar on anti-SIR protests
Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
stories.summary: Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 and send its first astronaut for a space mission. The astronaut, selected from candidates trained in China, is expected to participate in scientific experiments. Cooperation with China enhances Pakistan's aspirations in space exploration and technological advancement. Additionally, plans for establishing the first Space Museum at the University of Narowal were announced to promote scientific awareness.

stories.title: CISF to reorganise eight territorial sectors into specialised functional units from November 1
stories.summary: Starting November 1, the Central Industrial Security Force will reorganize into functional sectors to enhance security management. This restructuring aims to address the specialized needs of various industries and government installations. Eleven sectors will be transformed to focus on specific sectors like coal, power, and petroleum. Existing arrangements for the Department of Atomic Energy and airports will remain unchanged. The move is expected to improve operational oversight and sector-specific expertise.

stories.title: 'Nothing to do with Imran': MNS after Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid legal troubles for actor's nephew
Brazilian man sells all, travels 1,200 miles to marry online girlfriend, discovers she was AI-generated
stories.summary: A Brazilian man sold all his belongings and travelled over 1,200 miles to meet the online girlfriend he hoped to marry. Edimar Martins, 49, discovered that the woman, featured on a TikTok account with around 300,000 followers, was AI-generated. After running out of money, he received assistance to return home but remains hopeful about finding love.

stories.title: Florida appeals court overturns $2,675 monthly alimony after a 249-day marriage
stories.summary: A recent decision by a Florida appeals court reversed an alimony order for a short marriage lasting 249 days. The court found insufficient evidence regarding the former wife's need for financial support. The trial court had awarded nine months of temporary alimony based on prior cases instead of specific proof. The appeals court emphasized the importance of individual cases and relevant evidence in such rulings.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Rijiju alleges violence plot during protests, CM Suvendu orders probe into home guards after stampede & more
stories.summary: Kiren Rijiju alleged that opposition leaders are conspiring to incite violence amidst the Special Intensive Revision protests. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has ordered an investigation following a tragic stampede in Kolkata. Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and others of voter fraud while urging public support for Congress in upcoming elections.

stories.title: Florida opens $191.8M water plant to protect the Matanzas River and conserve drinking water
stories.summary: St. Johns County Utilities officials celebrated the completion of the State Road 207 Water Reclamation Facility. This facility, costing $191.8 million, will treat wastewater and provide reclaimed water for irrigation purposes. The project aims to reduce dependence on the Floridan Aquifer, especially during ongoing drought conditions. Capacity of the facility can be expanded to meet future demand while preventing nutrient pollution in local waters.

stories.title: 'Refrain from taking photos, take shelter': India advisory amid Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia
Michigan court allows Kalamazoo County to seize a family’s lakefront cottage for park expansion
stories.summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals has confirmed Kalamazoo County's legal right to acquire a residential cottage located near Prairie View County Park, ending a protracted legal battle. County officials want to integrate the cottage into their plans for park expansion, but the owners have raised objections, arguing that the public purpose claims are obsolete. The issue of fair compensation continues to be debated if a mutual valuation is not achieved.

stories.title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
stories.summary: Egypt announced its willingness to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia to ensure its security and stability. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi convened the National Defence Council to discuss potential support amid Houthi assaults. These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited.

stories.title: ‘What's the need for SSR?’ Akhilesh Yadav says BJP conspiring to add fake votes, urges SP workers to be vigilant
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has accused the BJP of manipulating electoral rolls by adding fake votes and deleting genuine votes. He urged party workers to remain vigilant at polling booths and defend against electoral malpractice. Yadav raised concerns over the Election Commission's rationale for revising electoral rolls, questioning the need for it. He also criticized the BJP government's performance on various issues impacting citizens, including education and corruption.

stories.title: Menopause is normal, suffering through it shouldn't be
Meet Sgiath: The mountain rescue Labrador who has won IFAW’s 2026 Animal of the Year Award
stories.summary: Sgiath, a remarkable six-year-old black Labrador, has recently made headlines for her extraordinary ability to detect invasive sea squirt, leading her to win the prestigious 2026 Animal of the Year Award. Partnering with marine ecologist Dr. Texa Sim, Sgiath's keen sense of smell plays a vital role in identifying this invasive organism. Her early detection skills contribute significantly to marine conservation efforts.

stories.title: In 2001, Tony Bennett and his wife opened an arts school for 250 students; how it looks 25 years later
stories.summary: Tony Bennett and Susan Benedetto co-founded the Frank Sinatra School of the Arts in 2001 in New York. The school offers specialized training in various art forms while maintaining a strong academic curriculum. Students can major in dance, drama, film, fine art, vocal music, or instrumental music. The school moved to a permanent facility in 2009, equipped with state-of-the-art spaces for performance and production.

stories.title: Graft charges at home, arrest in Qatar: Former Bangladesh Air Force chief held
Texas Supreme Court to decide if city can seize land for a privately run golf facility
stories.summary: The Texas Supreme Court will examine an eminent domain case involving Westworth Village's attempt to acquire land from Jim Burgess for a golf facility. Following a previous ruling that deemed the taking unconstitutional on public use grounds, the case delves into the legality of local governments appropriating private property for private enterprise projects. This decision holds the potential to set a major precedent for eminent domain laws throughout Texas.

stories.title: ‘Where did the 56-inch chest go?’ Rahul targets PM Modi, Shah in Goa, says BJP’s ‘expiry date’ is near
JD Vance’s immigration tiger is turning on its rider
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance admitted his rhetoric on H-1B visas was flawed during a recent town hall event. An Indian-American woman challenged him on his stance, suggesting it scapegoats immigrants. Vance defended his position by claiming he was criticizing corporate practices rather than foreign workers. His remarks have led to significant backlash from various groups regarding his mixed heritage.

stories.title: Russia sold Alaska for peanuts. Now it guards America against Moscow
stories.summary: In 1867, Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, reflecting strategic concerns. The decision stemmed from fears of potential conflict with Britain during the Crimean War. Subsequent discoveries of natural resources transformed Alaska's economic importance significantly over the years. Alaska emerged as a crucial military platform for the United States against the Russian Far East.

stories.title: In 2015, Taylor Swift gave $50,000 to Seattle Symphony; 11 years later, its school programme lives on
stories.summary: In December 2015, Taylor Swift made a notable donation of $50,000 to the Seattle Symphony. This contribution supported the Link Up education programme, which introduces orchestral music to young students. The funding also benefitted the musicians' pension fund as part of the symphony's broader mission. Over the years, Link Up has successfully engaged thousands of children through interactive music experiences.

stories.title: Houston’s vacant lot becomes a colourful park built from discarded art
Charity shop raises £85,860 from donated banknotes, including one featuring young Queen Elizabeth II
stories.summary: An anonymous donation of nearly 160 lots of rare banknotes to a British Heart Foundation charity shop in Edinburgh has raised £85,860 at auction. The collection included a banknote featuring a young Queen Elizabeth II and rare currency specimens from Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Staff initially had no idea of its value. The proceeds will support research into heart and circulatory diseases.

stories.title: The Dimple factor: Can she crack BJP's women-voter fortress?
stories.summary: Dimple Yadav is stepping into the spotlight with a heightened political presence within the Samajwadi Party. As she actively campaigns and addresses rallies in anticipation of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, her efforts aim to connect with women voters—a key demographic for the party's triumph. Her initiatives are centered on empowering women and addressing social issues that speak to the electorate.

stories.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.

stories.title: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu over alleged links to foreign intelligence operatives
Sudden rain, poor crowd management likely led to Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: What we know so far
'India is neither Bangladesh nor France': Rijiju alleges plot to trigger violence during anti-SIR protests
‘With help of God & your prayers’: Pope makes first public appearance after surgery
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV recently made his first public appearance following surgery for lung cancer. He expressed gratitude for the prayers and support he received during his recovery. The pontiff confirmed that he will gradually return to his duties with continued prayer and divine assistance. His next major engagement is planned for November, which includes an overseas trip to South America.

stories.title: Gwalior temple tragedy: CM Mohan Yadav orders removal of City SP, suspension of 8 others after 14 killed
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav has ordered the removal of nine police personnel due to negligence. A truck incident at Sheetla Mata temple resulted in 14 deaths and 28 injuries, prompting immediate action. Compensation of Rs 4 lakh has been announced for the families of the deceased. The chief minister stated that a detailed investigation would be initiated to identify responsible parties.

stories.title: A tiny patch could help rescuers perform CPR better; student invention wins $10,000
stories.summary: Four University of Washington students have developed CPRight, a wallet-sized patch that uses LED lights to guide rescuers during CPR. The device provides real-time feedback on chest compression depth and rate without requiring additional equipment. The invention won the $10,000 undergraduate first prize at the 2026 Collegiate Inventors Competition, which also recognised innovations in cancer treatment, rehabilitation and neurological monitoring.

stories.title: 'Could not prevent regime change within own party': Devendra Fadnavis mocks Uddhav Thackeray
Barbra Streisand center leads $7.5m NIH study on women’s healthy aging
Rare I.M. Pei mansion in Texas hits market for $22 million
stories.summary: A unique Fort Worth estate designed by architect I.M. Pei is now listed for sale at $22 million. This is the first time the property has been available since its construction in 1969. Known as Westover House, it is one of only three private residences created by Pei. The home features spacious living areas, multiple bedrooms and modern amenities across nearly four acres.

stories.title: After India’s strong protest, Vance clarifies H-1B 'indentured servants' remark
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged that his rhetoric regarding H-1B visa workers was imperfect and apologised. He clarified that his remarks were aimed at companies exploiting the system rather than the workers themselves. Following criticisms from India, he stressed the importance of protecting foreign professionals’ rights while also considering American jobs. India’s Ministry of External Affairs expressed strong objections to Vance's terminology.

stories.title: ‘Unacceptable’: Chirag Paswan slams Imran Khan’s role in Mumbai protests, backs ‘Leave India’ notice
When Jennifer Lopez helped launch a telemedicine network for children in Panama
stories.summary: In 2012, Jennifer Lopez and her sister Lynda Lopez donated telemedicine equipment through their family foundation to improve healthcare access for children in Panama. The initiative connected hospitals and health centres across the country with specialists at Children's Hospital Los Angeles, allowing doctors to seek medical advice remotely. The programme also supported medical training, specialist consultations and knowledge-sharing among healthcare professionals.

stories.title: She bought a glass vase for £1 at Scottish car-boot sale, used it as a plant pot; it sold for £32,450
stories.summary: In 2008, a woman bought a glass vase for just £1 at a car-boot sale in Dumfries, Scotland, and used it as a plant pot. She later discovered it was a rare 1929 creation by French designer René Lalique. After experts valued it at £25,000 on Antiques Roadshow, the vase sold at Christie’s in London for £32,450.

stories.title: Balochistan unrest: Teacher's killing by 'Pak-backed death squads' sparks outrage
Utah couple built a $2 million backyard pool with a 90-foot mountain and a scuba-diving tunnel
stories.summary: In Utah, a dedicated couple has poured $2 million into an extraordinary backyard pool designed specifically for scuba diving. This stunning installation boasts a remarkable 90-foot artificial mountain, five magnificent waterfalls, and an exhilarating underwater tunnel. By creating such a bespoke sanctuary, they provide a fantastic recreational escapade for scuba lovers, complete with a lazy river and a fully equipped kitchen set within the mountain's embrace.

stories.title: Florida commits $8.7 million to preserve two working ranches
stories.summary: Florida has enacted a permanent conservation measure for two significant ranches located in Manatee and Highlands counties, encompassing nearly 1,500 acres. This initiative is designed to safeguard local agricultural practices and boost the economy. Through the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, the state aims to uphold agricultural land under conservation, as stressed by Commissioner Wilton Simpson for forthcoming generations, highlighting Florida's intent to preserve its agricultural legacy sustainably.

stories.title: Trade & connectivity in focus: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO meet in Tajikistan
stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh's upcoming trip to Dushanbe, Tajikistan, marks a pivotal event as he leads India's delegation to the 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting on October 19 and 20. The discussions will highlight crucial themes of trade, economic collaboration, and improved connectivity among SCO nations, providing India a platform to advocate for enhanced trade partnerships and innovative strategies across sectors.

stories.title: Marilyn Monroe-linked home with four bedrooms and a private pool sells for $2.81 million
stories.summary: A Palm Springs house linked to Hollywood actress Marilyn Monroe has sold for $2.81 million, months after being listed for $3.3 million. Local designer Violet Moran purchased the four-bedroom property and plans to restore it while preserving its original features. Built in 1961, the house is known as the "Marilyn Monroe Doll House", although reports have questioned whether the actress ever owned it.

stories.title: ‘Anti-India Ravana’ posters put up in Lucknow with Rahul Gandhi, Elon Musk among faces- watch
Mother left two sons out of her will after family dispute; New Jersey court sides with daughters
stories.summary: A New Jersey mother who initially planned to divide her estate equally among her four children changed her will in 2016, excluding both sons after their relationship deteriorated. Following her death in 2024, the sons challenged the decision, alleging that their sisters had influenced her. One daughter had been her sole caregiver since 1996. However, on October 16, 2026, a New Jersey appeals court upheld the revised will.

stories.title: Demi Moore’s Idaho home has a river, mountain views and wild elk in her backyard
stories.summary: Demi Moore has chosen to settle in Hailey, Idaho, immersed in the enchanting landscape of Sun Valley. She revels in the outdoor experiences available at her riverside retreat, including swimming, kayaking, and fly-fishing throughout the summer months. Initially intended as a vacation haven, the property has become her permanent residence. The area seamlessly marries rustic allure with an artistic vibe, drawing in art lovers for gallery excursions.

stories.title: 5-year-old asks for a baseball field, Ohio dad spends $30,000 building one in backyard
stories.summary: An Ohio father spent nearly two years and around $30,000 building a baseball field in his backyard after his five-year-old son requested one. Jason Kidd transformed his property into a playing field with professional-grade clay, regulation bases and a raised pitcher's mound. Despite complaints from neighbours and unfinished additions, Kidd said the project was about spending time with his son and teaching him baseball.

stories.title: Side Hustle Grows Steadily: $500 yard games fund Little Party Co.; she keeps corporate job
stories.summary: Vanessa Romano launched Little Party Co. with just a $500 investment in outdoor party games, inspired by social media trends. Within a few months, her savvy approach catapulted her revenue to over $9,000. She strategically reinvested her profits while balancing a full-time corporate career and family. Rather than abandoning her corporate job, Romano embraces both roles, demonstrating that entrepreneurship can flourish without choosing between them.

stories.title: 12-year-old saves mother after she collapses at 60mph, wins courage award
Gwalior accident kills 14 devotees: PM Modi announces Rs 2 lakh relief for kin
AI cuts job demand in exposed occupations by nearly 10% across Asia: IMF report
California farm earns 10 times more leasing land for solar than growing wheat
stories.summary: In Tulare County, California, the Changala family farm has embraced a transformative shift from dry-farmed wheat to solar energy. Driven by financial incentives, solar leases are now yielding significantly greater income compared to traditional crops. Facing water scarcity in the San Joaquin Valley, farmers are increasingly investing in solar technologies.

stories.title: Amit Shah visits injured after deadly stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal
In 1968, Cassandra Henderson graduated from a North Carolina school; 58 years later, she returned to its restored building, now 53 senior apartments
stories.summary: After years away, Cassandra Henderson has made her way back to Yanceyville, North Carolina, settling into the revitalized Dillard School Apartments. Originally a school from 1949 until 2002, this historical building has now been transformed into 53 affordable housing units for seniors, tackling the local housing crisis. This renovation not only honors the past but also strengthens community ties by providing necessary living spaces.

stories.title: How a Brooklyn crypto cop took down a global scam network
Two oil tankers on fire after hitting mines: Iran’s Guards
Zelenskyy terms restricting military use of Starlink in Ukraine deliberate
FSSAI may curb sugar in baby food, set pesticide caps for tea
Trump blocking Russia curbs historic moment: Putin envoy
One teacher, multiple languages: NCERT eyes new training model
Cost-of-living protests: Italian police clash with protesters in Milan, Bologna
stories.summary: Protests against inflation, low wages, and public service issues turned violent in multiple Italian cities. In Milan, protests erupted in Piazza Duomo where demonstrators clashed with police and vandalized property. Bologna saw similar unrest, with hooded youths attacking the central railway station and throwing projectiles at security forces. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence while supporting peaceful demonstrations.

stories.title: FSSAI cracks down on Priyagold biscuit maker
San Diego weighs $4.2B project with 4,254 homes and $460M in public upgrades
stories.summary: San Diego is pushing forward with an ambitious redevelopment project for 48.5 acres surrounding Pechanga Arena. This initiative aims to introduce 4,254 housing units, a significant number of which will be affordable. In addition to a new 16,000-seat arena, the plan includes approximately $460 million in upgrades to local infrastructure. The goal is to foster a more walkable community with improved public spaces.

stories.title: Crowd, rain or misleading announcement: What led to Kolkata stampede tragedy?
Nonstop Delhi-Mumbai drive may have to wait until December 2029
SC: No need for nod to prosecute govt official seeking bribe
In 2016, Muhammad Ali’s former training camp was bought for $520,000; in 2019 it opened as Fighter’s Heaven
stories.summary: Mike Madden's dedication to preserving sports history shines brightly as he invests $1.5 million into restoring Fighter's Heaven, the legendary training camp originally founded by Muhammad Ali in 1972. After years of neglect, the camp reopened to an enthusiastic public in June 2019, earning praise from Pennsylvania’s State Historic Preservation Office for its cultural importance.

stories.title: Rare gold LEGO mask found in donated jewellery bag sold for $18,101
stories.summary: A small gold LEGO mask found inside a donated jewellery bag at a Goodwill store in Pennsylvania turned out to be a rare collector's item. Initially listed for $14.95, the 14-karat gold Bionicle Kanohi Hau mask attracted bids from collectors and eventually sold for $18,101 in March 2024. Only 30 such masks were produced in 2001.

stories.title: Prices of 137 cancer drugs to fall by up to 70% from November 9
Internet is fundamental right of all, even children: Supreme Court
Martha’s Vineyard rejects 54-acre housing plan after seven marathon meetings
stories.summary: Martha's Vineyard's planning board has turned down the Katama Meadows housing initiative after thorough discussions. This project sought to meet housing demands through a mix of affordable and market-rate homes catering to essential workers. However, environmental concerns regarding nitrogen pollution and the inclusion of luxury properties raised significant opposition, leading to the decision. The land remains with the developers, who may consider a revised proposal in the future.

stories.title: SC panel opens web portal for complaints on July NEET protests
Legal profession is not for faint-hearted: CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU
19 killed in Kolkata stampede; CM Suvendu announces jobs, Rs 25 lakh for kin
Drone LiDAR reveals three unregistered Aboriginal rock shelters in Australia's rugged Blue Mountains
stories.summary: Researchers utilized drone technology to discover three previously unregistered Aboriginal rock shelters in the Blue Mountains region, revealing significant cultural heritage. Collaboration with the Dharug Custodian Aboriginal Corporation ensured accurate documentation of red hand stencils and stone artifacts. This innovative approach may improve archaeological surveys in difficult-to-navigate areas, thereby preserving cultural heritage. Ongoing efforts will assess the method's applicability to different Australian landscapes, ensuring continued protection.

stories.title: Ariana Grande sends Christmas gifts to Manchester children years after arena attack
stories.summary: Ariana Grande maintains a tradition of sending Christmas gifts to children in hospitals across Greater Manchester. Her donations reached four hospitals, including Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital. Grande began this charitable connection following the tragic Manchester Arena attack in 2017, which claimed 22 lives. Over the years, her repeated contributions have comforted young patients during difficult festive seasons.

stories.title: 1923 Aus church transformed into a $950,000 home is up for sale
stories.summary: Nestled in Tyabb, Victoria, a stunning transformation has taken place as a historic 1923 Methodist church is now a three-bedroom haven ready for new owners. This charming residence boasts impressive cathedral ceilings, original windows, and contemporary kitchen features. Perfect for hosting, it includes a spacious living area and a dedicated bedroom wing, all while preserving a landmark rich in history—including its past as a Sunday school and dance venue.

stories.title: 'Do something. You can’t die like this': flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchar recounts cockpit attack
Bob Dylan and his brother bought a 25-acre Scottish estate for £2.2 million; after pandemic it was sold for £4.26 million
stories.summary: In December 2023, Bob Dylan and his brother David Zimmerman listed their expansive Aultmore House estate for an impressive £4.257 million. This stunning 25-acre property, featuring 16 bedrooms, is nestled in the picturesque Cairngorms National Park. Since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic, the siblings had not returned to the mansion, prompting their decision to sell.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia executes five nationals on terrorism charges, death toll hits 188
stories.summary: Five men were executed in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province for terrorism-related charges after their convictions were upheld. The total number of executions in the kingdom has now reached 188 this year, marking a significant increase. According to the Ministry of Interior, these men were convicted of serious crimes against security personnel and were affiliated with a foreign terrorist organization.

stories.title: 'He kept on hitting': Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar reveals what happened mid-flight as he was stabbed
stories.summary: Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot during a routine Flydubai flight, which he initially misinterpreted. As he attempted to defend himself, he lost consciousness amidst his desperate fight for survival. Other crew members intervened and helped regain control of the aircraft after he opened the cockpit door. The pilot expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received after safely landing in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: 'AIADMK would welcome Dhanush with both hands', says Rajendra Balaji
stories.summary: During a recent press conference, AIADMK leader K T Rajendra Balaji expressed enthusiasm about actor Dhanush possibly entering politics. He mentioned that the party would gladly accept Dhanush's involvement, highlighting the significant appeal actors like him have over the youth. Additionally, it was observed that Dhanush has rebranded his fan club to align with his evolving public persona, showcasing his readiness for greater engagement.

stories.title: 'Thoughts with those who have lost their loved ones': PM Modi on Kolkata stampede
stories.summary: The incident occurred around 7.40 pm in the Girish Park police station area amid heavy crowds of pandal visitors and rainfall. As rain began, people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede, a senior police officer told PTI. All the injured were rescued and taken to Calcutta Medical College for treatment.

stories.title: Kolkata Durga Puja Stampede: 19 dead; PM Modi, Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee express grief
stories.summary: In a heartbreaking incident at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, a stampede claimed the lives of at least 19 people and left 25 others injured amid a surge of visitors driven by panic from heavy rains. Rescue efforts were promptly initiated, and medical staff rushed the injured to hospitals.

stories.title: US man accused of drugging college student with fentanyl, raping her before death
stories.summary: Moises Freire, who was not a student at the Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), allegedly gave the drug to student Annabel Richter and her roommate at their dormitory in Manhattan's Chelsea neighbourhood on the night of March 18. Both women lost consciousness and were taken to hospital. Richter never regained consciousness and died on March 21, according to the indictment cited by the Manhattan US Attorney's Office.

stories.title: Sabarimala temple opens for Thulam month rituals; CM Satheesan offers prayers
stories.summary: The revered Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple was opened on Saturday for the rituals of the Thulam month, drawing numerous devotees eager to pay their respects. Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan, along with other esteemed guests, visited the shrine for prayers. The temple's opening for devotees is scheduled for 5 am on Sunday, coinciding with Mahanavami and Vijayadashami, a unique occurrence in many decades.

stories.title: Kolkata pandal stampede: Heavy rush amid rain led to deadly incident - top developments
stories.summary: A chaotic stampede unfolded at the Sarada Park Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata due to a crowd surge, leading to at least 1 deaths and 15 injuries. Emergency services transported the injured to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital for immediate medical assistance. The West Bengal health minister, alongside other political leaders, responded by visiting the scene and the hospital.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu BJP slams ministers for allowing Muslim aide in skull cap into temple
stories.summary: The BJP alleged that the incident, which took place on Saturday, went against a Madras high court order issued in January 2024 that restricts non-Hindus from proceeding beyond the temple’s flagmast unless they submit an undertaking affirming their faith in the deity and their willingness to follow Hindu customs. The party also claimed that the entry violated the temple’s dress code and religious traditions.

stories.title: Blind man turns 1,000 job rejections into award-winning accessibility business
‘Taking away right to vote, protest’: Uddhav backs opposition's ‘regime change’ call against government
NCB busts two synthetic drug labs in Greater Noida, seizes drugs worth Rs 50 crore
stories.summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau conducted a significant raid on two synthetic-drug laboratories in Greater Noida. During the operation, authorities seized large quantities of Methamphetamine and precursor chemicals. Two individuals were arrested, including a Nigerian national using a false identity. Investigators are tracing financial and chemical supply networks linked to the suspects. Citizens are urged to report suspicious activities to promote public safety and environmental health.

stories.title: Supreme Court’s enquiry committee launches complaint portal over violence during July protests
stories.summary: A complaint portal has been launched by the High Powered Enquiry Committee for individuals affected by protests. This portal allows victims to confidentially submit their complaints regarding violence that occurred in July. The Ministry of Home Affairs stated that submissions can also be made in person or via post. The committee will prioritize cases involving serious violence, especially against women protesters.

stories.title: Wyoming landowner rejects reservoir deal; $80 million project considers eminent domain for final land
stories.summary: In Wyoming, the Alkali Creek Reservoir project encounters significant hurdles as landowners resist easement agreements. Local landowner Paul Hughes has rejected an offer of $3,600 per acre, leading to discussions about eminent domain. While the project seeks to supply irrigation water to families, concerns about equitable benefit sharing arise, with landowners feeling they will endure construction impacts without receiving direct advantages.

stories.title: Trump aide helped set up ‘sanctioned hit’ on Katie Zacharia: Report
Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur
stories.summary: A tragic incident unfolded in Chassad village, Manipur, where a militant attack led to the death of one man and injuries to four others. Gunfire erupted between the militants and a local armed faction, with the violence persisting into the evening. Emergency services promptly transported the injured to a hospital, but sadly, one victim did not survive.

stories.title: Woman journalist, who accused Rahul Gandhi of manhandling, files complaint against him, others
stories.summary: Richa Parasar has alleged mistreatment, threats and use of criminal force against her while she was reporting on a protest near the Supreme Court on October 12, 2026. Parashar, who said she was three months pregnant, has alleged that Rahul Gandhi 'grabbed her hand' and 'pulled her' forward before his security personnel pushed her away while she was covering the INDIA bloc's protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on October 12.

stories.title: Black ink, burnt posters: Congress workers vandalise BJP office in Ajmer over Madan Rathore's Pakistan remark
'Nine murders' claim, then a clarification: How 'Chhote Sarkar' has put Nitish, JD(U) on the spot
stories.summary: Anant Singh is no ordinary legislator as locals rarely use his given name. They call him 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s. His story begins with his elder brother, Dilip Singh, who won as an independent and became a minister in Lalu Prasad’s cabinet during its first term, from 1990 to 1995.

stories.title: Over 1,000 residents oppose A$15bn data centre planned near Wagga Wagga
stories.summary: A proposed A$15 billion data-centre campus near Wagga Wagga has ignited a heated community conversation. Local residents express concerns about the impact on agricultural land, increased energy requirements, and ripple effects on the environment. Conversely, advocates highlight the prospects of enhanced economic growth and job opportunities for the area. The state government will assess these implications before making a final decision, with residents urging thorough evaluations to address their worries.

stories.title: Phulpati Dashain Messages: Nepal PM and President urge unity; Shah recalls Bhotekoshi floods
stories.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah and President Ramchandra Paudel share heartfelt festive wishes for Bada Dashain, underlining family cohesion and social harmony. In light of recent floods, Shah expresses sympathy for those affected while advocating for recovery efforts. Paudel notes the festival’s significance in fostering goodwill and cultural richness across Nepal’s communities, urging citizens to cherish their traditions and unite in celebration despite struggles.

stories.title: 'Can't die like this': Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recalls flydubai flight ordeal
stories.summary: In a shocking incident on September 30, Indian Captain Smit Machchhar endured an assault by his Omani co-pilot aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. With injury and determination, Machchhar opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers to step in and restrain the assailant. The aircraft landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, following a critical altitude drop.

stories.title: White House lists over $330 billion investments from India
FSSAI proposes ban on added sugars in infant food for babies up to 6 months
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has proposed a ban on adding fructose and sucrose in infant food. This proposal aims to impose stricter regulations for foods intended for infants up to six months old. The draft amendment seeks to enhance nutritional safeguards during a critical development period. Stakeholders are invited to submit their objections and suggestions regarding the proposal.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Dipke granted bail within 24 hours, Air India extends Saudi flight suspensions, Congress defends ‘regime change’ remark and more
'An evening in Paris': Opposition questions 'nature' of Punjab CM Mann's France visit
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's trip to Paris has triggered criticism from opposition leaders and parties. Concerns have been raised regarding drug abuse, law and order, and recent violent incidents in the state. Critics question the appropriateness of Mann's foreign visit, especially as he celebrated his birthday during a crisis. Allegations suggest that he attended a police meeting under the influence of alcohol, which raises further concerns.

stories.title: Violent Albania Protests Escalate: Student movement confronts Edi Rama; hundreds detained, dozens injured
stories.summary: In Tirana, a large assembly of students is rallying for Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation, citing rampant corruption. Tensions escalated into violent confrontations with riot police, resulting in several injuries. The protests highlight widespread dissatisfaction in Albania linked to job scarcity and corruption, aligning with similar movements across Europe regarding public services and living expenses.

stories.title: 'How it feels': Dipke shares cheeky SRK post after walking out of jail on conditional bond
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke was granted bail on certain conditions on Saturday, less than 24 hours after Delhi Police took him into preventive custody over his planned 'Tiranga Yatra' in Connaught Place (CP). Dipke was detained shortly after leaving the residence of NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande, where he had been staying, to attend the planned flag march in Connaught Place.

stories.title: US Congressman claims H-1B visa holders from India, China replacing Americans
Russia targets energy grid: Russia launches 320 missiles and drones; Zelenskyy warns of winter blackout
Texas landlord kept couple’s $2,600 deposit and sued; tenants won damages as appeal mostly failed
stories.summary: In a recent Texas court case, a landlord's attempt to retain a couple's security deposit, along with demands for extra payments post-move-out, was contested. The tenants triumphed, though the court adjusted some damage estimates. Texas statutes mandate landlords to avoid withholding deposits for usual wear and tear and to furnish detailed deductions. The ruling underlines the necessity for landlords to adhere to security deposit regulations strictly.

stories.title: Reese Witherspoon moves to buy back Hello Sunshine after 2021’s $900 million deal
stories.summary: Reese Witherspoon's recent collaboration with Mediawan to reacquire Hello Sunshine from Candle Media marks a pivotal moment in the entertainment sector. This transaction underscores rising transformations in valuation methods, as Hello Sunshine had previously commanded a valuation surpassing $900 million. With an ambition to enhance its narrative quality and global presence, Witherspoon is dedicated to guiding the company's creative trajectory and upcoming projects.

stories.title: Tear Gas At France Protests: Police clash with crowds over rising costs; authorities fear unrest
stories.summary: Nationwide protests erupted in France against soaring living costs and a decline in social welfare. Major cities like Paris and Marseille witnessed intense confrontations between law enforcement and demonstrators as tensions flared. With thousands taking to the streets, authorities are wary of possible chaos. Originating in northern suburbs where public service grievances peaked, both governmental and opposition factions are blaming each other for the unrest.

stories.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke granted bail within 24 hours of detention; court sets conditions
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke was detained shortly after leaving the residence where he was staying to attend the 'Tiranga Yatra' at Delhi's Connaught Place (CP). As Dipke left the residence of NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande, a police official told him, "We are placing you under preventive detention. Section 163 is in force in Connaught Place. You are being detained."

stories.title: Mother tried to protect daughter's property rights in 1987; 39 years later, court rules against her
stories.summary: A property transfer made by a Queens mother in 1987 led to a legal dispute nearly four decades later. Mary Mangiaracina had tried to secure lifetime rights to the Ridgewood property for herself and her daughter. However, after the property was sold to new owners, her daughter challenged the sale-related ownership claims in court. In April 2026, a New York appeals court ruled that the daughter had never legally received those lifetime rights.

stories.title: 'Another institution being destroyed’: Congress alleges RSS-BJP agenda behind Census 2027 changes
stories.summary: The Congress party on Saturday expressed alarm over the BJP-led government's decision to broaden the pool of eligible enumerators for Census 2027, prompting the inclusion of teachers from various educational institutions as census officers. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh has argued that this change jeopardizes the integrity of the census.

stories.title: Brad Paisley and wife pledged $1 million for a free grocery store in 2024; it opened in 2026
stories.summary: Brad Paisley and Kimberly Williams-Paisley have expanded their philanthropic efforts by launching a second location of The Store, a nonprofit grocery aimed at combating food insecurity in Nashville. Following their first store's success in 2020, which garnered over 3,100 dedicated volunteers, the couple has invested $1 million into this new initiative to ensure families receive dignified access to food choices and additional resources.

stories.title: Retirement Fuels Bushland Restoration: Ken and Jill revive 970ha bush; older Australians follow
stories.summary: In their eighties, Ken and Jill Hooper have become dedicated stewards of bushland in Australia, showcasing an inspiring commitment to conservation post-retirement. Over the last twenty years, after acquiring properties in Victoria and New South Wales, they focus on enhancing biodiversity and curbing invasive species to safeguard native wildlife. Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV to be discharged from hospital after successful lung cancer surgery today
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to leave the hospital after a successful lung cancer surgery, demonstrating commendable recovery progress. He engaged positively with his senior aides, expressing heartfelt gratitude towards the medical team for their dedicated care. As doctors await crucial test results to plan further treatment, the pontiff's upcoming trip to Latin America from November 6 to 17 highlights his determination to fulfill his commitments.

stories.title: ‘JD wanted to chat with us real quick’: How Trump’s press secretary was fired mid-interview
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia's brief tenure as White House press secretary ended abruptly after just five days due to a rocky start marked by an underwhelming briefing and questions regarding her qualifications. Despite Donald Trump's warning to reconsider the role, she was determined to fulfill her duties to the president and the nation. Her departure leaves the press office in limbo, especially with midterm elections approaching.

stories.title: Islandwide Power Outage: Sri Lanka hit by multi-hour blackout; hydropower failure probed
stories.summary: Sri Lanka faced a significant power outage that affected the entire island for over three hours. Essential services such as water supply, internet, and mobile connectivity were disrupted during this time. Authorities are investigating the cause, with a potential failure at a hydropower station being considered. Citizens were warned to conserve water due to the impact on supplies from power cuts.

stories.title: Stalin turns fire on Congress over SIR; serves up Bihar, Soren exit reminder
stories.summary: MK Stalin endorsed protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and criticized Congress for its inconsistent positions. During a DMK Parliamentary Party meeting, four resolutions were adopted, including the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The DMK emphasized its early opposition to the SIR process and questioned Congress's credibility on the issue. Resolutions included support for student protests and criticism of local party leaders’ silence.

stories.title: CJI flags ‘external forces’ that threatened to disrupt NLSIU convocation in his address
stories.summary: At the NLSIU convocation ceremony in Bengaluru, Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged external challenges that threatened the event, inspiring graduates to champion legal principles with unwavering integrity. Deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar reinforced the notion of law as a civic duty, sharing plans to bolster the state's legal system. Students were proudly awarded their degrees, marking the start of their professional journeys in the legal field.

stories.title: CJI Surya Kant urges NLSIU graduates to uphold ethics, defend justice and constitutional values
US ranchers win pipeline compensation fight but face $300,000 legal bill, Supreme Court to hear case
stories.summary: A group of North Dakota ranchers who spent nearly $300,000 fighting a pipeline company over land compensation have taken their dispute over legal expenses to the US Supreme Court. Although they reached a settlement, an appeals court ruled that the company need not cover their legal costs. The Supreme Court will hear the case on November 9.

stories.title: 10 charred to death in fire at seaside resort in Bangladesh
stories.summary: At least 10 people were killed and nine injured after a fire gutted a three-storey seaside resort in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar district early Saturday, The Express Tribune reported. The blaze broke out around 6.30am at TUPTUP Resto and Resort, built mainly of bamboo and wood. The cause remains unknown, while several people’s whereabouts were unclear. Injured victims were taken to hospital.

stories.title: Stephen King’s $3 million pledge helped transform hometown library into a $9.6 million project
stories.summary: Stephen and Tabitha King have committed $3 million to the Bangor Public Library renovation, provided that $6 million is raised through community efforts. Thanks to local support and a municipal bond, the library hit its $9 million target, kickstarting essential upgrades like roof repairs and improved community spaces, honoring both its historical significance and modern audience requirements.

stories.title: Forgotten John Constable Painting: $37 buy authenticated at $315,000; other 2024 finds hidden in plain sight
stories.summary: Hidden away in a cupboard for years, a painting believed to be by John Constable was recently found and has skyrocketed in value from its auction price of $37 to an astounding $315,000. This extraordinary revelation joins the ranks of remarkable discoveries, like a rare Lego mask and a Victorian brooch, which emphasize that ordinary objects can possess extraordinary worth.

stories.title: Snakes Found Inside Airport: Venomous western browns spotted in terminal; experts explain heat-driven visits
stories.summary: As summer approaches, Alice Springs Airport is preparing for an influx of snake sightings, with multiple reports emerging from terminal areas. In response, the airport management has put in place monitoring systems and hired professionals for safe snake removal. Travelers are encouraged to remain alert and immediately report any sightings to airport personnel, emphasizing safety first in this reptilian season.

stories.title: ‘Law and order does not exist’: SAD chief Badal holds CM Mann responsible for Punjab anti-drug activist’s murder
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal has held Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann accountable for the breakdown of law and order following the tragic murder of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh, also known as Jhota. The incident occurred during an altercation over drug sales at a pharmacy. CM Mann expressed his regret over the incident and assured citizens of a comprehensive investigation.

stories.title: ‘Nepalese nationals added to Goa voter rolls’: GFP chief claims SIR irregularities, seeks probe
‘Agenda to set country on fire’: BJP retorts to opposition’s ‘regime change’ call
In 2013, Tope Awotona emptied about $200,000 of his savings to build Calendly; eight years later investors valued the company at $3 billion
stories.summary: In 2013, Tope Awotona launched Calendly to tackle the difficulties professionals face in scheduling meetings. His journey began with personal funds, retirement savings, and loans, slowly gathering momentum. By 2021, Calendly had soared to a valuation exceeding $3 billion, driven by a booming user base and the demand for streamlined online scheduling.

stories.title: Sanjay Raut submits explanation in SC contempt case, says ‘we expect justice’
DMK seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, rules out joint protests with Congress
stories.summary: DMK has called a parliamentary party meeting emphasizing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They are demanding the immediate dismissal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and urge for an inquiry into his conduct. The party criticized Congress for perceived hypocrisy in its stance on the revisions while denouncing police actions against protests at Jantar Mantar. Furthermore, DMK MPs are set to discuss their grievances with President Droupadi Murmu.

stories.title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
New York’s Plaza Hotel to close for four years to restore its historic facade
stories.summary: Starting in January 2027, New York City's iconic Plaza Hotel will embark on a significant facade restoration that is projected to last a minimum of four years. This closure will impact not only guests but also local residents. With previous renovations totaling $450 million between 2005 and 2008, and a pandemic-related shutdown in 2020, this restoration seeks to uphold the hotel's renowned architectural significance for generations to come.

stories.title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has declared that internet access is a fundamental right applicable to all, including children. This decision reinforces the significance of achieving a balance between safety and individual freedoms online for minors. Moreover, the court advocates for enhancements in identifying harmful content. This landmark ruling builds upon earlier verdicts that recognized digital access as a constitutional entitlement.

stories.title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee faces court warrants over 2018 video targeting BJP IT cell
‘He spoke to Putin to buy diesel’: Ex-diplomat Fabian after Trump waives sanctions over Russian oil
McClellan base closed in 2001; 25 years later, its 3,000-acre site boasts $600m in investment
stories.summary: Following its shutdown in 2001, McClellan Air Force Base prompted worries about economic decline. However, the area has been revitalized with McClellan Park, which boasts a $600 million investment and encompasses 10 million square feet of facilities. The site now functions as a public-use regional hub, enhancing local transportation and offering significant employment opportunities, while also emphasizing environmental restoration initiatives since the base's closure.

stories.title: Indian woman jailed over son’s fatal stabbing faces possible deportation from UK
stories.summary: Kiran Kaur, convicted for aiding her son’s murder, has been sentenced to three years. Her son, Vickrum Digwa, is serving life for fatally stabbing an 18-year-old student. Kaur may face deportation back to India if released early under a government initiative. This case highlights concerns over religious symbols linked to violence. Appeals from both Kaur and Digwa are set to be heard in November.

‘Why is govt scared?’ Congress’s Vijay Wadettiwar slams Centre over delimitation, delay in all-party meet

BJP veteran LK Advani in ICU under medical observation after chest infection
'Verify before she vilifies': India rejects UN rapporteur's claims on youth protests
